posts.altText: They say insomnia is a medical condition but they never speak of the kind that comes from long buried trauma, the kind where your past returns as dreams, your dreams turn into nightmares, and your nightmares are nothing but recycled pieces of reality.
posts.text:
They say insomnia is a medical
condition, but they never speak of
the kind that comes from long
buried trauma, the kind where your
past returns as dreams, your
dreams turn into nightmares, and
your nightmares are nothing but
recycled pieces of reality.
posts.explanation: People say not being able to sleep is a health problem, but the writer says his comes from old pain he buried long ago. That pain comes back as dreams, the dreams turn bad, and the bad dreams are just real things that happened to him.

posts.displayTitle: I kept writing all the things I had to
posts.altText: I kept writing all the things I had to, but there was one thing I always fumbled. I could explain anything, any topic, any feeling, yet I still lost my way in the labyrinth of you. Perhaps I could articulate the entire universe. For I carried too much feeling to fit into sentences, and the world simply ran out of words to contain you.
posts.text:
I kept writing all the things I had
to, but there was one thing I
always fumbled. I could explain
anything, any topic, any feeling,
yet I still lost my way in the
labyrinth of you. Perhaps I could
articulate the entire universe. For I
carried too much feeling to fit into
sentences, and the world simply
ran out of words to contain you.
posts.explanation: The writer can put any topic or feeling into words, maybe even the whole universe, but he always gets lost when he tries to describe the person he loves. His feelings for them are too big for sentences, and the world does not have enough words to hold them.

posts.altText: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young age - to see yourself trapped. Some wounds don't bleed they grow roots inside you, turning your heart into a battlefield you walk through every day. And sometimes the cruelest part of suffering is realising you learned endurance before you ever learned joy.
posts.text:
You won't understand what it means to be
abandoned by hope at a young age - to see
yourself trapped. Some wounds don't bleed
they grow roots inside you, turning your
heart into a battlefield you walk through
every day. And sometimes the cruelest part
of suffering is realising you learned
endurance before you ever learned joy.
posts.explanation: The writer says others cannot understand losing hope while still young and feeling stuck. Some hurts do not show but grow deep inside, so every day feels like a fight. The saddest part is learning to put up with pain before ever learning to be happy.

Leave me to my grief and you'll find me
glowing in a different way, for I love my
sorrow more fiercely than anything
else-and, eventually, everything I love
abandons me anyway. Ironically, even this
grief shall one day grow weary of my
presence and slip away in quiet
indifference, for even sorrow grows
fatigued by its host. The tribulations I once
embraced will forsake me as well.
posts.explanation: The writer asks to be left alone with his sadness, saying he shines in his own way there because he loves it most. But everything he loves leaves him, so he thinks even his sadness and his troubles will one day get tired of him and quietly go.

posts.displayTitle: You build entire futures in the quiet corners of your mind
posts.altText: You build entire futures in the quiet corners of your mind, only to watch them collapse under the weight of reality. You mistake longing for destiny, believing the universe owes you what it never promised. And in the end, you realise the cruelest betrayal is the one you crafted with your own hands. And you still dare to hope!
posts.text:
You build entire futures in the quiet
corners of your mind, only to watch
them collapse under the weight of
reality.You mistake longing
for destiny, believing the universe
owes you what it never promised.
And in the end, you realise the
cruelest betrayal is the one you
crafted with your own hands.
And you still dare to hope!
posts.explanation: The writer says people dream up whole futures in their heads, then watch them fall apart in real life. They mistake wanting something for it being meant to be, so the worst letdown is one they made themselves. And still, he says almost in disbelief, they keep hoping.

posts.text:
You find them in everything - in the petals of
flowers, in passing crowds where you miss
them a little more than usual. You catch
yourself laughing at their memories, smiling
without realizing why. But when night
arrives, they become the very reason your
eyes ache with tears. It's strange how
happiness and sadness can coexist so
quietly within the same person, even when
that person no longer exists in your life.
posts.explanation: After someone leaves your life, you still see them everywhere, in flowers and in crowds, and their memory can make you smile. But at night the same memories bring tears. The writer finds it strange that happy and sad feelings can quietly live together over someone who is gone.

how time asks for reflection as if everyone

I healed, but because stopping was never an
option. Maybe that’s what this year
leaves me with not clarity or closure,
just the knowledge that I’m still here,
and that somehow had a cost.
posts.explanation: As the year ends, the writer says he did not grow, he just got through it. He lost things and learned hard lessons he never wanted, and kept going only because he could not stop. The year leaves him only knowing he is still here, and that this cost him something.

posts.text:
When I die, come with flowers
not because death asks for rituals but out of habit

and if you find yourself wondering
which ones I liked,
understand that the question no longer matters.

Flowers were never the point—
they were only a detail, the way love remembers small preferences.

I loved them because they reminded me of you.

and if you ask whether I loved them or you,
the answer is simple—I loved both in the
same quiet way things are loved right before
they stop meaning anything.
posts.explanation: The writer asks the person he loves to bring flowers when he dies, just out of habit. Which ones he liked will not matter; he only loved flowers because they reminded him of that person. He loved both quietly, the way you love things just before they stop mattering.

posts.text:
I have divided myself into quiet,
necessary layers—

from a certain fear of being seen whole
for I have learned that the closer one
comes to the center of a man, the more
unbearable he is, even to himself

and so I leave something in reserve—
hidden even from my own understanding

and the fact that the more someone
tries to cut open through me, the more
they cry...
posts.explanation: The writer has split himself into layers, afraid of being seen whole. He thinks the deeper you get into a person, the harder he is to bear, even for himself. So he hides a part even from himself, and, like cutting an onion, whoever cuts deeper into him ends up crying.

posts.caption:
my name is triyan. I am 20 and I live in kolkata.
I am a writer, a poet, and someone who keeps turning thoughts into words even when they don’t make complete sense.

I play guitar, I sketch sometimes, I take photos of things people usually ignore.
I read books not just to escape but to understand.

I am also a part time mali(the one who plants trees), I like watching things grow even if I don’t always feel like I am.
i sing when no one is listening or sometimes even when they are.

i love sports, badminton, football, cricket, basketball, table tennis and anything that makes me feel alive in the moment.

i love philosophy, not the textbook kind but the kind that hits you randomly at 2am and refuses to leave.
i write what i observe.
real life, small moments, conversations, silence, the way people change, the way they stay.

i overthink a lot, maybe too much, but instead of fighting it i turn it into something i can hold onto.

i am still figuring out who i am becoming, but i know i feel deeply, notice quietly, and express honestly.

there’s so much more to know, so much more to tell
and yet so little time to live it all, tell it all. —triyan

posts.text:
What do I relate myself to?
Perhaps I am a moth drawn towards a flame, for I knew it would burn me,

or perhaps I am the flame itself,
burning through all the emotions of mine I have called moths

And if you ask me whether I loved it or not,I did—
enough to let it burn me whole...

So much that I sacrificed myself at the altar of love.
But did I suffer?
I did—

All these dreadful thoughts turned my love into a pyre,
enough to burn these moths for eternity in endless suffering.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if he is a moth flying to a fire he knows will burn him, or the fire itself, burning up his own feelings. He loved enough to let it burn him whole, and he suffered; dark thoughts turned that love into a funeral fire that keeps burning his feelings forever.

with your presence.

Tomorrow,
Perhaps I'll be spared from
this grief you left behind,
I'll be a fool again or maybe
I'll be full again...
posts.explanation: Yesterday the writer and the person he loved were together. Today he grieves and fools himself by pretending they are still there. Tomorrow he might be free of this pain, though he is not sure if he will be fooled again or feel whole again.

posts.caption: Fools day
posts.displayTitle: It's funny how months have passed… it's April now—
posts.altText: It's funny how months have passed… it's April now— and I still lie to myself about your love, deceiving my own heart. December will come again… and I'll still be waiting for you.
posts.text:
It’s funny how months have passed...
it's April now—

and I still lie to myself about your love,
deceiving my own heart.

December will come again...
and I’ll still be waiting for you.
posts.explanation: Months have passed and it is April, yet the writer still lies to himself that the person loves him. He knows December will come again and he will still be waiting for them.

posts.caption: They do not listen...
posts.displayTitle: We spend our lives explaining ourselves in fragments, in half sentenc…
posts.altText: We spend our lives explaining ourselves in fragments, in half sentences and silences, hoping someone will gather the pieces and call it whole. But people do not listen to understand, they listen to recognize something of themselves. And if you do not resemble their wounds, they will never recognize yours.
posts.text:
We spend our lives explaining ourselves
in fragments, in half sentences and
silences, hoping someone will gather the
pieces and call it whole. But people do
not listen to understand, they listen to
recognize something of themselves. And
if you do not resemble their wounds,
they will never recognize yours.
posts.explanation: The writer says we show who we are only in bits and pieces, hoping someone will put them together and understand us fully. But people listen mainly to find themselves in what we say, so if your pain does not look like theirs, they will never see it.

posts.caption: They choose themselves always!
posts.displayTitle: perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
posts.altText: perhaps the cruelest realization is this— that most people do not intend to hurt you. They simply choose themselves in moments where you hoped they would choose you. And that difference, so small in action, becomes immeasurable in consequence.
posts.text:
perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
that most people do not intend to hurt you.

They simply choose themselves in moments
where you hoped they would choose you
And that difference,
so small in action,
becomes immeasurable in consequence.
posts.explanation: The writer says the hardest thing to accept is that most people do not mean to hurt you. They just pick themselves at the moments you hoped they would pick you, and that small choice ends up hurting more than can be measured.

posts.caption: Why were you the only one?
posts.displayTitle: Out of everyone— who could have left me, why were you the only one?
posts.altText: Out of everyone— who could have left me, why were you the only one?
posts.text:
Out of everyone—
who could have left me,
why were you the only one?
posts.explanation: The writer asks why, out of everyone who could have left him, this person was the only one who did.

posts.caption: Traces of you in me remains forever!
posts.displayTitle: There is a strange kind of honesty in what decays—
posts.altText: There is a strange kind of honesty in what decays— When flesh forgets its shape and time begins to speak through rot, nothing pretends anymore. The heart that once held warmth, promises, and trembling hope becomes just another hollow space with nothingness, no different from bone or dust. and yet, I wonder... if someone were to reach inside what remains of me, would they still…
posts.text:
There is a strange kind of honesty in what decays—

When flesh forgets its shape and time begins to
speak through rot, nothing pretends anymore.

The heart that once held warmth, promises, and trembling
hope becomes just another hollow space with nothingness,
no different from bone or dust.

and yet, I wonder...

if someone were to reach inside what
remains of me,

would they still find traces of you carved deeper
than the veins themselves?
posts.explanation: The writer says rotting is honest, because a dead body no longer pretends. A heart that once held warmth and hope becomes just empty space, like bone or dust. Still, he wonders if someone looking inside what is left of him would find the person he loved, marked deep in him.

posts.caption: I was just gloomy
posts.displayTitle: Oh, you loved the rain—
posts.altText: Oh, you loved the rain— but look how funny it is, that I came into your life like the clouds which never rained, even after covering the whole sky...
posts.text:
Oh, you loved the rain—

but look how funny it is, that I came into your
life like the clouds which never rained,

even after covering the whole sky...
posts.explanation: The person the writer loved adored the rain. Sadly, he says, he came into their life like clouds that cover the whole sky but never rain, filling their life without ever giving them what they loved.

posts.caption: What I am is half life half death...
posts.displayTitle: I felt it not in sorrow— but in absence.
posts.altText: I felt it not in sorrow— but in absence. In the way joy no longer reached me in the way even pain seemed distant, as though it belonged to someone else. And it was then, not in despair but in a kind of cold clarity, not as a question anymore but as something I had already become what I am is half life and half death.
posts.text:
I felt it not in sorrow—
but in absence.

In the way joy no longer reached me
in the way even pain seemed distant,
as though it belonged to someone else.

And it was then, not in despair but in a kind of cold clarity,

not as a question anymore but as something
I had already become
what I am is half life and half death.
posts.explanation: The writer did not feel his pain as sadness but as emptiness: joy no longer reached him, and even pain felt far away, like someone else's. In a calm, cold moment he understood that he had already become half alive and half dead.

posts.caption: So close yet so distant...
posts.displayTitle: You see, the most terrifying thing is not that I suffer, but that I o…
posts.altText: You see, the most terrifying thing is not that I suffer, but that I observe— I watch myself exist the way one watches a stranger through a window, recognizing the gestures but feeling no ownership of them. My voice sounds familiar— my thoughts even resemble my own, and yet there is always that thin, unbridgeable distance.
posts.text:
You see, the most terrifying thing is not that I suffer,
but that I observe—

I watch myself exist the way one watches
a stranger through a window,
recognizing the gestures but feeling no ownership of them.

My voice sounds familiar—

my thoughts even resemble my own,
and yet there is always that thin, unbridgeable distance.
posts.explanation: The writer says the scariest part is not his suffering but that he watches himself live, like watching a stranger through a window. His voice and thoughts seem like his own, yet there is always a thin gap between him and his own life that he cannot cross.

posts.caption: These rings won't fit others
posts.displayTitle: You asked me to find someone better, but how could I—
posts.altText: You asked me to find someone better, but how could I— how do I take these rings I shaped for your fingers and pretend they were meant for someone else how do I call it love again when it still carries your name in silence
posts.text:
You asked me to find someone better,
but how could I—

how do I take these rings I shaped for your fingers
and pretend they were meant for someone else

how do I call it love again
when it still carries your name in silence
posts.explanation: The person he loved told the writer to find someone better, but he cannot. He made his love, like rings, to fit only them, and he cannot pretend it was meant for anyone else, because his love still quietly carries their name.

posts.caption: I am more dead than alive
posts.displayTitle: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me,
posts.altText: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me, I die everyday a little more than yesterday, Perhaps I am more dead than alive each passing day..
posts.text:
Greif, chaos, and an endless noise
of things that rots within me ,

I die everyday a little more than yesterday,

Perhaps I am more dead than alive
each passing day..
posts.explanation: Grief, confusion and constant noise are rotting inside the writer. He feels he dies a little more each day, until he seems more dead than alive.

posts.caption: Just a left over..
posts.displayTitle: What I am is me— just the leftovers from yesterday.
posts.altText: What I am is me— just the leftovers from yesterday.
posts.text:
What I am is me—
just the leftovers from yesterday.
posts.explanation: The writer feels that who he is now is only what is left over from yesterday, the scraps of his past self.

posts.caption: It never does
posts.displayTitle: Because some loves do not die with the body.
posts.altText: Because some loves do not die with the body. They linger, quietly decomposing, turning into something nameless, something that no longer hurts the way it used to. but never truly leaves either.
posts.text:
Because some loves do not die
with the body. They linger,
quietly decomposing, turning
into something nameless,
something that no longer hurts
the way it used to. but never
truly leaves either.
posts.explanation: The writer says some love does not end when a person dies. It stays on, slowly changing into something without a name; it no longer hurts the way it did, but it never really goes away.

posts.caption: Do i exist only to be buried one day?
posts.displayTitle: when I die— what will you raise my grave for?
posts.altText: when I die— what will you raise my grave for? To honor a man who survived his decay, yet never escaped his grief? Or to admit that all I ever was ends here, beneath this grave my entirety?
posts.text:
when I die—
what will you raise my grave for?
To honor a man who survived his decay,
yet never escaped his grief?
Or to admit that all I ever was
ends here,
beneath this grave my entirety?
posts.explanation: The writer asks what his grave will stand for once he dies. Will it honor a man who lived through falling apart but never got free of his sadness, or will it simply mark that everything he was ends there?

posts.caption: Insomnia
posts.displayTitle: They say insomnia is a medical condition…
posts.altText: They say insomnia is a medical condition… But they never speak of the kind— that comes from long buried trauma, the kind where your past returns as dreams your dreams turn into nightmares, and your nightmares are nothing but recycled pieces of reality.
posts.text:
They say insomnia is a medical condition...
But they never speak of the kind—
that comes from long buried trauma,
the kind where your past returns as dreams
your dreams turn into nightmares,
and your nightmares are nothing
but recycled pieces of reality.
posts.explanation: People say not being able to sleep is a health problem, but the writer says his comes from old pain he buried long ago. That pain comes back as dreams, the dreams turn bad, and the bad dreams are just real things that happened to him.

posts.caption: Will you grief?
posts.displayTitle: My grief is the only thing that has stayed with me over time
posts.altText: My grief is the only thing that has stayed with me over time, so if I start loving you, grief... "will you leave me too?"
posts.text:
My grief is the only thing
that has stayed with me over time,
so if I start loving you, grief...
"will you leave me too?"
posts.explanation: Sadness is the only thing that has stayed with the writer over the years. So if he starts to love his grief, he fears it will leave him too, like the things he loved before.

posts.caption: How much more god?
posts.displayTitle: God— How many more trials How many more provings
posts.altText: God— How many more trials How many more provings till I am worthy enough...
posts.text:
God—
How many more trials
How many more provings
till I am worthy enough...
posts.explanation: The writer asks God how many more tests and hard times he must go through before he is finally good enough.

posts.caption: Poetry has its own soul i believe...
posts.displayTitle: Poetry exists even before it's written by the poet
posts.altText: Poetry exists even before it's written by the poet and every poetry, poet has a story of its own.
posts.text:
Poetry exists even
before it's written by
the poet and every
poetry, poet has a
story of its own.
posts.explanation: The writer says a poem already exists before the poet writes it down, and every poem, like every poet, has its own story.

posts.caption: Faith...
posts.displayTitle: A soul is born without a name for faith
posts.altText: A soul is born without a name for faith, yet the world is quick to give it one. What stays— though, is not what is assigned but what is felt. In the end, whatever brings peace quietly becomes your faith even a love, even an absence.
posts.text:
A soul is born without a name for faith,
yet the world is quick to give it one.
What stays—
though,
Is not what is assigned but what is felt.
In the end,
whatever brings peace quietly becomes your faith
even a love,.
even an absence.
posts.explanation: The writer says a person is born without any religion, but the world quickly gives them one. What really stays is not the faith you are given but what you feel, so whatever brings you peace quietly becomes your faith, even a love, or even someone's absence.

posts.caption: It kills you everyday day...
posts.displayTitle: What doesn't kill you leaves you unable to breathe in the middle of t…
posts.altText: What doesn't kill you leaves you unable to breathe in the middle of the night, lets you feel the tremors, lets you know how easily you can be replaced, and what doesn't kill you kills you a little more every day than yesterday.
posts.text:
What doesn’t kill you
leaves you unable to breathe
in the middle of the night,
lets you feel the tremors,
lets you know how easily you can be replaced,
and what doesn’t kill you
kills you a little more every day than yesterday.
posts.explanation: People say what does not kill you makes you stronger, but the writer disagrees. It leaves you unable to breathe at night, shaking, and aware of how easily you can be replaced, and it slowly kills you a little more each day.

posts.caption: It still burns...
posts.displayTitle: I yearn for you— so where are you now?
posts.altText: I yearn for you— so where are you now? All those promises of forever turned into dust and I into ashes for the fire you burned in my chest still lies there inextinguishable...
posts.text:
I yearn for you—
so where are you now?
All those promises of forever turned into dust
and I into ashes
for the fire you burned in my chest
still lies there inextinguishable...
posts.explanation: The writer longs for the person he loved and asks where they are now. Their promises of forever have turned to dust, and he has burned down to ashes, because the fire they lit in his heart still cannot be put out.

posts.caption: I could have.. even better
posts.displayTitle: I could have loved you— with a kind of devotion that ruins a man
posts.altText: I could have loved you— with a kind of devotion that ruins a man, that strips him bare before himself.
posts.text:
I could have loved you—
with a kind of devotion
that ruins a man,
that strips him bare before himself.
posts.explanation: The writer says he could have loved this person with a devotion so complete that it would have destroyed him and left him with nothing to hide, even from himself.

posts.caption: Point of no return
posts.displayTitle: The tragedy is— you begin to measure your worth in their presence
posts.altText: The tragedy is— you begin to measure your worth in their presence and worse, in their absence and once that begins, there is no dignity left in you only dependence dressed up as devotion. And that is a point of no return in love.
posts.text:
The tragedy is—
you begin to measure your worth in their presence
and worse,
in their absence and once that begins,
there is no dignity left in you only
dependence dressed up as devotion.
And that is a point of no return in love
posts.explanation: The writer says the sad thing is when you start judging your own value by whether someone is with you or not. Once that starts, you lose your self-respect and simply depend on them while calling it love, and there is no coming back from that.

posts.caption: What should I do?
posts.displayTitle: Must we understand all— to be understood the way we desire?
posts.altText: Must we understand all— to be understood the way we desire? Or should we understand all, just to acknowledge that no one can ever truly understand us?
posts.text:
Must we understand all—
to be understood the way we desire?
Or should we understand all,
just to acknowledge that
no one can ever truly understand us?
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if we must understand everything in order to be understood the way we want. Or does understanding everything only teach us that no one can ever truly understand us?

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: It is strange— isn't it?
posts.altText: It is strange— isn't it? How a heart can hold so much and still feel like it has nothing at all.
posts.text:
It is strange—
isn’t it?
How a [heart image] can hold so much
and still feel like
it has nothing at all.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that a heart can be holding so much and still feel completely empty.

posts.caption: Still held intact ❤️‍🩹
posts.displayTitle: They say we are the museum of things we love
posts.altText: They say we are the museum of things we love but I am The rage fueled by my father's destruction, I am the sorrow of my mother's wounds. I am my lover's abandonment, the silence it left behind. I am my friend's betrayal, the faithlessness it took with it. "I am every ounce of it, still held intact."
posts.text:
They say we are the museum of things we love
but I am The rage fuelled by
my father's destruction
I am the sorrow of my mother's wounds
I am my lover's abandonment,
the silence it left behind
I am my friend's betrayal,
the faithlessness it took with it.
"I am every ounce of it, still held intact."
posts.explanation: People say we are made of the things we love, but the writer says he is made of his hurts: anger from his father's ruin, sorrow from his mother's pain, the silence a lover left behind, and a friend's betrayal. He still carries every bit of it.

posts.caption: I have!
posts.displayTitle: I have stared at my ceiling—far more than I've dared to meet another'…
posts.altText: I have stared at my ceiling— far more than I've dared to meet another's eyes. Hours dissolve into nights as I lie there, scrutinising the void above me, attempting to fill its blankness with thoughts too heavy to speak aloud.
posts.text:
I have stared at my ceiling—
far more than I've dared to meet another's eyes.
Hours dissolve into nights as I lie there,
scrutinising the void above me,
attempting to fill its blankness with
thoughts too heavy to speak aloud.
posts.explanation: The writer has spent more time staring at his ceiling than looking into other people's eyes. He lies awake for hours into the night, trying to fill that blank space with thoughts too heavy to say out loud.

posts.caption: Fragments...
posts.displayTitle: And maybe that is what we are—
posts.altText: And maybe that is what we are— fragments pretending to be whole, carrying oceans within us yet thirsting for something we cannot even name.
posts.text:
And maybe that is what we are—
fragments pretending to be whole,
carrying oceans within us
yet thirsting for something
we cannot even name.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks maybe we are all broken pieces pretending to be whole. We hold huge feelings inside, like oceans, yet still feel thirsty for something we cannot even name.

posts.caption: How can I be a fool again?
posts.displayTitle: I have left a piece of myself in everything I have loved,
posts.altText: I have left a piece of myself in everything I have loved, And here I stand before myself, with nothing left inside me. My heart aches to be full again but how can I full again without being a fool again? I am too understanding now to be fooled again with emotions again.
posts.text:
I have left a piece of myself
in everything I have loved,
And here I stand before myself,
with nothing left inside me.
My heart aches to be full again but how can
I full again without being a fool again?
I am too understanding now to be
fooled again to be full with emotions again.
posts.explanation: The writer has left a part of himself in everything he loved, and now he feels empty inside. He wants to feel full again, but he fears that means being fooled again, and he understands too much now to let himself be fooled.

posts.caption: Tell me is it?
posts.displayTitle: Tell me, is it not absurd?
posts.altText: Tell me, is it not absurd? To crave permanence in a world that refuses to grant it— and yet to sabotage it the moment it dares to appear. There is, within me, a contradiction so profound that I cannot resolve it. I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch, as though kindness itself were a prelude to loss.
posts.text:
Tell me, is it not absurd?
To crave permanence in a world
that refuses to grant it—
and yet to sabotage it
the moment it dares to appear.
There is, within me,
a contradiction so profound
that I cannot resolve it,
I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch,
as though kindness itself were a prelude to loss.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that he wants things to last in a world where nothing does, yet he ruins them as soon as they show up. He longs to be held but tenses up when touched, as if kindness always comes just before a loss.

posts.caption: The curse of being abandoned 🥀
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps this is the true nature of my curse—
posts.altText: Perhaps this is the true nature of my curse— not that I am abandoned, but that I have come to expect it with such conviction that I unknowingly assist in its arrival. A silent accomplice to my own solitude. I carry the curse of being abandoned
posts.text:
Perhaps this is the true nature of my curse—
not that I am abandoned,
but that I have come to expect it with such
conviction that I unknowingly assist in its arrival.
A silent accomplice to my own solitude
I carry the curse of being abandoned.
posts.explanation: The writer says his real curse is not being left, but expecting it so strongly that, without meaning to, he helps it happen. In a quiet way, he helps make himself alone.

posts.caption: I would peel them for eternity if that's what you want 🍊
posts.displayTitle: abandonment is an orange…
posts.altText: abandonment is an orange... the peels are the threshold the line between staying and leaving. I'll peel it unknowingly, making it easier for you to abandon me until there is nothing left for you to do and once I peel it, you are free to eat it
posts.text:
abandonment is an orange...

the peels are
the threshold
the line between
staying and leaving

I'll peel it unknowingly,
making it easier for you to abandon me

until there is nothing left for you to do

and once I peel it,
you are free to ~~leave~~ eat it
posts.explanation: The writer says being left is like an orange. The peel is the line between staying and leaving, and he peels it himself without knowing, making it easy for the other person to go. Once it is peeled, they can leave, or simply take and enjoy what he opened up.

posts.caption: Neither fully alone nor truly accompanied!
posts.displayTitle: And so I remain—neither wholly alone, nor ever truly accompanied…
posts.altText: And so I remain— neither wholly alone, nor ever truly accompanied... standing at the threshold of every connection, already mourning its end.
posts.text:
And so I remain—
neither wholly alone,
nor ever truly accompanied...
standing at the threshold of every connection,
already mourning its end.
posts.explanation: The writer feels he is never fully alone but never truly with anyone either. At the start of every new friendship or love, he is already sad about how it will end.

posts.caption: I became the paradox...
posts.displayTitle: I used to adore paradoxes, until I accidentally became one
posts.altText: I used to adore paradoxes, until I accidentally became one. I built a maze out of my own feelings and never found the way out. Perhaps I named that trap love... my own Labyrinth, and I the Minotaur guarding it.
posts.text:
I used to adore paradoxes,
until I accidentally became one.
I built a maze out of my own feelings
and never found the way out.
Perhaps I named that trap love...
my own Labyrinth, and I the Minotaur guarding it.
posts.explanation: The writer used to love things that go against themselves, until he became one. He built a trap out of his own feelings, maybe calling it love, and got lost in it, like the monster in the old Greek story who guards a maze he can never leave.

posts.caption: Lost for eternity...
posts.displayTitle: They say what cannot be forgotten comes to your dreams,
posts.altText: They say what cannot be forgotten comes to your dreams, maybe it's true, because the ache of losing what you once believed was yours is far beyond what words can explain. Maybe to soothe that pain, the mind projects it into our dreams, letting us live with what we lost for eternity.
posts.text:
They say what cannot be forgotten
comes to your dreams,
maybe it's true,
because the ache of losing what you once believed
was yours is far beyond what words can explain.
Maybe to soothe that pain,
the mind projects it into our dreams,
letting us live with what we lost for eternity.
posts.explanation: The writer says the things we cannot forget come back in our dreams. Losing something you believed was yours hurts beyond words, so perhaps the mind shows it in dreams to ease the pain, letting us keep living with what we lost forever.

posts.caption: Unfair exchange...
posts.displayTitle: I offered blood in return for pomegranate juice an unfair exchange I…
posts.altText: I offered blood in return for pomegranate juice an unfair exchange I mistook for love. For theirs was real and mine was devotion. Maybe it wasn't their fault, maybe it was me.. I offered too much... I kept pouring myself out even when the cup was already full. I mistook my sacrifice for love and their silence for acceptance and in the end, I was the only one who walked away bl…
posts.text:
I offered blood in return for pomegranate juice
an unfair exchange I mistook for love.
For theirs was real and mine was devotion.
Maybe it wasn't their fault, maybe it was me..
I offered too much...
I kept pouring myself out even
when the cup was already full.
I mistook my sacrifice for love and
their silence for acceptance and in the end,
I was the only one who walked away bleeding....
posts.explanation: The writer gave his whole self, something deep and costly, and got back only something that looked similar, a trade he mistook for love. He wonders if it was his fault for giving too much and taking their silence as acceptance, since he was the only one left hurt.

posts.caption: They are still buried inside me
posts.displayTitle: I have abandoned countless versions of myself just to survive the exp…
posts.altText: I have abandoned countless versions of myself just to survive the expectations of others. My past selves are buried inside me alive. Their unrest haunts me still, for I walk each day over the graves I dug with my own hands. It was I who condemned them. It was I who buried them alive.
posts.text:
I have abandoned countless versions of myself
just to survive the expectations of others.
My past selves are buried inside me alive.
Their unrest haunts me still,
for I walk each day over the
graves I dug with my own hands.
It was I who condemned them.
It was I who buried them alive.
posts.explanation: To live up to what others expected, the writer gave up many versions of who he was. Those old selves are still alive inside him, buried, and they trouble him. He walks over their graves every day, knowing he was the one who buried them.

posts.caption: I hoped that was my biggest mistake 🥀
posts.displayTitle: I hope—I hoped—I'm still hoping..
posts.altText: I hope—I hoped—I'm still hoping.. god— the word is tearing mee apart. Hopehopehopehope—until it breaks open like a seizure in my chest. I hoped so hard it started screaming back at me. I hoped till it warped, till it twisted the knife inside my chest, till it turned on me. And now it's just HOP E HOPE HOPE— a mess I can't clean out of my head. I hoped-and that was my first mis…
posts.text:
I hope—I hoped—I’m still hoping..
god— the word is tearing mee apart.
Hopehopehopehope—until it breaks open
like a seizure in my chest.
I hoped so hard it started screaming back at me.
I hoped till it warped, till it twisted
the knife inside my chest, till it turned on me.
And now it’s just HOP E H O P E H O P E—
a mess I can’t clean out of my head.
I hoped-and that was my first mistake
I hoped until the echo of it scraped against my ribs.
And now hope feels like a wound I keep touching,
just to remind myself it's still bleeding...
posts.explanation: The writer keeps hoping, over and over, until hope stops helping and starts hurting him. It twists inside him like a knife and fills his head with noise. He now sees hoping as his first mistake, a wound he keeps touching just to feel that it still hurts.

posts.caption: Endless act
posts.displayTitle: Sometimes the greatest actors aren't the ones on the screens
posts.altText: Sometimes the greatest actors aren't the ones on the screens, they are into the crowd pretending to be fine.
posts.text:
Sometimes the greatest actors aren't
the ones on the screens ,

they are into the crowd
pretending to be fine.
posts.explanation: The writer says the best actors are often not on screen but ordinary people in the crowd, pretending they are fine.

posts.caption: It should never be...
posts.displayTitle: I hope no one ever uncovers the desolate feelings abandoned long ago
posts.altText: I hope no one ever uncovers the desolate feelings abandoned long ago, for the frightened child I once was still sits there shivering in the shadows I left behind. Those memories remain sealed like a room no one should enter. Every now and then, the door rattles and I keep walking past it, pretending I don't hear the trembling inside.
posts.text:
I hope no one ever uncovers
the desolate feelings abandoned long ago,
for the frightened child I once was still sits
there shivering in the shadows I left behind.
Those memories remain sealed
like a room no one should enter.
Every now and then, the door rattles
and I keep walking past it,
pretending I don't hear the trembling inside.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes no one ever finds the lonely feelings he pushed away long ago, where the scared child he once was is still shaking. He keeps those memories locked like a room, and when they stir, he walks past and pretends not to notice.

posts.caption: I wish i could...
posts.displayTitle: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions now lying in…
posts.altText: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions now lying in the coldest part of my heart once belonged to you. How the colourful flowers that once bloomed for you have now grown into thorny vines that pierce my heart instead. I hope that someday, when you come back, I'll have enough flowers left to offer you not just trembling hands numbed by cold
posts.text:
I wish I could tell you that
all the abandoned emotions
now lying in the coldest part
of my heart once belonged to you.
How the colourful flowers
that once bloomed for you
have now grown into thorny vines
that pierce my heart instead.
I hope that someday, when you come back,
I'll have enough flowers left to offer you
not just trembling hands numbed by cold.
posts.explanation: The writer wishes he could tell the person he loved that the left-behind feelings in his heart were once for them. The love that grew for them has turned sharp and hurts him. He hopes that if they return, he will still have some love left to give, not just numb, shaking hands.

posts.caption: I lie to myself still...
posts.displayTitle: I came home to rest from an unfair world,
posts.altText: I came home to rest from an unfair world, but the home itself doesn't feel like home without you in it. I lay on the bed to rest, but the unjust of being betrayed by the world feels like termites crawling beneath my skin, eating the flesh the world itself has already left to rot. So I just lie on the floor instead, lying myself with your warmth, yet shivering with the ache of…
posts.text:
I came home to rest from an unfair world,
but the home itself doesn’t
feel like home without you in it.
I lay on the bed to rest,
but the unjust of being betrayed by the world
feels like termites crawling beneath my skin,
eating the flesh the world itself
has already left to rot.
So I just lie on the floor instead,
lying myself with your warmth,
yet shivering with the ache of losing you
posts.explanation: The writer came home to rest from an unfair world, but home does not feel like home without the person he lost. The hurt of being betrayed makes his bed feel like bugs eating under his skin, so he lies on the floor, comforting himself with their warmth while shaking from losing them.

posts.caption: I'll be left with it...
posts.displayTitle: Grief has learned my shape so well
posts.altText: Grief has learned my shape so well it fits into me perfectly, as if it has become an undeniable part of me that I no longer refuse. It's already running through my veins. I just know— wherever I may go, I'll be left with it.
posts.text:
Grief has learned my shape so well
it fits into me perfectly,
as if it has become an undeniable part of me
that I no longer refuse.
It’s already running through my veins.
I just know—
wherever I may go,
I’ll be left with it.
posts.explanation: The writer says grief knows him so well that it fits him perfectly and has become a part of him he no longer fights. It runs through his whole body, and he knows that wherever he goes, it will stay with him.

posts.caption: I hope death feels like the happy life I never had...
posts.displayTitle: When I'm about to die and my mind begins to project the best moments…
posts.altText: When I'm about to die and my mind begins to project the best moments of my life, I hope it isn't filled with the endless grief I've carried almost all my days. I hope instead it finds you, your hand in mine, And us in the rain. And maybe… it will be kind enough to create a few non existing ones like being loved by my parents.
posts.text:
When I’m about to die and my mind begins to
project the best moments of my life,
I hope it isn’t filled with the endless grief
I’ve carried almost all my days.
I hope instead it finds you,
your hand in mine, And us in the rain.
And maybe...
it will be kind enough to create a few
non existing ones like being loved by my parents.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes that as he dies, the best moments his mind replays will not be his lifelong grief, but the person he loves holding his hand in the rain. Maybe it will even make up moments that never happened, like being loved by his parents.

posts.caption: Something so foreign...
posts.displayTitle: I was forced into adulthood so prematurely
posts.altText: I was forced into adulthood so prematurely that now even the simplest gestures of childhood feel foreign to me, as if something essential had already withered in me, as if I am merely acting out a role whose truth was denied to me.
posts.text:
I was forced into adulthood so prematurely

that now even the simplest gestures
of childhood feel foreign to me,

as if something essential had
already withered in me,

as if I am merely acting out a role
whose truth was denied to me.
posts.explanation: The writer had to grow up far too early, so now even simple childlike things feel strange to him. It is as if something important in him dried up, and he is only playing a part in a life he was never allowed to truly have.

posts.caption: Clever they are...
posts.displayTitle: They gave me poison, and they gave me my memories.
posts.altText: They gave me poison, and they gave me my memories. Without hesitation, I chose the latter.. yet I died, How clever of them.
posts.text:
They gave me poison,
and they gave me my memories.
Without hesitation,
I chose the latter..

yet I died, How clever of them.
posts.explanation: The writer was offered either poison or his memories, and he chose his memories. But the memories killed him anyway, and he bitterly notes that the people who offered them must have known they would hurt just as much.

posts.caption: My heart reels!!
posts.displayTitle: My heart reeks of memories from the past.
posts.altText: My heart reeks of memories from the past. For I turned myself into a crime scene, each part of me revealing a different crime. Crime? The crime of holding something too dear, of loving while expecting, and a crime that can never be investigated, for it holds more paradoxes than anything else. So I ask you, are you also a part of that crime?
posts.text:
My heart reeks of memories from the past.
For I turned myself into a crime scene,
each part of me revealing a different crime.
Crime? The crime of holding something too dear,
of loving while expecting,
and a crime that can never be investigated,
for it holds more paradoxes than anything else.
So I ask you, are you also a part of that crime?
posts.explanation: The writer feels his heart is full of past memories, like a crime scene where every part shows a different wrong. His crimes were holding something too dear and loving while expecting love back, things too confusing to ever solve. He asks if the person he speaks to was part of it too.

posts.caption: Endless loop
posts.displayTitle: Memories are destined to return,
posts.altText: Memories are destined to return, piercing through your heart with a cruelty nothing else can replicate and still, you find yourself slipping back into the very emotions that once drowned you. It's strange how the past resurrects itself, wearing the perfume of what you once longed for. And stranger still, how your soul leans into the pain, as if hoping it will finally feel like…
posts.text:
Memories are destined to return,
piercing through your heart with a cruelty
nothing else can replicate and still,
you find yourself slipping back into the very
emotions that once drowned you.
It's strange how the past resurrects itself, wearing
the perfume of what you once longed for.
And stranger still,
how your soul leans into the pain,
as if hoping it will finally feel like home.
posts.explanation: The writer says memories always come back and hurt the heart like nothing else. Yet you still fall back into the same feelings that once overwhelmed you. The past returns smelling like what you once wanted, and strangely, your soul leans into the pain, hoping it will finally feel like home.

posts.caption: The pain reminded me of you...
posts.displayTitle: "The thorns made me bleed so much that the roses
posts.altText: "The thorns made me bleed so much that the roses eventually started smelling like you."
posts.text:
"The thorns made me bleed
so much that the
roses eventually started
smelling like you."
posts.explanation: The writer was hurt so much by love's sharp side that even its sweet side, the roses, came to remind him of the person who hurt him.

posts.caption: Leave me at it...
posts.displayTitle: Leave me at my grief and you'll find me glowing in a different way,
posts.altText: Leave me at my grief and you'll find me glowing in a different way, for I love my sorrow more fiercely than anything else and inevitably, everything I love abandons me anyway.
posts.text:
Leave me at my grief and you’ll find me
glowing in a different way,
for I love my sorrow more fiercely than anything else
and inevitably,
everything I love abandons me anyway.
posts.explanation: The writer asks to be left alone with his sadness, where he shines in his own way, because he loves his sorrow more than anything. And in the end, everything he loves leaves him anyway.

posts.caption: I have made myself an onion haha..
posts.displayTitle: I have divided myself into necessary layers—
posts.altText: I have divided myself into necessary layers— from a certain fear of being seen whole for I have learned that the closer one comes to the center of a man, the more unbearable he is, even to himself... and so I leave something in reserve— hidden even from my own understanding and the fact that the more someone tries to cut open through me, the more they cry...
posts.text:
I have divided myself into necessary layers—

from a certain fear of being seen whole for
I have learned that the closer one comes to
the center of a man, the more unbearable he
is, even to himself...

and so I leave something in reserve—
hidden even from my own understanding

and the fact that the more someone tries to
cut open through me, the more they cry...
posts.explanation: Afraid of being seen completely, the writer has split himself into layers, believing the closer anyone gets to a person's center, the harder he is to bear, even for himself. He hides a part even from himself, and, like with an onion, whoever cuts deeper into him ends up crying.

posts.caption: Did you?
posts.displayTitle: Mother, I am that dust from the corners of the walls
posts.altText: Mother, I am that dust from the corners of the walls that goes unnoticed by you. Mother, did you know my presence before father reached his hands out to clean my entirety?
posts.text:
Mother,
I am that dust from the corners of the walls
that goes unnoticed by you.

Mother,
did you know my presence
before father reached his hands
out to clean my entirety?
posts.explanation: The writer tells his mother he is like the dust in the corners of the walls that she never notices. He asks whether she even knew he was there before his father reached out to wipe all of him away.

posts.caption: The world ran out of words to contain you...
posts.displayTitle: I kept writing all the things I had to,
posts.altText: I kept writing all the things I had to, but there was one thing I always fumbled. I could explain anything, any topic, any feeling, yet I still lost my way in the labyrinth of you. Perhaps I could articulate the entire universe. For I carried too much feeling to fit into sentences, and the world simply ran out of words to contain you.
posts.text:
I kept writing all the things I had to,
but there was one thing I always fumbled.
I could explain anything,
any topic, any feeling,
yet I still lost my way in the labyrinth of you.
Perhaps I could articulate the entire universe.
For I carried too much feeling to fit into sentences,
and the world simply ran out of words
to contain you.
posts.explanation: The writer can put any topic or feeling into words, maybe even the whole universe, but he always gets lost when he tries to describe the person he loves. His feelings for them are too big for sentences, and the world does not have enough words to hold them.

posts.caption: Unable to refuse
posts.displayTitle: There are things I couldn't have lived without,
posts.altText: There are things I couldn't have lived without, there are things I was never meant to lose, ruins I never asked to inherit. But I was mistaken. What stayed with me was never what I wanted, just fragments of those ruins, the unnecessary weight of what I once thought was everything, carved deep into my bones only because I lacked the will to refuse.
posts.text:
There are things I couldn’t have lived without,
there are things I was never meant to lose,
ruins I never asked to inherit.
But I was mistaken.
What stayed with me was never what I wanted,
just fragments of those ruins,
the unnecessary weight
of what I once thought was everything,
carved deep into my bones
only because I lacked the will to refuse.
posts.explanation: The writer thought some things were too important to live without or to lose. He was wrong: what stayed was never what he wanted, only broken pieces he never asked for and the heavy weight of what once meant everything, stuck deep in him because he lacked the strength to refuse.

posts.caption: Half of me 🥀
posts.displayTitle: Everything I did was in half, half efforts,
posts.altText: Everything I did was in half, half efforts, half hearted studies, half life and half death, as if doing things halfway would leave me something to hope for more, but my love for you was full, so tell me, why did you leave me, leaving me half, still hoping for more.
posts.text:
Everything I did was in half, half efforts,
half hearted studies,
half life and half death,
as if doing things halfway would
leave me something to hope for more,
but my love for you was full,
so tell me,
why did you leave me,
leaving me half, still hoping for more?
posts.explanation: The writer did everything halfway, his work, his studies, even living, as if leaving things half done would give him something more to hope for. But he loved this person fully, so he asks why they left, leaving him only half, still hoping for more.

posts.caption: Silence kills you even when love doesn't...
posts.displayTitle: Someone once taught me that there is a strange kind of violence in si…
posts.altText: Someone once taught me that there is a strange kind of violence in silence, the kind that leaves you hanging between an unfinished story and a thousand unanswered paradoxes. A silence that doesn't break, doesn't explain, doesn't close the chapter, it just leaves you suspended in the ache of not knowing. Maybe that's why silence feels less like peace and more like a punishment.
posts.text:
Someone once taught me that there
is a strange kind of violence in silence,
the kind that leaves you hanging between an
unfinished story and a thousand unanswered paradoxes
A silence that doesn't break,
doesn't explain,
doesn't close the chapter,
it just leaves you suspended in
the ache of not knowing.
Maybe that's why silence feels less like
peace and more like a punishment.
posts.explanation: The writer says silence can hurt like violence. When someone goes quiet without explaining or ending things, you are left stuck, not knowing what happened. So silence feels less like peace and more like a punishment.

posts.caption: You won't!!
posts.displayTitle: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young…
posts.altText: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young age— to see yourself trapped. Some wounds don't bleed they grow roots inside you, turning your heart into a battlefield you walk through every day. And sometimes the cruelest part of suffering is realising you learned endurance before you ever learned…
posts.text:
You won't understand what it means
to be abandoned by hope at a young age—
to see yourself trapped.
Some wounds don't bleed
they grow roots inside you,
turning your heart into a battlefield
you walk through every day.
And sometimes the cruelest part of suffering
is realising you learned endurance
before you ever learned joy.
posts.explanation: The writer says others cannot understand losing hope while still young and feeling stuck. Some hurts do not show but grow deep inside, so every day feels like a fight. The saddest part is learning to put up with pain before ever learning to be happy.

posts.caption: My old clothes still smells like you
posts.displayTitle: There is something strange about memories,
posts.altText: There is something strange about memories, about they don't leave, and they don't get replaced. They just sit quietly at the core of your existence, like old clothes you no longer wear but still cannot let go of. Maybe we keep them because letting go would mean admitting that time moved on without us. Or maybe because we're hesitant to let someone else have what once belonged…
posts.text:
There is something strange about memories,
about they don't leave,
and they don't get replaced.
They just sit quietly at the core of your existence,
like old clothes you no longer
wear but still cannot let go of.
Maybe we keep them because letting go would
mean admitting that time moved on without us.
Or maybe because we're hesitant to let
someone else have what once belonged to us.
posts.explanation: The writer says memories never leave and are never replaced. They stay deep inside, like old clothes you no longer wear but cannot throw away. He thinks we keep them because letting go would mean time moved on without us, or because we don't want anyone else to have what was once ours.

posts.caption: Like sand...
posts.displayTitle: I am convinced that nothing stays forever—
posts.altText: I am convinced that nothing stays forever— not feelings, not even the moments we swear we'll remember for a lifetime. Everything we try to hold eventually slips through our fingers like sand. And in the process of trying to become something new, like sand we raise our temperature to turn into something else we eventually become glass, and a glass too is meant to be broken.
posts.text:
I am convinced that nothing stays forever—
not feelings,
not even the moments we swear
we’ll remember for a lifetime.
Everything we try to hold eventually
slips through our fingers like sand.
And in the process of trying to become something new,
like sand we raise our temperature to turn
into something else we eventually become glass,
and a glass too is meant to be broken.
posts.explanation: The writer believes nothing lasts, not feelings and not even moments we promise to remember. Everything slips away like sand. When we try to change into someone new, we are like sand heated into glass, and glass, too, will one day break.

posts.caption: Ink flowing through my pen..
posts.displayTitle: Maybe the only way I can bleed is through words
posts.altText: Maybe the only way I can bleed is through words and maybe I do not bleed red anymore it is just ink
posts.text:
Maybe the only way I can bleed
is through words and maybe
I do not bleed red anymore
it is just ink
posts.explanation: The writer says the only way he can let his pain out is by writing. His hurt no longer comes out as blood; it comes out as ink on the page.

posts.caption: Three stages theory!!
posts.displayTitle: There are three stages of existence—
posts.altText: There are three stages of existence— to be born, to truly live, and to die. But people rarely reach the second and are left as hollow shells, "so empty" that even death feels like nothing. And if you ask me whether I am alive or dead, know that I have survived just enough to mourn the grief of your loss every day
posts.text:
There are three stages of existence—
to be born,
to truly live,
and to die.
But people rarely reach the second
and are left as hollow shells,
"so empty" that even death feels like nothing.
And if you ask me whether I am alive or dead,
know that I have survived just enough
to mourn the grief of your loss every day
posts.explanation: The writer says life has three steps: being born, really living, and dying. Most people never really live, so they feel so empty that even death means nothing. He himself is only alive enough to grieve, every day, the person he lost.

posts.caption: The way she looked at me..
posts.displayTitle: If you take away all the night from within me,
posts.altText: If you take away all the night from within me, will I still, ever be able to outshine the light of her eyes, I saw when she looked at me?
posts.text:
If you take away all the night
from within me, will I still,
ever be able to outshine the light of her eyes,
I saw when she looked at me?
posts.explanation: The writer asks whether, if all the darkness inside him were taken away, he could ever shine brighter than the light he saw in her eyes when she looked at him. He seems to feel nothing in him could ever match that look.

posts.caption: Silence...
posts.displayTitle: You looked at me with blurry eyes,
posts.altText: You looked at me with blurry eyes, holding out a bouquet of flowers, asking if we could start it all over again in the name of love. But I stayed silent because silence is the only weapon I have left, now that I no longer have the voice to speak from six feet under.
posts.text:
You looked at me with blurry eyes,
holding out a bouquet of flowers,
asking if we could start it
all over again in the name of love.
But I stayed silent because
silence is the only weapon I have left,
now that I no longer have the
voice to speak from six feet under.
posts.explanation: Someone he loved comes to him with teary eyes and flowers, asking to start over. But the writer is already dead and buried, so he cannot speak. Silence is all he has left, and it is his only answer.

posts.caption: Anhedonia..
posts.displayTitle: These days the world appears uncannily altered,
posts.altText: These days the world appears uncannily altered, as though someone has surreptitiously stole the colour from everything I once found radiant. And they say beauty lies in the eyes of the beholder, but maybe I've become too colourblind to understand its meaning...
posts.text:
These days the world appears uncannily altered,
as though someone has
surreptitiously stole the colour
from everything I once found radiant.
And they say beauty lies
in the eyes of the beholder,
but maybe I've become too
colourblind to understand its meaning...
posts.explanation: The writer says the world now looks strangely different, as if someone secretly took the color out of everything he used to find bright and lovely. People say beauty depends on who is looking, but he fears he can no longer see beauty at all.

posts.caption: Love kills before any cigarette could ever
posts.displayTitle: I smoked love as though it were a cigarette,
posts.altText: I smoked love as though it were a cigarette, and believe me, it devastates the lungs far more mercilessly than any tobacco ever could. It constricts your breath, wringing your chest until air itself becomes a luxury. Even cancer feels almost courteous in comparison. And still, addicted to its ruin, I lit it up anyway.
posts.text:
I smoked love as though it were a cigarette,
and believe me,
it devastates the lungs far more
mercilessly than any tobacco ever could.
It constricts your breath,
wringing your chest until
air itself becomes a luxury.
Even cancer feels almost courteous in comparison.
And still,
addicted to its ruin,
I lit it up anyway.
posts.explanation: The writer compares love to smoking. He says love hurt him worse than cigarettes ever could, squeezing his chest until he could barely breathe. Even cancer seems gentle next to it. Still, he was hooked and kept going back to it, knowing it would ruin him.

posts.caption: A little late to post this but yeah ok...
posts.displayTitle: It's May again, and I wonder may I ever see you again?
posts.altText: It's May again, and I wonder may I ever see you again? and if I may, will you be the same again may I fall in love with you again may it still be you or may it just be a memory wearing your face once more, again
posts.text:
It’s May again, and I wonder
may I ever see you again?
and if I may,
will you be the same again
may I fall in love with you again
may it still be you
or may it just be a memory
wearing your face once more, again...
posts.explanation: It is May again, and the writer wonders if he will ever see the person he loved again. If he does, will they be the same? Will he fall for them again, or will it only be a memory that looks like them?

posts.caption: Time took everything...
posts.displayTitle: I have lost my perception of time while waiting for you.
posts.altText: I have lost my perception of time while waiting for you. They said time would heal everything, but I lost time, lost to time, lost in time itself... You buried me in it... tell me, what year is it? when did I die?
posts.text:
I have lost my perception of time
while waiting for you.
They said time would heal everything,
but I lost time,
lost to time,
lost in time itself...
You buried me in it... tell me,
what year is it? when did I die?
posts.explanation: While waiting for the person he loved, the writer lost all sense of time. People said time would heal him, but he only got lost in it. He feels as if they buried him in that waiting, and he asks what year it is and when he died.

posts.caption: What is this curse??
posts.displayTitle: What is this curse I carry?
posts.altText: What is this curse I carry? To be abandoned by everything I love, or to love so deeply that I forget how to stay? Why does every propinquity turn into distance, every promise into silence, and every "forever" into something that leaves? Is it fate, or is it something in me that holds too tightly until everything slips away? Like hands that grip, but instead of hands, it's the…
posts.text:
What is this curse I carry?
To be abandoned by everything I love,
or to love so deeply that I forget how to stay?
Why does every propinquity turn into distance,
every promise into silence,
and every “forever” into something that leaves?
Is it fate, or is it something in me
that holds too tightly.
until everything slips away?
Like hands that grip,
but instead of hands, it’s the neck...
posts.explanation: The writer asks why everything he loves leaves him: closeness turns to distance, promises to silence, and forever never lasts. He wonders if it is fate, or if he holds on so tightly that his love chokes things, like hands around a neck, until they slip away.

posts.caption: It rots!!
posts.displayTitle: Time doesn't heal anything,
posts.altText: Time doesn't heal anything, it makes you rot, decays every memory, it only moves on while dragging you with it. and still, we live on with the decay of our rotting bodies, surviving but at what cost?
posts.text:
Time doesn’t heal anything,
it makes you rot,
decays every memory,
it only moves on while dragging you with it.
and still,
we live on with the decay
of our rotting bodies,
surviving but at what cost?
posts.explanation: The writer says time does not heal pain. It makes everything rot, wears away memories, and drags people along with it. We keep living with this slow decay, and he asks whether just surviving is worth what it costs.

posts.caption: What a strange ritual
posts.displayTitle: Strange how love learns to arrive only after absence becomes permanen…
posts.altText: Strange how love learns to arrive only after absence becomes permanent, like the flowers on my grave when I didn't even receive one when I was alive, as if a heartbeat matters only once it stops, as if I only mattered when I was dead.
posts.text:
Strange how love learns to arrive
only after absence becomes permanent,
like the flowers on my grave
when I didn’t even receive
one when I was alive,
as if a heartbeat matters only once it stops,
as if I only mattered when I was dead.
posts.explanation: The writer says love often shows up only after someone is gone for good. People bring flowers to his grave, though he never got a single flower while alive. It feels as if a person only matters once their heart stops.

posts.caption: Two sides of the same coin...
posts.displayTitle: love and separation exist as two sides of the same coin,
posts.altText: love and separation exist as two sides of the same coin, one always carrying the shadow of the other. as if every promise already knows its ending. as if every closeness rehearses its goodbye and we still call it love, knowing what it costs...
posts.text:
love and separation
exist as two sides of the same coin,
one always carrying the shadow of the other.
as if every promise already knows its ending.
as if every closeness rehearses its goodbye
and we still call it love,
knowing what it costs...
posts.explanation: The writer says love and parting always come together, like two sides of one coin. Every promise seems to already know how it will end, and every closeness is already practicing its goodbye. Still, people call it love, knowing how much it will cost them.

posts.caption: Purest form of devotion...
posts.displayTitle: I am a miserable being who sabotages his own happiness
posts.altText: I am a miserable being who sabotages his own happiness for others and calls it love, and somehow I convinced myself that this slow undoing was devotion, that losing myself piece by piece was the purest form of staying.
posts.text:
I am a miserable being
who sabotages his own happiness
for others and calls it love,
and somehow I convinced myself
that this slow undoing was devotion,
that losing myself piece by piece
was the purest form of staying.
posts.explanation: The writer calls himself miserable because he gives up his own happiness for others and calls it love. He fooled himself into thinking that slowly falling apart, losing himself bit by bit, was the truest way to stay loyal.

posts.caption: They sink..
posts.displayTitle: words meant to be weightless sink like anchors in the heart
posts.altText: words meant to be weightless sink like anchors in the heart while feelings so heavy often float away unheard. we guard ourselves from emotions yet let sentences walk in barefoot, leaving fingerprints on parts of us that were never meant to be touched.
posts.text:
words meant to be weightless
sink like anchors in the heart while feelings
so heavy often float away unheard.
we guard ourselves from emotions
yet let sentences walk in barefoot,
leaving fingerprints on parts of us
that were never meant to be touched.
posts.explanation: The writer says careless words can sink deep in the heart like heavy anchors, while big, heavy feelings often drift away unheard. We protect ourselves from feelings, but let words walk right in, and they leave marks on soft, private parts of us that no one should touch.

posts.caption: Did you get the ref?
posts.displayTitle: I stand just to stand till I start to crawl,
posts.altText: I stand just to stand till I start to crawl, I feel like falling but you won't let me fall, I call it love or just the need to fall, I fall, I'm bound to fall... to lose it all, I just had to say it
posts.text:
I stand just to stand
till I start to crawl,
I feel like falling
but you won’t let me fall,
I call it love or just the need to fall,
I fall, I’m bound to fall... to lose it all,
I just had to say it all.
posts.explanation: The writer is barely holding himself up and feels close to collapse. He wants to fall, but the person he loves will not let him. He cannot tell if this is love or just a need to give in, and he feels sure he will fall and lose everything. He just needed to say it.

posts.caption: Perhaps it's not the way we think it is..
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps heaven was never above us.
posts.altText: Perhaps heaven was never above us. Perhaps the body is merely a failed attempt at containing pain. Spines bend beneath the unbearable architecture of suffering while feathers erupt where language no longer survives. What we call pain may not be pain simply... every angel probably looked monstrous before the worship began.
posts.text:
Perhaps heaven was never above us.
Perhaps the body is merely a
failed attempt at containing pain.
Spines bend beneath the unbearable
architecture of suffering
while feathers erupt where
language no longer survives.
What we call pain may not be pain simply...
every angel probably looked
monstrous before the worship began.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if heaven was never in the sky, and if the body simply cannot hold all its pain. Suffering bends people, and wings grow where words run out. He seems to say pain can turn someone into something holy: even angels may have looked like monsters before anyone worshipped them.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: Some wounds do not bleed,
posts.altText: Some wounds do not bleed, they bloom beneath the skin. and perhaps that is why some people smile so beautifully, because the flower of grief learned how to wear their face.
posts.text:
Some wounds do not bleed,
they bloom beneath the skin.
and perhaps that is why
some people smile so beautifully,
because the flower of grief
learned how to wear their face.
posts.explanation: The writer says some hurts do not show on the outside; they grow quietly inside a person, like a flower under the skin. That may be why some people have such lovely smiles: their grief has learned to hide behind a happy face.

posts.caption: Missing pieces
posts.displayTitle: I tried to find the missing piece of myself in others,
posts.altText: I tried to find the missing piece of myself in others, but the whole of me got lost instead. Every search for myself led back to the ruin I became. I even searched within those ruins for a soul that disappeared while searching for itself.
posts.text:
I tried to find the missing
piece of myself in others,
but the whole of me got lost instead.
Every search for myself led
back to the ruin I became.
I even searched within those ruins for
a soul that disappeared while searching for itself.
posts.explanation: The writer tried to find the part of himself he was missing in other people, but he lost all of himself instead. Every time he looked for himself, he only found the broken person he had become, and even there his soul was gone, lost while searching for itself.

posts.caption: What are your thoughts about this?
posts.displayTitle: I carry grief like a second skin,
posts.altText: I carry grief like a second skin, stitched into everything I do. There are days I laugh so naturally that it feels like I am betraying this skin of grief I have too. Memories return like wounds reopening in the skin, the skin of grief beneath, beneath the laugh too. Maybe grief isn't any of this. Maybe it's the silence after happiness, realizing you have no one left to share i…
posts.text:
I carry grief like a second skin,
stitched into everything I do.
There are days I laugh so naturally
that it feels like I am betraying
this skin of grief I have too.
Memories return like wounds
reopening in the skin,
the skin of grief beneath,
beneath the laugh too.
Maybe grief isn't any of this.
Maybe it's the silence after happiness,
realizing you have no one left to share it with too.
posts.explanation: The writer says grief is like a second skin, part of everything he does. Laughing freely feels like betraying it, and memories keep opening old wounds. In the end he thinks grief may be the quiet after a happy moment, when you realize no one is left to share it with.

posts.caption: Share your thoughts
posts.displayTitle: Do we seek God—
posts.altText: Do we seek God— because the war inside us needs a religion or do we seek Him, repenting for the tragedy of what the war turned us into?
posts.text:
Do we seek God—
because the war inside us needs a religion
or do we seek Him,
repenting for the tragedy
of what the war turned us into?
posts.explanation: The writer asks why we turn to God. Is it because the fight inside us needs something to believe in, or because we are sorry for what that inner fight has turned us into?

posts.caption: Happy mother's day ❤️‍🩹
posts.displayTitle: Mother, I wish I could take away the sadness
posts.altText: Mother, I wish I could take away the sadness from which you showed me love. in the way you kept giving warmth while forgetting you were cold too.
posts.text:
Mother,
I wish I could take away
the sadness from which
you showed me love.
in the way you kept giving warmth
while forgetting you were cold too.
posts.explanation: The writer speaks to his mother. He wishes he could take away the sadness she carried while loving him, because she kept giving him warmth while forgetting that she was cold and hurting too.

posts.caption: Love and insanity...
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps the only difference between, love and insanity
posts.altText: Perhaps the only difference between, love and insanity is how you distinguish between them, either ways it consumes you whole long before you realise it does...
posts.text:
Perhaps the only difference between,
love and insanity
is how you distinguish between them,
either ways it consumes you whole long before
you realise it does...
posts.explanation: The writer says love and madness may be almost the same; the only difference is how you choose to tell them apart. Either way, both swallow you whole before you even notice.

posts.caption: Will he now?
posts.displayTitle: God must find us embarrassing
posts.altText: God must find us embarrassing the way we turn people into religions just because they once knew how to calm the war inside us and here I thought healing would feel noble instead, it feels like forgetting the sound of your voice... There was a time when losing you felt impossible to survive, now it survives without asking me first..
posts.text:
God must find us embarrassing
the way we turn people into religions
just because they once knew
how to calm the war inside us
and here I thought healing would feel noble
instead,
it feels like forgetting the sound of your voice...
There was a time
when losing you felt impossible to survive,
now it survives without asking me first..
posts.explanation: The writer thinks God must be embarrassed by how we treat people like gods just because they once calmed the fight inside us. He expected healing to feel proud, but it feels like forgetting the lost person's voice. Once the loss seemed impossible to survive; now he is surviving it without having chosen to.

posts.caption: Beautiful isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: What's beautiful is that after all that you did to me,
posts.altText: What's beautiful is that after all that you did to me, I still love you with everything I have. What's beautiful is that even with the dagger inside my heart, I would still offer it to you without hesitation. What's beautiful is that I keep returning to the fire, hoping it won't burn me this time.
posts.text:
What’s beautiful is that
after all that you did to me,
I still love you with everything I have.
What’s beautiful is that
even with the dagger inside my heart,
I would still offer it to you without hesitation.
What’s beautiful is that
I keep returning to the fire,
hoping it won’t burn me this time.
