posts.explanation: The writer says that after all the hurt this person caused him, he still loves them completely. Even with the wound they gave him in his heart, he would hand that heart to them. He keeps going back to the one who burns him, hoping this time will be different, and calls this beautiful.

posts.caption: Do i not?
posts.displayTitle: Do I not deserve to be loved?
posts.altText: Do I not deserve to be loved? Or am I so unlovable that love itself detests me for loving it? Do I not deserve to be kept? Or has grief taken a special liking to me that I keep pushing away everything that tries to keep me, love me?
posts.text:
Do I not deserve to be loved?
Or am I so unlovable
that love itself detests me for loving it?
Do I not deserve to be kept?
Or has grief taken a special liking to me
that I keep pushing away
everything that tries to keep me, love me?
posts.explanation: The writer asks if he does not deserve love, or if he is so hard to love that love itself hates him for trying. He asks if he does not deserve to be kept, or if grief likes him so much that he keeps pushing away everyone who tries to love him.

posts.caption: Sliping away..
posts.displayTitle: What is so wrong with this life of mine
posts.altText: What is so wrong with this life of mine that everything I drag closer by the day only goes farther away at night? I try to be held by those hands of yours yet I keep slipping away through the narrow spaces between them. Why is it that everything I love leaves me and everything I try to save kills me instead.
posts.text:
What is so wrong with this life of mine
that everything I drag closer by the day
only goes farther away at night?
I try to be held by those hands of yours
yet I keep slipping away
through the narrow spaces between them.
Why is it that everything I love leaves me
and everything I try to save
kills me instead?
posts.explanation: The writer asks what is wrong with his life, that everything he pulls close during the day slips away by night. He tries to hold on to the person he loves but keeps slipping through their fingers. Everything he loves leaves him, and everything he tries to save ends up destroying him.

posts.caption: My prayers never reach him..
posts.displayTitle: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well
posts.altText: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome, like light entering a house that has forgotten how to open its windows. Like the prayer in an abandoned church that never reaches its God.
posts.text:
Sometimes I wonder,
if sorrow learned my name so well
that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome,
like light entering a house that has
forgotten how to open its windows.
Like the prayer in an abandoned church
that never reaches its God.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if sadness knows him so well that even happiness feels like an unwanted guest when it comes. He feels like a house that has forgotten how to open its windows to let light in, or a prayer in an empty church that never reaches God.

posts.caption: Dear grief, I ask you why?
posts.displayTitle: Has happiness never found its way to me,
posts.altText: Has happiness never found its way to me, or did grief make its hive inside my chest, building a home from everything that I have ever tried to heal from?
posts.text:
Has happiness never
found its way to me,
or did grief make
its hive inside my chest,
building a home from everything
that I have ever tried to heal from?
posts.explanation: The writer asks if happiness never found him at all, or if grief moved into his chest like bees building a hive, making its home out of every pain he has tried to heal from.

posts.caption: May 13
posts.displayTitle: And when my soul leaves my body,
posts.altText: And when my soul leaves my body, it will search for yours through eternity so that we meet, we fall in love and you leave again... turning me into a poet all over again. I write for you again... or maybe I already am.
posts.text:
And when my soul leaves my body,
it will search for yours through eternity
so that we meet,
we fall in love and
you leave again...
turning me into a poet all over again.
I write for you again... or maybe I already am.
posts.explanation: The writer says that when he dies, his soul will look for this person forever. They will meet, fall in love, and the person will leave again, and the pain will make him a poet once more. He ends by wondering if this is already happening now.

posts.caption: Was it?
posts.displayTitle: There is a stain of memories on my soul that I try to erase,
posts.altText: "There is a stain of memories on my soul that I try to erase, but if it is destined to fade, was it ever truly a stain to begin with?" God, that name is stitched into my soul.
posts.text:
“There is a stain of memories
on my soul that I try to erase,
but if it is destined to fade,
was it ever truly a stain to begin with?”
God, that name is stitched into my soul.
posts.explanation: The writer has memories stuck to his soul like a stain he tries to wash off. He wonders: if it is bound to fade, was it ever really a stain? But one person's name is sewn into his soul, and that will not come out.

posts.caption: I lose myself whole...
posts.displayTitle: I try to hold everything while losing everything of myself.
posts.altText: I try to hold everything while losing everything of myself. even so, I keep holding on. even so, I feel numb, until my hands no longer know whether they are carrying love, you, or just the weight of losing it all.
posts.text:
I try to hold everything
while losing everything of myself.
even so, I keep holding on.
even so, I feel numb,
until my hands no longer know
whether they are carrying love, you,
or just the weight of losing it all.
posts.explanation: The writer tries to hold on to everything while losing himself in the process. He keeps holding on anyway, though he feels numb, until his hands can no longer tell if they are carrying love, the person he loves, or just the heavy weight of losing it all.

posts.caption: They smile beautifully
posts.displayTitle: Some wounds do not bleed,
posts.altText: Some wounds do not bleed, they bloom beneath the skin. and perhaps that is why some people smile so beautifully, because the flower of grief learned how to wear their face.
posts.text:
Some wounds do not bleed,
they bloom beneath the skin.
and perhaps that is why
some people smile so beautifully,
because the flower of grief
learned how to wear their face.
posts.explanation: The writer says some hurts do not show on the outside; they grow quietly inside a person, like a flower under the skin. That may be why some people have such lovely smiles: their grief has learned to hide behind a happy face.

posts.caption:
7 stages of grief..
Collab with @wordsbyurwa
posts.displayTitle: What do vultures and other scavengers feed on?
posts.altText: Grief (Shock/Disbelief, Denial, Anger, Bargaining, Depression, Guilt, Acceptance). What do vultures and other scavengers feed on? The decay of one's body and soul. Grief is much the same, it engulfs you the moment you are left to rot. Shock: I was never a vulture; humans taught me to be one. They betrayed me and fed me the venom of their words…
posts.text:
What do vultures and other scavengers
feed on? The decay of one's body and soul.
Grief is much the same, it engulfs you the
moment you are left to rot.
---
Shock

I was never a vulture; humans taught me to be
one. They betrayed me and fed me the venom
of their words. But how? How, in the end, am
I the one accused of eating others' souls and
flesh? How do I tell them I'm just good at
preying? I'm just good at preying! they made
me a vulture. Humans curse the monster,
but they forget that they're the ones who are
uglier, filthier monsters for creating other
monsters.
—Urwa Noor
---
Denial

What do mirrors do to shattered reflections?
They continue pretending you are whole.
Denial is much the same,
it teaches the heart to rehearse normalcy...
while grief bleeds beneath it,
like the grief stitched into my skin
pretending to be fine, like memories
acting as anesthesia upon my soul,
numbing the ache.
---
Anger

What do wildfires feed on?
Anything dry enough to burn.
Anger is much the same,
it turns you, memories into
dry leaves, dry enough for you to burn
sets your soul ablaze from within.
—Urwa Noor
---
Bargaining

What do gamblers lose themselves to?
The illusion that one more chance
might change everything.
Bargaining is no different,
it keeps you kneeling before closed doors,
While begging and asking the
doors to be opened.
---
Depression

A phase where grief starts eating a person alive.
A place where I don't hear my mother's voice
anymore, where I don't comb my hair, staring
at a single point for so long that it hurts my
eyes. Endless grief, endless suffering, endless
mourning– for what I have become, and for
what I could have been.
—Urwa Noor
---
Guilt

What do parasites survive on?
A host that blames itself for being
consumed. Guilt behaves the same way,
it feeds on your conscience until
even survival begins to feel undeserved,
worse than death itself.
---
Acceptance

An ant gets crushed underfoot, and we
finally realize that we only pretend to be
saints; we are sinners, biologically born to
destroy. Acceptance hits the sinner the same
way. It crawls inside my skin like a maggot,
eating and hollowing me out slowly until it
consumes all of my saintliness and only
my sins are left.
—Urwa Noor
posts.explanation: The writer shows grief in stages, each like something that feeds on a person. Grief eats you once you are left alone; cruel people turn you cruel, then blame you; denial pretends you are fine; anger burns you up; bargaining begs at locked doors; depression and guilt eat you alive; acceptance leaves only your sins.

posts.caption: What love does to your heart...
posts.displayTitle: What do curtains do to a burning room?
posts.altText: What do curtains do to a burning room? They hide the flames, not the smoke. love is no different, it covers the grief and holds your heart gently, while everything inside your heart continues to collapse.
posts.text:
What do curtains do to a burning room?
They hide the flames, not the smoke.
love is no different,
it covers the grief and holds your heart gently,
while everything inside your
heart continues to collapse.
posts.explanation: The writer says a curtain in a burning room can hide the flames but not the smoke. Love works the same way: it covers up grief and holds the heart gently, but inside, the heart keeps falling apart.

posts.caption: What is it??
posts.displayTitle: What is the meaning of love?
posts.altText: What is the meaning of love? Maybe it is a mother cooling hot food with her breath before feeding her child, or a trembling hand refusing to let go of another when the days are numbered, perhaps it is a prayer whispered for someone who is ill when life is more uncertain than death, or maybe the sacrifices…
posts.text:
What is the meaning of love?
Maybe it is a mother cooling hot food
with her breath before feeding her child,
or a trembling hand refusing to let go
of another when the days are numbered,
perhaps it is a prayer whispered for someone
who is ill when life is more uncertain than death,
or maybe the sacrifices we continue to make
even when they offer us nothing in return?
posts.explanation: The writer wonders what love really is. Maybe it is a mother blowing on hot food before feeding her child, a shaking hand that will not let go of someone who is dying, a quiet prayer for someone sick, or the sacrifices we keep making even when we get nothing back.

posts.caption: Perhaps i worship the wrong religion
posts.displayTitle: Your presence was a devotion to me.
posts.altText: Your presence was a devotion to me. Your absence turned it into a religion, and somehow, I still worship, as if my God would finally hear me.
posts.text:
Your presence was a
devotion to me.

Your absence turned
it into a religion,
and somehow,

I still worship,

as if my God
would finally hear me.
posts.explanation: When this person was near, the writer was deeply devoted to them. After they left, that love grew into something like a religion, and he still worships them, hoping, as with a god, that they will finally hear him.

posts.caption: My love....
posts.displayTitle: The distance between you and me now is that of heaven and hell
posts.altText: The distance between you and me now is that of heaven and hell, heaven, you, and hell, me. I ache to be with you, but all these sins inside me have held me back, held me down. I cannot reach you from here.
posts.text:
The distance between you and me now
is that of heaven and hell,
heaven, you, and hell, me.
I ache to be with you,
but all these sins
inside me have held me back ,
held me down.
I cannot reach you from here.
posts.explanation: The writer feels the gap between him and the person he loves is as wide as the gap between heaven and hell: they are heaven, and he is hell. He longs to be with them, but his own wrongs hold him back, so he cannot reach them.

posts.caption: Maybe death isn't what we think it is
posts.displayTitle: And maybe death is not a man in black carrying a scythe.
posts.altText: And maybe death is not a man in black carrying a scythe. Maybe it is your mother's arms waiting to hold you warmly. Maybe it is your father's voice, filled with pride for the final time and maybe, it is your lover looking at you again, with the same love still alive in her eyes.
posts.text:
And maybe death is not
a man in black carrying a scythe.
Maybe it is your mother's arms
waiting to hold you warmly.
Maybe it is your father's voice,
filled with pride for the final time
and maybe, it is your lover looking at you again,
with the same love still alive in her eyes.
posts.explanation: The writer says death may not be the scary figure in black that people imagine. Maybe it is your mother's arms waiting to hug you, your father's proud voice one last time, or the one you love looking at you again, still with love in her eyes.

posts.caption: Dead souls...
posts.displayTitle: dead bodies have no soul, dead souls have bodies
posts.altText: dead bodies have no soul, dead souls have bodies that are devoided of emotions and somewhere between the two, i exist.. neither fully dead, nor fully alive
posts.text:
dead bodies have no soul,
dead souls have bodies

that are devoided
of emotions

and somewhere
between the two, i exist..

neither fully dead,
nor fully alive
posts.explanation: The writer says dead bodies have no soul, and some living people have bodies with no feelings, as if their souls have died. He feels he lives somewhere between the two, not fully dead and not fully alive.

posts.caption: Weight..
posts.displayTitle: While trying to hold everything,
posts.altText: While trying to hold everything, I lost everything of myself while holding onto it, until my hands no longer knew whether they were carrying love or just the weight of losing it.
posts.text:
While trying to hold everything,
I lost everything of myself
while holding onto it,
until my hands
no longer knew
whether they
were carrying love

or just the weight of losing it.
posts.explanation: While trying to hold on to everything, the writer lost himself. In the end his hands could no longer tell whether they were holding love or only the heavy weight of losing it.

posts.caption: Why is it that?
posts.displayTitle: I try to be held by those hands of yours
posts.altText: I try to be held by those hands of yours yet I keep slipping away through the narrow spaces between them. What is so wrong with this life of mine that everything I drag closer by the day goes farther away at night?
posts.text:
I try to be held by those
hands of yours
yet I keep slipping away
through the narrow spaces
between them.
What is so wrong
with this life of mine
that everything I drag closer by the day
goes farther away at night?
posts.explanation: The writer tries to hold on to the person he loves, but keeps slipping through their fingers. He asks what is wrong with his life, that everything he pulls close during the day drifts far away by night.

posts.caption: It will!!
posts.displayTitle: "When love seeps into my veins and reaches through the bone,
posts.altText: "When love seeps into my veins and reaches through the bone, it will merge itself with my soul, and through the veins, it will be carried to my heart, and all they will hear through my heartbeat will be your name."
posts.text:
"When love seeps into my veins
and reaches through the bone,
it will merge itself
with my soul,
and through the veins,
it will be carried to my heart,
and all they will hear through
my heartbeat will be your name."
posts.explanation: The writer says love will soak into him so deeply, through his blood, his bones and his soul, that it will reach his heart. Then every heartbeat will sound like the name of the person he loves.

posts.caption: I am afraid it won't
posts.displayTitle: By the time your silence reaches the deepest parts of me,
posts.altText: By the time your silence reaches the deepest parts of me, I fear there will be nothing left untouched by you, love. Not even this silence will be able to stop the flowing pulse, the beating heart, and the chants they make of your name.
posts.text:
By the time your silence reaches
the deepest parts of me,
I fear there
will be nothing
left untouched
by you, love.
Not even this silence will be
able to stop the flowing pulse,
the beating heart,
and the chants they make of your name.
posts.explanation: The writer fears that by the time this person's silence sinks all the way into him, every part of him will already belong to them. Even that silence will not stop his heart from beating, and every beat will still call out their name.

posts.caption: Your hand is cold, mine are burning like fire. how blind are you nastenka? —white nights
posts.displayTitle: "My heart beats with devotion" but my God
posts.altText: "My heart beats with devotion" but my God is too heartless to notice how loudly it begs untouched by every "prayer" inside it, till it goes silent..
posts.text:
"My heart beats with devotion"

but my God
is too heartless
to notice how
loudly it begs

untouched by every
"prayer"
inside it,
till it goes silent..
posts.explanation: The writer's heart is full of devotion, but his God, perhaps the person he loves, is too cold to notice how loudly it begs. None of the prayers inside his heart reach them, and it keeps begging until it finally goes silent.

posts.caption: Unstayable..
posts.displayTitle: I am astonished by how easily I am betrayed rather than stood by.
posts.altText: I am astonished by how easily I am betrayed rather than stood by.
posts.text:
I am
astonished
by how easily

I am betrayed
rather than
stood by.
posts.explanation: The writer is shocked at how easily people betray him instead of standing by him.

posts.caption: Your heart and mine...
posts.displayTitle: Somewhere between your heart and mine,
posts.altText: Somewhere between your heart and mine, there is an unbridgeable distance which separates us from all the love we had.
posts.text:
Somewhere
between your heart
and mine,

there is an unbridgeable
distance which separates
us from all the
love we had.
posts.explanation: The writer feels there is now a gap between his heart and the other person's that can never be crossed. It keeps them apart from all the love they once had.

posts.caption: Removing it feels like moving on
posts.displayTitle: There's a dagger in my heart I've left untouched,
posts.altText: There's a dagger in my heart I've left untouched, because removing it somehow, feels more painful than letting it stay there.
posts.text:
There's a dagger
in my heart
I've left untouched,
because removing it
somehow,
feels more painful
than letting it stay there.
posts.explanation: The writer has a deep hurt in his heart, like a knife, that he has not tried to remove. Taking it out feels like it would hurt even more than living with it.

posts.caption: triyanwrites on May 19, 2026: "They'll end with me
posts.displayTitle: What scares me is that I'll have to spend a lifetime with memories
posts.altText: "What scares me is that I'll have to spend a lifetime with memories which will end with me one day."
posts.text:
"What scares me is
that I'll have to
spend a lifetime
with memories
which will end with
me one day."
posts.explanation: The writer is scared that he must carry his memories for a whole lifetime, and that they will only end when he does.

posts.caption: It aches to belong
posts.displayTitle: Maybe at the end of the day I just want to rest my heart in a place
posts.altText: Maybe at the end of the day I just want to rest my heart in a place which belongs to me, in a heart which is mine, in a heart which is devoted to mine. I too a heart belong somewhere.
posts.text:
Maybe at the
end of the day

I just want to rest
my heart in a place
which belongs to me,

in a heart which is mine,
in a heart which is devoted to mine.
I too a heart belong somewhere.
posts.explanation: At the end of the day, the writer just wants a place where his heart can rest and belong: a heart that is his, and one that loves his back. He wants his heart to belong somewhere too.

posts.caption: Good and evil
posts.displayTitle: every person has their own language of good and evil,
posts.altText: every person has their own language of good and evil, maybe that's why I became one in yours and even mine.
posts.text:
every person has
their own language
of good and evil,

maybe that's why
I became one in yours
and even mine.
posts.explanation: The writer says each person has their own idea of what is good and what is evil. He seems to say that is why he became the bad one in the other person's eyes, and even in his own.

posts.caption: Lifetime...
posts.displayTitle: There's a lifetime within my mind,
posts.altText: There's a lifetime within my mind, yet all I could ever explain to you was a moment. I could have said more, but those feelings had grown too vast for words and too heavy for a heart to carry into another's hands.
posts.text:
There's a lifetime
within my mind,
yet all
I could ever explain
to you was a moment.
I could have
said more, but those
feelings had grown
too vast for words and
too heavy for a heart
to carry into another's hands.
posts.explanation: The writer has a whole lifetime of thoughts and feelings inside him, but could only share a tiny moment of it with the person he loves. He could have said more, but his feelings had grown too big for words and too heavy to hand to someone else.

posts.caption: I try to hide you? Or pain.
posts.displayTitle: I try to hide your pain in the words
posts.altText: I try to hide you pain in the words but they just spill through the pages, and I find my heart in those blood inks.
posts.text:
I try to hide ~~you~~
pain in the words
but they just spill

through the pages ,
and I find my heart
in those ~~blood~~ inks.
posts.explanation: The writer tries to hide his pain in his writing, but it spills out onto the pages anyway, and in the ink he finds his own heart. The crossed-out words hint that the pain is really about a person, and that the ink feels like blood.

posts.caption: Mother
posts.displayTitle: Mother, The kindest place I have been to is still your womb.
posts.altText: Mother, The kindest place I have been to is still your womb. because the world has spent years trying to make me feel like I take up too much space. for the same existence you once carried without complaint.
posts.text:
Mother,
The kindest place
I have been to is still
your womb.
because the world has
spent years trying to
make me feel like
I take up too much space.
for the same existence
you once carried without
complaint.
posts.explanation: The writer tells his mother that her womb is still the kindest place he has known. The world has spent years making him feel like he takes up too much room, while she carried that same life inside her without ever complaining.

posts.caption: Your name
posts.displayTitle: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire
posts.altText: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire thinking your name was another word for heaven. and maybe that is the tragedy of my heart, that even destruction felt beautiful as long as it arrived wearing your face.
posts.text:
If loving YOU
was a way to hell then
I would walk
into the fire thinking
your name was another
word for heaven.
and maybe that is
the tragedy of my heart,
that even destruction felt
beautiful as long as it
arrived wearing your face.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving this person led to hell, he would walk into the fire believing their name meant heaven. That is the sad part of his heart: even being destroyed felt beautiful, as long as it came looking like the person he loved.

posts.caption: Never meant to stay
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps in my heart I was never searching for love,
posts.altText: Perhaps in my heart I was never searching for love, only for a place where my soul didn't feel temporary, for eyes that looked at me and chose to stay. and perhaps I always knew that some people are meant to feel like home, even if they were never meant to stay.
posts.text:
Perhaps in my heart
I was never searching for love,
only for a place where my soul
didn't feel temporary,
for eyes that looked at me
and chose to stay.

and perhaps
I always knew that
some people are meant to feel like home,
even if they
were never meant to stay.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks he was never really looking for love, but for a place where his soul did not feel like a short visitor, and for someone who would look at him and choose to stay. Deep down he always knew some people feel like home, even if they are never meant to stay.

posts.caption: Sun and the moon
posts.displayTitle: There's a distance between us that I can't cross,
posts.altText: There's a distance between us that I can't cross, you and I were always meant to be like the sun and the moon, existing beneath the same sky yet never enough to stay close. You the sun and I the moon, always taking your light just to survive but I am afraid to even call myself the moon…
posts.text:
There's a distance between us
that I can't cross,
you and I were always meant
to be like the sun and the moon,
existing beneath the same sky
yet never enough to stay close.

You the sun and I the moon,
always taking your light just to survive but
I am afraid to even call myself the moon,
because I saw the moon in your eyes,
but never myself within them.
posts.explanation: The writer says he and the person he loves are like the sun and the moon: under the same sky but never close. Like the moon, he lives off their light. Yet he is afraid to call himself their moon, because he saw a moon in their eyes, and it was never him.

posts.caption: What would happen?
posts.displayTitle: What would happen if an angel and a demon fell in love?
posts.altText: What would happen if an angel and a demon fell in love? They would be bound by reality for eternity, punished with the sin of never meeting again. and maybe that is what happened when I fell for an angel, because loving you felt like standing at heaven's gates with hell inside my chest.
posts.text:
What would happen
if an angel and a demon
fell in love?
They would be bound
by reality for eternity,
punished with the sin
of never meeting again.

and maybe that is what
happened when I fell for an angel,
because loving you felt like standing
at heaven's gates with
hell inside my chest.
posts.explanation: The writer imagines an angel and a demon falling in love: they would be punished forever by never meeting again. He feels that is what happened when he loved someone so good, because loving them felt like standing at heaven's door with hell inside his chest.

posts.caption: I see you in everything
posts.displayTitle: I see you in old streets, in unfinished poems,
posts.altText: I see you in old streets, in unfinished poems, in every passing face that carries a fragment of your eyes. Perhaps that is what love does. It dissolves into your existence until every beautiful thing begins to resemble them, until they stop being a person and become the way you see the world.
posts.text:
I see you in old streets,
in unfinished poems,
in every passing face that
carries a fragment of your eyes.

Perhaps that is what love does.
It dissolves into your existence
until every beautiful thing begins
to resemble them, until they
stop being a person and
become the way you see the world.
posts.explanation: The writer sees the person he loves everywhere: in old streets, unfinished poems, and strangers' eyes. He says love does this. It soaks into your life until every beautiful thing looks like them, and they become not just a person but the way you see the world.

posts.caption: Footprint
posts.displayTitle: There's love you left in my heart,
posts.altText: There's love you left in my heart, in every grain of existence I have, I said there's "love you left" like a footprint on my heart that even my own footprint has become that of yours.
posts.text:
There's love you
left in my heart,
in every grain
of existence I have,

I said there's "love you left"
like a footprint on my heart
that even
my own footprint
has became that of yours.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person he loved left love in every part of him, like a footprint pressed into his heart. Their mark is so deep that even his own footprints now look like theirs, as if he has turned into them.

posts.caption: What do you?
posts.displayTitle: You exist in the smallest parts of my life.
posts.altText: You exist in the smallest parts of my life. so naturally that sometimes I forget where the world ends and where you begin. what do you call this? love or a paradox?
posts.text:
You exist
in the smallest
parts of my life.

so naturally
that sometimes I forget
where the world ends
and where you begin.

what do you call this?
love or a paradox?
posts.explanation: The writer says this person is part of even the smallest things in his life, so naturally that he sometimes cannot tell where the world stops and they start. He wonders whether this is love or something that makes no sense.

posts.caption: Can love also be called burning?
posts.displayTitle: We say "light" and refer to the fire.
posts.altText: We say "light" and refer to the fire. My body was engulfed with light, but was I burning or was it just love?
posts.text:
We say "light"
and refer to the fire.

My body was
engulfed with light,
but was I burning
or was it just love?
posts.explanation: The writer notes that we call fire light. He felt full of light, and he wonders whether he was being burned or simply in love, as if the two might feel the same.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: How much grief can a little child's hand hold?
posts.altText: How much grief can a little child's hand hold? any amount that is placed into it by their parents, and somehow they keep carrying it throughout their life.
posts.text:
How much grief can
a little child's hand hold?

any amount that is
placed into it by their parents,
and somehow they keep
carrying it throughout their life.
posts.explanation: The writer asks how much sadness a small child's hand can hold. His answer is: as much as the parents put into it. And the child somehow keeps carrying it for the rest of their life.

posts.caption: Do not pretend to be one
posts.displayTitle: Do not pretend to be a saint when your hands are stained with my bloo…
posts.altText: Do not pretend to be a saint when your hands are stained with my blood, You speak of devotion as if I wasn't the sacrifice laid beneath your feet, as if my pain wasn't the price of your peace. All this was still fine until I saw you washing your hands and pretending the blood wasn't even mine.
posts.text:
Do not pretend to be a saint
when your hands are stained
with my blood,
You speak of devotion
as if I wasn't the sacrifice
laid beneath your feet,
as if my pain wasn't
the price of your peace.

All this was still fine
until I saw you washing
your hands and pretending
the blood wasn't even mine.
posts.explanation: The writer tells someone not to act like a good person after hurting him so badly. They talk about love while he was sacrificed for their peace. He could bear even that, until he saw them wash their hands of it and act as if his pain had nothing to do with them.

posts.caption: Holding hand?
posts.displayTitle: The distance between heaven and earth
posts.altText: The distance between heaven and earth is that of the space between our hands when they hold each other, small enough to disappear in a moment and vast enough to carry everything we never say.
posts.text:
The distance
between heaven and earth
is that of the space
between our hands
when they hold each other,

small enough to disappear
in a moment and
vast enough to carry
everything we never say.
posts.explanation: The writer says the gap between heaven and earth is like the small space between two people's hands when they hold each other. It is small enough to vanish in a moment, yet big enough to hold everything they never say.

posts.caption: Isn't the moon beautiful?
posts.displayTitle: There are nights when I sit beside my window watching the moon
posts.altText: There are nights when I sit beside my window watching the moon and mistaking every passing breeze for your arrival and every ray of moonlight for your eyes, as if my lungs still remember your smell, as if my eyes still seeks your light in every shard of the moon, as if my heart has forgotten the difference between hope and memory.
posts.text:
There are nights when
I sit beside my window watching
the moon and mistaking
every passing breeze for your arrival
and every ray of moonlight
for your eyes,

as if my lungs still
remember your smell,
as if my eyes still seeks your light
in every shard of the moon,
as if my heart has forgotten
the difference between hope and memory.
posts.explanation: On some nights the writer sits by his window looking at the moon. Every breeze feels like the person he loves arriving, and every moonbeam reminds him of their eyes. He still seems to remember their smell and look for their light, and his heart can no longer tell hope from memory.

posts.caption: Beneath the same sky.
posts.displayTitle: I sometimes wonder how a heart continues beating
posts.altText: I sometimes wonder how a heart continues beating after carrying so many funerals inside itself, how it continues to love even after burying people who are still alive somewhere beneath the same sky.
posts.text:
I sometimes wonder how
a heart continues beating
after carrying so many funerals
inside itself,

how it continues to love even
after burying people who are
still alive somewhere
beneath the same sky.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders how a heart keeps beating after so many losses, as if it holds many funerals inside. He asks how it keeps loving after letting go of people who are not dead, but still alive somewhere under the same sky.

posts.caption: Who'll judge me if not you dear God?
posts.displayTitle: if there is a God listening beyond all this silence,
posts.altText: if there is a God listening beyond all this silence, then let Him forgive me for having loved this life so painfully, even when it gave me every reason not to. I am the sin I am the sinner
posts.text:
if there is a God
listening beyond all this silence,
then let Him forgive me
for having loved this life
so painfully,

even when it gave me
every reason not to.
I am the sin
I am the sinner
posts.explanation: The writer says that if God is out there listening past all the silence, he hopes God will forgive him for loving this life so painfully, even though life gave him every reason not to. He feels he is both the wrong and the one who did it.

posts.caption: Someone someday
posts.displayTitle: May someone one day love you without fear,
posts.altText: May someone one day love you without fear, without leaving wounds between their affection, without turning tenderness into tragedy and when they hold your hands, I hope they do not tremble the way mine always did, as if they already knew they were destined to lose you.
posts.text:
May someone one day
love you without fear,
without leaving wounds
between their affection,
without turning tenderness
into tragedy and when they
hold your hands,
I hope they do not tremble
the way mine always did,
as if they already knew
they were destined to lose you.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes that one day someone will love this person without fear, without hurting them, and without turning gentle love into pain. He hopes their hands will not shake when they hold this person, the way his always did, as if they knew from the start he would lose them.

posts.caption: Remember me
posts.displayTitle: If you remember me, remember not my suffering,
posts.altText: If you remember me, remember not my suffering, but the way I continued to survive it. Remember that even in the darkest corners of human despair, I still searched desperately for your light, for something that kept me alive in this rotten world. At last, remember me as a human, not as something that slowly rotted away by suffering.
posts.text:
If you remember me,
remember not my suffering,
but the way I continued
to survive it.
Remember that even in
the darkest corners of human despair,
I still searched desperately
for your light,
for something that kept me
alive in this rotten world.
At last, remember me as a human,
not as something that
slowly rotted away by suffering.
posts.explanation: The writer asks to be remembered not for his pain but for how he kept going through it. Even at his darkest, he kept searching for the other person's light to stay alive in a cruel world. Most of all, he wants to be remembered as a human, not as something pain slowly destroyed.

posts.caption: Three poetries in one 🥀
posts.displayTitle: The lover, the sinner, the saint.
posts.altText: The lover, the sinner, the saint. i stayed, i waited beside heavens for your voice with empty hands. but it is your silence which became a prayer, that stayed inside me, that no god answered. i stayed long after the light left, you ruined my temple. loving you that it felt like devotion, felt like worship and too much like grief. and still, i knelt before my ruin your altar.
posts.text:
The lover, the sinner, the saint.

i stayed, i waited beside heavens
for your voice with empty hands.

but it is your silence which became a prayer,
that stayed inside me, that no god answered.

i stayed long after
the light left, you ruined my temple.

loving you that it felt like devotion,
felt like worship and too much like grief

and still, i knelt before
my ruin your altar.

thoughts of
a man mourning
a lover.
(the abandoned)

thoughts of
a dying believer.
(the martyr)

thoughts of a sinner kneeling
before something holy.
(the sinner)
posts.explanation: The writer waited, empty-handed, for the voice of the one he loved, but got only silence, a prayer no god answered. Loving them felt like worship and grief at once, and even after they ruined him, he still knelt before them. He sees himself as an abandoned lover, a dying believer and a sinner.

posts.caption: I hope you don't
posts.displayTitle: But still, despite everything, I wish you a beautiful life.
posts.altText: But still, despite everything, I wish you a beautiful life. Even if it is one that no longer has me in it. I hope you don't come searching for me within those memories of ruin..
posts.text:
But still,
despite everything,
I wish you a beautiful life.

Even if it is one that
no longer has me in it.
I hope you don't come
searching for me within
those memories of ruin..
posts.explanation: Even after everything, the writer wishes the other person a beautiful life, even one without him in it. He hopes they never come looking for him in those broken, painful memories.

posts.caption: but i have never forgotten those eyes of yours
posts.displayTitle: I have forgotten many things about you.
posts.altText: I have forgotten many things about you. the exact shape of your smile, the sound of your step. but somehow my grief remembers everything, and refuses to tell me what it knows.
posts.text:
I have forgotten
many things about you.
the exact shape
of your smile,

the sound of your step.
but somehow my grief
remembers everything,
and refuses to tell me
what it knows.
posts.explanation: The writer has forgotten many small things about the person he lost, like the exact shape of their smile and the sound of their footsteps. But his grief seems to remember everything, and it will not give those memories back to him.

posts.caption: To love is to live..
posts.displayTitle: I know I will be abandoned.
posts.altText: I know I will be abandoned. Yet still, I pour the glass full of love. There is a strange beauty in offering abundance to a world that has taught you scarcity. To love is to never cease to exist.
posts.text:
I know
I will be abandoned.

Yet still,
I pour the glass
full of love.

There is a strange
beauty in offering
abundance to a world .

that has taught
you scarcity.
To love is to never
cease to exist
posts.explanation: The writer knows he will be left in the end, yet he still loves fully, like filling a glass to the top. He finds something beautiful in giving so much to a world that taught him to expect little. To him, loving is how a person never stops existing.

posts.caption: I'll let you choose
posts.displayTitle: I know one day these hands will close with emptiness
posts.altText: I know one day these hands will close with emptiness and I will still be brim with love, as my heart has never learned the difference between love and loss, so I'll call it a doomed act of faith, repeated until my hands forget how to hold anything else except for joining them and I'll let you decide whether it's begging or praying.
posts.text:
I know one day these
hands will close with emptiness
and I will still
be brim with love,
as my heart has never learned
the difference between love and loss,
so I'll call it a doomed act of faith,
repeated until my hands forget
how to hold anything else
except for joining them
and I'll let you decide
whether it's begging or praying.
posts.explanation: The writer knows his hands will one day be empty, yet his heart will still be full of love, because it cannot tell love and loss apart. He calls it a hopeless act of faith, kept up until his hands can only fold together, and lets the listener decide if that is begging or praying.

posts.caption: It'll be June again
posts.displayTitle: It's June again and there is something cruel about it
posts.altText: It's June again and there is something cruel about it. It teaches flowers how to bloom while teaching my hearts how to ache again. Is it the smell of wet soil or my rotting skin that is in the air beside these old memories like withered flowers? I cannot tell anymore. What is it that kept me alive, It's June again and somehow both my love and my grief still resemble you.
posts.text:
It's June again
and there is something cruel about it.
It teaches flowers how to bloom while
teaching my hearts how to ache again.
Is it the smell of wet soil
or my rotting skin that is
in the air beside these
old memories like withered flowers?
I cannot tell anymore.
What is it that kept me alive,
It's June again and somehow both
my love and my grief still resemble you.
posts.explanation: It is June again, and the writer finds it cruel: it makes flowers bloom but makes his heart ache again. He cannot tell if the air smells of wet soil or of himself rotting among old, dead memories. Somehow both his love and his grief still look like the person he lost.

posts.caption: Has it never truly?
posts.displayTitle: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well
posts.altText: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome, like light entering a house that has forgotten how to open its windows. Like the prayer in an abandoned church that never reaches its God.
posts.text:
Sometimes I wonder,
if sorrow learned my name
so well that even joy
arrives feeling unwelcome,

like light entering a house
that has forgotten how
to open its windows.

Like the prayer in an
abandoned church that
never reaches its God.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if sadness knows him so well that even happiness feels like an unwanted guest when it comes. He feels like a house that has forgotten how to open its windows to let light in, or a prayer in an empty church that never reaches God.

posts.caption: Pretense is the key for survival
posts.displayTitle: I have worn the appearance of being well for so long
posts.altText: I have worn the appearance of being well for so long that I can no longer distinguish myself from the disguise. I wonder now whether pretense was only a way to survive, or whether it slowly became the god I learned to worship.
posts.text:
I have worn the appearance
of being well for so long
that I can no longer distinguish
myself from the disguise.

I wonder now whether
pretense was only a way to survive,
or whether it slowly became
the god I learned to worship.
posts.explanation: The writer has pretended to be fine for so long that he can no longer tell his real self from the act. He wonders if pretending was just a way to get by, or if it slowly became the thing he bows to, like a god.

posts.caption: That's me
posts.displayTitle: a cracked cup remains on the shelf longer than a broken one.
posts.altText: a cracked cup remains on the shelf longer than a broken one. No one throws it away, yet no one trusts it either. there are people who live exactly this way too damaged to be held, too intact to be mourned.
posts.text:
a cracked cup remains
on the shelf longer
than a broken one.

No one throws it away,
yet no one trusts it either.
there are people
who live exactly this way
too damaged to be held,
too intact to be mourned.
posts.explanation: The writer says a cracked cup stays on the shelf longer than a broken one: no one throws it out, but no one trusts it either. Some people live just like that, too hurt for anyone to hold them, yet not broken enough for anyone to grieve for them.

posts.caption: I hope i do!
posts.displayTitle: I hope the next time we meet, my hands won't tremble at the sight of…
posts.altText: I hope the next time we meet, my hands won't tremble at the sight of you. I hope your name will no longer echo like a prayer inside my empty chest. I hope, for once, I will be able to look at you without my heart remembering everything.
posts.text:
I hope the next time
we meet,
my hands won't tremble
at the sight of you.
I hope your name
will no longer
echo like a prayer
inside my empty chest.
I hope, for once,
I will be able to look
at you without my heart
remembering everything.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes that the next time he meets this person, his hands will not shake when he sees them. He hopes their name will stop sounding like a prayer in his empty chest, and that he can finally look at them without his heart remembering everything.

posts.caption: What will they hear?
posts.displayTitle: When they check the pulse of the dying man, what will they hear?
posts.altText: When they check the pulse of the dying man, what will they hear? 1) blood flowing 2) blood stopping 3) pulse of a dying man 4) or the you sitting beside me, caressing my hair?
posts.text:
When they check
the pulse of the dying man,
what will they hear?

1) ~~you~~ blood flowing

2) ~~you leaving~~ blood stopping

3) ~~you~~ pulse of a dying man

~~4) or the you sitting beside me,~~
~~caressing my hair?~~
posts.explanation: The writer asks what people will hear when they check a dying man's pulse, meaning his own. He lists plain answers, like blood flowing or stopping, but the crossed-out words show his pulse is really full of the person he loves and their leaving, and he wishes they were beside him, stroking his hair.

posts.caption: Fish bowl
posts.displayTitle: What is love? to make an ocean fit inside a bowl for a fish,
posts.altText: What is love? to make an ocean fit inside a bowl for a fish, or to admire its waves without ever claiming the sea? Possession or devotion?
posts.text:
What is love?
to make an ocean
fit inside a bowl
for a fish,
or to admire its waves
without ever
claiming the sea?
Possession or devotion?
posts.explanation: The writer asks what love really is. Is it squeezing an ocean into a small bowl to keep a fish, or enjoying the waves without ever trying to own the sea? He wonders if love means owning someone or loving them freely.

posts.caption: I hope I don't
posts.displayTitle: "I hope I dream so well that..
posts.altText: "I hope I dream so well that.. I don't have to wake up the next day."
posts.text:
"I hope I dream
so well that..

I don't have
to wake up
the next day."
posts.explanation: The writer hopes he will have such a good dream that he will not have to wake up the next day. It reads as a quiet wish not to wake up at all.

posts.caption: Absurd
posts.displayTitle: Grief love is absurd
posts.altText: Grief love is absurd. I can bury an entire lifetime, watch the earth close over it, and still turn my head at certain footsteps, like a fool who believes that the dead can resurrect.
posts.text:
Grief ~~love~~ is absurd.
I can bury
an entire lifetime,
watch the earth
close over it,
and still turn my head
at certain footsteps,
like a fool who believes that
the dead can resurrect.
posts.explanation: The writer says grief makes no sense. He can bury a whole lifetime and watch the ground close over it, yet still turn his head at certain footsteps, like a fool who believes the dead can come back. A crossed-out word hints that love is just as strange.

posts.caption: Had to post this twice!!
posts.displayTitle: The lover, the sinner, the saint.
posts.altText: The lover, the sinner, the saint. i stayed, i waited beside heavens for your voice with empty hands. but it is your silence which became a prayer, that stayed inside me, that no god answered. i stayed long after the light left, you ruined my temple. loving you that it felt like devotion, felt like worship and too much like grief. and still, i knelt before my ruin your altar.
posts.text:
The lover, the sinner, the saint.

i stayed, i waited beside heavens
for your voice with empty hands.

but it is your silence which became a prayer,
that stayed inside me, that no god answered.

i stayed long after
the light left, you ruined my temple.

loving you that it felt like devotion,
felt like worship and too much like grief

and still, i knelt before
my ruin your altar.

thoughts of
a man mourning
a lover.
(the abandoned)

thoughts of
a dying believer.
(the martyr)

thoughts of a sinner kneeling
before something holy.
(the sinner)
posts.explanation: The writer waited, empty-handed, for the voice of the one he loved, but got only silence, a prayer no god answered. Loving them felt like worship and grief at once, and even after they ruined him, he still knelt before them. He sees himself as an abandoned lover, a dying believer and a sinner.

posts.caption: Parallel lines
posts.displayTitle: You and I are meant to be like parallel lines
posts.altText: You and I are meant to be like parallel lines, cursed forever within sight of one another, forever forbidden from touching. We travel in the same direction, witness the same horizons and yet the universe keeps us apart all the way to infinity.
posts.text:
You and I are meant to be like parallel lines,
cursed forever within sight of one
another, forever forbidden
from touching.
We travel in the same direction,
witness the same horizons and yet
the universe keeps us apart all the
way to infinity.
posts.explanation: The writer says he and the person he loves are like two lines that run side by side forever. They go the same way and see the same things, but they can never meet or touch.

posts.caption: Your name.
posts.displayTitle: If I could hear your name within this hell, it wouldn't be hell…
posts.altText: If I could hear your name within this hell, it wouldn't be hell anymore and if you were to call this broken soul by its name, even this wreckage would mistake itself for paradise.
posts.text:
If I could hear
your name within this hell,
it wouldn't be hell
anymore

and if you were
to call this broken soul
by its name,
even this wreckage
would mistake itself
for paradise.
posts.explanation: The writer is in deep pain, but just hearing the name of the one he loves would end that pain. If she called him by his name, even his broken life would feel like heaven.

posts.caption: You have!!
posts.displayTitle: You have seeped into my bones so well that I can't distinguish
posts.altText: You have seeped into my bones so well that I can't distinguish between you and the marrow and perhaps that is why broken ones hurts the most.
posts.text:
You have seeped
into my bones
so well that I can't
distinguish between
you and the marrow

and perhaps that
is why broken ones
hurts the most.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person he loves has gone so deep inside him that he can't tell her apart from his own bones. Maybe that is why, when it breaks, it hurts the most.

posts.caption: What is love?
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps what love is can be heard between the pulses of my flowing…
posts.altText: Perhaps what love is can be heard between the pulses of my flowing blood, for what they chant is your name and it is the same blood that flows through my whole body... my heart, my eyes, my brain, my lungs. I love you, I see you, I think you, I breathe you. Tell me, how am I to love anything but you? Tell me, how am I to forget you?
posts.text:
Perhaps what love is can
be heard between the pulses
of my flowing blood,
for what they chant
is your name and it is
the same blood that flows
through my whole body...

my heart, my eyes, my brain, my lungs.
I love you, I see you,
I think you, I breathe you.

Tell me, how am I to love anything but you?
Tell me, how am I to forget you?
posts.explanation: The writer feels his love in his blood, which seems to repeat her name as it reaches every part of him. His heart, eyes, mind and lungs all love her, so he asks how he could ever love anything else or forget her.

posts.caption: If my eyes could speak!!
posts.displayTitle: If eyes could speak, they would tell you of the wars I survived
posts.altText: If eyes could speak, they would tell you of the wars I survived and the one I never did. They would tell you that grief is sometimes just love with nowhere left to go. They would tell you how a single absence can outlive a thousand presences, how some names become prayers without ever being spoken.
posts.text:
If eyes could speak,
they would tell you of the wars
I survived and the one I never did.

They would tell you that grief
is sometimes just love
with nowhere left to go.

They would tell you how
a single absence can
outlive a thousand presences,
how some names become prayers
without ever being spoken.
posts.explanation: If his eyes could talk, they would tell of the hard times he survived and the one he did not. They would say grief is love left with no one to give it to, that missing one person lasts longer than many others being near, and that some names become silent prayers.

posts.caption: If only they could speak
posts.displayTitle: If eyes could speak, they would ask why the universe made…
posts.altText: If eyes could speak, they would ask why the universe made recognition so easy and belonging so difficult. Why I could find you in a crowd of thousands, yet could not find a place beside you. and if eyes could speak, they would not weep. They would stand as witnesses to every word I swallowed, every hope I buried, and every part of me that still turns toward you as flowers…
posts.text:
If eyes could speak,
they would ask why the universe
made recognition so easy
and belonging so difficult.
Why I could find you in a crowd of thousands,
yet could not find a place beside you.
and if eyes could speak, they would not weep.
They would stand as witnesses
to every word I swallowed,
every hope I buried,
and every part of me
that still turns toward you
as flowers turn toward light.
posts.explanation: His eyes would ask why it is so easy to spot her in a huge crowd, yet so hard to have a place beside her. They would not cry; they would quietly show every word he held back, every hope he gave up, and how part of him still turns toward her.

posts.caption: Maybe I still am
posts.displayTitle: I believed all I had was suffering, but I was wrong
posts.altText: I believed all I had was suffering, but I was wrong. all feelings in me were suffering, as if they were in a prison, as if suffering itself was a prison, and all I could do was watch.
posts.text:
I believed all
I had was suffering,
but I was wrong.
all feelings in
me were suffering,
as if they were
in a prison,
as if suffering itself
was a prison,
and all I could do
was watch.
posts.explanation: The writer first thought pain was just one thing he had. Then he saw that all his feelings had turned into pain, locked up as if in a jail, and he could do nothing but watch.

posts.caption: Tragedy
posts.displayTitle: The cruelest part of my existence is not that I can't love anymore
posts.altText: The cruelest part of my existence is not that I can't love anymore. I can. But everywhere my sight goes, it is still you. and that is the tragedy of this miserable being.
posts.text:
The cruelest part of my existence
is not that I can't love anymore.
I can. But everywhere my sight goes,
it is still you.
and that is the tragedy of this
miserable being.
posts.explanation: The writer says he can still love, so that is not the worst part. The worst part is that wherever he looks, he still sees only her, and that makes his whole life sad.

posts.caption: Do we?
posts.displayTitle: Must we understand all— to be understood the way we desire?
posts.altText: Must we understand all— to be understood the way we desire? Or should we understand all, just to acknowledge that no one can ever truly understand us?
posts.text:
Must we understand all—
to be understood the way we desire?
Or should we understand all,
just to acknowledge that
no one can ever truly understand us?
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if we must understand everything in order to be understood the way we want. Or does understanding everything only teach us that no one can ever truly understand us?

posts.caption: Just a chapter
posts.displayTitle: One day, when everything grows apart, I won't know your story anymore
posts.altText: One day, when everything grows apart, I won't know your story anymore. I won't know what makes you smile, what keeps you awake, or who you became without me. I'll only remember that once, I was a chapter in it, before the pages turned without me.
posts.text:
One day, when everything
grows apart, I won’t know
your story anymore.
I won’t know what
makes you smile,
what keeps you awake, or
who you became without me.
I’ll only remember that once,
I was a chapter in it,
before the pages turned
without me.
posts.explanation: The writer knows that one day they will drift apart and he won't know her life anymore, like what makes her smile or who she has become. He will only remember that he was once part of her story, before it went on without him.

posts.caption: Read the underlined part
posts.displayTitle: There's a fire burning me from within, which only you can extinguish
posts.altText: There's a fire burning me from within, which only you can extinguish, for I have carried these flames for longer than I can remember, amid the burning of countless me, myself and when they finally burn me, you won't smell anything, for empty things leave no scent behind. So come before I am only ashes. Make your home within this burning heart. Find me before they scatter…
posts.text:
There’s a fire burning me from within,
which only you can extinguish,
for I have carried these flames
for longer than I can remember,
amid the burning of countless me, myself
and when they finally burn me,
you won’t smell anything,
for empty things leave no scent behind.
So come before I am only ashes.
Make your home within this burning heart.
Find me before they scatter these ashes
and leave me whole before
I disappear into emptiness.

Now Read the underlined part
posts.explanation: The writer has carried a pain like a fire inside him for a very long time, and only the one he loves can put it out. He begs her to come and live in his heart before it burns him down to nothing. The last line points to a hidden message in underlined words.

posts.caption: When death does
posts.displayTitle: And when death fills my chest and I am not able to breathe anymore
posts.altText: And when death fills my chest and I am not able to breathe anymore, it'll still be less suffocating than the night you left.
posts.text:
And when death
fills my chest
and I am not able
to breathe anymore,

it’ll still be less
suffocating than
the night you left.
posts.explanation: The writer says that even dying, when he can no longer breathe, will feel easier than the night the person he loved left him.

posts.caption: And that is the dreamers misery
posts.displayTitle: A writer is often a liar
posts.altText: A writer is often a liar. He lies to himself with things he never got and the presence of the things he lost. He writes people back into his life, knowing they are already gone, because what he calls "imagination" is just a recycled piece of reality.
posts.text:
A writer is often a liar.
He lies to himself
with things he never got
and the presence
of the things he lost.

He writes people
back into his life,
knowing they are already gone,
because what he calls
“imagination” is just a
recycled piece of reality.
posts.explanation: The writer says a writer often fools himself. He writes about things he never had and people he has lost as if they were still there, and what looks made-up is really just pieces of his real life used again.

posts.caption: If I could
posts.displayTitle: If I could
posts.altText: A hand with red threads on the wrist gently strokes a white and ginger cat lying on a weathered stone ledge.
posts.text:
If I could hear
your name within this hell,
it wouldn’t be hell
anymore

and if you were
to call this broken soul
by its name,
even this wreckage
would mistake itself
for paradise.
posts.explanation: The writer is in deep pain, but just hearing the name of the one he loves would end that pain. If she called him by his name, even his broken life would feel like heaven.

posts.caption: Belief is a strange creature
posts.displayTitle: Maybe that's what belief has always been closing your eyes
posts.altText: Maybe that's what belief has always been closing your eyes and hoping that when you open them again, the person you trusted hasn't disappeared or worse, hasn't become someone you never knew.
posts.text:
Maybe that’s what belief
has always been
closing your eyes
and hoping that when
you open them again,

the person you trusted
hasn’t disappeared or worse,
hasn’t become someone
you never knew.
posts.explanation: He says trusting someone may be like shutting your eyes and hoping that when you open them, that person is still there, and has not turned into someone you don't know at all.

posts.caption: I hope you don't
posts.displayTitle: I do not hope you'll remember my face forever
posts.altText: I do not hope you'll remember my face forever. I only hope that when my name wanders through your mind years from now, it will not feel like the name of a stranger who happened to pass by, but like a room you once lived in, because for a brief and terrible moment, we mistook each other for home.
posts.text:
I do not hope you’ll
remember my face forever.
I only hope that when my
name wanders through your
mind years from now,
it will not feel like
the name of a stranger
who happened to pass by,
but like a room you once lived in,
because for a brief
and terrible moment,
we mistook each other for home.
posts.explanation: The writer does not need her to remember his face forever. He only hopes that years later his name feels to her not like a passing stranger but like a home she once lived in, because for a short, painful time they each felt like home to the other.

posts.caption: Dear God please understand
posts.displayTitle: God, If You ever wonder why I no longer pray with folded hands
posts.altText: God, If You ever wonder why I no longer pray with folded hands, know that I spent them holding together a heart You kept breaking.
posts.text:
God,
If You ever wonder why
I no longer pray
with folded hands,

know that I spent them
holding together a
heart You kept breaking.
posts.explanation: The writer tells God he no longer prays with folded hands. His hands have been busy holding his heart together, because God kept letting it break.

posts.caption: How does a blind man cross the road (with hope)
posts.displayTitle: I wait for you
posts.altText: I wait for you. I wait for you like a blind man walking across the street. I wait for you the way he lives, desperately. I wait for you like a blind man waits for light in his darkest dark.
posts.text:
I wait for you.
I wait for you like
a blind man walking
across the street.

I wait for you the way
he lives, desperately.

I wait for you
like a blind man

in his darkest dark.
posts.explanation: The writer waits for the person he loves with great need and little hope, like a blind man crossing a street, or a blind man longing for light when all he knows is darkness.

posts.caption: Hell
posts.displayTitle: I think hell may be far simpler than what you and I imagined
posts.altText: I think hell may be far simpler than what you and I imagined. to meet, by chance, the person you could have been, and discover that he suffered no less than you did. or the eyes you thought would look at you looking at other.
posts.text:
I think hell may be
far simpler than
what you and I imagined.

to meet, by chance,
the person you could have been,
and discover that he
suffered no less than you did.

or the eyes you
thought would look at you
looking at other.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks hell might be simple. It could be meeting the person you might have become and finding he hurt just as much, or seeing the eyes you hoped would look at you looking at someone else.

posts.caption: Why God?
posts.displayTitle: God, if loss is a part of Your design,
posts.altText: God, if loss is a part of Your design, then tell me why did You make the heart so stubborn that it continues loving what You have already taken away?
posts.text:
God,
if loss is a part
of Your design,

then tell me why
did You make the heart
so stubborn that it
continues loving
what You have already
taken away?
posts.explanation: The writer asks God: if losing people is part of His plan, why did He make the heart so stubborn that it keeps loving the ones He has already taken away?

posts.caption: Collab with @byhaadi
posts.displayTitle: give me the parts you hide in daylight
posts.altText: give me the parts you hide in daylight. i have always preferred things that bloom in the dark— for i have buried enough flowers to know— that the prettiest ones are often the first to die are often first to be plucked.
posts.text:
give me the parts
you hide in daylight.
i have always preferred things
that bloom in the dark—

for i have buried
enough flowers to know—
that the prettiest ones
are often the first to die
are often first to be plucked.
posts.explanation: The writer asks the person to show him the parts they hide from others. He likes what grows in the dark, because he has lost enough to know that the most beautiful things are often the first to die or be taken.

posts.displayTitle: When they burn me, they won't just burn my body
posts.altText: When they burn me, they won't just burn my body. They will burn the skin you once loved dearly they will burn the bones that held together a man who died long ago. And when the fire reaches the deepest parts of my mind and soul, my heart and brain, it will burn all the memories I once held close. But when it reaches my chest, I hope it does not extinguish beneath the weight…
posts.text:
When they burn me, they won’t just
burn my body. They will burn the skin you
once loved dearly they will burn the bones
that held together a man who died long ago.

And when the fire reaches
the deepest parts of
my mind and soul,
my heart and brain,
it will burn all the memories
I once held close.

But when it reaches my chest, I hope it does
not extinguish beneath the weight of losing you.
posts.explanation: The writer pictures his body being burned after death: the skin she once loved, the bones of a man who died inside long ago, and all his memories. He seems to say the pain of losing her sits so heavy in his chest it could put out even that fire, and hopes it does not.

posts.caption: What a strange creature
posts.displayTitle: What a ridiculous creature man is.
posts.altText: What a ridiculous creature man is. spending half his life longing for what he does not possess and the other half grieving what he has already lost.
posts.text:
What a ridiculous
creature man is.
spending half his life
longing for what he
does not possess

and the other half
grieving what
he has already lost.
posts.explanation: The writer says people are silly: they spend half their life wanting what they don't have, and the other half being sad about what they have lost.

posts.caption: Atlas
posts.displayTitle: There are parasites within my heart
posts.altText: There are parasites within my heart. They do not feed on flesh, they feed on proportion. Grain by grain, they alter the measurements of my inner world until an entire mountain can pass through the eye of a needle, and a single missing stone outweighs the earth itself and I, the victim, notice nothing. I merely wake up one day to find that gravity has developed a preference.

Grain by grain,
they alter the measurements

entire mountain can pass
through the eye of a needle,
and a single missing stone outweighs the earth

I merely wake up one day to find that
gravity has developed a preference.
posts.explanation: The writer says something in his heart slowly changes how big or small things feel. Bit by bit, huge things feel tiny and one small loss feels heavier than the whole world, and he does not notice until one day everything in him pulls toward that one loss.

posts.caption: Years later
posts.displayTitle: Years later, when I remember us, what will remain is neither love nor
posts.altText: Years later, when I remember us, what will remain is neither love nor the one who was loved but a careful arrangement of absences pretending to be memory.

when I remember us,
what will remain is
neither love nor

the one who was loved
but a careful arrangement
of absences pretending
to be memory.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks that years from now, when he looks back on them, he won't really remember the love or the person. He will only have the empty spaces they left, set up to look like memories.

posts.caption: 7 stages of love
posts.displayTitle: 7 stages of love
posts.altText: 7 stages of love: Attraction, attachment, Trust, Worship, Passion, death around a triangle of Love. There is a space between "you" and "I". From "I" to "you", and I call it love. Attraction: At first you think you have found another person. In truth, you have only misplaced the boundary of your own existence…
posts.text:
7 stages of love

Attraction
attachment
Trust
Worship
Passion
death
Love

There is a space between "you" and "I".
From "I" to "you", and I call it love.
---
Attraction

At first you think you have found
another person. In truth, you have
only misplaced the boundary of your
own existence. Everything appears
larger because you have become
smaller. You call this happiness. No
one corrects you. Like dawn entering
a valley that has never known light.
Like a drop of rain believing it has
discovered the sea.
---
Attachment

It is like a blind man waiting for light
in his darkest dark, learning the shape
of a face with his bare hands. He does
not know its colour nor the light that
falls upon it. He only knows that the
world ends where that face is absent.
So his hands continue searching with
the same certainty. No one has the
heart to tell him that hope can survive
even where light cannot. Perhaps
attachment is not refusing to let go but
forgetting that there was ever anything
else to hold.
---
Trust

Maybe that's what trust has
always been closing your eyes
and hoping that, when you
open them again, the person
you trusted hasn't disappeared
or, worse, hasn't become
someone you never knew. You
never ask to see the path you
just walk walk into it.
---
Love

Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into
"us" is love. Maybe giving yourself
wholly is love. Maybe existing for
one particularity entirely is love.
maybe to love is to love beyond
yourself, Maybe it is remembering
another heartbeat before your own
and maybe I am still figuring out
what love is and that for me that is
very much love.
---
Devotion

Then love becomes a cathedral
with no god inside it. You kneel
anyway because the echo sounds
more merciful than the beloved's
screams. Every prayer returns
wearing the beloved's voice. Faith
grows larger than truth. Soon you
cannot tell whether you worship a
person or the space they carved in
your heart to be worshipped.
---
Passion

Perhaps passion is the moth, circling
a flame it knows will ruin it, yet
mistaking its warmth for mercy. Or
perhaps I was the flame, burning
through every hope and calling the
ashes "moths." And if you ask
whether I loved, I did... enough to
offer myself to the fire(love),
mistaking its hunger for warmth.
---
Death

And if they ask me how much
I loved, I would say, enough to
be Icarus. Because the sea
remembers only the fall, but I
remember the sun. Because the
fall meant I flew, and the death
meant I loved.
Such is the fate of the "fool" in
love.
posts.explanation: The writer walks through the stages of love: feeling the world grow bigger, needing the person, trusting them, giving all of yourself, almost worshipping them, and burning for them. In the end loving that much ruins him, like a boy in an old story who flew too near the sun, yet he would choose it.

posts.caption: Lifeee
posts.displayTitle: But just when you believe life has exhausted all its cruelties,
posts.altText: But just when you believe life has exhausted all its cruelties, it comes with another to ruin you in a different way. What is peace, if not merely an interval between one catastrophe and another?
posts.text:
But just when you believe
life has exhausted
all its cruelties,
it comes with another to
ruin you in a different way.

What is peace,
if not merely an
interval between one
catastrophe and another?
posts.explanation: The writer says that just when you think life has no more ways to hurt you, it finds a new one. He wonders if peace is only a short break between one disaster and the next.

posts.caption: He who has seen it knows it
posts.displayTitle: The strangeness of the human heart is that it desires the very things
posts.altText: The strangeness of the human heart is that it desires the very things which will ruin it, which has ruined it. He who sees it, he who feels it calls it love. What a fool
posts.text:
The strangeness of the
human heart is that
it desires the very things
which will ruin it,
which has ruined it.

He who sees it ,
he who feels it calls it love.
What a fool
posts.explanation: The writer says the human heart is strange because it wants the very things that hurt it, again and again. People who see and feel this call it love, and he calls that foolish.

posts.caption: Locked doors are knocked
posts.displayTitle: The tragedy of longing is not that it reaches for what it cannot…
posts.altText: The tragedy of longing is not that it reaches for what it cannot possess. It is that, given the entire world, it would still choose the locked door. because some desires do not seek fulfillment. They seek permanence. What is love if not permanence in the architecture of heart.
posts.text:
The tragedy of longing
is not that it reaches for
what it cannot possess.

entire world, it would
still choose the locked door.
because some desires
do not seek fulfillment.
They seek permanence.

What is love if not permanence
in the architecture of heart.
posts.explanation: The writer says the sad thing about longing is that, even with the whole world open to it, it would still choose the one thing it can't have. Some wishes don't want to come true; they want to last forever, and he says love is that lasting thing built inside the heart.

posts.caption: Ghost of possibilities
posts.displayTitle: we can survive almost any truth.
posts.altText: we can survive almost any truth. What ruins us are the possibilities. The lives we might have lived, the words we might have said, the people we might have kept. In the end, ghosts require no death to exist they die inside us, they live inside us.
posts.text:
we can survive almost
any truth. What ruins us
are the possibilities.

The lives we might
have lived, the words we
might have said, the people
we might have kept.

In the end,
ghosts require no death
to exist they die inside us,
they live inside us.
posts.explanation: The writer says we can handle almost any hard truth, but what breaks us is thinking about what might have been: other lives, unsaid words, people we could have kept. These what-ifs are like ghosts that live inside us, and no one has to die for them to exist.

posts.caption: Hand in hand
posts.displayTitle: I think love and loss go hand in hand.
posts.altText: I think love and loss go hand in hand. Because I have lost everyone I have loved. I tell you, the heaviest tears are those which are shed at loss, because you lose yourself too. Parts of you leave because you aren't you anymore, and what you once were never finds its way back to you ever again.

go hand in hand.

Because I have lost
everyone I have loved.

I tell you, the heaviest tears are those
which are shed at loss, because you lose
yourself too. Parts of you leave because
you aren’t you anymore, and what you
once were never finds its way back to you
ever again.
posts.explanation: The writer feels love and loss always come together, since he has lost everyone he loved. He says the tears over a loss are the heaviest because you lose part of yourself too, and the person you were never comes back.

own existence. Everything appears
larger because you have become
smaller. You call this happiness. No
one corrects you. Like dawn entering
a valley that has never known light.
Like a drop of rain believing it has
discovered the sea.
posts.explanation: At the start of love, you think you have found someone new, but really you have lost track of where you end and they begin. The world feels bigger because you feel smaller, and you call it happiness, like a raindrop thinking it has found the sea.

posts.caption: Stages of love 2/7
posts.displayTitle: Attachment: It is like a blind man waiting for light in his darkest…
posts.altText: Attachment. It is like a blind man waiting for light in his darkest dark, learning the shape of a face with his bare hands. He does not know its colour nor the light that falls upon it. He only knows that the world ends where that face is absent. So his hands continue searching with the same certainty. No one has the heart to tell him that hope can survive even where light…
posts.text:
Attachment

It is like a blind man waiting for light
in his darkest dark, learning the shape
of a face with his bare hands. He does
not know its colour nor the light that
falls upon it. He only knows that the
world ends where that face is absent.
