So his hands continue searching with
the same certainty. No one has the
heart to tell him that hope can survive
even where light cannot. Perhaps
attachment is not refusing to let go but
forgetting that there was ever anything
else to hold.
posts.explanation: Being attached is like a blind man learning a face with his hands. He doesn't know how it looks, only that his world ends where that face is gone, so he keeps searching. The writer says attachment is not refusing to let go, but forgetting you ever had anything else to hold.

posts.caption: Stages of love 3/7
posts.displayTitle: Trust: Maybe that's what trust has always been closing your eyes
posts.altText: Trust. Maybe that's what trust has always been closing your eyes and hoping that, when you open them again, the person you trusted hasn't disappeared or, worse, hasn't become someone you never knew. You never ask to see the path you just walk walk into it.
posts.text:
Trust

Maybe that's what trust has
always been closing your eyes
and hoping that, when you
open them again, the person
you trusted hasn't disappeared
or, worse, hasn't become
someone you never knew. You
never ask to see the path you
just walk walk into it.
posts.explanation: Trusting someone is like shutting your eyes and hoping that when you open them, that person is still there and has not become a stranger. You don't ask to see the road first; you just walk into it.

posts.caption: Stages of love 4/7
posts.displayTitle: Love: Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into "us" is love
posts.altText: Love. Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into "us" is love. Maybe giving yourself wholly is love. Maybe existing for one particularity entirely is love. maybe to love is to love beyond yourself, Maybe it is remembering another heartbeat before your own and maybe I am still figuring out what love is and that for me that is very much love.
posts.text:
Love

Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into
"us" is love. Maybe giving yourself
wholly is love. Maybe existing for
one particularity entirely is love.
maybe to love is to love beyond
yourself, Maybe it is remembering
another heartbeat before your own
and maybe I am still figuring out
what love is and that for me that is
very much love.
posts.explanation: The writer tries to say what love is: slowly turning from me into us, giving all of yourself, living fully for one person, caring about their heartbeat before your own. He admits he is still working it out, and that this searching is love to him too.

posts.caption: Stages of love 5/7
posts.displayTitle: Devotion: Then love becomes a cathedral with no god inside it
posts.altText: Devotion. Then love becomes a cathedral with no god inside it. You kneel anyway because the echo sounds more merciful than the beloved's screams. Every prayer returns wearing the beloved's voice. Faith grows larger than truth. Soon you cannot tell whether you worship a person or the space they carved in your heart to be worshipped.
posts.text:
Devotion

Then love becomes a cathedral
with no god inside it. You kneel
anyway because the echo sounds
more merciful than the beloved's
screams. Every prayer returns
wearing the beloved's voice. Faith
grows larger than truth. Soon you
cannot tell whether you worship a
person or the space they carved in
your heart to be worshipped.
posts.explanation: Here love turns into worship, like praying in a church with no god inside. You keep praying anyway, and every prayer comes back sounding like the one you love. In time you can't tell if you love the person or just the place they made for themselves in your heart.

posts.caption: Stages of love 6/7
posts.displayTitle: Passion: Perhaps passion is the moth, circling a flame it knows will…
posts.altText: Passion. Perhaps passion is the moth, circling a flame it knows will ruin it, yet mistaking its warmth for mercy. Or perhaps I was the flame, burning through every hope and calling the ashes "moths." And if you ask whether I loved, I did... enough to offer myself to the fire(love), mistaking its hunger for warmth.
posts.text:
Passion

Perhaps passion is the moth, circling
a flame it knows will ruin it, yet
mistaking its warmth for mercy. Or
perhaps I was the flame, burning
through every hope and calling the
ashes "moths." And if you ask
whether I loved, I did... enough to
offer myself to the fire(love),
mistaking its hunger for warmth.
posts.explanation: Passion is like a moth flying around a flame that will kill it, thinking the heat is kindness. Or maybe the writer was the flame, burning up every hope. He says he did love, enough to throw himself into it, thinking its hunger was warmth.

posts.caption: Stages of love 7/7
posts.displayTitle: And if they ask me how much I loved, I would say, enough to be Icarus
posts.altText: Death. And if they ask me how much I loved, I would say, enough to be Icarus. Because the sea remembers only the fall, but I remember the sun. Because the fall meant I flew, and the death meant I loved. Such is the fate of the "fool" in love.
posts.text:
Death

And if they ask me how much
I loved, I would say, enough to
be Icarus. Because the sea
remembers only the fall, but I
remember the sun. Because the
fall meant I flew, and the death
meant I loved.
Such is the fate of the "fool" in
love.
posts.explanation: The writer says he loved like a boy in an old story who flew too close to the sun and fell into the sea. Others remember only the fall, but he remembers the sun: falling meant he flew, and dying meant he loved. He calls this the fate of a fool in love.

posts.caption: Father
posts.displayTitle: Father, I have always carried you within my anger
posts.altText: Father, I have always carried you within my anger. I sometimes become you. Tell me, how did you manage to control it after the world gave you every reason not to? I inherited your anger, but I fear I did not inherit your strength. What is this incurable wound that you have carried without ever showing it?
posts.text:
Father,
I have always carried you
within my anger.
I sometimes become you.
Tell me, how did you manage to
control it after the world gave you
every reason not to?
I inherited your anger,
but I fear I did not inherit your strength.
What is this incurable wound
that you have carried without
ever showing it?
posts.explanation: The writer tells his father he has the same anger and sometimes acts just like him. He asks how his father kept it under control when life gave him every reason not to, fears he got the anger but not the strength, and wonders what hidden pain his father carried.

posts.caption: What is love?
posts.displayTitle: There's something tragic about me, because when love happened
posts.altText: There's something tragic about me, because when love happened i had let it consume me. When absence happened i let it consume me too. If I love i love everything about it. Even the presence, even the absence. What is love if not this?
posts.text:
There’s something tragic
about me, because
when love happened
i had let it consume me.
When absence happened
i let it consume me too.

If I love i love everything
about it. Even the presence,
even the absence.
What is love if not this?
posts.explanation: The writer gives himself fully to whatever he feels. When love came, he let it fill him, and when it was gone, he let the missing fill him too. To him, real love means loving all of it, both the being together and the being apart.

posts.caption: You broke me
posts.displayTitle: Then you arrived and what neither time nor loneliness could break
posts.altText: Then you arrived and what neither time nor loneliness could break, you did with nothing more than your presence. Perhaps that is the tragedy of warmth once you have known it, the cold becomes unbearable.
posts.text:
Then you arrived
and what neither time
nor loneliness could break,

you did with nothing more
than your presence.
Perhaps that is the tragedy
of warmth once
you have known it,
the cold becomes unbearable.
posts.explanation: The writer had a hardness that time and being alone could not break, but the person he loves broke it just by being near. The sad part is that once you have felt that warmth, being cold and alone again becomes too hard to bear.

posts.caption: Hope is a cruel thing
posts.displayTitle: I loved you even when I was told not to
posts.altText: I loved you even when I was told not to. Long after reason had withdrawn its support, long after hope had strangled me, I kept hanging from hope itself. Hope acted like an anesthesia upon my soul. It numbed me so completely that I failed to realize how long I had been hanged.
posts.text:
I loved you even
when I was told not to.
Long after reason had
withdrawn its support,
long after hope had strangled me,
I kept hanging from hope itself.
Hope acted like an anesthesia
upon my soul. It numbed me
so completely that I failed
to realize how long
I had been hanged.
posts.explanation: The writer kept loving her even when he was told to stop and when it made no sense. Hope kept him holding on, but it also numbed him like a painkiller, so he did not notice how long it had been choking him.

posts.caption:
Pride..
7 deadly sins 1/7
posts.displayTitle: There is a peculiar dignity in destruction when it was earned by…
posts.altText: There is a peculiar dignity in destruction when it was earned by caring too deeply. For what is more tragic to leave blood upon the earth because you held on too long, or to leave none at all because you never dared to hold anything close?
posts.text:
There is a peculiar dignity in destruction
when it was earned by caring too deeply.
For what is more tragic to leave blood upon
the earth because you held on too long,
or to leave none at all because you never
dared to hold anything close?
posts.explanation: The writer says there is something to respect in being hurt because you cared too much. He asks which is sadder: being torn up because you held on too long, or never being hurt because you never dared to get close to anything.

posts.caption:
Pride..
Seven deadly sins 1/7
posts.displayTitle: This wreckage takes pride in its own ruin
posts.altText: This wreckage takes pride in its own ruin because innocent leave no scars upon the world. It is those who have loved recklessly, disastrously, beyond reason, he who walks away stained by their own devotion has every wound bearing the shape of a dagger they never refused to stop loving.
posts.text:
This wreckage takes pride in its own ruin
because innocent leave no scars upon the world.
It is those who have loved recklessly,
disastrously, beyond reason, he who walks away
stained by their own devotion has every wound
bearing the shape of a dagger they never refused
to stop loving.
posts.explanation: The writer is proud of how broken he is, because people who never risked anything leave no marks on the world. Those who loved wildly, beyond sense, come away hurt, and each wound comes from something they kept loving even though it cut them.

posts.caption: Pride
posts.displayTitle: I am proud of this tragedity of my ruin
posts.altText: I am proud of this tragedity of my ruin because it proves there was once something magnificent enough to collapse. The blood upon my hands condemns me. The love inside my heart absolves me and somewhere between those two verdicts, I continue to live.
posts.text:
I am proud of this tragedity of my ruin
because it proves there was once something
magnificent enough to collapse. The blood
upon my hands condemns me. The love inside
my heart absolves me and somewhere between
those two verdicts, I continue to live.
posts.explanation: The writer is proud of how badly he was broken, because it shows there was once something great enough to fall apart. The wrong he has done makes him guilty, but his love makes him feel forgiven, and he goes on living stuck between those two.

posts.caption:
Envy
Seven deadly sins 2/7
posts.displayTitle: All hatred returns to the self.
posts.altText: All hatred returns to the self.
posts.text:
All hatred returns
to the self.
posts.explanation: The writer says any hate you feel ends up coming back to hurt you.

posts.caption:
Envy
Seven deadly sins 2/7
posts.displayTitle: we do not suffer from the lives of others
posts.altText: we do not suffer from the lives of others. We suffer from our inability to stop devouring our own. The stars do not steal light from the moon. The serpent never catches what it seeks because what it seeks is itself. So do we.
posts.text:
we do not suffer from
the lives of others.
We suffer from our inability
to stop devouring our own.
The stars do not steal
light from the moon.

The serpent never catches
what it seeks because
what it seeks is itself.
So do we.
posts.explanation: The writer says we are not hurt by other people's lives but by how we keep eating away at our own. Stars don't take light from the moon, so others are not the problem. Like a snake chasing itself, we never catch what we chase, because what we chase is ourselves.

posts.caption:
Envy
Seven deadly sins 2/7
posts.displayTitle: The child longs to become an adult.
posts.altText: The child longs to become an adult. The adult longs for his childhood again. The lonely pray for love. The loved mourn who they were before it. No one is truly happy because we spend our lives chasing what is absent, only to realise we abandoned what was already ours.
posts.text:
The child longs
to become an adult.
The adult longs
for his childhood again.
The lonely pray for love.
The loved mourn
who they were before it.
No one is truly happy
because we spend our lives
chasing what is absent,
only to realise we
abandoned what was
already ours.
posts.explanation: The writer says people always want what they don't have: children want to grow up, adults miss being children, lonely people want love, and people in love miss who they were before. No one is fully happy, because we chase what is missing and leave behind what we already had.

posts.caption:
Wrath.
Seven deadly sins 3/7
posts.displayTitle: There was a time I believed every wound deserved a wound in return
posts.altText: There was a time I believed every wound deserved a wound in return. That if the world handed me fire, I was entitled to become the one to burn. What a magnificent lie.
posts.text:
There was a time
I believed every
wound deserved a
wound in return.

That if the world
handed me fire,
I was entitled to
become the one to burn.
What a magnificent lie.
posts.explanation: The writer once believed that if someone hurt him, he had the right to hurt back, and if life gave him pain, he could pass it on. Now he sees that this was a big, grand lie.

posts.caption:
Wrath
Seven deadly sins 3/7
posts.displayTitle: There's a fire within me that burns through every emotion I have
posts.altText: There's a fire within me that burns through every emotion I have. I think the cruelest thing about these flames is that they do not distinguish between enemy and a shelter, they burn indiscriminately. I wonder how much they have taken away from me, and how much I have willingly sacrificed.
posts.text:
There’s a fire within
me that burns through
every emotion I have.
I think the cruelest thing
about these flames is that
they do not distinguish
between enemy and a shelter,
they burn all indiscriminately.
I wonder how much
they have taken away from me,
and how much
I have willingly sacrificed.
posts.explanation: The writer feels a fire inside him that burns through all his feelings. The worst part is that it burns everything, both what hurts him and what keeps him safe, and he wonders how much it took from him and how much he gave up himself.

posts.caption:
Wrath
Seven deadly sins 3/7
posts.displayTitle: My father's eyes carried enough fire to burn through every happiness
posts.altText: My father's eyes carried enough fire to burn through every happiness my family ever knew. Still, I could not help becoming him. cruelest inheritance of all is not the wounds he left behind, but the realization that I spent years running from his shadow only to become him when the light left.
posts.text:
My father’s eyes carried
enough fire to burn through every
happiness my family ever knew.

Still, I could not
help becoming him.

cruelest inheritance of all
is not the wounds he left behind,
but the realization that
I spent years running from his
shadow only to become
him when the light left.
posts.explanation: The writer's father had an anger that burned away his family's happiness. The writer spent years trying not to be like him, but when the good times ended he became just like him, and that hurts more than any wound his father left.

posts.caption:
Greed
Seven deadly sins 4/7
posts.displayTitle: the greatest love is the one that does not bounds itself for…
posts.altText: the greatest love is the one that does not bounds itself for possession. For there is a peculiar tragedy in belonging the hunger that once made us reach so desperately often dies the moment our hands finally close around what they desired.
posts.text:
the greatest love is the
one that does not bounds
itself for possession.

For there is a peculiar
tragedy in belonging
the hunger that once made
us reach so desperately
often dies the moment our
hands finally close around
what they desired.
posts.explanation: The writer says the greatest love does not try to own the other person. The sad thing about having someone is that the strong wish that pulled you to them often fades the moment you finally have them.

posts.caption:
Greed
Seven deadly sins 4/7
posts.displayTitle: perhaps the rarest freedom is not having everything
posts.altText: perhaps the rarest freedom is not having everything. Perhaps it is looking at what remains, at who remains, and finding no desire to ask for more.
posts.text:
perhaps the rarest freedom is not
having everything. Perhaps it is looking
at what remains, at who remains,
and finding no desire to ask for more.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks real freedom may not be having everything. It may be looking at what and who you still have, and feeling no need to ask for anything more.

posts.caption:
Greed
Seven deadly sins 4/7
posts.displayTitle: perhaps the rarest freedom is not having everything
posts.altText: perhaps the rarest freedom is not having everything. Perhaps it is looking at what remains, at who remains, and finding no desire to ask for more.
posts.text:
perhaps the rarest freedom is not
having everything. Perhaps it is looking
at what remains, at who remains,
and finding no desire to ask for more.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks real freedom may not be having everything. It may be looking at what and who you still have, and feeling no need to ask for anything more.

posts.caption:
Greed
Seven deadly sins 4/7
posts.displayTitle: What I possessed ceased to move me, and what I lacked became sacred
posts.altText: What I possessed ceased to move me, and what I lacked became sacred. but to spend a lifetime possessing more is the greatest slavery of all, but at some point, I just want to belong and never ask for more.
posts.text:
What I possessed
ceased to move me,
and what I lacked
became sacred.

but to spend a lifetime
possessing more is the
greatest slavery of all,
but at some point,
I just want to belong
and never ask for more.
posts.explanation: What the writer had stopped meaning much to him, and what he didn't have started to feel holy. He sees that always wanting more is like being a slave, and now he just wants to belong somewhere and stop asking for more.

posts.caption:
Lust
Seven deadly sins 5/7
posts.displayTitle: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it
posts.altText: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it. Perhaps some desires are not born from love at all. Perhaps they are born from our inability to let beautiful things remain free.
posts.text:
What a strange thing
it is to admire a flower,
then wish to pluck it.

Perhaps some desires are
not born from love at all.
Perhaps they are born
from our inability to let
beautiful things remain free.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that we see a beautiful flower and then want to pick it. He thinks some wants don't come from love at all, but from not being able to let beautiful things stay free.

posts.caption:
Lust
Seven deadly sins 5/7
posts.displayTitle: a bird sings because it belongs to the sky
posts.altText: a bird sings because it belongs to the sky. The moment we place it in a cage, we keep the bird and lose the song. We become so afraid of losing beautiful things that we clutch them tightly enough to crush them.
posts.text:
a bird sings because
it belongs to the sky.
The moment we place
it in a cage, we keep the
bird and lose the song.

We become so afraid
of losing beautiful things
that we clutch them tightly
enough to crush them.
posts.explanation: A bird sings because it is free in the sky; put it in a cage and you keep the bird but lose its song. The writer says we are so scared of losing beautiful things that we hold them too tight and crush them.

posts.caption:
Lust
Seven deadly sins 5/7
posts.displayTitle: There are ways of looking at a person that resemble blindness
posts.altText: There are ways of looking at a person that resemble blindness. I knew the color of her eyes long before I knew what made them weep by the time I distinguished between her eyes and her tears she had already become a stranger I thought I loved. It isn't about the shell it is about the soul.
posts.text:
There are ways of
looking at a person that
resemble blindness.
I knew the color of
her eyes long before I knew
what made them weep
by the time I distinguished
between her eyes and her tears
she had already become
a stranger I thought I loved.
It isn’t about the shell
it is about the soul.
posts.explanation: The writer says you can look at someone and still not really see them. He knew how she looked long before he knew what made her sad, and by the time he understood her pain, she had become a stranger. What matters is the person inside, not the outside.

posts.caption:
Gluttony
Seven deadly sins 6/7
posts.displayTitle: I wonder how much grief I had to devour every bit of my happiness
posts.altText: I wonder how much grief I had to devour every bit of my happiness.
posts.text:
I wonder how much grief
I had to devour every bit
of my happiness.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders how much sadness it took to eat up every bit of his happiness.

posts.caption:
Gluttony
Seven deadly sins 6/7
posts.displayTitle: I desired love, yet each time it was offered, it felt lesser than…
posts.altText: I desired love, yet each time it was offered, it felt lesser than before. I kept asking for more and more, until one day I could feel none of it at all. Perhaps that is the tragedy of an endless hunger it does not starve because it is empty. It starves because nothing is ever enough and while understanding it all I was left with nothing at all.
posts.text:
I desired love,
yet each time it was offered,
it felt lesser than before.
I kept asking for more
and more, until one day
I could feel none of it at all.
Perhaps that is the tragedy
of an endless hunger it does not
starve because it is empty.
It starves because nothing
is ever enough and while
understanding it all I was left
with nothing at all.
posts.explanation: The writer wanted love, but each time he got it, it felt like less than before. He kept wanting more until he couldn't feel it at all. He says that kind of hunger starves not because it has nothing, but because nothing is ever enough, and in the end he was left with nothing.

posts.caption:
Gluttony
Seven deadly sins 6/7
posts.displayTitle: to fill the void inside me, I have devoured many things
posts.altText: to fill the void inside me, I have devoured many things. even you even your memories.
posts.text:
to fill the void inside me,
I have devoured many things.
even you even your memories.
posts.explanation: To fill the emptiness inside him, the writer has used up many things, even the person he loved and his memories of her.

posts.caption:
Sloth
Seven deadly sins 7/7
posts.displayTitle: you could, but did you?
posts.altText: you could, but did you?
posts.text: you could, but did you?
posts.explanation: The writer asks someone a short, sharp question. He seems to say that being able to do something is not the same as actually doing it.

posts.caption:
Sloth
Seven deadly sins 7/7
posts.displayTitle: I deserve neither hell nor heaven;
posts.altText: I deserve neither hell nor heaven; I do not belong anywhere except for her eyes.
posts.explanation: The writer feels he deserves neither heaven nor hell. The only place he feels he belongs is in the eyes of the woman he loves.

posts.caption:
Gluttony
Seven deadly sins 7/7
posts.displayTitle: There is a prison that has no walls
posts.altText: There is a prison that has no walls. It is built from all the lives we meant to live and never began and it is funny how I did not lose myself chasing the wrong path. I lost it while standing still, waiting for the right one.
posts.text:
There is a prison
that has no walls.
It is built from all the
lives we meant to live
and never began

and it is funny how
I did not lose myself
chasing the wrong path.
I lost it while standing still,
waiting for the right one.
posts.explanation: The writer says there is a jail with no walls, made of all the lives we planned but never started. He finds it strange that he didn't lose himself by going the wrong way, but by standing still and waiting for the right one.

posts.caption: What is peace?
posts.displayTitle: What is peace, if not merely an interval between one catastrophe and…
posts.altText: What is peace, if not merely an interval between one catastrophe and another?
posts.text:
What is peace, if not merely
an interval between one catastrophe
and another?
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if peace is only a short break between one disaster and the next.

posts.caption: I fear
posts.displayTitle: What a peculiar curse it is. To stand at heaven's gate
posts.altText: What a peculiar curse it is. To stand at heaven's gate and still searching for the hell inside it. To hate the very love which once kept you alive. i fear this tragic end..
posts.text:
What a peculiar
curse it is.
To stand at heaven's gate
and still searching for the
hell inside it.

To hate
the very love which once
kept you alive.
i fear this tragic end..
posts.explanation: The writer says it is a strange curse to be somewhere wonderful and still look for the bad in it, or to hate the love that once kept you alive. He is afraid this sad ending will be his own.

posts.caption: To love is to suffer then to suffer is to love.. haha
posts.displayTitle: While writing live, my autocorrect changed it to love.
posts.altText: While writing live, my autocorrect changed it to love. Then I realized— to love is to live. But love is to die too. and if love contains both life and death, perhaps living is merely learning how to die for the things we cannot bear to lose. So, to live is to love = To love is to die = and to die, perhaps, is simply another way of having lived.
posts.text:
While writing live,
my autocorrect changed it to love.
Then I realized—
to love is to live.
But to love is to die too.
and if love contains both life and death,
perhaps living is merely
learning how to die for
the things we cannot bear to lose.

So, to live is to love = To love is to die
= and to die, perhaps, is simply
another way of having lived.
posts.explanation: When his phone changed live to love, the writer started thinking. Loving is living, but loving also means losing, a kind of dying. So he thinks living may be learning to give yourself up for what you can't bear to lose, and dying may just be another way of having lived.

posts.caption: Smoking is injurious to health so is love.
posts.displayTitle: Smoking is injurious to health
posts.altText: Smoking is injurious to health. So is love. Maybe I don't deserve it all, maybe it's me, maybe it's my fate. Because everything I love leaves me. I have no faith left in permanence.
posts.text:
Smoking is injurious
to health

So is love Maybe
I don't deserve it
all, maybe it's me ,
maybe it's my fate.
because everything
i love leaves me
i have no faith left
in permanence.
posts.explanation: The writer says love, like smoking, is bad for you. Everything he loves leaves him, so he wonders if it is his fault or just his fate, and he no longer believes anything can last.

posts.caption: My heart is a prisoner
posts.displayTitle: My rib is a cage that keeps my heart from coming to you.
posts.altText: My rib is a cage that keeps my heart from coming to you. What a cruel design to carry the prisoner that longs for you and the prison that keeps it away within the same body.
posts.text:
My rib is a cage
that keeps my heart
from coming to you.

What a cruel design
to carry the prisoner
that longs for you
and the prison that
keeps it away within
the same body.
posts.explanation: The writer says his ribs are like a cage that keeps his heart from going to the person he loves. He finds it cruel that his one body holds both the heart that wants her and the cage that keeps it away.

posts.caption: Is it too much to ask for?
posts.displayTitle: I do not ask you to remember me forever.
posts.altText: I do not ask you to remember me forever. I only ask that, if you ever go looking for someone again, remember me for once. I only ask that you remember me the way I loved you, not the way you thought I did. I ask you Let yourself be loved let yourself stay.
posts.text:
I do not ask you to
remember me forever.
I only ask that,
if you ever go looking
for someone again,
remember me for once.
I only ask that you
remember me the way
I loved you, not the
way you thought I did.
I ask you Let yourself
be loved let yourself stay.
posts.explanation: The writer does not ask to be remembered forever. He only asks that if she ever looks for love again, she remembers him once, and remembers how he truly loved her, not how she thought he did. He asks her to let herself be loved and to stay.

posts.caption: Isn't it
posts.displayTitle: But to survive what you once loved is the greatest tragedy of all
posts.altText: But to survive what you once loved is the greatest tragedy of all. How do I make peace with the fact that the person I once believed was my everything is now only a scar across my chest?
posts.text:
But to survive what you once loved is the
greatest tragedy of all. How do I make
peace with the fact that the person I
once believed was my everything is now only
a scar across my chest?
posts.explanation: The writer says the worst thing is to keep living after losing someone you loved. He asks how to accept that the person who was once his whole world is now just a painful mark on his heart.

posts.caption: It's July again
posts.displayTitle: July came by again, but still you haven't
posts.altText: July came by again, but still you haven't. How much more do I have to wait? How much more do I have to pray? Soon it'll be October. Soon, the prayer will turn into a dirge for us.
posts.text:
July came by again,
but still you haven't.
How much more
do I have to wait?
How much more
do I have to pray?

Soon it'll be October.
Soon, the prayer will
turn into a dirge for us.
posts.explanation: July has come again, but the person he waits for has not. He asks how much longer he must wait and pray, and fears that soon, by October, his prayers for them will turn into a funeral song.

posts.caption: Flowing blood
posts.displayTitle: If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood
posts.altText: If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood, I don't know how much difference in color you'll see. But whatever difference remains that difference will be my love for you.
posts.text:
If you keep a rose
beside my flowing blood,
I don't know how
much difference in color
you'll see.

But whatever difference
remains that difference
will be my love for you.
posts.explanation: The writer says if you put a red rose next to his blood, you might barely see a difference in color. Whatever small difference there is, that is his love for her.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: It's not about who stays or who leaves
posts.altText: It's not about who stays or who leaves. It's about for whom you stop in the middle of a prayer just to pray for them as well. Because there are people you stop asking God to bring back, yet you never stop asking God to keep them safe.
posts.text:
It's not about who
stays or who leaves.
It's about for whom
you stop in the middle
of a prayer just to pray
for them as well.

Because there are
people you stop asking
God to bring back,
yet you never stop asking
God to keep them safe.
posts.explanation: The writer says what matters is not who stays or leaves, but who you stop to pray for in the middle of your own prayer. Some people you stop asking God to bring back, but you never stop asking God to keep them safe.

posts.caption: I give and give
posts.displayTitle: Maybe that's my problem. I would give everything and ask for nothing…
posts.altText: Maybe that's my problem. I would give everything and ask for nothing in return. But there is a peculiar tragedy in giving you never know when the cup has become full, when it has begun to overflow. You never know where generosity ends and self-abandonment begins. You never know where to stop.
posts.text:
Maybe that's my problem.
I would give everything and
ask for nothing in return.
But there is a peculiar
tragedy in giving
you never know when
the cup has become full,
when it has begun to overflow.
You never know where generosity ends
and self-abandonment begins.
You never know where to stop.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks his problem is that he gives everything and asks for nothing back. The sad part of giving is that you can't tell when it is too much, or where being kind ends and losing yourself begins, so you never know when to stop.

posts.caption: Collab with @inkedbyshrad
posts.displayTitle: Maybe fate waits until we stop searching for it
posts.altText: Maybe fate waits until we stop searching for it because the best things bloom in gardens we weren't looking at. Perhaps love has always disliked being chased. Perhaps it only arrives when our hands are too tired to keep knocking on closed doors. and maybe, when we stop asking where happiness is, we will find it us sitting among the flowers we never thought were growing for us.
posts.text:
Maybe fate waits until
we stop searching for it
because the best things bloom
in gardens we weren't looking at.
Perhaps love has always
disliked being chased.
Perhaps it only arrives when
our hands are too tired to keep
knocking on closed doors.
and maybe, when we stop asking
where happiness is, we will find it us
sitting among the flowers we never
thought were growing for us.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks good things like love and happiness may come once we stop chasing them. They show up where we weren't looking, when we are too tired to keep pushing, and we find them already growing around us.

posts.caption: I do
posts.displayTitle: I search for you the way my fingers trace old memories
posts.altText: I search for you the way my fingers trace old memories, only to find the friction of love, like the way you used to caress my hair. My fingers always return to the same place, and still I wonder, why do I keep living through a heart that no longer knows whether it beats out of love or out of habit?
posts.text:
I search for you
the way my fingers
trace old memories, only to
find the friction of love,
like the way you
used to caress my hair.
My fingers always return
to the same place,
and still I wonder, why do
I keep living through a heart
that no longer knows whether it
beats out of love or out of habit?
posts.explanation: The writer looks for the person he lost in old memories, like the feel of her hand in his hair. He keeps going back to the same memories and wonders if his heart still beats out of love for her or just out of habit.

posts.caption: Ways to cope up
posts.displayTitle: There are ways people survive after love
posts.altText: There are ways people survive after love. I think it's only two strangers learning how to share the same body without actually sharing one. One still waits at a door that will never open. The other has already started walking home.
posts.text:
There are ways people
survive after love.
I think it's only two
strangers learning how
to share the same body
without actually sharing one.

One still waits at a
door that will never open.
The other has already
started walking home.
posts.explanation: He seems to say that after love ends, it is like two strangers living in one body. One part still waits at a door that will never open, while the other part has already started moving on.

posts.caption: Cruelty
posts.displayTitle: There's a cruelty in writing your name and forgetting what to write a…
posts.altText: There's a cruelty in writing your name and forgetting what to write after it. "Perhaps love was never the words I wrote." Perhaps it was always your name.
posts.text:
There's a cruelty in
writing your name
and forgetting what
to write after it.

"Perhaps love was
never the words
I wrote."
Perhaps it was always
your name.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it painful to write her name and then not know what to write next. He thinks maybe love was never in the words he wrote, but only in her name itself.

posts.caption: July!!
posts.displayTitle: June burnt my flesh. July has peeked into my heart through my peeling…
posts.altText: June burnt my flesh. July has peeked into my heart through my peeling skin, and sneaked into my lungs to turn them gray. June offered a little mercy by letting me end, but July took it away terribly easily. Perhaps this is what punishment looks like the leftover of a body that keeps making promises on behalf of a heart that has already left.
posts.text:
June burnt my flesh.
July has peeked into
my heart through my
peeling skin, and sneaked
into my lungs to turn
them gray. June offered a
little mercy by letting me end,
but July took it away terribly easily.
Perhaps this is what punishment
looks like the leftover of a body
that keeps making promises on behalf
of a heart that has already left.
posts.explanation: The writer says June and July hurt him badly, burning him and filling his chest with gray. June seemed to offer him an ending, but July took even that away. He feels this is punishment: a body that keeps going and making promises for a heart that is already gone.

posts.caption: I am stuck
posts.displayTitle: The more I talk to people, the more I realize how unbearable your abs…
posts.altText: The more I talk to people, the more I realize how unbearable your absence has become. There is a repetitive disaster in taking out your pictures from my wallet and keeping them inside it again. I am stuck.
posts.text:
The more I talk to
people, the more
I realize how
unbearable your
absence has become.

There is a repetitive disaster
in taking out your pictures
from my wallet and keeping
them inside it again.
I am stuck.
posts.explanation: The more the writer talks to other people, the more he feels how much he misses the person who is gone. He keeps taking her photos out of his wallet and putting them back again, and he feels stuck.

posts.caption: Is it ?
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps love was never the opposite of sorrow
posts.altText: Perhaps love was never the opposite of sorrow. Perhaps it was simply the name we gave to what we knew we would lose and chose to love anyway.
posts.text:
Perhaps love was
never the opposite
of sorrow.

Perhaps it was simply
the name we gave to
what we knew we
would lose and chose
to love anyway.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks love may not be the opposite of sadness. Maybe love is just the name for caring about something we know we will lose, and choosing to care anyway.

posts.caption: I hope whatever is wrong with me, stays wrong!
posts.displayTitle: Roses are red. So is my blood.
posts.altText: Roses are red. So is my blood. Is that why you mistook them for it? Tell me, which one do you love? I'll bring that for you next time. If you don't know what is grief, then what is grief? There's you and then there are things that makes me remember you, oh god how beautiful they are.
posts.text:
Roses are red. So
is my blood. Is that
why you mistook
them for it? Tell me,
which one do you
love? I'll bring that
for you next time.
---
If you don't
know what is
grief, then
what is grief?
---
There's you and
then there are
things that makes
me remember
you, oh god how
beautiful they are.
---
कह देना कि प्यार है,
भी प्यार है♡
---
If you don't
know what's
wrong, then
what's
wrong?
---
If you don't
know what's
wrong, then
what's
wrong?
posts.explanation: These are short thoughts. The writer asks if she mistook his blood for roses, since both are red, and which she loves. He wonders what grief or wrong even is if you can't name it, finds things that remind him of her beautiful, and says in Hindi that saying it is love is love too.

posts.caption: Unbearable
posts.displayTitle: To be forgiven is to admit that one has been seen completely
posts.altText: To be forgiven is to admit that one has been seen completely and loved nonetheless, and there are souls for whom such a thing is more unbearable than punishment.
posts.text:
To be forgiven is to
admit that one has
been seen completely
and loved nonetheless,

and there are souls
for whom such a thing
is more unbearable
than punishment.
posts.explanation: The writer says being forgiven means someone has seen all of you, even the bad parts, and still loves you. For some people, that is harder to bear than being punished.

posts.caption: Hello
posts.displayTitle: Behind my every breath, there is an air of you
posts.altText: Behind my every breath, there is an air of you. and I keep forgetting that what I once inhaled, I must now exhale. Perhaps that is why I fear breathing now, unable to bear this loss, I may simply forget how to breathe.
posts.text:
Behind my every breath,
there is an air of you.
and I keep
forgetting that what
I once inhaled,
I must now exhale.
Perhaps that is why
I fear breathing now,
unable to bear this loss,
I may simply forget
how to breathe.
posts.explanation: The writer feels the person he lost is in every breath he takes. He keeps forgetting that he must let her go, like breathing out, and because the loss is too much, he fears he might just forget how to breathe.

posts.caption: Hello
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us
posts.altText: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us. Perhaps we cling to it because it is the last hope that cannot be taken away without taking us with it.
posts.text:
Perhaps we do not
cling to our suffering
because it is dear
to us.

Perhaps we cling
to it because it is
the last hope that
cannot be taken away
without taking us with it.

(now read the
underlined part)
posts.explanation: The writer thinks we don't hold on to our pain because we love it. We hold on because it is our last hope, and it cannot be taken without taking us too. The last line points to a hidden message in underlined words.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: I have begun to suspect that the most terrible thing about guilt
posts.altText: I have begun to suspect that the most terrible thing about guilt is not that it condemns a man, but that it leaves him with nothing left to accuse except himself.
posts.text:
I have begun to
suspect that the
most terrible thing
about guilt is not that
it condemns a man,

but that it leaves
him with nothing
left to accuse except
himself.
posts.explanation: The writer has started to think the worst thing about guilt is not that it judges a man. It is that it leaves him with no one to blame but himself.

posts.caption: Yes they did hold
posts.displayTitle: There are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved
posts.altText: There are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved, and then there is cutting your hair off. Yes, it held a lot of memories.
posts.text:
There are ways to let go,
there are ways to show
how much you loved,

and then there is
cutting your hair off.
Yes, it held a
lot of memories.
posts.explanation: The writer says there are many ways to let go of someone and to show how much you loved them. He cut his hair off, because that hair carried a lot of memories.

posts.caption: There will be no you in it
posts.displayTitle: I realised i didn't have insomnia at all it was just lack of love
posts.altText: I realised i didn't have insomnia at all it was just lack of love when I closed my eyes, uncertainty that, when I close my eyes there will be no you in it, there will be no you in it..
posts.text:
I realised i didn't
have insomnia at all
it was just
lack of love
when I closed my eyes,

uncertainty that,
when I close my eyes
there will be no you in it,
there will be no you in it..
posts.explanation: The writer thought he had trouble sleeping, but it was not an illness. He could not sleep because he felt a lack of love, and he was afraid that when he closed his eyes, the person he loves would not be there anymore.

posts.caption: How can I not?
posts.displayTitle: Between your heart and mine lies an unbridgeable distance
posts.altText: Between your heart and mine lies an unbridgeable distance, somewhere along it, I am lost. But how can I stop admiring you when you are all that my heart desires?
posts.text:
Between your heart and mine
lies an unbridgeable distance,
somewhere along it,
I am lost.
But how can I stop
admiring you when you
are all that my heart desires?
posts.explanation: The writer feels a huge distance between his heart and the heart of the person he loves, too big to ever cross, and he feels lost in it. Still, he cannot stop admiring that person, because they are all his heart wants.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: There is a peculiar dignity in destruction when it was earned by cari…
posts.altText: There is a peculiar dignity in destruction when it was earned by caring too deeply. For what is more tragic to leave blood upon the earth because you held on too long, or to leave none at all because you never dared to hold anything close?
posts.text:
There is a peculiar dignity
in destruction when it was
earned by caring too deeply.

For what is more tragic
to leave blood upon the
earth because you held
on too long,

or to leave none at all
because you never dared
to hold anything close?
posts.explanation: The writer says there is something to respect in being hurt because you cared too much. He asks which is sadder: being torn up because you held on too long, or never being hurt because you never dared to get close to anything.

posts.caption: Hello
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us
posts.altText: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us. Perhaps we cling to it because it is the last hope that cannot be taken away without taking us with it.
posts.text:
Perhaps we do not
cling to our suffering
because it is dear
to us.

Perhaps we cling
to it because it is
the last hope that
cannot be taken away
without taking us with it.

(now read the
underlined part)
posts.explanation: The writer thinks we don't hold on to our pain because we love it. We hold on because it is our last hope, and it cannot be taken without taking us too. The last line points to a hidden message in underlined words.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: the greatest love is the one that does not bounds itself for possessi…
posts.altText: the greatest love is the one that does not bounds itself for possession. For there is a peculiar tragedy in belonging the hunger that once made us reach so desperately often dies the moment our hands finally close around what they desired.
posts.text:
the greatest love is the
one that does not bounds
itself for possession.

For there is a peculiar
tragedy in belonging
the hunger that once made
us reach so desperately
often dies the moment our
hands finally close around
what they desired.
posts.explanation: The writer says the greatest love does not try to own the other person. The sad thing about having someone is that the strong wish that pulled you to them often fades the moment you finally have them.

posts.caption: Endless grief I am
posts.displayTitle: Grief, grief and an endless ocean of it—
posts.altText: Grief, grief and an endless ocean of it— so much of it that I am unable to tell any of it, I drown every night in the endless depth of the unseen regrets I have, endless grief I am— now I get confused is it me or the grief?
posts.text:
Grief, grief and an endless ocean of it—

so much of it that I am unable to tell any of it,

I drown every night in the endless
depth of the unseen regrets I have,

endless grief I am—

now I get confused is it me or the grief?
posts.explanation: The writer is so full of sadness that he cannot even put it into words. Every night he sinks into hidden regrets, and the grief has become so much a part of him that he can no longer tell himself and the grief apart.

posts.caption: More dead than alive
posts.displayTitle: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me
posts.altText: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me, I die everyday a little more than yesterday, Perhaps I am more dead than alive each passing day..
posts.text:
Grief, chaos, and an endless noise
of things that rots within me,

I die everyday a little more than yesterday,

Perhaps I am more dead than alive
each passing day..
posts.explanation: The writer is full of grief, mess and noise, like something rotting inside him. He feels a little more of him dies each day, until he seems more dead than alive.

posts.caption: You won't know it..
posts.displayTitle: there are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved
posts.altText: there are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved, and then there is cutting your hair off to show how much you did. yes, it held alot of memories.
posts.text:
there are ways to let go,
there are ways
to show how much
you loved,

and then there is
cutting your hair off
to show how much
you did. yes, it held
alot of memories.
posts.explanation: The writer says there are many ways to let go and to show how much you loved someone. He cut his hair off to show how much he loved, because that hair held many memories.

posts.caption: Permanence
posts.displayTitle: Any place where you stay for long becomes your home
posts.altText: Any place where you stay for long becomes your home, Some places Dont ask you to stay, Only to rest for a while, Enough to let the storm calm down.. It can be anywhere, even a person, even a heart, even a presence, even a feeling. Do not mistake it for permanence...
posts.text:
Any place where you stay for long
becames your home,

Some places Dont ask you to stay,
Only to rest for a while,

Enough to let the storm calm down..

It can be anywhere, even a person, even a heart,
even a presence, even a feeling.

Do not mistake it for permanence...
posts.explanation: The writer says any place you stay in long becomes home. But some places, even a person or a feeling, only let you rest for a while until your troubles calm down. He says not to think they will last forever.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: But just when you believe life has exhausted all its cruelties
posts.altText: But just when you believe life has exhausted all its cruelties, it comes with another to ruin you in a different way. What is peace, if not merely an interval between one catastrophe and another?
posts.text:
But just when you believe
life has exhausted
all its cruelties,
it comes with another to
ruin you in a different way.

What is peace,
if not merely an
interval between one
catastrophe and another?
posts.explanation: The writer says that just when you think life has no more ways to hurt you, it finds a new one. He wonders if peace is only a short break between one disaster and the next.

posts.caption: Seep
posts.displayTitle: When love seeps into my veins and reaches through the bone
posts.altText: "When love seeps into my veins and reaches through the bone, it will merge itself YOU with my soul, and through the veins, it will be carried to my heart, and all they will hear through my heartbeat will be your name."
posts.text:
"When love seeps into my veins
and reaches through the bone,
it will merge itself
with my soul,
and through the veins,
it will be carried to my heart,
and all they will hear through
my heartbeat will be your name."
posts.explanation: The writer says love will soak into him so deeply, through his blood, his bones and his soul, that it will reach his heart. Then every heartbeat will sound like the name of the person he loves.

posts.caption: After you
posts.displayTitle: Unfortunately after you everything was going well when I thought it w…
posts.altText: Unfortunately after you everything was going well when I thought it wouldn't. But some how my heart still remembers what you gave to it I still ache for you that's the biggest tragedy.
posts.text:
Unfortunately after you
everything was going
well when I thought
it wouldn't.

But some how my heart
still remembers what
you gave to it I still ache
for you that's
the biggest tragedy.
posts.explanation: After the person left, the writer's life went well, even though he expected it would not. Still, his heart remembers what that person gave it, and he still longs for them. To him, that longing is the saddest part.

posts.caption: I would peel my heart
posts.displayTitle: Tragedy is, Like oranges i would peel my heart out to you too
posts.altText: Tragedy is, Like oranges i would peel my heart out to you too. But like my heart you would never keep eat them too. But yet foolishness of love never made me realise that the peels you loved so much were always to spray the citrus into my eyes. I am blind in love now.
posts.text:
Tragedy is, Like oranges
i would peel
my heart out to you too.

But like my heart
you would never
keep ~~eat~~ them too.

But yet foolishness of love
never made me realise that
the peels you loved so much
were always to spray
the citrus into my eyes.

I am blind ~~in love~~ now.
posts.explanation: The writer opened his heart to the person he loved, the way you peel an orange for someone. But that person never kept it, and the parts they liked were only used to hurt him. Love kept him from seeing it, and now he is blinded, by pain and by love.

posts.caption: There are ways
posts.displayTitle: There are ways people survive after love
posts.altText: There are ways people survive after love. I think it's only two strangers learning how to share the same body without actually sharing one. One still waits at a door that will never open. The other has already started walking home.
posts.text:
There are ways people
survive after love.
I think it's only two
strangers learning how
to share the same body
without actually sharing one.

One still waits at a
door that will never open.
The other has already
started walking home.
posts.explanation: He seems to say that after love ends, it is like two strangers living in one body. One part still waits at a door that will never open, while the other part has already started moving on.

posts.caption: I am
posts.displayTitle: Somewhere along the way, I stopped becoming myself
posts.altText: Somewhere along the way, I stopped becoming myself. I am what I was never meant to be. I am what I was left with.
posts.text:
Somewhere
along the way,
I stopped becoming myself.

I am what
I was never
meant to be.
I am what
I was left with.
posts.explanation: The writer says that at some point he stopped being his true self. Now he is someone he was never supposed to be, just what was left of him after everything that happened.

posts.caption: Mother
posts.displayTitle: Mother, I have been hiding myself
posts.altText: Mother, I have been hiding myself. But you looked at my face and knew something was wrong with me. No one else noticed. Only you.
posts.text:
Mother,
I have been hiding
myself. But you looked
at my face

and knew something
was wrong with me.
No one else noticed.
Only you.
posts.explanation: The writer had been hiding his pain from everyone. His mother looked at his face and knew something was wrong, and she was the only one who noticed.

posts.caption: Way to hell
posts.displayTitle: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire
posts.altText: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire thinking your name was another word for heaven. and maybe that is the tragedy of my heart, that even destruction felt beautiful as long as it arrived wearing your face.
posts.text:
If loving YOU
was a way to hell then
I would walk
into the fire thinking
your name was another
word for heaven.

and maybe that is
the tragedy of my heart,
that even destruction felt
beautiful as long as it
arrived wearing your face.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving this person led to hell, he would walk into the fire believing their name meant heaven. That is the sad part of his heart: even being destroyed felt beautiful, as long as it came looking like the person he loved.

posts.caption: Smile
posts.displayTitle: There are certain people whom you can know by my smiles
posts.altText: There are certain people whom you can know by my smiles because behind every smile I still carry a fragment of their existence
posts.text:
There are certain
people whom you
can know
by my smiles

because behind
every smile I still
carry a fragment
of their existence
posts.explanation: The writer says some people still live on in his smiles. Every time he smiles, he carries a small piece of them, so you could know those people just by watching him smile.

posts.caption: Plucked
posts.displayTitle: Flowers aren't meant to be plucked
posts.altText: Flowers aren't meant to be plucked. But who am I to say that, when I was the one who plucked my own happiness every time it came alive?
posts.text:
Flowers aren't
meant to be plucked.

But who am
I to say that,
when I was the one
who plucked my
own happiness every
time it came alive?
posts.explanation: The writer says flowers should not be picked. But he feels he has no right to say that, because every time happiness started to grow in his life, he was the one who killed it.

posts.caption: God
posts.displayTitle: Your presence was a devotion to me
posts.altText: Your presence was a devotion to me. Your absence turned it into a religion, and somehow, I still worship, as if my God would finally hear me.
posts.text:
Your presence was a
devotion to me.

Your absence turned
it into a religion,
and somehow,

I still worship,

as if my God
would finally hear me.
posts.explanation: When this person was near, the writer was deeply devoted to them. After they left, that love grew into something like a religion, and he still worships them, hoping, as with a god, that they will finally hear him.

posts.caption: Endurance
posts.displayTitle: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young…
posts.altText: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young age, to see yourself trapped. Some wounds don't bleed they grow roots inside you, turning your heart into a battlefield you walk through every day. And sometimes the cruelest part of suffering is realising you learned endurance before you ever learned joy.
posts.text:
You won't understand what it means
to be abandoned by hope at a young age—
to see yourself trapped.

Some wounds don't bleed
they grow roots inside you,

turning your heart into a battlefield
you walk through every day.

And sometimes the cruelest part of suffering
is realising you learned endurance
before you ever learned joy.
posts.explanation: The writer says others cannot understand losing hope while still young and feeling stuck. Some hurts do not show but grow deep inside, so every day feels like a fight. The saddest part is learning to put up with pain before ever learning to be happy.

posts.caption: Cruelty
posts.displayTitle: There's a cruelty in writing your name and forgetting what to write a…
posts.altText: There's a cruelty in writing your name and forgetting what to write after it. "Perhaps love was never the words I wrote." Perhaps it was always your name.
posts.text:
There's a cruelty in
writing your name
and forgetting what
to write after it.

"Perhaps love was
never the words
I wrote."
Perhaps it was always
your name.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it painful to write her name and then not know what to write next. He thinks maybe love was never in the words he wrote, but only in her name itself.

posts.caption: I hope it doesn't
posts.displayTitle: If loving me comes with a cost then I hope it's not love
posts.altText: If loving me comes with a cost then I hope it's not love. Because my love was never meant to be felt like something you had to pay for.
posts.text:
If loving me
comes with a cost
then I hope
it's not love

Because my love
was never meant
to be felt like
something you had
to pay for.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving him feels like it costs something, he hopes that is not really his love. His love was never meant to feel like a price someone has to pay.

posts.caption: Living
posts.displayTitle: Living ofcourse is merely an act letting go
posts.altText: Living ofcourse is merely an act letting go. Even your breath, even your love.
posts.text:
Living ofcourse
is merely an act
letting go.
Even your breath,
even your love.
posts.explanation: The writer says living is really just letting go, again and again. We let go of every breath, and we let go of love too.

posts.caption: Maybe mind does it for survival
posts.displayTitle: They say what cannot be forgotten comes to your dreams
posts.altText: They say what cannot be forgotten comes to your dreams, maybe it's true, because the ache of losing what you once believed was yours is far beyond what words can explain. Maybe to soothe that pain, the mind projects it into our dreams, letting us live with what we lost for eternity.
posts.text:
They say what cannot be forgotten
comes to your dreams,

maybe it's true,
because the ache of losing what you once believed
was yours is far beyond what words can explain.
Maybe to soothe that pain,
the mind projects it into our dreams,

letting us live with what we lost for eternity.
posts.explanation: The writer says the things we cannot forget come back in our dreams. Losing something you believed was yours hurts beyond words, so perhaps the mind shows it in dreams to ease the pain, letting us keep living with what we lost forever.

posts.caption: I wonder
posts.displayTitle: There were endless possibilities but life chose to do us apart
posts.altText: There were endless possibilities but life chose to do us apart, i wonder how, i wonder why.
posts.text:
There were endless
possibilities
but life chose
to do us apart ,

i wonder how,
i wonder why.
posts.explanation: The writer says he and someone else could have had many different futures together, but life pulled them apart. He keeps wondering how and why it happened.

posts.caption: I weep
posts.displayTitle: Every time I cry, my tears begin to shape you
posts.altText: Every time I cry, my tears begin to shape you from the traces you left behind, so that the next time I miss you, I can look upon them and find another reason to weep.
posts.text:
Every time I cry,
my tears begin to shape you

from the traces you left behind,
so that the next time I miss you,

I can look upon them
and find another reason to weep.
posts.explanation: Each time the writer cries, his tears seem to build a picture of the person he lost from what they left behind. So the next time he misses them, he has one more reason to cry.

posts.caption: Grief like skin
posts.displayTitle: I carry grief like a second skin, stitched into everything I do
posts.altText: I carry grief like a second skin, stitched into everything I do. There are days I laugh so naturally that it feels like I am betraying this skin of grief I have too.
posts.text:
I carry grief like
a second skin,
stitched into
everything I do.

There are days
I laugh so naturally
that it feels like
I am betraying this
skin of grief I have too.
posts.explanation: The writer says grief is part of him, like a second skin that touches everything he does. On days he laughs easily, he feels guilty, as if being happy is turning his back on his grief.

posts.caption: Shit government
posts.displayTitle: The most dangerous thieves don't wear masks, they wear authority
posts.altText: The most dangerous thieves don't wear masks, they wear authority.
posts.text:
The most
dangerous thieves
don't wear
masks, they wear
authority.
posts.explanation: The writer says the most dangerous people who steal do not hide behind masks. They are the ones in power, who take from others openly.

posts.caption: Please god
posts.displayTitle: if there is a God listening beyond all this silence
posts.altText: if there is a God listening beyond all this silence, then let Him forgive me for having loved this life so painfully, even when it gave me every reason not to. I am the sin I am the sinner
posts.text:
if there is a God
listening beyond all this silence,
then let Him forgive me
for having loved this life
so painfully,

even when it gave me
every reason not to.
I am the sin
I am the sinner
posts.explanation: The writer says that if God is out there listening past all the silence, he hopes God will forgive him for loving this life so painfully, even though life gave him every reason not to. He feels he is both the wrong and the one who did it.

posts.caption: Living is waiting
posts.displayTitle: My mother says there are some people you should never wait for
posts.altText: My mother says there are some people you should never wait for. I smile, because she doesn't know that my entire way of living is waiting.
posts.text:
My mother says
there are some people
you should never
wait for.

I smile, because
she doesn't know
that my entire way of
living is waiting.
posts.explanation: The writer's mother tells him some people are not worth waiting for. He smiles, because she does not know that his whole life has become waiting.

posts.caption: Ladder
posts.displayTitle: The spine is a strange thing like a ladder built inside us
posts.altText: The spine is a strange thing like a ladder built inside us so that someday memory may climb to our throat and die there, unable to become a language.
posts.text:
The spine is
a strange thing
like a ladder
built inside us

so that someday
memory may climb
to our throat
and die there,
unable to become
a language.
posts.explanation: The writer pictures the backbone as a ladder inside the body. Memories climb it up to the throat, but get stuck there and die, because they can never be turned into words.

posts.caption: Water shows your reflection
posts.displayTitle: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does
posts.altText: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does. I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection, but even the reflection shows your face. I wonder why it shows you when you were the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.text:
The rain always knows when to stop.
My grief never does.

I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection,
but even the reflection shows your face.

I wonder why it shows you when you were
the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.explanation: The writer says rain knows when to stop, but his grief does not. When he looks at his reflection in a puddle, he sees the face of the person he lost, and wonders why, since that person left him alone in his hard times.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar.
posts.altText: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar. Is it because living is merely the slow act of leaving behind everything we have loved our whole lives, or because to leave is, in its own cruel way, to love? Or is it because they knew we would lose everything we ever loved? Because I am still trying to understand why you left.
posts.text:
I wonder why leaving and living
sound so similar.
Is it because living is merely
the slow act of leaving
behind everything we have loved
our whole lives,
or because to leave is,
in its own cruel way, to love?
Or is it because they knew we would
lose everything we ever loved?
Because I am still trying
to understand why you left.
posts.explanation: The writer notices that leaving and living sound almost the same. He wonders if living is just slowly leaving behind everyone we love, or if leaving is a hard kind of love. Under it all, he is still trying to understand why the person he loved left.

posts.caption: It shows you
posts.displayTitle: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does
posts.altText: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does. I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection, but even the reflection shows your face. I wonder why it shows you when you were the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.text:
The rain always knows when to stop.
My grief never does.

I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection,
but even the reflection shows your face.

I wonder why it shows you when you were
the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.explanation: The writer says rain knows when to stop, but his grief does not. When he looks at his reflection in a puddle, he sees the face of the person he lost, and wonders why, since that person left him alone in his hard times.

posts.caption: Oh love too..
posts.displayTitle: If there is a God inside the human body, He abandoned mine long ago
posts.altText: If there is a God inside the human body, He abandoned mine long ago. All that remains is a cathedral like empty chest, full of abandonment, where my thoughts kneel every night, praying to a saint who has forgotten the language of mercy. oh, and love too.
posts.text:
If there is a God
inside the human body,
He abandoned
mine long ago.
All that remains
is a cathedral like
empty chest,
full of abandonment,

where my thoughts kneel every night,
praying to a saint who has forgotten
the language of mercy. oh, and love too.
posts.explanation: The writer feels that if God lives inside people, God left him long ago. His chest feels like an empty church, and every night his thoughts pray to someone who no longer shows kindness, or love.

posts.caption: Heart
posts.displayTitle: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent…
posts.altText: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent in loss, yet I remember the exact silence that settled between my heart and you before you left. I remember the weight of the air, the way the world was silent, as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.text:
I have forgotten
the language my heart
spoke before it became
fluent in loss,
yet I remember the exact
silence that settled
between my heart and you
before you left.
I remember the weight of the air,
the way the world was silent,
as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.explanation: The writer has forgotten how his heart felt before it was full of loss. But he clearly remembers the silence between him and the person just before they left, how heavy the air felt, and how quiet the world was while his heart was screaming inside.

posts.caption: If only
posts.displayTitle: But every now and then, your memories rush into me
posts.altText: But every now and then, your memories rush into me. Then I hear things collapsing inside me, i wonder what tragedy you left me into, That I never collapsed at once just piece by piece, weathering. perhaps I have spent my whole life arriving too late to rescue myself, if only i had come a little sooner, i could have saved it all.
posts.text:
But every now and then,
your memories rush into me.
Then I hear things
collapsing inside me,
i wonder what tragedy
you left me into,
That I never collapsed at once
just peice by peice, Weathering.
perhaps I have spent my whole
life arriving too late to rescue myself,
if only i had come a little sooner,
i could have saved it all.
posts.explanation: Sometimes memories of the person flood back, and the writer feels himself breaking inside. He did not fall apart all at once, but slowly, bit by bit, over time. He feels he has always come too late to save himself, and wishes he had come sooner.

posts.caption: Language of heart
posts.displayTitle: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent…
posts.altText: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent in loss, yet I remember the exact silence that settled between my heart and you before you left. I remember the weight of the air, the way the world was silent, as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.text:
I have forgotten
the language my heart
spoke before it became
fluent in loss,
yet I remember the exact
silence that settled
between my heart and you
before you left.
I remember the weight of the air,
the way the world was silent,
as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.explanation: The writer has forgotten how his heart felt before it was full of loss. But he clearly remembers the silence between him and the person just before they left, how heavy the air felt, and how quiet the world was while his heart was screaming inside.

posts.caption: Abandonment
posts.displayTitle: I used to think poison kills
posts.altText: I used to think poison kills. Then I met your memories that arrive as comfort, speak like home, and leave, that you mistake the abandonment, slowly, for your own heartbeat. You know, the cruelest poisons are not the ones that stop your heart. They are the ones that teach it to survive on what is killing it.
posts.text:
I used to think poison kills.
Then I met your memories
that arrive as comfort,
speaks like home, and leaves,
that you mistake the
abandonment, slowly,
for your own heartbeat.

You know, the cruelest poisons are
not the ones that stop your heart.
They are the ones that teach it
to survive on what is killing it.
posts.explanation: The writer once thought only poison could kill. But memories of the lost person feel like comfort and home, until being left alone feels as normal as his own heartbeat. He says the worst poison does not stop your heart; it teaches it to keep living on what is hurting it.

posts.caption: Love
posts.displayTitle: If loving me comes with a cost then I hope it's not love
posts.altText: If loving me comes with a cost then I hope it's not love. Because my love was never meant to be felt like something you had to pay for.
posts.text:
If loving me
comes with a cost
then I hope
it's not love

Because my love
was never meant
to be felt like
something you had
to pay for.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving him feels like it costs something, he hopes that is not really his love. His love was never meant to feel like a price someone has to pay.

posts.caption: How can I be?
posts.displayTitle: I have left a piece of myself in everything I have loved
posts.altText: I have left a piece of myself in everything I have loved, and here I stand before myself, with nothing left inside me. My heart aches to be full again but how can I full again without being a fool again? I am too understanding now to be fooled again to be full with emotions again.
posts.text:
I have left a piece of myself
in everything I have loved,

And here I stand before myself,
with nothing left inside me.

My heart aches to be full again but how can
I full again without being a fool again?

I am too understanding now to be
fooled again to be full with emotions again.
posts.explanation: The writer has left a part of himself in everything he loved, and now he feels empty inside. He wants to feel full again, but he fears that means being fooled again, and he understands too much now to let himself be fooled.

posts.caption: Silence
posts.displayTitle: Someone once taught me that there is a strange kind of violence in si…
posts.altText: Someone once taught me that there is a strange kind of violence in silence, the kind that leaves you hanging between an unfinished story and a thousand unanswered paradoxes. A silence that doesn't break, doesn't explain, doesn't close the chapter, it just leaves you suspended in the ache of not knowing. Maybe that's why silence feels less like peace and more like a punishment.
posts.text:
Someone once taught me that there
is a strange kind of violence in silence,

the kind that leaves you hanging between an
unfinished story and a thousand unanswered paradoxes

A silence that doesn't break,
doesn't explain,
doesn't close the chapter,
it just leaves you suspended in
the ache of not knowing.

Maybe that's why silence feels less like
peace and more like a punishment.
posts.explanation: The writer says silence can hurt like violence. When someone goes quiet without explaining or ending things, you are left stuck, not knowing what happened. So silence feels less like peace and more like a punishment.

posts.caption: Nails
posts.displayTitle: I wonder why nails grow beneath the grave too
posts.altText: I wonder why nails grow beneath the grave too. Is it because even after everything ends, things still find a way to grow? I think it is a universal law that nothing ends when it truly does. Thus, my love for you.
posts.text:
I wonder why
nails grow beneath
the grave too.
Is it because even
after everything ends,
things still find
a way to grow?
I think it is a universal law
that nothing ends when it truly does.
Thus, my love for you.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders why nails keep growing even in the grave. He takes it to mean that even after things end, something still grows. His love for the person is like that: it keeps going even though it is over.

posts.caption:
A surprise theme. Fifty hours. One story.
Excited to be a part of the IFP 50 Hour Writing Challenge.
Use IFPTRIYAN2107 to get 20% off.
posts.displayTitle: Nobody tells you this about writing.
posts.altText: Nobody tells you this about writing. People think writing begins with inspiration. It doesn't. It begins with sitting in front of an empty page with undissolved feelings that refuses to love you back. Most people don't quit because they aren't talented. They quit because they forget what writing means to them.
posts.text:
Nobody tells you
this about writing.
---
People think writing
begins with inspiration.
It doesn't.

It begins with sitting
in front of an empty page
with undissolved feelings
that refuses to
love you back.
---
Most people don't quit
because they aren't talented.
They quit because they
forget what writing
means to them.

Every writer has a drawer
full of unfinished stories,
each one abandoned the
day they stopped believing
it deserved to be finished.
---
And for this particular reason
I'm taking the IFP 50 Hour
Writing Challenge to remind
myself that writing is
still a part of me.
It begins with a surprise theme,
and you have just 50 hours to
turn it into a finished piece.

If writing has been waiting for you,
maybe this is the sign you've been
looking for. don't let your words die
let it flow!
---
Use my code
IFPTRIYAN2107
to get 20% off
posts.explanation: The writer says writing does not start with a sudden great idea but with facing an empty page and heavy feelings, and people quit when they forget what it means to them. He is joining the IFP 50 Hour Writing Challenge to remind himself he still writes, and gives a code for 20% off.

posts.caption: It's august now
posts.displayTitle: It's August now, and I wonder how you've been
