posts.altText: It's August now, and I wonder how you've been. I wonder whether you've eaten today or not. I am no longer close enough to ask, but then I wonder— How far apart can two people truly be after having shared so much of themselves?
posts.text:
It's August now,
and I wonder how you've been.
I wonder whether you've
eaten today or not.
I am no longer close enough to ask,
but then I wonder—
How far apart can two people truly be
after having shared so much of themselves?
posts.explanation: It is August, and the writer wonders how a person he was once close to is doing, even whether they have eaten today. He is no longer close enough to ask, but he wonders how two people who shared so much can ever be truly far apart.

posts.caption: Original words do not copy without permission
posts.displayTitle: tears will tear you.
posts.altText: tears will tear you.
posts.text: tears will tear you.
posts.explanation: The writer says that crying from sadness, if it goes on, will rip you apart inside.

posts.caption: Consequence
posts.displayTitle: perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
posts.altText: perhaps the cruelest realization is this— that most people do not intend to hurt you. They simply choose themselves in moments where you hoped they would choose you. And that difference, so small in action, becomes immeasurable in consequence.
posts.text:
perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
that most people do not intend to hurt you.

They simply choose themselves in moments
where you hoped they would choose you
And that difference,
so small in action,
becomes immeasurable in consequence.
posts.explanation: The writer says the hardest thing to accept is that most people do not mean to hurt you. They just pick themselves at the moments you hoped they would pick you, and that small choice ends up hurting more than can be measured.

posts.caption: Friendship day
posts.displayTitle: My existence in the lives of others has always been measured by the…
posts.altText: My existence in the lives of others has always been measured by the weight of what I could offer. Once their need for me faded, so did my place in their world.
posts.text:
My existence in the lives of others
has always been measured by the

weight of what I could offer.

Once their need for me faded,
so did my place in their world.
posts.explanation: The writer feels people only valued him for what he could give them. When they no longer needed him, they no longer kept a place for him in their lives.

posts.caption: You did
posts.displayTitle: You happened to me, poetry came much later.
posts.altText: You happened to me, poetry came much later.
posts.text:
You happened to me,
poetry came much later.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person came into his life first, and his poems came only later, because of them.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: Tell me, is it not absurd? To crave permanence in a world that refuse…
posts.altText: Tell me, is it not absurd? To crave permanence in a world that refuses to grant it and yet to sabotage it the moment it dares to appear. There is, within me, a contradiction so profound that I cannot resolve it, I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch, as though kindness itself were a prelude to loss.
posts.text:
Tell me, is it not absurd?

To crave permanence in a world
that refuses to grant it—

and yet to sabotage it
the moment it dares to appear.

There is, within me,

a contradiction so profound
that I cannot resolve it,

I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch,
as though kindness itself were a prelude to loss.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that he wants things to last in a world where nothing does, yet he ruins them as soon as they show up. He longs to be held but tenses up when touched, as if kindness always comes just before a loss.

posts.caption: To love is to live
posts.displayTitle: I know I will be abandoned. Yet still, I pour the glass full of love
posts.altText: I know I will be abandoned. Yet still, I pour the glass full of love. There is a strange beauty in offering abundance to a world that has taught you scarcity. To love is to never cease to exist, to love is to live and give.
posts.text:
I know I will be abandoned.
Yet still,
I pour the glass full of love.

There is a strange beauty in offering abundance
to a world that has taught you scarcity.
To love is to
never cease to exist,
to love is to live and give.
posts.explanation: The writer knows he will be left alone in the end, but he still gives his love fully. He finds something beautiful in giving a lot to a world that has given him little, and believes loving means truly living and giving.

posts.caption: My heart and you
posts.displayTitle: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent…
posts.altText: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent in loss, yet I remember the exact silence that settled between my heart and you before you left. I remember the weight of the air, the way the world was silent, as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.text:
I have forgotten the language my heart
spoke before it became fluent in loss,

yet I remember the exact silence that settled
between my heart and you before you left.

I remember the weight of the air,
the way the world was silent,
as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
posts.explanation: The writer has forgotten how his heart felt before it was full of loss. But he clearly remembers the silence between him and the person just before they left, how heavy the air felt, and how quiet the world was while his heart was screaming inside.

posts.caption: Rope
posts.displayTitle: There's a tight rope of hope that binds me with you!
posts.altText: There's a tight rope of hope that binds me with you! But that rope too is about to tear away just like my heart, just like us. I wonder is it the hope that binds me or just a glimpse of you, again or is it love I wonder...
posts.text:
There's a tight rope of hope
that binds me with you!

But that rope too is about to tear away
just like my heart, just like us.
I wonder is it the hope that binds me
or just a glimpse of you,
again or is it love I wonder....
posts.explanation: The writer feels tied to the person by a thin rope of hope, but that rope is about to break, just like his heart and their bond. He wonders what really holds him there: hope, the wish to see them again, or love.

posts.caption: You and me
posts.displayTitle: You and I are meant to be like parallel lines
posts.altText: You and I are meant to be like parallel lines, cursed forever within sight of one another, forever forbidden from touching. We travel in the same direction, witness the same horizons and yet the universe keeps us apart all the way to infinity.
posts.text:
You and I are meant to be like parallel lines,
cursed forever within sight of one
another, forever forbidden
from touching.
We travel in the same direction,
witness the same horizons and yet
the universe keeps us apart all the
way to infinity.
posts.explanation: The writer says he and the person he loves are like two lines that run side by side forever. They go the same way and see the same things, but they can never meet or touch.

posts.caption: Original words do not copy or reuse
posts.displayTitle: soul is deeper than an abyss.
posts.altText: soul is deeper than an abyss.
posts.text: soul is deeper than an abyss.
posts.explanation: The writer says what is inside a person goes deeper than any bottomless pit.

posts.caption: Grave
posts.displayTitle: The grave was never a piece of land, it was always my heart
posts.altText: The grave was never a piece of land, it was always my heart with all the buried memories. Every time my heart aches, I know there are more memorial corpses being buried alive. What a tragedy it is to hear a requiem with every heartbeat, knowing each pulse is another eulogy for a part of me that has just died.
posts.text:
The grave was never a piece of land, it was
always my heart with all the buried memories.

Every time my heart aches,
I know there are more memorial corpses
being buried alive.
What a tragedy it is to hear
a requiem with every heartbeat,
knowing each pulse is another eulogy
for a part of me that has just died.
posts.explanation: The writer says his heart is the real grave, where his memories are buried. Each time it aches, more memories are buried while still alive, and every heartbeat feels like a funeral song for another part of him that has died.

posts.caption: Original words
posts.displayTitle: tears will tear you.
posts.altText: tears will tear you.
posts.text: tears will tear you.
posts.explanation: The writer says that crying from sadness, if it goes on, will rip you apart inside.

posts.displayTitle: my soul desires to be understood more than it does to be loved.
posts.altText: my soul desires to be understood more than it does to be loved.
posts.text:
my soul desires to be understood
more than it does to be loved.
posts.explanation: The writer wants to be understood even more than he wants to be loved.

posts.caption: Two fates
posts.displayTitle: There are only two fates for a single story it happens, or it never d…
posts.altText: There are only two fates for a single story it happens, or it never does. Everything else is merely the space between those two truths the almost and the what happens, the hands that nearly touch and the hands that are held. But the story never truly ends. Some are lived, some are lost, and some remain suspended on the verge of what could have been of what could have been of u…
posts.text:
There are only two
fates for a single story
it happens,
or it never does.
Everything else is merely the
space between those two truths
the almost and the what happens,
the hands that nearly touch and the hands
that are held. But the story never truly ends.
Some are lived, some are lost, and some
remain suspended on the verge of what could
have been of what could have been of us.
posts.explanation: The writer says a story either happens or it never does, and everything else is the space in between, like two people almost holding hands. Some stories are lived, some are lost, and some, like his story with this person, stay stuck forever at what could have been.

posts.caption: Love
posts.displayTitle: Do I not deserve to be loved?
posts.altText: Do I not deserve to be loved? Or am I so unlovable that love itself detests me for loving it? Do I not deserve to be kept? Or has grief taken a special liking to me that I keep pushing away everything that tries to keep me, love me?
posts.text:
Do I not deserve to be loved?
Or am I so unlovable
that love itself detests me for loving it?
Do I not deserve to be kept?
Or has grief taken a special liking to me
that I keep pushing away
everything that tries to keep me, love me?
posts.explanation: The writer asks if he does not deserve love, or if he is so hard to love that love itself hates him for trying. He asks if he does not deserve to be kept, or if grief likes him so much that he keeps pushing away everyone who tries to love him.

posts.displayTitle: you can feel the loss of something before you've even lost it.
posts.altText: you can feel the loss of something before you've even lost it.
posts.text:
you can feel the loss of something
before you've even lost it.
posts.explanation: The writer says you can start to feel the pain of losing something even before it is actually gone.

posts.caption: Hell in my chest
posts.displayTitle: My forbidden fruit was never an apple it was you
posts.altText: My forbidden fruit was never an apple it was you. I knew that loving you would cost me hell, yet still, I loved you passionately, as if I were meant to reach for you knowing hell means heaven with you. Perhaps that is why temptation tastes so much like grief because I mistook your sweetness for my salvation.
posts.text:
My forbidden fruit
was never an apple
it was you. I knew that
loving you would cost me
hell, yet still, I loved you
passionately, as if I were
meant to reach for you
knowing hell means heaven
with you. Perhaps that is
why temptation tastes so
much like grief because
I mistook your sweetness
for my salvation.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person he loved was like forbidden fruit: something he knew he should not reach for. He loved them anyway, even knowing it would cost him dearly. Now that wanting feels like grief, because he thought their sweetness would save him.

posts.displayTitle: all these acts, all these pretending only to hide how deeply I feel.
posts.altText: all these acts, all these pretending only to hide how deeply I feel.
posts.text:
all these acts, all these pretending
only to hide how deeply I feel.
posts.explanation: The writer says all his acting and pretending is only a way to hide how strongly he feels.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: Some wounds do not bleed, they bloom beneath the skin
posts.altText: Some wounds do not bleed, they bloom beneath the skin. and perhaps that is why some people smile so beautifully, because the flower of grief learned how to wear their face.
posts.text:
Some wounds do not bleed,
they bloom beneath the skin.
and perhaps that is why
some people smile so beautifully,

because the flower of grief
learned how to wear their face.
posts.explanation: The writer says some hurts do not show on the outside; they grow quietly inside a person, like a flower under the skin. That may be why some people have such lovely smiles: their grief has learned to hide behind a happy face.

posts.displayTitle: Being desired isn't the same as being loved.
posts.altText: Being desired isn't the same as being loved.
posts.text:
Being desired isn't the
same as being loved.
posts.explanation: The writer says that someone wanting you is not the same as someone truly loving you.

posts.caption: Flowerz
posts.displayTitle: Strange how love learns to arrive only after absence becomes permanent
posts.altText: Strange how love learns to arrive only after absence becomes permanent, like the flowers on my grave when I didn't even receive one when I was alive, as if a heartbeat matters only once it stops, as if I only mattered when I was dead.
posts.text:
Strange how love learns to arrive
only after absence becomes permanent,
like the flowers on my grave
when I didn't even receive
one when I was alive,
as if a heartbeat matters only once it stops,
as if I only mattered when I was dead.
posts.explanation: The writer says love often shows up only after someone is gone for good. People bring flowers to his grave, though he never got a single flower while alive. It feels as if a person only matters once their heart stops.

posts.caption: Soul
posts.displayTitle: my soul desires to be understood more than it does to be loved
posts.altText: my soul desires to be understood more than it does to be loved.
posts.text:
my soul desires to be understood
more than it does to be loved.
posts.explanation: The writer wants to be understood even more than he wants to be loved.

posts.displayTitle: I return to the fire hoping it won't burn me this time.
posts.altText: I return to the fire hoping it won't burn me this time.
posts.text:
I return to the fire hoping
it won't burn me this time.
posts.explanation: The writer keeps going back to the thing that hurt him before, hoping that this time it will not hurt him again.

posts.caption: I hope
posts.displayTitle: When I'm about to die and my mind begins to project the best moments…
posts.altText: When I'm about to die and my mind begins to project the best moments of my life, I hope it isn't filled with the endless grief I've carried almost all my days. I hope instead it finds you, your hand in mine, And us in the rain. And maybe… it will be kind enough to create a few non existing ones like being loved by my parents.
posts.text:
When I'm about to die and my mind begins to
project the best moments of my life,

I hope it isn't filled with the endless grief
I've carried almost all my days.

I hope instead it finds you,
your hand in mine, And us in the rain.
And maybe...

it will be kind enough to create a few
non existing ones like being loved by my parents.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes that as he dies, the best moments his mind replays will not be his lifelong grief, but the person he loves holding his hand in the rain. Maybe it will even make up moments that never happened, like being loved by his parents.

posts.displayTitle: love, greif, hope, death all while being alive.
posts.altText: love, greif, hope, death all while being alive.
posts.text:
love, greif, hope, death
all while being alive.
posts.explanation: He seems to say that a person goes through love, grief, hope and even something like death, all while still being alive.

posts.caption: Poison
posts.displayTitle: I used to think poison kills
posts.altText: I used to think poison kills. Then I met your memories that arrive as comfort, speaks like home, and leaves, that you mistake the abandonment, slowly, for your own heartbeat. You know, the cruelest poisons are not the ones that stop your heart. They are the ones that teach it to survive on what is killing it.
posts.text:
I used to think poison kills.
Then I met your memories
that arrive as comfort,
speaks like home, and leaves,
that you mistake the
abandonment, slowly,
for your own heartbeat.

You know, the cruelest poisons are
not the ones that stop your heart.
They are the ones that teach it
to survive on what is killing it.
posts.explanation: The writer once thought only poison could kill. But memories of the lost person feel like comfort and home, until being left alone feels as normal as his own heartbeat. He says the worst poison does not stop your heart; it teaches it to keep living on what is hurting it.

posts.caption: Love and loss
posts.displayTitle: I think love and loss go hand in hand
posts.altText: I think love and loss go hand in hand. Because I have lost everyone I have loved. I tell you, the heaviest tears are those which are shed at loss, because you lose yourself too. Parts of you leave because you aren't you anymore, and what you once were never finds its way back to you ever again.
posts.text:
I think love and loss
go hand in hand.

Because I have lost
everyone I have loved.

I tell you, the heaviest tears are those
which are shed at loss, because you lose
yourself too. Parts of you leave because
you aren't you anymore, and what you
once were never finds its way back to you
ever again.
posts.explanation: The writer feels love and loss always come together, since he has lost everyone he loved. He says the tears over a loss are the heaviest because you lose part of yourself too, and the person you were never comes back.

posts.displayTitle: SMOKING KILLS so does love! i know it will kill me so does memories b…
posts.altText: SMOKING KILLS so does love! i know it will kill me so does memories but can you be saved anyway?
posts.text:
so does love!
i know it will kill me
so does memories
but can you be saved anyway?
posts.explanation: The writer says love will destroy him, and so will memories. Even knowing this, he asks whether someone can still be saved.

posts.caption: Weep
posts.displayTitle: Every time I cry, my tears begin to shape you
posts.altText: Every time I cry, my tears begin to shape you from the traces you left behind, so that the next time I miss you, I can look upon them and find another reason to weep.
posts.text:
Every time I cry,
my tears begin to shape you

from the traces you left behind,
so that the next time I miss you,

I can look upon them
and find another reason to weep.
posts.explanation: Each time the writer cries, his tears seem to build a picture of the person he lost from what they left behind. So the next time he misses them, he has one more reason to cry.

posts.displayTitle: Everything you lost will scream through the emptiness it left behind.
posts.altText: Everything you lost will scream through the emptiness it left behind.
posts.text:
Everything you lost will scream
through the emptiness it left behind.
posts.explanation: The writer says everything you lose leaves an empty space behind, and that emptiness keeps loudly reminding you of what is gone.

posts.caption: Rain
posts.displayTitle: The rain always knows when to stop
posts.altText: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does. I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection, but even the reflection shows your face. I wonder why it shows you when you were the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.text:
The rain always knows when to stop.
My grief never does.

I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection,
but even the reflection shows your face.

I wonder why it shows you when you were
the very one who left me standing in the rain.
posts.explanation: The writer says rain knows when to stop, but his grief does not. When he looks at his reflection in a puddle, he sees the face of the person he lost, and wonders why, since that person left him alone in his hard times.

posts.displayTitle: Even heaven would feel hell without you, it's still earth.
posts.altText: Even heaven would feel hell without you, it's still earth.
posts.text:
Even heaven would feel hell
without you, it's still earth.
posts.explanation: The writer says that without the person he loves, even heaven would feel like hell. He seems to say no place could feel special to him without them.

posts.caption: Loving you!
posts.displayTitle: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire think…
posts.altText: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire thinking your name was another word for heaven. and maybe that is the tragedy of my heart, that even destruction felt beautiful as long as it arrived wearing your face.
posts.text:
If loving YOU
was a way to hell then
I would walk
into the fire thinking
your name was another
word for heaven.

and maybe that is
the tragedy of my heart,
that even destruction felt
beautiful as long as it
arrived wearing your face.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving this person led to hell, he would walk into the fire believing their name meant heaven. That is the sad part of his heart: even being destroyed felt beautiful, as long as it came looking like the person he loved.

posts.caption: Graves
posts.displayTitle: I have abandoned countless versions of myself
posts.altText: I have abandoned countless versions of myself just to survive the expectations of others. My past selves are buried inside me alive. Their unrest haunts me still, for I walk each day over the graves I dug with my own hands. It was I who condemned them. It was I who buried them alive.
posts.text:
I have abandoned countless versions of myself
just to survive the expectations of others.
My past selves are buried inside me alive.
Their unrest haunts me still,
for I walk each day over the
graves I dug with my own hands.
It was I who condemned them.
It was I who buried them alive.
posts.explanation: To live up to what others expected, the writer gave up many versions of who he was. Those old selves are still alive inside him, buried, and they trouble him. He walks over their graves every day, knowing he was the one who buried them.

posts.displayTitle: memories don't fade, they feed on you.
posts.altText: memories don't fade, they feed on you.
posts.text: memories don't fade, they feed on you.
posts.explanation: The writer says memories do not slowly go away. Instead, they keep eating away at you.

posts.caption: Angel and demon
posts.displayTitle: What would happen if an angel and a demon fell in love?
posts.altText: What would happen if an angel and a demon fell in love? They would be bound by reality for eternity, punished with the sin of never meeting again. and maybe that is what happened when I fell for an angel, because loving you felt like standing at heaven's gates with hell inside my chest.
posts.text:
What would happen
if an angel and a demon
fell in love?
They would be bound
by reality for eternity,
punished with the sin
of never meeting again.

and maybe that is what
happened when I fell for an angel,
because loving you felt like standing
at heaven's gates with
hell inside my chest.
posts.explanation: The writer imagines an angel and a demon falling in love: they would be punished forever by never meeting again. He feels that is what happened when he loved someone so good, because loving them felt like standing at heaven's door with hell inside his chest.

posts.caption: Abandoned
posts.displayTitle: But where do you return after being Abandoned?
posts.altText: But where do you return after being Abandoned? But where do you return A B A N D O N E D by you. Return but where? I have been abandoned I called you Home. Where does a heart go After being abandoned by H O M E
posts.text:
But where do you return after being Abandoned?
But where do you return
A B A N D O N E D by you
Return but where?
I have been abandoned
I called you Home.
Where does a heart go
After being abandoned by H O M E
posts.explanation: The writer called someone his home, and they left him. He keeps asking where a heart can go when the very place it called home has abandoned it.

posts.displayTitle: nostalgia is grief with a memory
posts.altText: nostalgia is grief with a memory
posts.text: nostalgia is grief with a memory
posts.explanation: The writer says missing the past is really a kind of grief, sadness tied to a memory.

posts.caption: I would do it again
posts.displayTitle: If loving you was a beautiful mistake
posts.altText: If loving you was a beautiful mistake, then I would make it again, knowing exactly where it would lead me. Perhaps that is the tragedy of my heart I never feared being broken as long as the pieces still remembered the shape of you.
posts.text:
If loving you
was a beautiful mistake,
then I would make it again,
knowing exactly where
it would lead me.
Perhaps that is
the tragedy of my heart
I never feared being broken
as long as the pieces
still remembered
the shape of you.
posts.explanation: The writer says loving the person was a beautiful mistake, and he would make it again even knowing how it ends. The sad part is that he never feared being broken, as long as the broken pieces still remembered that person.

posts.caption: Colours
posts.displayTitle: These days the world appears uncannily altered
posts.altText: These days the world appears uncannily altered, as though someone has surreptitiously stole the colour from everything I once found radiant. And they say beauty lies in the eyes of the beholder, but maybe I've become too colourblind to understand its meaning…
posts.text:
These days the world appears uncannily altered,

as though someone has
surreptitiously stole the colour
from everything I once found radiant.

And they say beauty lies
in the eyes of the beholder,
but maybe I've become too
colourblind to understand its meaning...
posts.explanation: The writer says the world now looks strangely different, as if someone secretly took the color out of everything he used to find bright and lovely. People say beauty depends on who is looking, but he fears he can no longer see beauty at all.

posts.displayTitle: We miss what made us miserable.
posts.altText: We miss what made us miserable.
posts.text: We miss what made us miserable.
posts.explanation: The writer says we often miss the very things that made us unhappy.

posts.caption: You never know
posts.displayTitle: Maybe that's my problem
posts.altText: Maybe that's my problem. I would give everything and ask for nothing in return. But there is a peculiar tragedy in giving you never know when the cup has become full, when it has begun to overflow. You never know where generosity ends and self-abandonment begins. You never know where to stop.
posts.text:
Maybe that's my problem.
I would give everything and
ask for nothing in return.
But there is a peculiar
tragedy in giving
you never know when
the cup has become full,
when it has begun to overflow.
You never know where generosity ends
and self-abandonment begins.
You never know where to stop.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks his problem is that he gives everything and asks for nothing back. The sad part of giving is that you can't tell when it is too much, or where being kind ends and losing yourself begins, so you never know when to stop.

posts.caption: When did i?
posts.displayTitle: I have lost my perception of time while waiting for you
posts.altText: I have lost my perception of time while waiting for you. They said time would heal everything, but I lost time, lost to time, lost in time itself… You buried me in it… tell me, what year is it? when did I die?
posts.text:
I have lost my perception of time
while waiting for you.
They said time would heal everything,
but I lost time,
lost to time,
lost in time itself...
You buried me in it... tell me,
what year is it? when did I die?
posts.explanation: While waiting for the person he loved, the writer lost all sense of time. People said time would heal him, but he only got lost in it. He feels as if they buried him in that waiting, and he asks what year it is and when he died.

posts.displayTitle: your absence penetrates the deepest parts of me.
posts.altText: your absence penetrates the deepest parts of me.
posts.text:
your absence penetrates
the deepest parts of me.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person being gone hurts him deep down, in the most hidden parts of him.

posts.caption: Ribs
posts.displayTitle: My rib is a cage that keeps my heart from coming to you
posts.altText: My rib is a cage that keeps my heart from coming to you. What a cruel design to carry the prisoner that longs for you and the prison that keeps it away within the same body.
posts.text:
My rib is a cage
that keeps my heart
from coming to you.

What a cruel design
to carry the prisoner
that longs for you
and the prison that
keeps it away within
the same body.
posts.explanation: The writer says his ribs are like a cage that keeps his heart from going to the person he loves. He finds it cruel that his one body holds both the heart that wants her and the cage that keeps it away.

posts.displayTitle: once your heart turns cold, warmth becomes unbearable.
posts.altText: once your heart turns cold, warmth becomes unbearable.
posts.text:
once your heart turns cold,
warmth becomes unbearable.
posts.explanation: The writer says that once your heart has gone cold from hurt, kindness and love become hard to bear.

posts.caption: Strange
posts.displayTitle: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it.
posts.altText: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it. Perhaps some desires are not born from love at all. Perhaps they are born from our inability to let beautiful things remain free.
posts.text:
What a strange thing
it is to admire a flower,
then wish to pluck it.

Perhaps some desires are
not born from love at all.
Perhaps they are born
from our inability to let
beautiful things remain free.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that we see a beautiful flower and then want to pick it. He thinks some wants don't come from love at all, but from not being able to let beautiful things stay free.

posts.displayTitle: I saw the moon in your eyes, but never a place for myself in it.
posts.altText: I saw the moon in your eyes, but never a place for myself in it.
posts.text:
I saw the moon in your eyes,
but never a place for myself in it.
posts.explanation: The writer saw beauty and light in the person's eyes, but never saw any room for himself there.

posts.caption: I just do
posts.displayTitle: I die when I have to pretend
posts.altText: I die when I have to pretend that your absence does not hurt. I die when I see you happy and realise I am no longer part of it. I die when I almost tell you how much I miss you then remember you stopped asking.
posts.text:
I die when
I have to pretend
that your absence
does not hurt.
I die when
I see you happy
and realise I am no
longer part of it.

I die when I almost tell you
how much I miss you then
remember you stopped asking.
posts.explanation: The writer feels like he dies inside when he has to pretend the person being gone does not hurt, and when he sees them happy without him. It hurts most when he almost tells them he misses them, then remembers they stopped asking about him.

posts.displayTitle: love is a prelude to loss
posts.altText: love is a prelude to loss
posts.text: love is a prelude to loss
posts.explanation: The writer says love always comes before loss, as if loving something is the first step to losing it.

posts.caption: No one is
posts.displayTitle: The child longs to become an adult
posts.altText: The child longs to become an adult. The adult longs for his childhood again. The lonely pray for love. The loved mourn who they were before it. No one is truly happy because we spend our lives chasing what is absent, only to realise we abandoned what was already ours.
posts.text:
The child longs
to become an adult.
The adult longs
for his childhood again.
The lonely pray for love.
The loved mourn
who they were before it.
No one is truly happy
because we spend our lives
chasing what is absent,
only to realise we
abandoned what was
already ours.
posts.explanation: The writer says people always want what they don't have: children want to grow up, adults miss being children, lonely people want love, and people in love miss who they were before. No one is fully happy, because we chase what is missing and leave behind what we already had.

posts.displayTitle: After love, you start killing it.
posts.altText: After love, you start killing it.
posts.text:
After love,
you start killing it.
posts.explanation: The writer seems to say that once love has come, people slowly start to destroy it themselves.

posts.caption: If there is any
posts.displayTitle: If there is a God inside the human body, He abandoned mine long ago
posts.altText: If there is a God inside the human body, He abandoned mine long ago. All that remains is a cathedral like empty chest, full of abandonment, where my thoughts kneel every night, praying to a saint who has forgotten the language of mercy. oh, and love too.
posts.text:
If there is a God
inside the human body,
He abandoned
mine long ago.
All that remains
is a cathedral like
empty chest,
full of abandonment,

where my thoughts kneel every night,
praying to a saint who has forgotten
the language of mercy. oh, and love too.
posts.explanation: The writer feels that if God lives inside people, God left him long ago. His chest feels like an empty church, and every night his thoughts pray to someone who no longer shows kindness, or love.

posts.displayTitle: All the love lying inside me, Only to become heartless.
posts.altText: All the love lying inside me, Only to become heartless.
posts.text:
All the love lying inside me,
Only to become heartless.
posts.explanation: The writer has so much love inside him, but in the end it has only left him cold and without feeling.

posts.caption: Leaving and living
posts.displayTitle: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar
posts.altText: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar. Is it because living is merely the slow act of leaving behind everything we have loved our whole lives, or because to leave is, in its own cruel way, to love? Or is it because they knew we would lose everything we ever loved? Because I am still trying to understand why you left.
posts.text:
I wonder why leaving and living
sound so similar.
Is it because living is merely
the slow act of leaving
behind everything we have loved
our whole lives,
or because to leave is,
in its own cruel way, to love?
Or is it because they knew we would
lose everything we ever loved?
Because I am still trying
to understand why you left.
posts.explanation: The writer notices that leaving and living sound almost the same. He wonders if living is just slowly leaving behind everyone we love, or if leaving is a hard kind of love. Under it all, he is still trying to understand why the person he loved left.

posts.caption: Layered
posts.displayTitle: I have divided myself into necessary layers—
posts.altText: I have divided myself into necessary layers— from a certain fear of being seen whole for I have learned that the closer one comes to the center of a man, the more unbearable he is, even to himself… and so I leave something in reserve— hidden even from my own understanding and the fact that the more someone tries to cut open through me, the more they cry…
posts.text:
I have divided myself into necessary layers—

from a certain fear of being seen whole for
I have learned that the closer one comes to
the center of a man, the more unbearable he
is, even to himself...

and so I leave something in reserve—
hidden even from my own understanding

and the fact that the more someone tries to
cut open through me, the more they cry...
posts.explanation: Afraid of being seen completely, the writer has split himself into layers, believing the closer anyone gets to a person's center, the harder he is to bear, even for himself. He hides a part even from himself, and, like with an onion, whoever cuts deeper into him ends up crying.

posts.displayTitle: people who suffer from cold, would starve themselves for warmth.
posts.altText: people who suffer from cold, would starve themselves for warmth.
posts.text:
people who suffer from cold,
would starve themselves for warmth.
posts.explanation: The writer says people who have felt cold for a long time would give up even food just to feel warm. He seems to mean that people without love will give up a lot to get some.

posts.caption: I wonder why
posts.displayTitle: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well
posts.altText: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome, like light entering a house that has forgotten how to open its windows. Like the prayer in an abandoned church that never reaches its God.
posts.text:
Sometimes I wonder,
if sorrow learned my name so well
that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome,
like light entering a house that has
forgotten how to open its windows.
Like the prayer in an abandoned church
that never reaches its God.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders if sadness knows him so well that even happiness feels like an unwanted guest when it comes. He feels like a house that has forgotten how to open its windows to let light in, or a prayer in an empty church that never reaches God.

posts.displayTitle: I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch.
posts.altText: I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch.
posts.text:
I ache to be held, and
yet I stiffen at the touch.
posts.explanation: The writer badly wants someone to hold him, but when someone does touch him, his body tenses up.

posts.caption: If love was
posts.displayTitle: If love was a sin, I would be the deepest kind of sinner,
posts.altText: If love was a sin, I would be the deepest kind of sinner, because my love for you is selfish yet selfless. I would give you everything and yet ask for nothing in return, because if falling out of love after it ends diminishes what it once was, then heaven without it would feel utterly worthless.
posts.text:
If love was a sin,
I would be the deepest
kind of sinner,
because my love for you
is selfish yet selfless.

I would give you everything
and yet ask for nothing in return,
because if falling out of love after it
ends diminishes what it once was,
then heaven without it would
feel utterly worthless.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if love were a sin, he would be the worst sinner, because his love is both selfish and giving. He would give the person everything and want nothing back. To him, even heaven without this love would be worthless.

posts.displayTitle: People choose themselves in the very moment we hoped they would choos…
posts.altText: People choose themselves in the very moment we hoped they would choose us.
posts.text:
People choose themselves in the very
moment we hoped they would choose us.
posts.explanation: The writer says people often put themselves first at the exact moment we were hoping they would choose us.

posts.caption: One must imagine Sisyphus happy!
posts.displayTitle: Maybe the cruelest thing about time is that it doesn't just pass
posts.altText: Maybe the cruelest thing about time is that it doesn't just pass, it makes us pass with it. We lose Days, Days turn into people, people turn into pieces of ourselves, until one day we realise the person who once lived through it all is someone we can no longer return to. Neither the people nor ourselves.
posts.text:
Maybe the cruelest
thing about time is
that it doesn't just pass,
it makes us pass with it.
We lose Days,
Days turn into people,
people turn into pieces of ourselves.

until one day we realise the person
who once lived through it all is someone
we can no longer return to.
Neither the people nor ourselves.
posts.explanation: The writer says time does not just go by; it changes us as it goes. We lose days, those days become people we lost, and those people become parts of us. In the end, we cannot go back to who we were, or to those people.

posts.caption: It's September
posts.displayTitle: It's September again, and I still can't let go
posts.altText: It's September again, and I still can't let go, your memories with the scent of rain and the faint aftertaste of promises. The year is close enough to its ending, but what about us? Tell me, how do I tell this heart full of hope that it was abandoned by the very thing it ached to belong to?
posts.text:
It's September again,
and I still can't let go,
your memories with the scent of rain
and the faint aftertaste of promises.
The year is close enough to its ending,
but what about us? Tell me,
how do I tell this heart full of hope
that it was abandoned by the very thing
it ached to belong to?
posts.explanation: It is September, and the writer still cannot let go. Memories of the person come back with the smell of rain and old promises. The year is nearly over, and he wonders how to tell his hopeful heart that the one it longed to belong to has left it.

posts.displayTitle: i keep pushing away everything that tries to keep me.
posts.altText: i keep pushing away everything that tries to keep me.
posts.text:
i keep pushing away
everything that tries to keep me.
posts.explanation: The writer keeps pushing away every person and thing that tries to hold on to him.

posts.displayTitle: The tragedy of belonging is never finding where you belong.
posts.altText: The tragedy of belonging is never finding where you belong.
posts.text:
The tragedy of belonging is
never finding where you belong.
posts.explanation: The writer says the sad part about wanting to belong is that you may never find the place where you truly fit.

posts.caption: Praying
posts.displayTitle: If loving you was a prayer, then I would pray until your eyes finally…
posts.altText: If loving you was a prayer, then I would pray until your eyes finally gazed upon this filthy soul. There is a strange beauty in praying even after the answer has refused you. You do not stop because you did not receive what you asked for, you pray harder. Perhaps that's exactly how love is…
posts.text:
If loving you
was a prayer,
then I would pray until
your eyes finally gazed
upon this filthy soul.
There is a strange beauty in praying even
after the answer has refused you. You do
not stop because you did not receive what
you asked for, you pray harder. Perhaps
that's exactly how love is you cling to it
despite knowing you can never make it yours.
It's all hope until it's your love.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if loving the person were a prayer, he would keep praying until they finally looked at him, even though he feels unworthy. Like someone who prays harder after the answer is no, he holds on to his love even knowing that person can never be his.

posts.displayTitle: Even the lines on my hand says your name how could I not mistake you…
posts.altText: Even the lines on my hand says your name how could I not mistake you for destiny?
posts.text:
Even the lines on my hand
says your name
how could I not mistake you
for destiny?
posts.explanation: The writer feels the person is so much a part of him that even the lines on his palm seem to spell their name. So it was easy for him to believe, maybe wrongly, that they were meant to be.

posts.caption: Ridiculous
posts.displayTitle: What a ridiculous creature man is
posts.altText: What a ridiculous creature man is, spending half his life longing for what he does not possess and the other half grieving what he has already lost.
posts.text:
What a ridiculous
creature man is.
spending half his life
longing for what he
does not possess

and the other half
grieving what
he has already lost.
posts.explanation: The writer says people are silly: they spend half their life wanting what they don't have, and the other half being sad about what they have lost.

posts.displayTitle: If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood
posts.altText: If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood, I don't know how much difference in color you'll see. But whatever difference remains that difference will be my love for you.
posts.text:
If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood,
I don't know how much difference in color
you'll see. But whatever difference remains
that difference will be my love for you.
posts.explanation: The writer says if you put a red rose next to his blood, you might barely see a difference in color. Whatever small difference there is, that is his love for her.

posts.caption: Oh god
posts.displayTitle: It's not about who stays or who leaves
posts.altText: It's not about who stays or who leaves. It's about for whom you stop in the middle of a prayer just to pray for them as well. Because there are people you stop asking God to bring back, yet you never stop asking God to keep them safe.
posts.text:
It's not about who
stays or who leaves.
It's about for whom
you stop in the middle
of a prayer just to pray
for them as well.

Because there are
people you stop asking
God to bring back,
yet you never stop asking
God to keep them safe.
posts.explanation: The writer says what matters is not who stays or leaves, but who you stop to pray for in the middle of your own prayer. Some people you stop asking God to bring back, but you never stop asking God to keep them safe.

posts.caption: September
posts.displayTitle: September
posts.altText: A photograph of two bare feet in jeans on stone steps beside a tray of small green plants.

posts.caption: Leaving and living
posts.displayTitle: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar
posts.altText: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar. Is it because living is merely the slow act of leaving behind everything we have loved our whole lives, or because to leave is, in its own cruel way, to love? Or is it because they knew we would lose everything we ever loved? Because I am still trying to understand why you left.
posts.text:
I wonder why leaving and living
sound so similar.
Is it because living is merely
the slow act of leaving
behind everything we have loved
our whole lives,
or because to leave is,
in its own cruel way, to love?
Or is it because they knew we would
lose everything we ever loved?
Because I am still trying
to understand why you left.
posts.explanation: The writer notices that leaving and living sound almost the same. He wonders if living is just slowly leaving behind everyone we love, or if leaving is a hard kind of love. Under it all, he is still trying to understand why the person he loved left.

posts.displayTitle: flowers of grief grows beneath my skin.
posts.altText: flowers of grief grows beneath my skin.
posts.text: flowers of grief grows beneath my skin.
posts.explanation: The writer says grief is growing inside him, under his skin, the way flowers grow from the ground.

posts.caption: They don't
posts.displayTitle: There is something strange about memories
posts.altText: There is something strange about memories, about they don't leave, and they don't get replaced. They just sit quietly at the core of your existence, like old clothes you no longer wear but still cannot let go of. Maybe we keep them because letting go would mean admitting that time moved on without us. Or maybe because we're hesitant to let someone else have what once belonged…
posts.text:
There is something strange about memories,
about they don't leave,
and they don't get replaced.
They just sit quietly at the core of your existence,
like old clothes you no longer
wear but still cannot let go of.
Maybe we keep them because letting go would
mean admitting that time moved on without us.
Or maybe because we're hesitant to let
someone else have what once belonged to us.
posts.explanation: The writer says memories never leave and are never replaced. They stay deep inside, like old clothes you no longer wear but cannot throw away. He thinks we keep them because letting go would mean time moved on without us, or because we don't want anyone else to have what was once ours.

posts.caption: Panic attack
posts.displayTitle: They say panic attacks come from nowhere
posts.altText: They say panic attacks come from nowhere but the body usually knows before the mind admits it funny how it senses old memories rushing back breath turns shallow like it's bracing for impact the room stays the same and you wait to settle again.
posts.text:
They say panic attacks come from nowhere
but the body usually knows
before the mind admits it
funny how it senses old memories rushing back
breath turns shallow like it's bracing for impact
the room stays the same
and you wait to settle again
posts.explanation: The writer says panic attacks seem to come from nowhere, but the body often knows first, sensing old memories coming back. Breathing gets short as if getting ready for a hit, and though nothing in the room changes, you just wait to calm down again.

posts.displayTitle: Heaven above my thoughts, A hell beneath my skin.
posts.altText: Heaven above my thoughts, A hell beneath my skin.
posts.text:
Heaven above my thoughts,
A hell beneath my skin.
posts.explanation: The writer says his mind reaches for something peaceful and good, while under his skin he is suffering badly.

posts.displayTitle: Scars on my hand, Bleeds nothing but you.
posts.altText: Scars on my hand, Bleeds nothing but you.
posts.text:
Scars on my hand,
Bleeds nothing but you.
posts.explanation: The writer says the scars on his hand hold nothing but the person he lost; all his pain comes from them.

posts.caption: I rot
posts.displayTitle: I stink of the memories that rot within me
posts.altText: I stink of the memories that rot within me, their decay fermenting beneath the skin of my consciousness, until even maggots refuse to eat what I have become, until forgetting itself becomes impossible, and nothing remains but the rot.
posts.text:
I stink of the
memories that
rot within me,

their decay fermenting beneath
the skin of my consciousness,

until even maggots refuse
to eat what I have become,
until forgetting itself
becomes impossible,
and nothing remains but the rot.
posts.explanation: The writer feels his memories are rotting inside him, so badly that he feels spoiled by them. The rot goes so deep that even maggots would not want him, he can no longer forget, and nothing is left of him but the rot.

posts.displayTitle: I dream of heaven with, a hell inside my chest.
posts.altText: I dream of heaven with, a hell inside my chest.
posts.text:
I dream of heaven with,
A hell inside my chest.
posts.explanation: The writer dreams of a happy, peaceful place, even while his chest feels full of pain.

posts.caption: I hope they do
posts.displayTitle: I hope when your lips meet mine
posts.altText: I hope when your lips meet mine, they'll tell all the stories that we have been hiding from each other. I hope they'll tell how much you have loved me along the way and through all the memories. I hope they'll say that the distance has been unbearable, just like mine would say to yours.
posts.text:
I hope when your
lips meet mine,
they'll tell all the stories
that we have been hiding
from each other.
I hope they'll tell how
much you have loved
me along the way and
through all the memories.
I hope they'll say that the
distance has been unbearable,
just like mine would say to yours.
posts.explanation: The writer hopes that when he and the person kiss, it will say all the things they have kept hidden from each other. He hopes it will show how much the person has loved him, and that being apart has been as painful for them as it was for him.

posts.displayTitle: Memories in my heart burn, like my soul is in purgatory.
posts.altText: Memories in my heart burn, like my soul is in purgatory.
posts.text:
Memories in my heart burn,
like my soul is in purgatory.
posts.explanation: The writer says the memories in his heart burn him, as if his soul is stuck in a place of punishment, waiting between heaven and hell.

posts.caption: Isn't it true?
posts.displayTitle: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us
posts.altText: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us. Isn't it funny how we create our own delusions to survive the grief, because what used to make us happy isn't there to make us smile anymore?
posts.text:
I still think you
love me,
just like I still think
the moon follows us.

Isn't it funny how
we create our own
delusions to survive the grief,
because what used to make
us happy isn't there to
make us smile anymore?
posts.explanation: The writer still believes the person loves him, the same way people believe the moon follows them. He says we tell ourselves untrue things to get through grief, because what once made us happy is gone.

posts.caption: To mother I say
posts.displayTitle: to mother, I say, "I am tired."
posts.altText: to mother, I say, "I am tired." And she looks at me as if she has known all the ways I have been breaking before I ever learned how to call it grief.
posts.text:
to mother, I say,
"I am tired."

And she looks at me
as if she has known
all the ways
I have been breaking
before I ever learned
how to call it grief.
posts.explanation: The writer tells his mother he is tired. She looks at him as if she has always known how he has been breaking inside, even before he knew to call it grief.

posts.caption: I still do
posts.displayTitle: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us
posts.altText: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us. Isn't it funny how we create our own delusions to survive the grief, because what used to make us happy isn't there to make us smile anymore?
posts.text:
I still think you
love me,
just like I still think
the moon follows us.

Isn't it funny how
we create our own
delusions to survive the grief,
because what used to make
us happy isn't there to
make us smile anymore?
posts.explanation: The writer still believes the person loves him, the same way people believe the moon follows them. He says we tell ourselves untrue things to get through grief, because what once made us happy is gone.

posts.displayTitle: Loneliness is a religion of the forsaken, and grief is its only scrip…
posts.altText: Loneliness is a religion of the forsaken, and grief is its only scripture.
posts.text:
Loneliness is a religion of the forsaken,
and grief is its only scripture.
posts.explanation: The writer says loneliness is like a religion for people who have been left behind, and grief is the only holy book it has.

posts.caption: Read the underlined part
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us
posts.altText: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us. Perhaps we cling to it because it is the last hope that cannot be taken away without taking us with it.
posts.text:
Perhaps we do not
cling to our suffering
because it is dear
to us.

Perhaps we cling
to it because it is
the last hope that
cannot be taken away
without taking us with it.
posts.explanation: The writer says maybe we do not hold on to our pain because we love it. Maybe we hold on because it is the last hope we have, and it cannot be taken from us without taking us too.

posts.displayTitle: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence.
posts.altText: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence.
posts.text:
I would trade my soul with the devil
for a moment of your presence.
posts.explanation: The writer would give up his soul to the devil just to be near the person for one moment.

posts.displayTitle: Absence of hope leads to despair.
posts.altText: Absence of hope leads to despair.
posts.text: Absence of hope leads to despair.
posts.explanation: The writer says that when there is no hope left, a person falls into deep sadness and gives up.

posts.caption: Tragedy
posts.displayTitle: The tragedy of longing is not that it reaches for what it cannot poss…
posts.altText: The tragedy of longing is not that it reaches for what it cannot possess. It is that, given the entire world, it would still choose the locked door. because some desires do not seek fulfillment. They seek permanence. What is love if not permanence in the architecture of heart.
posts.text:
The tragedy of longing
is not that it reaches for
what it cannot possess.
It is that, given the
entire world, it would
still choose the locked door.
because some desires
do not seek fulfillment.
They seek permanence.

What is love if not permanence
in the architecture of heart.
posts.explanation: The writer says the sad thing about longing is that, even with the whole world open to it, it would still choose the one thing it can't have. Some wishes don't want to come true; they want to last forever, and he says love is that lasting thing built inside the heart.

posts.displayTitle: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what destroyed it.
posts.altText: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what destroyed it.
posts.text:
Nostalgia seduces the soul
into worshipping what destroyed it.
posts.explanation: The writer says missing the past can trick a person into loving and longing for the very thing that ruined them.

posts.caption: Maybe that's my problem
posts.displayTitle: Maybe that's my problem
posts.altText: Maybe that's my problem. I would give everything and ask for nothing in return. But there is a peculiar tragedy in giving you never know when the cup has become full, when it has begun to overflow. You never know where generosity ends and self-abandonment begins. You never know where to stop.
posts.text:
Maybe that's my problem.
I would give everything and
ask for nothing in return.

But there is a peculiar
tragedy in giving
you never know when
the cup has become full,
when it has begun to overflow.
You never know where generosity ends
and self-abandonment begins.
You never know where to stop.
posts.explanation: The writer thinks his problem is that he gives everything and asks for nothing back. The sad part of giving is that you can't tell when it is too much, or where being kind ends and losing yourself begins, so you never know when to stop.

posts.displayTitle: The human heart invents gods to absolve the sins it cannot forget.
posts.altText: The human heart invents gods to absolve the sins it cannot forget.
posts.text:
The human heart invents gods
to absolve the sins it cannot forget.
posts.explanation: The writer says people make up gods so they can feel forgiven for the wrongs they cannot stop remembering.

posts.caption: I would
posts.displayTitle: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence
posts.altText: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence, for what is eternity worth to a heart that has forgotten how to feel alive? Because even heaven would become unbearably lonely without you.
posts.text:
I would trade my soul
with the devil

for a moment
of your presence,
for what is eternity
worth to a heart
that has forgotten
how to feel alive?

Because even heaven
would become unbearably
lonely without you.
posts.explanation: The writer would give his soul to the devil just to be with the person for one moment. Living forever means nothing to a heart that no longer feels alive, and even heaven would feel too lonely without them.

posts.caption: I do
posts.displayTitle: I return to the fire hoping it won't burn me this time
posts.altText: I return to the fire hoping it won't burn me this time.
posts.text:
I return to the fire hoping
it won't burn me this time.
posts.explanation: The writer keeps going back to the thing that hurt him before, hoping that this time it will not hurt him again.

posts.displayTitle: Abandonment smells like a perfume we breathe in again and again.
posts.altText: Abandonment smells like a perfume we breathe in again and again.
posts.text:
Abandonment smells like a perfume
we breathe in again and again.
posts.explanation: Being left by someone is a hurt that keeps coming back. Like a smell you keep breathing in, it stays close, and we feel it again and again.

posts.caption: Nostalgia
posts.displayTitle: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what once destroyed it
posts.altText: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what once destroyed it. It perfumes the ashes so that we mistake the smoke for the scent of home. How nostalgic. The longer you dwell in memories, the deeper the ache becomes. I wonder if ruins grow roses only because we keep bleeding into their soil. No wonder memories bloom beautifully, even when all they ever did was destroy us.
posts.text:
Nostalgia seduces
the soul into worshipping
what once destroyed it.
It perfumes the ashes
so that we mistake the smoke for
the scent of home. How nostalgic.

The longer you dwell in memories,
the deeper the ache becomes.
I wonder if ruins grow roses only
because we keep bleeding into their soil.
No wonder memories bloom beautifully,
even when all they ever did was destroy us.
posts.explanation: The writer says missing the past makes us love the very things that hurt us. Memory makes old pain seem sweet, like home. The longer we stay in memories, the more it hurts, and memories look beautiful only because we keep feeding them with our pain.

posts.caption: I would
posts.displayTitle: I would trade my soul with the devil
posts.altText: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence, for what is eternity worth to a heart that has forgotten how to feel alive? Because even heaven would become unbearably lonely without you.
posts.text:
I would trade my soul
with the devil

for a moment
of your presence,
for what is eternity
worth to a heart
that has forgotten
how to feel alive?

Because even heaven
would become unbearably
lonely without you.
posts.explanation: The writer would give his soul to the devil just to be with the person for one moment. Living forever means nothing to a heart that no longer feels alive, and even heaven would feel too lonely without them.

posts.displayTitle: Liar, just like your presence was all that love a lie too?
posts.altText: Liar, just like your presence was all that love a lie too?
posts.text:
Lair, just like your presence
was all that love a lie too?
posts.explanation: The writer calls someone a liar. He asks if their love was fake too, just as their being with him turned out to be false.

posts.displayTitle: Hunger for warmth will leave you into the cold.
posts.altText: Hunger for warmth will leave you into the cold.
posts.text:
Hunger for warmth will
leave you into the cold.
posts.explanation: Wanting warmth and closeness too badly can end with you being left alone and cold.

posts.caption: My love
posts.displayTitle: My Love, is not the desire to have you
posts.altText: My Love, is not the desire to have you, but a defect in the soul that mistakes the silence left behind your absence for a language that would tell what I did for you to leave, so I rot and rot and rot while understanding the meaning of the closed door that might open anytime, or maybe not.
posts.text:
My Love,
is not the desire
to have you,

but a defect in the soul
that mistakes the silence
left behind your absence
for a language that would
tell what I did for you to leave,

so I rot and rot and rot
while understanding the meaning
of the closed door that might
open anytime, or maybe not.
posts.explanation: The writer says his love is not about wanting to have the person. It is a broken part of him that keeps listening to their silence, hoping it will tell him what he did to make them leave. So he slowly falls apart, waiting by a door that may or may not open.

posts.caption: You don't
posts.displayTitle: You don't need a presence to love someone.
posts.altText: You don't need a presence to love someone. Love exists with or without them, just as faith does not require God to stand before you to make you believe. the existence of love is not dependent on the existence of the person to whom it belonged. They may leave you by a random Tuesday night, disappear, or become a stranger, but …
posts.text:
You don't need a
presence to love someone.
Love exists with
or without them,
just as faith does not
require God to stand before
you to make you believe.
the existence of love is not dependent on the
existence of the person to whom it belonged.
They may leave you by a random Tuesday
night, disappear , or become a stranger,
but the fire they started in your heart would
still burn without their oxygen like presence.
posts.explanation: The writer says you can love someone even when they are not there. Just as faith in God does not need to see God, love does not need the person. They may leave or become a stranger, but the love they started keeps burning inside you anyway.

posts.displayTitle: Love is a habitual process that Stops only when your heart does.
posts.altText: Love is a habitual process that Stops only when your heart does.
posts.text:
Love is a habitual process that Stops
only when your heart does.
posts.explanation: Love is like a habit that never stops. It only ends when your heart stops beating, which means when you die.

posts.caption: I can smell it
posts.displayTitle: I can almost smell the coming of October
posts.altText: I can almost smell the coming of October, as someone who earlier lost his everything in it. Autumn of abandonment, smells like a perfume we breathe again and again, like the nostalgia of memories we know we are bound to lose.
posts.text:
I can almost smell
the coming of October,
as someone who
earlier lost his
everything in it.

Autumn of abandonment,
smells like a perfume
we breathe again and again,

like the nostalgia of memories
we know we are bound to lose.
posts.explanation: The writer can feel October coming, the month he once lost everything in. The pain of being left comes back every autumn like a familiar smell, along with memories he knows he will lose one day.

posts.displayTitle: The inertia of memories binds you to the grief.
posts.altText: The inertia of memories binds you to the grief.
posts.text:
The inertia of memories
binds you to the grief.
posts.explanation: Memories keep you stuck in place, so you cannot move on from your grief.

posts.caption: I may always
posts.displayTitle: I may tell you I love you
posts.altText: I may tell you I love you, But deep down i know what parts of me I have abandoned to keep this love alive. What parts of me I have thrown into the fire to keep it burning. I am the martyr I am the martyrdom, and love? it's my religion.
posts.text:
I may tell you
I love you,
But deep down
i know what parts of me
I have abandoned to
keep this love alive.

What parts of me I have thrown
into the fire to keep it burning.

I am the martyr
I am the martyrdom,
and love? it's my religion.
posts.explanation: The writer says he loves someone, but he knows he gave up parts of himself to keep that love going, burning pieces of himself like fuel. He sees himself as the one who suffers for love, and love is what he worships.

posts.displayTitle: all I am is an actor, destined to perform for rest of my life.
posts.altText: all I am is an actor, destined to perform for rest of my life.
posts.text:
all I am is an actor, destined
to perform for rest of my life.
posts.explanation: The writer feels his life is just acting, putting on a show, and that he will have to keep doing it for the rest of his life.

posts.displayTitle: My rib is a cage that mourns the absence of the bird it lost.
posts.altText: My rib is a cage that mourns the absence of the bird it lost.
posts.text:
My rib is a cage that mourns
the absence of the bird it lost.
posts.explanation: The writer's chest feels like an empty cage. It is sad because the person he loved, like a bird, has gone.

posts.caption: If loving you
posts.displayTitle: If loving you was a sin I would do it again and again
posts.altText: If loving you was a sin I would do it again and again Till both god and devil come to me and ask about what devotion of faith I have in you. I'll tell them about your eyes and they'll never be able to return again. Heaven or hell I deserve neither except for your eyes.
posts.text:
If loving you
was a sin
I would do it
again and again

Till both god and devil
come to me and ask about
what devotion of faith
I have in you.

I'll tell them about your eyes and
they'll never be able to return again.

Heaven or hell I deserve
neither except for your eyes.
posts.explanation: The writer says if loving the person is wrong, he would still do it again and again. If God and the devil asked about his faith, he would just describe the person's eyes, and they would be lost in them too. He wants neither heaven nor hell, only those eyes.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: Grief comes from the acceptance of the loss
posts.altText: Grief comes from the acceptance of the loss, of things you never thought you would lose. To make a home around a grave called the heart is what we call existing, and all we do in that home is mourn. Nobody prepares you for losing the permanence you once believed life possessed, and perhaps that is the cruelest tragedy.
posts.text:
Grief comes from
the acceptance of the loss,
of things you never
thought you would lose.

To make a home around
a grave called the heart
is what we call existing,
and all we do in that home is mourn.

Nobody prepares you for losing the
permanence you once believed life possessed,
and perhaps that is the cruelest tragedy.
posts.explanation: Grief begins when you accept losing something you never thought you would lose. Living feels like making a home around a heart that is like a grave, and just mourning there. The cruelest part is that nobody warns you that nothing in life lasts forever.

posts.displayTitle: Heart is no different than a grave,
posts.altText: Heart is no different than a grave, both holds people and their memories.
posts.text:
Heart is no different than a grave,
both holds people and their memories.
posts.explanation: The writer says a heart is like a grave. Both keep people inside, along with the memories of them.

posts.caption: October
posts.displayTitle: I can almost smell the coming of October
posts.altText: I can almost smell the coming of October, as someone who earlier lost his everything in it. Autumn of abandonment, smells like a perfume we breathe again and again, like the nostalgia of memories we know we are bound to lose.
posts.text:
I can almost smell
the coming of October,
as someone who
earlier lost his
everything in it.

Autumn of abandonment,
smells like a perfume
we breathe again and again,

like the nostalgia of memories
we know we are bound to lose.
posts.explanation: The writer can feel October coming, the month he once lost everything in. The pain of being left comes back every autumn like a familiar smell, along with memories he knows he will lose one day.

posts.displayTitle: I am Half hope, Half death;
posts.altText: I am Half hope, Half death;
posts.text: I am Half hope, Half death;
posts.explanation: The writer feels split in two: one half still hopes, and the other half feels dead inside.

posts.caption: Tell me!
posts.displayTitle: They say energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
posts.altText: They say energy can neither be created nor destroyed. Funny because the energy I poured into my bonds disappeared like smoke in an open sky, nothing to hold, nothing to return. I was broken by the very hands I warmed. So tell me, if feelings follow the same laws, where do they go when they're the ones left in ruins? …
posts.text:
They say energy can neither
be created nor destroyed.
Funny because
the energy I poured into
my bonds disappeared
like smoke in an open sky,
nothing to hold, nothing to return.
I was broken by the very hands I warmed.
So tell me, if feelings follow the same laws,
where do they go when they're the ones left
in ruins? Do they stay like ash in the lungs
unseen yet heavy? Or do they learn to survive
by changing form, becoming the silence we
carry forward?
posts.explanation: Science says energy never disappears, but the care the writer gave to people vanished with nothing coming back. The people he loved hurt him. He asks where feelings go after that: do they stay inside as a hidden, heavy weight, or turn into the silence we carry with us?

posts.caption: I wish
posts.displayTitle: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions
posts.altText: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions now lying in the coldest part of my heart once belonged to you. How the colourful flowers that once bloomed for you have now grown into thorny vines that pierce me instead. I hope that someday, when you come back, I'll have enough flowers left to offer you not just trembling hands numbed by cold.
posts.text:
I wish
I could tell you that
all the abandoned
emotions now lying in the
coldest part of my heart once
belonged to you.

How the colourful flowers that once
bloomed for you have now grown into
thorny vines that pierce me instead.

I hope that someday, when you come back,
I'll have enough flowers left to offer you
not just trembling hands numbed by cold.
posts.explanation: The writer wishes he could tell the person that the feelings now lying cold in his heart were once all for them. The love that grew for them has turned into something that hurts him. He hopes that if they return, he will still have love to give, not just cold, shaking hands.

posts.caption: Like sunflower
posts.displayTitle: Flower shall grow from within my grave,
posts.altText: Flower shall grow from within my grave, and it shall be in the colour of your eyes. I won't need any other visitors to visit my grave except you. just visit once in a while, you needn't bring flowers because those flowers will turn in the direction of your eyes like sunflower finding its sun.
posts.text:
Flower shall grow
from within my grave,
and it shall be in
the colour of your eyes.
I won't need any other
visitors to visit my grave
except you.
just visit once in a while ,
you needn't bring flowers because
those flowers will
turn in the direction of your eyes
like sunflower finding its sun.
posts.explanation: The writer imagines a flower growing from his grave in the color of the person's eyes. He wants no visitor but them, now and then. They need not bring flowers, because that flower will turn toward their eyes, the way a sunflower turns to the sun.

posts.displayTitle: you were the fire, I was the burning moth.
posts.altText: you were the fire, I was the burning moth.
posts.text:
you were the fire,
I was the burning moth.
posts.explanation: The person was like a flame, and the writer was like a moth flying into it. He was pulled toward them even though it burned him up.

posts.caption: If loving you
posts.displayTitle: If loving you was a beautiful mistake
posts.altText: If loving you was a beautiful mistake, then I would make it again, knowing exactly where it would lead me. Perhaps that is the tragedy of my heart I never feared being broken as long as the pieces still remembered the shape of you.
posts.text:
If loving you
was a beautiful mistake,
then I would make
it again, knowing exactly
where it would lead me.

Perhaps that is
the tragedy of my heart
I never feared being broken
as long as the pieces
still remembered
the shape of you.
posts.explanation: The writer says loving the person was a beautiful mistake, and he would make it again even knowing how it ends. The sad part is that he never feared being broken, as long as the broken pieces still remembered that person.

posts.displayTitle: Hellfire is still colder than the way love burns me.
posts.altText: Hellfire is still colder than the way love burns me.
posts.text:
Hellfire is still colder than
the way love burns me.
posts.explanation: The writer says love hurts him so much that even the fire of hell would feel cooler than it.

posts.caption: What did you do to me?
posts.displayTitle: My eyes have began to search you desparately in everything,
posts.altText: My eyes have began to search you desparately in everything, what did you do to me. I go to god to ask myself from but I end up asking you again, what did you do to me. I search for heaven with hell within my chest, What did you do to me.
posts.text:
My eyes have
began to search you
desparately in everything,
what did you do to me.

I go to god to ask
myself from but
I end up asking you again,
what did you do to me.

I search for heaven with
hell within my chest,
What did you do to me.
posts.explanation: The writer keeps looking for the person in everything. He goes to God to ask for himself back, but ends up asking for them instead. He looks for peace while carrying pain in his chest, and keeps wondering how they changed him so much.

posts.displayTitle: The desire itself contains its future absence.
posts.altText: The desire itself contains its future absence.
posts.text:
The desire itself
contains its future absence.
posts.explanation: The writer says that when you want something, losing it later is already part of that wanting. Everything we long for will one day be gone.

posts.caption: october
posts.displayTitle: It's October now, and I wonder what I shall lose this year
posts.altText: It's October now, and I wonder what I shall lose this year. October has become a monolithic cycle of losing things that were once dearer to me than I was to myself. Memories come like autumn, and I fall every time. I lost you, and I wonder if I shall lose these memories too.
posts.text:
It's October now,
and I wonder what
I shall lose this year.
October has become
a monolithic cycle of losing
things that were once dearer
to me than I was to myself.

Memories come like autumn,
and I fall every time.

I lost you,
and I wonder if I shall lose
these memories too.
posts.explanation: Every October the writer has lost something he loved more than himself, so now he waits to see what he will lose this year. Memories come like falling leaves, and each time he falls apart. He has lost the person and wonders if he will lose the memories too.

posts.caption: October it is.
posts.displayTitle: It's October again, no wonder that it's the season for fall.
posts.altText: It's October again, no wonder that it's the season for fall. The leaves begin to wither, and so do the things I once held dear. It's October again, and I find myself wondering what will fall this time- the leaves, the memories, or me.
posts.text:
It's October again,
no wonder that it's the season for fall.
The leaves begin to wither,
and so do the things I once held dear.
It's October again,
and I find myself wondering
what will fall this time-
the leaves, the memories, or me.
