posts.explanation: October is autumn, when leaves fall. The writer says the things he loved fall away too, just like the leaves. He wonders what will go this time: the leaves, his memories, or he himself.

posts.displayTitle: Hope lures you into believing there is love waiting beyond the pain.
posts.altText: Hope lures you into believing there is love waiting beyond the pain.
posts.text:
Hope lures you into believing there
is love waiting beyond the pain.
posts.explanation: Hope tricks you into thinking that love is waiting for you after all the pain.

posts.caption: Disaster
posts.displayTitle: The more I talk to people, the more I realize how unbearable your abs…
posts.altText: The more I talk to people, the more I realize how unbearable your absence has become. There is a repetitive disaster in taking out your pictures from my wallet and keeping them inside it again. I am stuck.
posts.text:
The more I talk to
people, the more
I realize how
unbearable your
absence has become.

There is a repetitive disaster
in taking out your pictures
from my wallet and keeping
them inside it again.
I am stuck.
posts.explanation: The more the writer talks to other people, the more he feels how much he misses the person who is gone. He keeps taking her photos out of his wallet and putting them back again, and he feels stuck.

posts.displayTitle: To love is to die; to die is to be loved.
posts.altText: To love is to die; to die is to be loved.
posts.text: To love is to die; to die is to be loved.
posts.explanation: He seems to say love and death are tied together: loving someone means losing yourself, like dying, and in death you are finally loved.

posts.displayTitle: Hope is a drug we willingly consume.
posts.altText: Hope is a drug we willingly consume.
posts.text: Hope is a drug we willingly consume.
posts.explanation: The writer says hope is like a drug: we know what it does to us, but we still choose to keep taking it.

posts.caption: Depends on you
posts.displayTitle: The rhythm of love is hope
posts.altText: The rhythm of love is hope, and hope lures you into believing there is love beyond all the pain & suffering. How far will you go for love? Depends on you, and addicted to hope, you may stay loyal to pain, until one day you realise you survive on hope rather than love itself.
posts.text:
The rhythm of love is hope,
and hope lures you into believing there
is love beyond all the pain & suffering.
How far will you go for love?
Depends on you,
and addicted to hope,
you may stay loyal to pain,
until one day you realise you survive
on hope rather than love itself.
posts.explanation: The writer says hope keeps love going, making you believe love waits after the pain. Hooked on that hope, you may keep staying with the pain, until one day you see you are living on hope, not on real love.

posts.caption: First line inspo by dostoevsky
posts.displayTitle: The price of loving is never loving again
posts.altText: The price of loving is never loving again, because you spend the rest of your life comparing every heart to the one that taught yours how to beat, every face to the one that once made you smile, because some people become a habit through which you see the world.
posts.text:
The price of loving
is never loving again,
because you spend
the rest of your life
comparing every heart
to the one that taught
yours how to beat,
every face to the one that
once made you smile,
because some people become a habit
through which you see the world.
posts.explanation: The writer says once you truly love someone, you may never love again. For the rest of your life you compare every person to the one who first taught your heart to love. Some people become the way you see everything.

posts.caption: I still do
posts.displayTitle: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us
posts.altText: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us. Isn't it funny how we create our own delusions to survive the grief, because what used to make us happy isn't there to make us smile anymore?
posts.text:
I still think you
love me,
just like I still think
the moon follows us.

Isn't it funny how
we create our own
delusions to survive the grief,
because what used to make
us happy isn't there to
make us smile anymore?
posts.explanation: The writer still believes the person loves him, the same way people believe the moon follows them. He says we tell ourselves untrue things to get through grief, because what once made us happy is gone.

posts.displayTitle: Love is a myth we die believing.
posts.altText: Love is a myth we die believing.
posts.text: Love is a myth we die believing.
posts.explanation: Love is like a made-up story that we keep believing in until the day we die.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: Days have started to get shorter, it'll be night soon
posts.altText: Days have started to get shorter, it'll be night soon, But in the darkness of the night grief knocks my door, night brings me closer to the things I spend my days trying to forget. The longer the night the deeper the grief, deeper the grief colder the heart becomes.
posts.text:
Days have started to get shorter,
it'll be night soon,

But in the darkness of the
night grief knocks my door,

night brings me closer
to the things I spend
my days trying to forget.

The longer the night the
Deeper the grief, deeper the grief
colder the heart becomes.
posts.explanation: The days are getting shorter as winter comes. At night, grief comes to the writer and brings back the things he tries to forget all day. The longer the night, the deeper his sadness, and the colder his heart grows.

posts.caption: Colder.
posts.displayTitle: Colder the heart the quieter the soul
posts.altText: Colder the heart the quieter the soul, the quieter the soul, the louder the memories become. And the louder the memories become, the harder it becomes to sleep. But you know, what makes the heart cold is very much the warmth it sought.
posts.text:
Colder the heart
the quieter the soul,
the quieter the soul,
the louder
the memories become.

And the louder
the memories become,
the harder it becomes to sleep.
But you know,
what makes the heart cold is
very much the warmth it sought.
posts.explanation: The writer says when the heart turns cold, the soul goes quiet, and in that quiet the memories get louder and keep him awake. What made his heart cold was the very warmth and love it went looking for.

posts.displayTitle: Before feeling nothing at all, you feel alot.
posts.altText: Before feeling nothing at all, you feel alot.
posts.text: Before feeling nothing at all, you feel alot.
posts.explanation: Before you go numb and feel nothing, you first feel far too much. The numbness comes after a lot of pain.

posts.caption: Why?
posts.displayTitle: why do you keep holding on to every pain inside your heart
posts.altText: why do you keep holding on to every pain inside your heart when even the heaven's cry by raining?
posts.text:
why do you
keep holding on
to every pain
inside your heart

when even the heaven's
cry by raining?
posts.explanation: The writer asks why you keep all your pain locked inside, when even the sky lets itself cry by raining. He seems to say it is okay to let the pain out.

posts.displayTitle: Till when will you mistake pain for love?
posts.altText: Till when will you mistake pain for love?
posts.text: Till when will you mistake pain for love?
posts.explanation: The writer asks how long you will keep thinking that being hurt is the same as being loved.

posts.caption: If loving you
posts.displayTitle: If loving you leads me to the loss of myself, then why am I loving…
posts.altText: If loving you leads me to the loss of myself, then why am I loving you? If loving you feels like a heaven within my mind and a hell beneath my ribs, then why am I loving you? Why must I become less of me every time I become more of you?
posts.text:
If loving you
leads me to the loss
of myself, then why
am I loving you?

If loving you feels like
a heaven within my mind
and a hell beneath my ribs,
then why am I loving you?

Why must I become less of me
every time I become more of you?
posts.explanation: The writer asks himself why he keeps loving someone when it makes him lose himself. The love feels like heaven in his mind but like hell in his chest. He asks why he must become less of himself the more he gives himself to them.

posts.caption: We all do
posts.displayTitle: We came from nothing, and will return to nothing
posts.altText: We came from nothing, and will return to nothing leaving nothing behind but the ache of having been nothing to someone for whom we felt everything.
posts.text:
We came from nothing,
and will return to nothing—
leaving nothing behind but the
ache of having been nothing
to someone
for whom we felt everything.
posts.explanation: We come from nothing and go back to nothing. All that is left behind is the pain of having meant nothing to someone who meant everything to us.

posts.caption: If he asks that is
posts.displayTitle: when god asks me what my last wish before returning to nothingness is
posts.altText: when god asks me what my last wish before returning to nothingness is. I'll ask him to let me relive my moments with you again. to be 18 again, naive and full of love, when I found my religion in those eyes. but that will be to much to ask for so I just die.
posts.text:
when god asks me
what my last wish
before returning
to nothingness is.
I'll ask him to let me relive
my moments with you again.
to be 18 again,
naive and full of love,
when I found
my religion in those eyes.
but that will be to much
to ask for so I just die.
posts.explanation: When he dies, the writer would ask God for one last wish: to live his time with the person again, to be 18, young, trusting and full of love, when their eyes were everything to him. But it feels like too much to ask, so he just dies.

posts.displayTitle: I am the Sin, I am the Sinner.
posts.altText: I am the Sin, I am the Sinner.
posts.text: I am the Sin , I am the Sinner.
posts.explanation: The writer feels he is both the wrong that was done and the one who did it, as if all the blame is his.

posts.displayTitle: You are the hope, I am the hopeless.
posts.altText: You are the hope, I am the hopeless.
posts.text: You are the hope, I am the hopeless.
posts.explanation: The writer says the other person is his hope, while he himself has no hope left.

posts.displayTitle: Grief is the residue left behind by love.
posts.altText: Grief is the residue left behind by love.
posts.text: Grief is the residue left behind by love.
posts.explanation: Grief is what is left behind after love. When love ends or is lost, the sadness that stays is grief.

posts.caption: I do
posts.displayTitle: I die when I have to pretend
posts.altText: I die when I have to pretend that your absence does not hurt. I die when I see you happy and realise I am no longer part of it. I die when I almost tell you how much I miss you then remember you stopped asking.
posts.text:
I die when
I have to pretend
that your absence
does not hurt.
I die when
I see you happy
and realise I am no
longer part of it.

I die when I almost tell you
how much I miss you then
remember you stopped asking.
posts.explanation: The writer feels like he dies inside when he has to pretend the person being gone does not hurt, and when he sees them happy without him. It hurts most when he almost tells them he misses them, then remembers they stopped asking about him.

posts.displayTitle: Vulnerable heart is a prey to love.
posts.altText: Vulnerable heart is a prey to love.
posts.text: Vulnerable heart is a prey to love.
posts.explanation: A soft, open heart is easy for love to catch and hurt, like an animal that gets hunted.

posts.displayTitle: we became heartless because, we once gave our heart.
posts.altText: we became heartless because, we once gave our heart.
posts.text:
we became heartless because,
we once gave our heart.
posts.explanation: The writer says we turned cold and stopped caring because we once gave our heart to someone, and now it is gone.

posts.caption: I know I'll be
posts.displayTitle: I know I will be abandoned.
posts.altText: I know I will be abandoned. Yet still, I pour the glass full of love. There is a strange beauty in offering abundance to a world that has taught you scarcity. To love is to never cease to exist, to love is to live and give.
posts.text:
I know I will be abandoned.
Yet still,
I pour the glass full of love.

There is a strange beauty in offering abundance
to a world that has taught you scarcity.
To love is to
never cease to exist,
to love is to live and give.
posts.explanation: The writer knows he will be left alone in the end, but he still gives his love fully. He finds something beautiful in giving a lot to a world that has given him little, and believes loving means truly living and giving.

posts.displayTitle: Half death, Half devotion
posts.altText: Half death, Half devotion
posts.text: Half death, Half devotion
posts.explanation: The writer feels he is half dead inside and half still fully given over to the one he loves.

posts.displayTitle: The more I love the more they leave.
posts.altText: The more I love the more they leave.
posts.text: The more I love the more they leave.
posts.explanation: The writer says the more he loves people, the more they leave him.

posts.caption: Moon
posts.displayTitle: My eyes still look for a glimpse of you
posts.altText: My eyes still look for a glimpse of you just like the way I find the moon in between the narrow space of the branches. I still find you in the moment of happiness. I still search for you in every way possible. everything Reminds me of you.
posts.text:
My eyes still look
for a glimpse of you
just like the way

I find the moon
in between the narrow
space of the branches.

I still find you in
the moment of happiness.

I still search for you in every way
possible. everything Reminds me of you.
posts.explanation: The writer still looks for the person everywhere, the way you catch the moon through small gaps between tree branches. He feels them in happy moments too. Everything reminds him of them.

posts.displayTitle: you survive on hope, rather than love itself.
posts.altText: you survive on hope, rather than love itself.
posts.text: you survive on hope, rather than love itself.
posts.explanation: You keep going because you hope things will get better, not because the love itself is still there.

posts.caption: Love
posts.displayTitle: What is love?
posts.altText: What is love? Maybe something which belongs to me, is me, around me and I can tell you so many things about love and it'll still be less, there's love in my pulse and even in my breath. Love revolves around my heart just like my existence does around yours.
posts.text:
What is love?
Maybe something
which belongs to me,
is me , around me
and I can tell you
so many things about
love and it'll still be less,

there's love in my pulse
and even in my breath.
Love revolves around my heart
just like my existence does around yours.
posts.explanation: The writer says love is part of him, inside him and all around him, and no words could ever fully explain it. Love is in his heartbeat and his breath. It circles his heart, just as his whole life circles around the person.

posts.caption: End
posts.displayTitle: October is about to end, and November will soon arrive.
posts.altText: October is about to end, and November will soon arrive. The streets will once again fall silent, leaving only memories to run aloud. Soon, the year will come to an end, but the memories won't. It's been the same ever since you left. Come back now.
posts.text:
October is about to end,
and November will soon arrive.
The streets will once again fall silent,
leaving only memories to run aloud.
Soon, the year will come to an end,
but the memories won't.
It's been the same ever since you left.
Come back now.
posts.explanation: As October ends and November comes, the streets will go quiet and only memories will feel loud. The year will end, but the memories will not. It has been like this since the person left, and the writer asks them to come back.

posts.displayTitle: Death is an ecstasy, so lovers die every day.
posts.altText: Death is an ecstasy, so lovers die every day.
posts.text:
Death is an ecstasy,
so lovers die every day
posts.explanation: He seems to say that losing yourself in love is like a sweet kind of dying, so people in love go through it every day.

posts.caption: If loving you
posts.displayTitle: If love was a sin, I would be the deepest kind of sinner
posts.altText: If love was a sin, I would be the deepest kind of sinner, because my love for you is selfish yet selfless. I would give you everything and yet ask for nothing in return, because if falling out of love after it ends diminishes what it once was, then heaven without it would feel utterly worthless.
posts.text:
If love was a sin,
I would be the deepest
kind of sinner,
because my love for you
is selfish yet selfless.

I would give you everything
and yet ask for nothing in return,
because if falling out of love after it
ends diminishes what it once was,
then heaven without it would
feel utterly worthless.
posts.explanation: The writer says that if love were a sin, he would be the worst sinner, because his love is both selfish and giving. He would give the person everything and want nothing back. To him, even heaven without this love would be worthless.

posts.displayTitle: Of all the ways to become strangers, love is the cruelest.
posts.altText: Of all the ways to become strangers, love is the cruelest.
posts.text:
Of all the ways to become strangers,
love is the cruelest.
posts.explanation: People can drift apart in many ways, but the most painful is when two people who loved each other end up as strangers.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering…
posts.altText: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering that you've forgotten what it feels like to exist without it. And perhaps, somewhere beneath all that, there is a part of you still waiting for them to notice that you haven't been okay for a very long time.
posts.text:
you've grown
so accustomed to
your suffering that you've
forgotten what it feels
like to exist without it.

And perhaps,
somewhere beneath all that,
there is a part of you
still waiting for them
to notice that you haven't
been okay for a very long time.
posts.explanation: The writer says you have lived with pain so long that you forget what life feels like without it. And deep down, part of you is still waiting for someone to notice that you have not been okay for a long time.

posts.displayTitle: It's all love until it's your hope.
posts.altText: It's all love until it's your hope.
posts.text: It's all love until it's your hope.
posts.explanation: He seems to say love feels simple and sweet until you start living on hope for it; then it turns into waiting and hurt.

posts.caption: Love
posts.displayTitle: What kind of love we live in?
posts.altText: What kind of love we live in? Where loving is mistaken for an act of weakness. Where waiting is mistaken for an act of letting go? If this is what loving feels like then I am happy being away from it because love was never meant to be our weakness it was always meant to be our strength.
posts.text:
What kind of
love we live in?
Where loving is mistaken
for an act of weakness
Where waiting is
mistaken for an act
of letting go?
If this is what loving feels
like then I am happy being
away from it because love was
never meant to be our weakness
it was always meant to be our strength.
posts.explanation: The writer asks what kind of love this is, where loving someone is seen as weak and waiting for someone is seen as giving up. If that is love, he would rather stay away from it, because love should make us strong, not weak.

posts.caption: How have you been?
posts.displayTitle: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering…
posts.altText: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering that you've forgotten what it feels like to exist without it. And perhaps, somewhere beneath all that, there is a part of you still waiting for them to notice that you haven't been okay for a very long time.
posts.text:
you've grown
so accustomed to
your suffering that you've
forgotten what it feels
like to exist without it.

And perhaps,
somewhere beneath all that,
there is a part of you
still waiting for them
to notice that you haven't
been okay for a very long time.
posts.explanation: The writer says you have lived with pain so long that you forget what life feels like without it. And deep down, part of you is still waiting for someone to notice that you have not been okay for a long time.

posts.displayTitle: Permanence is a myth.
posts.altText: Permanence is a myth.
posts.text: Permanence is a myth.
posts.explanation: Nothing lasts forever. The idea that things will always stay the same is not real.

posts.caption: Cold
posts.displayTitle: There's a familiar chill in the air
posts.altText: There's a familiar chill in the air. I wonder, is it the winter or abandonment? You sit with a profound sense of vulnerability as the chill seeps into your bones, and ask what are the boundaries between the weather and what someone's absence has left behind? Yeah, coldness.
posts.text:
There's a familiar chill in the air.
I wonder, is it the
winter or abandonment?
You sit with a profound sense of vulnerability
as the chill seeps into your bones.
and ask what are the boundaries
between the weather and what someone's
absence has left behind? Yeah, coldness.
posts.explanation: The writer feels a familiar cold in the air and wonders if it is winter or the feeling of being left. As the cold sinks in, you feel weak and unsafe, and you cannot tell the weather apart from the emptiness someone's leaving left behind. Both are just cold.

posts.displayTitle: I love, love from afar
posts.altText: I love, love from afar
posts.text: I love, love from afar
posts.explanation: The writer loves someone, but only from a distance.

posts.caption:
My book is out!
A special thanks to @byhaadi_ who designed the book 🥹🫶🏻 and to all those who have been a part of this journey @inkedbyshrad @aryaaa._.21 @writerspocketpublishing
posts.displayTitle: My first book leaving & living has been published!!
posts.altText: My first book leaving & living has been published!! Leaving and Living is an exploration of the human condition, of memories that refuse to fade and truths we were never meant to make peace with, without ever getting to rest in peace. Perhaps the tragedy of being human lies in knowing when to leave, yet finding a thousand reasons to stay. …
posts.text:
My first book
leaving & living
has been
published!!
---
Leaving and Living is an exploration
of the human condition, of memories that
refuse to fade and truths we were never
meant to make peace with,
without ever getting to rest in peace.
Perhaps the tragedy of being human lies
in knowing when to leave,
yet finding a thousand reasons to stay.

For sometimes, all our memories
lead us back to what
we must leave behind,
while reason teaches us the art of letting go.
---
Link for the book is
in my bio!!
posts.explanation: The writer shares that his first book, Leaving & Living, is out, says it is about memories that will not fade and how hard it is to leave when we keep finding reasons to stay, and says the link is in his bio.

posts.displayTitle: "I was born with a fate of moth."
posts.altText: "I was born with a fate of moth."
posts.text: “I was born with a fate of moth.”
posts.explanation: The writer feels he was born to be like a moth, always pulled toward the thing that will burn and hurt him, the way a moth flies into a flame.

posts.displayTitle: we survive on hope rather than love itself.
posts.altText: we survive on hope rather than love itself.
posts.text: we survive on hope rather than love itself.
posts.explanation: We keep going because of the hope that things will get better, not because the love is really still there.

posts.caption: Isn't it?
posts.displayTitle: Life has an unsettling way of putting a catastrophe in front of you
posts.altText: Life has an unsettling way of putting a catastrophe in front of you. On a random Tuesday you'll be confronted with the death of things you thought were eternal. Do not mistake the sunlight falling on the floor for a miracle. It's just sunlight, it's just life.
posts.text:
Life has an unsettling
way of putting
a catastrophe in front of you.
On a random Tuesday
you'll be confronted with
the death of things you
thought were eternal.

Do not mistake the sunlight falling
on the floor for a miracle.
It's just sunlight, it's just life.
posts.explanation: Life can suddenly put something terrible in front of you. On an ordinary day, things you thought would last forever can end. The writer says a bit of sunlight on the floor is not a miracle; it is just sunlight, just ordinary life going on.

posts.caption: It never
posts.displayTitle: Perhaps the hardest truths are not those that destroy what we possess
posts.altText: Perhaps the hardest truths are not those that destroy what we possess, but those that reveal how much of our lives we had already built around love that never existed. We continue performing the ordinary rituals of existence, because performing has become a new way of existing. We almost get offended by how little the universe gives us…
posts.text:
Perhaps the hardest truths
are not those that destroy
what we possess,
but those that reveal how
much of our lives we had already
built around love that never existed.
We continue performing the ordinary
rituals of existence, because performing
has became a new way of existing.
We almost get offended by how little
the universe gives us, all lies I must say
whatever, it never promised us anything.
posts.explanation: The writer says the hardest truths are not the ones that take things away, but the ones that show we built our lives around a love that was never real. We keep doing everyday things just to get by. We feel hurt by how little life gives us, but life never promised anything.

posts.caption: My book leaving and living is out now
posts.displayTitle: how many lives have you abandoned?
posts.altText: how many lives have you abandoned? let me ask you, again. from how many lives have you been abandoned by? or have you truly loved any of them? sit down stare at the sun, cry. ask yourself what does living means to you. I hope it doesn't merely means leaving.
posts.text:
how many lives have you abandoned?
let me ask you, again.
from how many lives
have you been abandoned by?
or have you truly loved any of them?
sit down stare at the sun, cry.
ask yourself what does living means to you.
I hope it doesn't merely means leaving.
posts.explanation: The writer asks how many people you have left, how many have left you, and whether you truly loved any of them. He tells you to sit, look at the sun, cry, and ask what living means to you, hoping it means more than just leaving.

posts.displayTitle: I wonder how much pain do you carry behind that smile.
posts.altText: I wonder how much pain do you carry behind that smile.
posts.text:
I wonder how much pain
do you carry behind that smile.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders how much pain someone is hiding behind their smile.

posts.caption: Pain
posts.displayTitle: Pain is an absurdity of human existence
posts.altText: Pain is an absurdity of human existence, there is more perversed in advance, about how suffering can render the inconsequential monumental, how an unremarkable silence acquires the jurisdiction of a catastrophe. Maybe pain teaches you how to become fluent in loss and how to die while living it.
posts.text:
Pain is an absurdity
of human existence,
There is more perversed
in advance, about how
suffering can render the
inconsequential monumental,

how an unremarkable silence acquires
the jurisdiction of a catastrophe.
Maybe pain teaches you
how to become fluent in loss
and how to die while living it.
posts.explanation: The writer says pain makes no sense. Suffering can make small things feel huge, and a simple silence can feel like a disaster. Maybe pain teaches you to get used to losing things, and to feel dead while you are still alive.

posts.displayTitle: fear of loss is bigger than the loss itself
posts.altText: fear of loss is bigger than the loss itself
posts.text: fear of loss is bigger than the loss itself
posts.explanation: Being afraid of losing something hurts more than actually losing it.

posts.caption: Heaven and hell
posts.displayTitle: If loving you was a sin I would do it again and again
posts.altText: If loving you was a sin I would do it again and again Till both god and devil come to me and ask about what devotion of faith I have in you. I'll tell them about your eyes and they'll never be able to return again. Heaven or hell I deserve neither except for your eyes.
posts.text:
If loving you
was a sin
I would do it
again and again

Till both god and devil
come to me and ask about
what devotion of faith
I have in you.

I'll tell them about your eyes and
they'll never be able to return again.

Heaven or hell I deserve
neither except for your eyes.
posts.explanation: The writer says if loving the person is wrong, he would still do it again and again. If God and the devil asked about his faith, he would just describe the person's eyes, and they would be lost in them too. He wants neither heaven nor hell, only those eyes.

posts.caption: November
posts.displayTitle: November has come, now everything I lost will echo in the cold air
posts.altText: November has come, now everything I lost will echo in the cold air. I wonder how many winters a heart must endure before it ceases to distinguish between the season and its own desolation. It's never the cold that kills us. It's always the memories.
posts.text:
November has come,
now everything
I lost will echo
in the cold air.

I wonder how many
winters a heart must
endure before it ceases to
distinguish between the
season and its own desolation.

It's Never the cold that kills us
It's always the memories.
posts.explanation: November has come, and in the cold air everything the writer lost comes back to him. He wonders how many winters a heart must go through before it cannot tell the cold season from its own emptiness. In the end, it is memories, not cold, that kill us.

posts.displayTitle: your eyes are the sin; I am the fallen.
posts.altText: your eyes are the sin; I am the fallen.
posts.text: your eyes are the sin; I am the fallen.
posts.explanation: The writer says the person's eyes are what pulled him into wrong, and he is the one who fell because of them.

posts.caption: November
posts.displayTitle: Be good to my soul, November.
posts.altText: Be good to my soul, November. October already took a lot. Now it's just me and my grief left to mourn the absence of everything I have lost. The trees are shedding what the seasons could not spare, much like I have been stripped of things I once mistook for permanence.
posts.text:
Be good to my soul,
November.
October already took a lot.
Now it's just me
and my grief left
to mourn the absence
of everything I have lost.

The trees are shedding what
the seasons could not spare,
much like I have been stripped
of things I once mistook for permanence.
posts.explanation: The writer asks November to be kind to him, because October already took so much. Now it is only him and his grief for all he has lost. Like trees losing their leaves, he has lost things he once thought would last forever.

posts.displayTitle: Curse of human soul is that it's never satisfied.
posts.altText: Curse of human soul is that it's never satisfied.
posts.text:
Curse of human soul is
that it's never satisfied.
posts.explanation: The sad thing about people is that they are never happy with what they have; they always want more.

posts.caption: Moon
posts.displayTitle: My eyes still look for a glimpse of you just like the way I find the…
posts.altText: My eyes still look for a glimpse of you just like the way I find the moon in between the narrow space of the branches. I still find you in the moment of happiness. I still search for you in every way possible. everything Reminds me of you.
posts.text:
My eyes still look
for a glimpse of you
just like the way

I find the moon
in between the narrow
space of the branches.

I still find you in
the moment of happiness.

I still search for you in every way
possible. everything Reminds me of you.
posts.explanation: The writer still looks for the person everywhere, the way you catch the moon through small gaps between tree branches. He feels them in happy moments too. Everything reminds him of them.

posts.caption: Suffering
posts.displayTitle: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering…
posts.altText: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering that you've forgotten what it feels like to exist without it. And perhaps, somewhere beneath all that, there is a part of you still waiting for them to notice that you haven't been okay for a very long time.
posts.text:
you've grown
so accustomed to
your suffering that you've
forgotten what it feels
like to exist without it.

And perhaps,
somewhere beneath all that,
there is a part of you
still waiting for them
to notice that you haven't
been okay for a very long time.
posts.explanation: The writer says you have lived with pain so long that you forget what life feels like without it. And deep down, part of you is still waiting for someone to notice that you have not been okay for a long time.

posts.displayTitle: you never reach the end of love.
posts.altText: you never reach the end of love.
posts.text: you never reach the end of love.
posts.explanation: Love has no ending. However far you go in it, there is always more.

posts.caption: Warmth
posts.displayTitle: Colder the heart the quieter the soul,
posts.altText: Colder the heart the quieter the soul, the quieter the soul, the louder the memories become. And the louder the memories become, the harder it becomes to sleep. But you know, what makes the heart cold is very much the warmth it sought.
posts.text:
Colder the heart
the quieter the soul,
the quieter the soul,
the louder
the memories become.

And the louder
the memories become,
the harder it becomes to sleep.
But you know,
what makes the heart cold is
very much the warmth it sought.
posts.explanation: The writer says when the heart turns cold, the soul goes quiet, and in that quiet the memories get louder and keep him awake. What made his heart cold was the very warmth and love it went looking for.

posts.displayTitle: I write your name and forget what to write after it.
posts.altText: I write your name and forget what to write after it.
posts.text:
I write your name and
forget what to write after it.
posts.explanation: The writer writes the person's name, and then his mind goes blank. Thinking of them leaves him with no other words.

posts.caption: Sunflower
posts.displayTitle: Flower shall grow from within my grave,
posts.altText: Flower shall grow from within my grave, and it shall be in the colour of your eyes. I won't need any other visitors to visit my grave except you. just visit once in a while, you needn't bring flowers because those flowers will turn in the direction of your eyes like sunflower, like sun.
posts.text:
Flower shall grow
from within my grave,
and it shall be in
the colour of your eyes.
I won't need any other
visitors to visit my grave
except you.
just visit once in a while ,
you needn't bring flowers because
those flowers will
turn in the direction of your eyes
like sunflower, like sun.
posts.explanation: The writer pictures a flower growing from his grave in the color of the person's eyes. He wants only them to visit, once in a while, with no need to bring flowers, because that flower will turn toward their eyes like a sunflower turns to the sun.

posts.displayTitle: How often have you mistaken kindness for love?
posts.altText: How often have you mistaken kindness for love?
posts.text:
How often have you
mistaken kindness for love?
posts.explanation: The writer asks how many times you have thought someone loved you when they were only being kind.

posts.displayTitle: How can two people go so far afar after knowing each other so closely.
posts.altText: How can two people go so far afar after knowing each other so closely.
posts.text:
How can two people go so afar
after knowing each other so closely.
posts.explanation: The writer wonders how two people who were once so close can end up so far apart.

posts.caption: What can they do
posts.displayTitle: What can a lover do except for waiting?
posts.altText: What can a lover do except for waiting? What can a lover do except for hoping? they do both to bring back the ruin of their existence alive, they do both to delve into those eyes to ruin themselves again. and somehow they still aches for more.
posts.text:
What can a lover
do except for waiting?
What can a lover
do except for hoping?

they do both to bring back
the ruin of their existence alive,
they do both to delve into those
eyes to ruin themselves again.
and somehow they
still aches for more.
posts.explanation: The writer says a lover can only wait and hope. They do both hoping to bring back the very person who broke them, and to get lost in those eyes and be broken again. Still, they keep wanting more.

posts.displayTitle: I'll raise my hands and I'll let you decide whether I am begging or…
posts.altText: I'll raise my hands and I'll let you decide whether I am begging or praying.
posts.text:
I'll raise my hands and I'll let you
decide whether I am begging or praying.
posts.explanation: The writer will raise his hands and let the person decide if he is begging them or praying to them. He seems to say his love is so deep that the two feel the same.

posts.caption: Beautiful things
posts.displayTitle: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it
posts.altText: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it. Perhaps some desires are not born from love at all. Perhaps they are born from our inability to let beautiful things remain free.
posts.text:
What a strange thing
it is to admire a flower,
then wish to pluck it.

Perhaps some desires are
not born from love at all.
Perhaps they are born
from our inability to let
beautiful things remain free.
posts.explanation: The writer finds it strange that we see a beautiful flower and then want to pick it. He thinks some wants don't come from love at all, but from not being able to let beautiful things stay free.

posts.displayTitle: But how can I stop loving you when you are all that my heart desires?
posts.altText: But how can I stop loving you when you are all that my heart desires?
posts.text:
But how can I stop loving you when
you are all that my heart desires?
posts.explanation: The writer asks how he could ever stop loving the person when they are everything his heart wants.

posts.caption: What can they do?
posts.displayTitle: What can a lover do except for waiting?
posts.altText: What can a lover do except for waiting? What can a lover do except for hoping? they do both to bring back the ruin of their existence alive, they do both to delve into those eyes to ruin themselves again. and somehow they still aches for more.
posts.text:
What can a lover
do except for waiting?
What can a lover
do except for hoping?

they do both to bring back
the ruin of their existence alive,
they do both to delve into those
eyes to ruin themselves again.
and somehow they
still aches for more.
posts.explanation: The writer says a lover can only wait and hope. They do both hoping to bring back the very person who broke them, and to get lost in those eyes and be broken again. Still, they keep wanting more.

posts.caption: Grief
posts.displayTitle: Grief comes from the acceptance of the loss,
posts.altText: Grief comes from the acceptance of the loss, of things you never thought you would lose. To make a home around a grave called the heart is what we call existing, and all we do in that home is mourn. Nobody prepares you for losing the permanence you once believed life possessed, and perhaps that is the cruelest tragedy.
posts.text:
Grief comes from
the acceptance of the loss,
of things you never
thought you would lose.

To make a home around
a grave called the heart
is what we call existing,
and all we do in that home is mourn.

Nobody prepares you for losing the
permanence you once believed life possessed,
and perhaps that is the cruelest tragedy.
posts.explanation: Grief begins when you accept losing something you never thought you would lose. Living feels like making a home around a heart that is like a grave, and just mourning there. The cruelest part is that nobody warns you that nothing in life lasts forever.

posts.displayTitle: you are the sun, I am the sunflower.
posts.altText: you are the sun, I am the sunflower.
posts.text: you are the sun, I am the sunflower.
posts.explanation: The person is like the sun to the writer, and he is like a sunflower that always turns toward them and needs them to live.

posts.caption: Yeah
posts.displayTitle: Days have started to get shorter, it'll be night soon,
posts.altText: Days have started to get shorter, it'll be night soon, But in the darkness of the night grief knocks my door, night brings me closer to the things I spend my days trying to forget. The longer the night the Deeper the grief, deeper the grief colder the heart becomes.
posts.text:
Days have started to get shorter,
it'll be night soon,

But in the darkness of the
night grief knocks my door,

night brings me closer
to the things I spend
my days trying to forget.

The longer the night the
Deeper the grief, deeper the grief
colder the heart becomes.
posts.explanation: The days are getting shorter as winter comes. At night, grief comes to the writer and brings back the things he tries to forget all day. The longer the night, the deeper his sadness, and the colder his heart grows.

posts.caption: Ok
posts.displayTitle: It's not about who stays or who leaves.
posts.altText: It's not about who stays or who leaves. It's about for whom you stop in the middle of a prayer just to pray for them as well. Because there are people you stop asking God to bring back, yet you never stop asking God to keep them safe.
posts.text:
It's not about who
stays or who leaves.
It's about for whom
you stop in the middle
of a prayer just to pray
for them as well.

Because there are
people you stop asking
God to bring back,
yet you never stop asking
God to keep them safe.
posts.explanation: The writer says what matters is not who stays or leaves, but who you stop to pray for in the middle of your own prayer. Some people you stop asking God to bring back, but you never stop asking God to keep them safe.

posts.displayTitle: We are the fragments of what we loved.
posts.altText: We are the fragments of what we loved.
posts.text: We are the fragments of what we loved.
posts.explanation: We are made of broken pieces of the people and things we loved. What we loved stays in us, in pieces.

posts.caption: Yeah
posts.displayTitle: when god asks me what my last wish before returning to nothingness is
posts.altText: when god asks me what my last wish before returning to nothingness is. I'll ask him to let me relive my moments with you again. to be 18 again, naive and full of love, when I found my religion in those eyes. but that will be to much to ask for so I just die.
posts.text:
when god asks me
what my last wish
before returning
to nothingness is.
I'll ask him to let me relive
my moments with you again.
to be 18 again,
naive and full of love,
when I found
my religion in those eyes.
but that will be to much
to ask for so I just die.
posts.explanation: When he dies, the writer would ask God for one last wish: to live his time with the person again, to be 18, young, trusting and full of love, when their eyes were everything to him. But it feels like too much to ask, so he just dies.

writings.title: They say insomnia is a medical condition but they never speak of the…
writings.content:
They say insomnia is a medical
condition, but they never speak of
the kind that comes from long
buried trauma, the kind where your
past returns as dreams, your
dreams turn into nightmares, and
your nightmares are nothing but
recycled pieces of reality.
writings.explanation: People say not being able to sleep is a health problem, but the writer says his comes from old pain he buried long ago. That pain comes back as dreams, the dreams turn bad, and the bad dreams are just real things that happened to him.

writings.title: I kept writing all the things I had to
writings.content:
I kept writing all the things I had
to, but there was one thing I
always fumbled. I could explain
anything, any topic, any feeling,
yet I still lost my way in the
labyrinth of you. Perhaps I could
articulate the entire universe. For I
carried too much feeling to fit into
sentences, and the world simply
ran out of words to contain you.
writings.explanation: The writer can put any topic or feeling into words, maybe even the whole universe, but he always gets lost when he tries to describe the person he loves. His feelings for them are too big for sentences, and the world does not have enough words to hold them.

writings.title: You won't understand what it means to be abandoned by hope at a young…
writings.content:
You won't understand what it means to be
abandoned by hope at a young age - to see
yourself trapped. Some wounds don't bleed
they grow roots inside you, turning your
heart into a battlefield you walk through
every day. And sometimes the cruelest part
of suffering is realising you learned
endurance before you ever learned joy.
writings.explanation: The writer says others cannot understand losing hope while still young and feeling stuck. Some hurts do not show but grow deep inside, so every day feels like a fight. The saddest part is learning to put up with pain before ever learning to be happy.

writings.title: Leave me to my grief and you'll find me glowing in a different way
writings.content:
Leave me to my grief and you'll find me
glowing in a different way, for I love my
sorrow more fiercely than anything
else-and, eventually, everything I love
abandons me anyway. Ironically, even this
grief shall one day grow weary of my
presence and slip away in quiet
indifference, for even sorrow grows
fatigued by its host. The tribulations I once
embraced will forsake me as well.
writings.explanation: The writer asks to be left alone with his sadness, saying he shines in his own way there because he loves it most. But everything he loves leaves him, so he thinks even his sadness and his troubles will one day get tired of him and quietly go.

writings.title: You build entire futures in the quiet corners of your mind
writings.content:
You build entire futures in the quiet
corners of your mind, only to watch
them collapse under the weight of
reality.You mistake longing
for destiny, believing the universe
owes you what it never promised.
And in the end, you realise the
cruelest betrayal is the one you
crafted with your own hands.
And you still dare to hope!
writings.explanation: The writer says people dream up whole futures in their heads, then watch them fall apart in real life. They mistake wanting something for it being meant to be, so the worst letdown is one they made themselves. And still, he says almost in disbelief, they keep hoping.

writings.title: I have abandoned countless versions of myself just to survive the exp…
writings.content:
I have abandoned countless
versions of myself just to survive
the expectations of others. My
past selves are buried inside
me-alive. Their unrest haunts me
still, for I walk each day over the
graves I dug with my own hands.It
was I who condemned them. It
was I who buried them alive.
writings.explanation: To live up to what others expected, the writer gave up many versions of who he was. Those old selves are still alive inside him, buried, and they trouble him. He walks over their graves every day, knowing he was the one who buried them.

writings.title: I offered blood in return for pomegranate juice an unfair exchange
writings.content:
I offered blood in return for pomegranate
juice an unfair exchange I mistook for
love. For theirs was real and mine was
devotion. Maybe it wasn't their fault..
maybe it was me.. I offered too much. I
kept pouring myself out even when the
cup was already full. I mistook my
sacrifice for love and their silence for
acceptance and in the end, I was the only
one who walked away bleeding.
writings.explanation: The writer gave his whole self, something deep and costly, and got back only something that looked similar, a trade he mistook for love. He wonders if it was his fault for giving too much and taking their silence as acceptance, since he was the only one left hurt.

writings.title: You find them in everything - in the petals of flowers
writings.content:
You find them in everything - in the petals of
flowers, in passing crowds where you miss
them a little more than usual. You catch
yourself laughing at their memories, smiling
without realizing why. But when night
arrives, they become the very reason your
eyes ache with tears. It's strange how
happiness and sadness can coexist so
quietly within the same person, even when
that person no longer exists in your life.
writings.explanation: After someone leaves your life, you still see them everywhere, in flowers and in crowds, and their memory can make you smile. But at night the same memories bring tears. The writer finds it strange that happy and sad feelings can quietly live together over someone who is gone.

writings.title: You feed stray dogs as if they are your own
writings.content:
You feed stray dogs as if they are
your own. You lower your gaze when
the world turns uncomfortable. You
pray even for those who burned your
soul over the smallest things. You
can't look away when someone is in
need, and still, you go searching for
love in others when you yourself
are the very definition of it.
writings.explanation: The writer describes a gentle, kind person who feeds stray dogs, stays quiet and modest, prays even for people who hurt them, and always helps those in need. Yet this person keeps looking for love in others without seeing that they are already full of love themselves.

writings.title: The irony of love is that people fall out of love when they are toget…
writings.content:
The irony of love is that people
fall out of love when they are
together, and love more deeply
when they are apart. Strange how
togetherness has turned into a
slow erosion of what we have,
instead of the force meant to
preserve it. Funny how presence
dull what distance keeps alive.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it strange that people often stop loving each other when they are together and love more when they are apart. Being close, which should keep love safe, slowly wears it down, while being far away keeps it alive.

writings.title: It's funny how I used to be an unpaid therapist for someone
writings.content:
It's funny how I used to be
an unpaid therapist for
someone and now I myself
hang onto the thin rope
called life, only to realize that
the one who was once the
patient is the very reason
that rope began to fray.
writings.explanation: The writer once listened to and helped someone through their problems, asking nothing back. Now he is barely holding on to life himself, and he sees that the same person he once helped is the reason his hold is wearing thin.

writings.title: You know, the year is ending, and it's funny how time asks for reflec…
writings.content:
You know, the year is ending, and it’s funny
how time asks for reflection as if everyone
survived gently. I didn’t grow this year,
I endured it. I lost things I never thought
I’d have to explain, learned lessons I never
asked for, and kept moving not because
I healed, but because stopping was never an
option. Maybe that’s what this year
leaves me with not clarity or closure,
just the knowledge that I’m still here,
and that somehow had a cost.
writings.explanation: As the year ends, the writer says he did not grow, he just got through it. He lost things and learned hard lessons he never wanted, and kept going only because he could not stop. The year leaves him only knowing he is still here, and that this cost him something.

writings.title: I saw the "moon" in her eyes
writings.content: I saw the "moon" in her eyes
writings.explanation: The writer found her eyes bright and beautiful, like looking at the moon.

writings.title: Funny how everything I love now starts with "I used to.
writings.content:
Funny how everything I love now
starts with “I used to.”
writings.explanation: The writer notices, with a sad smile, that all the things he loves now belong to his past.

writings.title: You'll always want to leave and I'll always try to stop you
writings.content:
You’ll always want to leave and I’ll always try to stop you

Ye
Dil
Sambhal
Toh
Le zara

Toh
Abh
Na
Mujhko
Tokna
writings.explanation: The writer says the other person will always want to leave, and he will always try to stop them. The Hindi lines seem to ask for a moment to steady the heart, and then ask not to be stopped or held back anymore.

writings.title: It's funny how people glorify leaving as their love language,
writings.content:
It’s funny how people glorify leaving
as their love language, when the
whole point of love was to hold on
until the very last moment of your
breath. Somewhere along the way,
endurance became weakness and
staying started to feel like a crime.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it strange that people now praise walking away as their way of loving. He believes love was meant to be about holding on until your last breath, but somehow staying has come to look weak, even wrong.

writings.title: When I die, come with flowers
writings.content:
When I die, come with flowers
not because death asks for rituals but out of habit

and if you find yourself wondering
which ones I liked,
understand that the question no longer matters.

Flowers were never the point—
they were only a detail, the way love remembers small preferences.

I loved them because they reminded me of you.

and if you ask whether I loved them or you,
the answer is simple—I loved both in the
same quiet way things are loved right before
they stop meaning anything.
writings.explanation: The writer asks the person he loves to bring flowers when he dies, just out of habit. Which ones he liked will not matter; he only loved flowers because they reminded him of that person. He loved both quietly, the way you love things just before they stop mattering.

writings.title: If ocean could know jealousy, he would drown in it
writings.content:
If ocean could know jealousy,
he would drown in it
while looking at her eyes
for the amount of depth it holds.
writings.explanation: The writer says her eyes are so deep that even the ocean, if it could feel, would be overcome with jealousy of them.

writings.title: But God, when no one has ruined me whom do I blame more than myself?
writings.content:
But God,
whom do I blame
when no one has ruined me
more than myself?
writings.explanation: The writer asks God who he can blame for being ruined, since no one has hurt him more than he has hurt himself.

writings.title: And still I ask, is this grief proof that I once lived honestly?
writings.content:
And still I ask, is this grief proof that I once lived honestly?

Or is it merely the consequence
of my own foolish hunger—

for something pure in a
world that does not promise
purity?
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if his deep sadness shows that he once lived honestly. Or is it just the price of foolishly wanting something pure in a world that never promised anything pure?

writings.title: When you burn me, all you'll smell is abandonment.
writings.content:
When you burn me,
all you’ll smell is abandonment.
writings.explanation: The writer says that when his body is burned after he dies, all that will come out is the hurt of being left by people, because that hurt fills him completely.

writings.title: Isn't the sunrise beautiful
writings.content:
Isn't the sunrise beautiful

A soul that has suffered enough learns to see beauty
not only in hope (sunrise) but also in endings (sunset).

Isn’t the sunset beautiful...
writings.explanation: A person who has suffered enough learns to find beauty not only in hope and new beginnings, like the sunrise, but also in endings, like the sunset.

writings.title: You don't need to be full to be loved
writings.content: " You don’t need to be full to be loved "
writings.explanation: The writer says you do not have to be whole or complete for someone to love you.

writings.title: But where do you return after being Abandoned?
writings.content:
But where do you return after being Abandoned?
But where do you return
ABANDONED by you
Return but where?
I have been abandoned
I called you Home.
Where does a heart go
After being abandoned by HOME
writings.explanation: The writer called someone his home, and they left him. He keeps asking where a heart can go when the very place it called home has abandoned it.

writings.title: And all I am is an actor,
writings.content:
And all I am is an
actor,
destined to perform —
for the rest of my life,
even when no one is looking.
writings.explanation: The writer feels he is always acting and putting on a show, and that he will keep doing it his whole life, even when he is alone.

writings.title: There is a guilt conscience in loving too deeply
writings.content:
There is a guilt conscience in loving too deeply
when you know it won't come back to you– and
you give and give till you have nothing left of
yourself then again you only realise this
while looking at your own ruins because in love
you are too blind to see your destruction. haha
writings.explanation: The writer says loving too much, knowing it will not be returned, brings a kind of guilt. You give until nothing of you is left, and only see the damage later, because love blinds you. He ends with a bitter little laugh.

writings.title: I have divided myself into quiet, necessary layers—
writings.content:
I have divided myself into quiet,
necessary layers—

from a certain fear of being seen whole
for I have learned that the closer one
comes to the center of a man, the more
unbearable he is, even to himself

and so I leave something in reserve—
hidden even from my own understanding

and the fact that the more someone
tries to cut open through me, the more
they cry...
writings.explanation: The writer has split himself into layers, afraid of being seen whole. He thinks the deeper you get into a person, the harder he is to bear, even for himself. So he hides a part even from himself, and, like cutting an onion, whoever cuts deeper into him ends up crying.

writings.title: everything in me leans a little closer—
writings.content:
everything in me leans a little closer—
when it’s you,
as if my [heart image] already knows where it belongs.
writings.explanation: When the writer is near the person he loves, everything in him is drawn closer to them, as if his heart already knows it belongs with them.

writings.title: All these acts, all these pretendings—
writings.content:
All these acts,
all these pretendings—
only to hide how deeply I feel.
writings.explanation: The writer says all his acting and pretending is only a way to hide how deeply he feels.

writings.title: Grief, grief and an endless ocean of it—
writings.content:
Grief, grief and an endless ocean of it—

so much of it that I am unable to tell any of it,

I drown every night in the endless
depth of the unseen regrets I have,

endless grief I am—

now I get confused is it me or the grief?
writings.explanation: The writer is so full of sadness that he cannot even put it into words. Every night he sinks into hidden regrets, and the grief has become so much a part of him that he can no longer tell himself and the grief apart.

writings.title: When my body decomposes and the bugs and maggots reach my heart
writings.content:
When my body decomposes and the bugs
and maggots reach my heart, all they will
find are the ways I have been abandoned
through, they’ll find loneliness, grief and
memories... unanswered prayers resting
like dust in my chest, words I never said
stitched into silence, nights that
stretched endlessly without a hand to
hold, dreams that withered before they
could become real and a love that
stayed... even when no one did.
writings.explanation: The writer imagines his body rotting after death. In his heart, the bugs would find only the hurt of being left, loneliness, sad memories, unanswered prayers, unsaid words, long lonely nights and dreams that died, along with a love that stayed even though no one stayed with him.

writings.title: What do I relate myself to?
writings.content:
What do I relate myself to?
Perhaps I am a moth drawn towards a flame, for I knew it would burn me,

or perhaps I am the flame itself,
burning through all the emotions of mine I have called moths

And if you ask me whether I loved it or not,I did—
enough to let it burn me whole...

So much that I sacrificed myself at the altar of love.
But did I suffer?
I did—

All these dreadful thoughts turned my love into a pyre,
enough to burn these moths for eternity in endless suffering.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if he is a moth flying to a fire he knows will burn him, or the fire itself, burning up his own feelings. He loved enough to let it burn him whole, and he suffered; dark thoughts turned that love into a funeral fire that keeps burning his feelings forever.

writings.title: Yesterday, We were together
writings.content:
Yesterday,
We were together

Today,
I mourn in grief, fooling myself
with your presence.

Tomorrow,
Perhaps I'll be spared from
this grief you left behind,
I'll be a fool again or maybe
I'll be full again...
writings.explanation: Yesterday the writer and the person he loved were together. Today he grieves and fools himself by pretending they are still there. Tomorrow he might be free of this pain, though he is not sure if he will be fooled again or feel whole again.

writings.title: It's funny how months have passed… it's April now—
writings.content:
It’s funny how months have passed...
it's April now—

and I still lie to myself about your love,
deceiving my own heart.

December will come again...
and I’ll still be waiting for you.
writings.explanation: Months have passed and it is April, yet the writer still lies to himself that the person loves him. He knows December will come again and he will still be waiting for them.

writings.title: We spend our lives explaining ourselves in fragments, in half sentenc…
writings.content:
We spend our lives explaining ourselves
in fragments, in half sentences and
silences, hoping someone will gather the
pieces and call it whole. But people do
not listen to understand, they listen to
recognize something of themselves. And
if you do not resemble their wounds,
they will never recognize yours.
writings.explanation: The writer says we show who we are only in bits and pieces, hoping someone will put them together and understand us fully. But people listen mainly to find themselves in what we say, so if your pain does not look like theirs, they will never see it.

writings.title: perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
writings.content:
perhaps the cruelest realization is this—
that most people do not intend to hurt you.

They simply choose themselves in moments
where you hoped they would choose you
And that difference,
so small in action,
becomes immeasurable in consequence.
writings.explanation: The writer says the hardest thing to accept is that most people do not mean to hurt you. They just pick themselves at the moments you hoped they would pick you, and that small choice ends up hurting more than can be measured.

writings.title: Out of everyone— who could have left me, why were you the only one?
writings.content:
Out of everyone—
who could have left me,
why were you the only one?
writings.explanation: The writer asks why, out of everyone who could have left him, this person was the only one who did.

writings.title: There is a strange kind of honesty in what decays—
writings.content:
There is a strange kind of honesty in what decays—

When flesh forgets its shape and time begins to
speak through rot, nothing pretends anymore.

The heart that once held warmth, promises, and trembling
hope becomes just another hollow space with nothingness,
no different from bone or dust.

and yet, I wonder...

if someone were to reach inside what
remains of me,

would they still find traces of you carved deeper
than the veins themselves?
writings.explanation: The writer says rotting is honest, because a dead body no longer pretends. A heart that once held warmth and hope becomes just empty space, like bone or dust. Still, he wonders if someone looking inside what is left of him would find the person he loved, marked deep in him.

writings.title: Oh, you loved the rain—
writings.content:
Oh, you loved the rain—

but look how funny it is, that I came into your
life like the clouds which never rained,

even after covering the whole sky...
writings.explanation: The person the writer loved adored the rain. Sadly, he says, he came into their life like clouds that cover the whole sky but never rain, filling their life without ever giving them what they loved.

writings.title: I felt it not in sorrow— but in absence.
writings.content:
I felt it not in sorrow—
but in absence.

In the way joy no longer reached me
in the way even pain seemed distant,
as though it belonged to someone else.

And it was then, not in despair but in a kind of cold clarity,

not as a question anymore but as something
I had already become
what I am is half life and half death.
writings.explanation: The writer did not feel his pain as sadness but as emptiness: joy no longer reached him, and even pain felt far away, like someone else's. In a calm, cold moment he understood that he had already become half alive and half dead.

writings.title: You see, the most terrifying thing is not that I suffer, but that I o…
writings.content:
You see, the most terrifying thing is not that I suffer,
but that I observe—

I watch myself exist the way one watches
a stranger through a window,
recognizing the gestures but feeling no ownership of them.

My voice sounds familiar—

my thoughts even resemble my own,
and yet there is always that thin, unbridgeable distance.
writings.explanation: The writer says the scariest part is not his suffering but that he watches himself live, like watching a stranger through a window. His voice and thoughts seem like his own, yet there is always a thin gap between him and his own life that he cannot cross.

writings.title: You asked me to find someone better, but how could I—
writings.content:
You asked me to find someone better,
but how could I—

how do I take these rings I shaped for your fingers
and pretend they were meant for someone else

how do I call it love again
when it still carries your name in silence
writings.explanation: The person he loved told the writer to find someone better, but he cannot. He made his love, like rings, to fit only them, and he cannot pretend it was meant for anyone else, because his love still quietly carries their name.

writings.title: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me,
writings.content:
Greif, chaos, and an endless noise
of things that rots within me ,

I die everyday a little more than yesterday,

Perhaps I am more dead than alive
each passing day..
writings.explanation: Grief, confusion and constant noise are rotting inside the writer. He feels he dies a little more each day, until he seems more dead than alive.

writings.title: What I am is me— just the leftovers from yesterday.
writings.content:
What I am is me—
just the leftovers from yesterday.
writings.explanation: The writer feels that who he is now is only what is left over from yesterday, the scraps of his past self.

writings.title: Because some loves do not die with the body.
writings.content:
Because some loves do not die
with the body. They linger,
quietly decomposing, turning
into something nameless,
something that no longer hurts
the way it used to. but never
truly leaves either.
writings.explanation: The writer says some love does not end when a person dies. It stays on, slowly changing into something without a name; it no longer hurts the way it did, but it never really goes away.

writings.title: when I die— what will you raise my grave for?
writings.content:
when I die—
what will you raise my grave for?
To honor a man who survived his decay,
yet never escaped his grief?
Or to admit that all I ever was
ends here,
beneath this grave my entirety?
writings.explanation: The writer asks what his grave will stand for once he dies. Will it honor a man who lived through falling apart but never got free of his sadness, or will it simply mark that everything he was ends there?

writings.title: My grief is the only thing that has stayed with me over time
writings.content:
My grief is the only thing
that has stayed with me over time,
so if I start loving you, grief...
"will you leave me too?"
writings.explanation: Sadness is the only thing that has stayed with the writer over the years. So if he starts to love his grief, he fears it will leave him too, like the things he loved before.

writings.title: God— How many more trials How many more provings
writings.content:
God—
How many more trials
How many more provings
till I am worthy enough...
writings.explanation: The writer asks God how many more tests and hard times he must go through before he is finally good enough.

writings.title: Poetry exists even before it's written by the poet
writings.content:
Poetry exists even
before it's written by
the poet and every
poetry, poet has a
story of its own.
writings.explanation: The writer says a poem already exists before the poet writes it down, and every poem, like every poet, has its own story.

writings.title: A soul is born without a name for faith
writings.content:
A soul is born without a name for faith,
yet the world is quick to give it one.
What stays—
though,
Is not what is assigned but what is felt.
In the end,
whatever brings peace quietly becomes your faith
even a love,.
even an absence.
writings.explanation: The writer says a person is born without any religion, but the world quickly gives them one. What really stays is not the faith you are given but what you feel, so whatever brings you peace quietly becomes your faith, even a love, or even someone's absence.

writings.title: What doesn't kill you leaves you unable to breathe in the middle of t…
writings.content:
What doesn’t kill you
leaves you unable to breathe
in the middle of the night,
lets you feel the tremors,
lets you know how easily you can be replaced,
and what doesn’t kill you
kills you a little more every day than yesterday.
writings.explanation: People say what does not kill you makes you stronger, but the writer disagrees. It leaves you unable to breathe at night, shaking, and aware of how easily you can be replaced, and it slowly kills you a little more each day.

writings.title: I yearn for you— so where are you now?
writings.content:
I yearn for you—
so where are you now?
All those promises of forever turned into dust
and I into ashes
for the fire you burned in my chest
still lies there inextinguishable...
writings.explanation: The writer longs for the person he loved and asks where they are now. Their promises of forever have turned to dust, and he has burned down to ashes, because the fire they lit in his heart still cannot be put out.

writings.title: I could have loved you— with a kind of devotion that ruins a man
writings.content:
I could have loved you—
with a kind of devotion
that ruins a man,
that strips him bare before himself.
writings.explanation: The writer says he could have loved this person with a devotion so complete that it would have destroyed him and left him with nothing to hide, even from himself.

writings.title: The tragedy is— you begin to measure your worth in their presence
writings.content:
The tragedy is—
you begin to measure your worth in their presence
and worse,
in their absence and once that begins,
there is no dignity left in you only
dependence dressed up as devotion.
And that is a point of no return in love
writings.explanation: The writer says the sad thing is when you start judging your own value by whether someone is with you or not. Once that starts, you lose your self-respect and simply depend on them while calling it love, and there is no coming back from that.

writings.title: Must we understand all— to be understood the way we desire?
writings.content:
Must we understand all—
to be understood the way we desire?
Or should we understand all,
just to acknowledge that
no one can ever truly understand us?
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if we must understand everything in order to be understood the way we want. Or does understanding everything only teach us that no one can ever truly understand us?

writings.title: It is strange— isn't it?
writings.content:
It is strange—
isn’t it?
How a [heart image] can hold so much
and still feel like
it has nothing at all.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it strange that a heart can be holding so much and still feel completely empty.

writings.title: They say we are the museum of things we love
writings.content:
They say we are the museum of things we love
but I am The rage fuelled by
my father's destruction
I am the sorrow of my mother's wounds
I am my lover's abandonment,
the silence it left behind
I am my friend's betrayal,
the faithlessness it took with it.
"I am every ounce of it, still held intact."
writings.explanation: People say we are made of the things we love, but the writer says he is made of his hurts: anger from his father's ruin, sorrow from his mother's pain, the silence a lover left behind, and a friend's betrayal. He still carries every bit of it.

writings.title: I have stared at my ceiling—far more than I've dared to meet another'…
writings.content:
I have stared at my ceiling—
far more than I've dared to meet another's eyes.
Hours dissolve into nights as I lie there,
scrutinising the void above me,
attempting to fill its blankness with
thoughts too heavy to speak aloud.
writings.explanation: The writer has spent more time staring at his ceiling than looking into other people's eyes. He lies awake for hours into the night, trying to fill that blank space with thoughts too heavy to say out loud.

writings.title: And maybe that is what we are—
writings.content:
And maybe that is what we are—
fragments pretending to be whole,
carrying oceans within us
yet thirsting for something
we cannot even name.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks maybe we are all broken pieces pretending to be whole. We hold huge feelings inside, like oceans, yet still feel thirsty for something we cannot even name.

writings.title: I have left a piece of myself in everything I have loved,
writings.content:
I have left a piece of myself
in everything I have loved,
And here I stand before myself,
with nothing left inside me.
My heart aches to be full again but how can
I full again without being a fool again?
I am too understanding now to be
fooled again to be full with emotions again.
writings.explanation: The writer has left a part of himself in everything he loved, and now he feels empty inside. He wants to feel full again, but he fears that means being fooled again, and he understands too much now to let himself be fooled.

writings.title: Tell me, is it not absurd?
writings.content:
Tell me, is it not absurd?
To crave permanence in a world
that refuses to grant it—
and yet to sabotage it
the moment it dares to appear.
There is, within me,
a contradiction so profound
that I cannot resolve it,
I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch,
as though kindness itself were a prelude to loss.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it strange that he wants things to last in a world where nothing does, yet he ruins them as soon as they show up. He longs to be held but tenses up when touched, as if kindness always comes just before a loss.

writings.title: Perhaps this is the true nature of my curse—
writings.content:
Perhaps this is the true nature of my curse—
not that I am abandoned,
but that I have come to expect it with such
conviction that I unknowingly assist in its arrival.
A silent accomplice to my own solitude
I carry the curse of being abandoned.
writings.explanation: The writer says his real curse is not being left, but expecting it so strongly that, without meaning to, he helps it happen. In a quiet way, he helps make himself alone.

writings.title: abandonment is an orange…
writings.content:
abandonment is an orange...

the peels are
the threshold
the line between
staying and leaving

I'll peel it unknowingly,
making it easier for you to abandon me

until there is nothing left for you to do

and once I peel it,
you are free to ~~leave~~ eat it
writings.explanation: The writer says being left is like an orange. The peel is the line between staying and leaving, and he peels it himself without knowing, making it easy for the other person to go. Once it is peeled, they can leave, or simply take and enjoy what he opened up.

writings.title: And so I remain—neither wholly alone, nor ever truly accompanied…
writings.content:
And so I remain—
neither wholly alone,
nor ever truly accompanied...
standing at the threshold of every connection,
already mourning its end.
writings.explanation: The writer feels he is never fully alone but never truly with anyone either. At the start of every new friendship or love, he is already sad about how it will end.

writings.title: I used to adore paradoxes, until I accidentally became one
writings.content:
I used to adore paradoxes,
until I accidentally became one.
I built a maze out of my own feelings
and never found the way out.
Perhaps I named that trap love...
my own Labyrinth, and I the Minotaur guarding it.
writings.explanation: The writer used to love things that go against themselves, until he became one. He built a trap out of his own feelings, maybe calling it love, and got lost in it, like the monster in the old Greek story who guards a maze he can never leave.

writings.title: They say what cannot be forgotten comes to your dreams,
writings.content:
They say what cannot be forgotten
comes to your dreams,
maybe it's true,
because the ache of losing what you once believed
was yours is far beyond what words can explain.
Maybe to soothe that pain,
the mind projects it into our dreams,
letting us live with what we lost for eternity.
writings.explanation: The writer says the things we cannot forget come back in our dreams. Losing something you believed was yours hurts beyond words, so perhaps the mind shows it in dreams to ease the pain, letting us keep living with what we lost forever.

writings.title: I hope—I hoped—I'm still hoping..
writings.content:
I hope—I hoped—I’m still hoping..
god— the word is tearing mee apart.
Hopehopehopehope—until it breaks open
like a seizure in my chest.
I hoped so hard it started screaming back at me.
I hoped till it warped, till it twisted
the knife inside my chest, till it turned on me.
And now it’s just HOP E H O P E H O P E—
a mess I can’t clean out of my head.
I hoped-and that was my first mistake
I hoped until the echo of it scraped against my ribs.
And now hope feels like a wound I keep touching,
just to remind myself it's still bleeding...
