writings.explanation: The writer keeps hoping, over and over, until hope stops helping and starts hurting him. It twists inside him like a knife and fills his head with noise. He now sees hoping as his first mistake, a wound he keeps touching just to feel that it still hurts.

writings.title: Sometimes the greatest actors aren't the ones on the screens
writings.content:
Sometimes the greatest actors aren't
the ones on the screens ,

they are into the crowd
pretending to be fine.
writings.explanation: The writer says the best actors are often not on screen but ordinary people in the crowd, pretending they are fine.

writings.title: I hope no one ever uncovers the desolate feelings abandoned long ago
writings.content:
I hope no one ever uncovers
the desolate feelings abandoned long ago,
for the frightened child I once was still sits
there shivering in the shadows I left behind.
Those memories remain sealed
like a room no one should enter.
Every now and then, the door rattles
and I keep walking past it,
pretending I don't hear the trembling inside.
writings.explanation: The writer hopes no one ever finds the lonely feelings he pushed away long ago, where the scared child he once was is still shaking. He keeps those memories locked like a room, and when they stir, he walks past and pretends not to notice.

writings.title: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions now lying in…
writings.content:
I wish I could tell you that
all the abandoned emotions
now lying in the coldest part
of my heart once belonged to you.
How the colourful flowers
that once bloomed for you
have now grown into thorny vines
that pierce my heart instead.
I hope that someday, when you come back,
I'll have enough flowers left to offer you
not just trembling hands numbed by cold.
writings.explanation: The writer wishes he could tell the person he loved that the left-behind feelings in his heart were once for them. The love that grew for them has turned sharp and hurts him. He hopes that if they return, he will still have some love left to give, not just numb, shaking hands.

writings.title: I came home to rest from an unfair world,
writings.content:
I came home to rest from an unfair world,
but the home itself doesn’t
feel like home without you in it.
I lay on the bed to rest,
but the unjust of being betrayed by the world
feels like termites crawling beneath my skin,
eating the flesh the world itself
has already left to rot.
So I just lie on the floor instead,
lying myself with your warmth,
yet shivering with the ache of losing you
writings.explanation: The writer came home to rest from an unfair world, but home does not feel like home without the person he lost. The hurt of being betrayed makes his bed feel like bugs eating under his skin, so he lies on the floor, comforting himself with their warmth while shaking from losing them.

writings.title: Grief has learned my shape so well
writings.content:
Grief has learned my shape so well
it fits into me perfectly,
as if it has become an undeniable part of me
that I no longer refuse.
It’s already running through my veins.
I just know—
wherever I may go,
I’ll be left with it.
writings.explanation: The writer says grief knows him so well that it fits him perfectly and has become a part of him he no longer fights. It runs through his whole body, and he knows that wherever he goes, it will stay with him.

writings.title: When I'm about to die and my mind begins to project the best moments…
writings.content:
When I’m about to die and my mind begins to
project the best moments of my life,
I hope it isn’t filled with the endless grief
I’ve carried almost all my days.
I hope instead it finds you,
your hand in mine, And us in the rain.
And maybe...
it will be kind enough to create a few
non existing ones like being loved by my parents.
writings.explanation: The writer hopes that as he dies, the best moments his mind replays will not be his lifelong grief, but the person he loves holding his hand in the rain. Maybe it will even make up moments that never happened, like being loved by his parents.

writings.title: I was forced into adulthood so prematurely
writings.content:
I was forced into adulthood so prematurely

that now even the simplest gestures
of childhood feel foreign to me,

as if something essential had
already withered in me,

as if I am merely acting out a role
whose truth was denied to me.
writings.explanation: The writer had to grow up far too early, so now even simple childlike things feel strange to him. It is as if something important in him dried up, and he is only playing a part in a life he was never allowed to truly have.

writings.title: They gave me poison, and they gave me my memories.
writings.content:
They gave me poison,
and they gave me my memories.
Without hesitation,
I chose the latter..

yet I died, How clever of them.
writings.explanation: The writer was offered either poison or his memories, and he chose his memories. But the memories killed him anyway, and he bitterly notes that the people who offered them must have known they would hurt just as much.

writings.title: My heart reeks of memories from the past.
writings.content:
My heart reeks of memories from the past.
For I turned myself into a crime scene,
each part of me revealing a different crime.
Crime? The crime of holding something too dear,
of loving while expecting,
and a crime that can never be investigated,
for it holds more paradoxes than anything else.
So I ask you, are you also a part of that crime?
writings.explanation: The writer feels his heart is full of past memories, like a crime scene where every part shows a different wrong. His crimes were holding something too dear and loving while expecting love back, things too confusing to ever solve. He asks if the person he speaks to was part of it too.

writings.title: Memories are destined to return,
writings.content:
Memories are destined to return,
piercing through your heart with a cruelty
nothing else can replicate and still,
you find yourself slipping back into the very
emotions that once drowned you.
It's strange how the past resurrects itself, wearing
the perfume of what you once longed for.
And stranger still,
how your soul leans into the pain,
as if hoping it will finally feel like home.
writings.explanation: The writer says memories always come back and hurt the heart like nothing else. Yet you still fall back into the same feelings that once overwhelmed you. The past returns smelling like what you once wanted, and strangely, your soul leans into the pain, hoping it will finally feel like home.

writings.title: The thorns made me bleed so much that the roses
writings.content:
"The thorns made me bleed
so much that the
roses eventually started
smelling like you."
writings.explanation: The writer was hurt so much by love's sharp side that even its sweet side, the roses, came to remind him of the person who hurt him.

writings.title: Leave me at my grief and you'll find me glowing in a different way,
writings.content:
Leave me at my grief and you’ll find me
glowing in a different way,
for I love my sorrow more fiercely than anything else
and inevitably,
everything I love abandons me anyway.
writings.explanation: The writer asks to be left alone with his sadness, where he shines in his own way, because he loves his sorrow more than anything. And in the end, everything he loves leaves him anyway.

writings.title: I have divided myself into necessary layers—
writings.content:
I have divided myself into necessary layers—

from a certain fear of being seen whole for
I have learned that the closer one comes to
the center of a man, the more unbearable he
is, even to himself...

and so I leave something in reserve—
hidden even from my own understanding

and the fact that the more someone tries to
cut open through me, the more they cry...
writings.explanation: Afraid of being seen completely, the writer has split himself into layers, believing the closer anyone gets to a person's center, the harder he is to bear, even for himself. He hides a part even from himself, and, like with an onion, whoever cuts deeper into him ends up crying.

writings.title: Mother, I am that dust from the corners of the walls
writings.content:
Mother,
I am that dust from the corners of the walls
that goes unnoticed by you.

Mother,
did you know my presence
before father reached his hands
out to clean my entirety?
writings.explanation: The writer tells his mother he is like the dust in the corners of the walls that she never notices. He asks whether she even knew he was there before his father reached out to wipe all of him away.

writings.title: There are things I couldn't have lived without,
writings.content:
There are things I couldn’t have lived without,
there are things I was never meant to lose,
ruins I never asked to inherit.
But I was mistaken.
What stayed with me was never what I wanted,
just fragments of those ruins,
the unnecessary weight
of what I once thought was everything,
carved deep into my bones
only because I lacked the will to refuse.
writings.explanation: The writer thought some things were too important to live without or to lose. He was wrong: what stayed was never what he wanted, only broken pieces he never asked for and the heavy weight of what once meant everything, stuck deep in him because he lacked the strength to refuse.

writings.title: Everything I did was in half, half efforts,
writings.content:
Everything I did was in half, half efforts,
half hearted studies,
half life and half death,
as if doing things halfway would
leave me something to hope for more,
but my love for you was full,
so tell me,
why did you leave me,
leaving me half, still hoping for more?
writings.explanation: The writer did everything halfway, his work, his studies, even living, as if leaving things half done would give him something more to hope for. But he loved this person fully, so he asks why they left, leaving him only half, still hoping for more.

writings.title: Someone once taught me that there is a strange kind of violence in si…
writings.content:
Someone once taught me that there
is a strange kind of violence in silence,
the kind that leaves you hanging between an
unfinished story and a thousand unanswered paradoxes
A silence that doesn't break,
doesn't explain,
doesn't close the chapter,
it just leaves you suspended in
the ache of not knowing.
Maybe that's why silence feels less like
peace and more like a punishment.
writings.explanation: The writer says silence can hurt like violence. When someone goes quiet without explaining or ending things, you are left stuck, not knowing what happened. So silence feels less like peace and more like a punishment.

writings.title: There is something strange about memories,
writings.content:
There is something strange about memories,
about they don't leave,
and they don't get replaced.
They just sit quietly at the core of your existence,
like old clothes you no longer
wear but still cannot let go of.
Maybe we keep them because letting go would
mean admitting that time moved on without us.
Or maybe because we're hesitant to let
someone else have what once belonged to us.
writings.explanation: The writer says memories never leave and are never replaced. They stay deep inside, like old clothes you no longer wear but cannot throw away. He thinks we keep them because letting go would mean time moved on without us, or because we don't want anyone else to have what was once ours.

writings.title: I am convinced that nothing stays forever—
writings.content:
I am convinced that nothing stays forever—
not feelings,
not even the moments we swear
we’ll remember for a lifetime.
Everything we try to hold eventually
slips through our fingers like sand.
And in the process of trying to become something new,
like sand we raise our temperature to turn
into something else we eventually become glass,
and a glass too is meant to be broken.
writings.explanation: The writer believes nothing lasts, not feelings and not even moments we promise to remember. Everything slips away like sand. When we try to change into someone new, we are like sand heated into glass, and glass, too, will one day break.

writings.title: Maybe the only way I can bleed is through words
writings.content:
Maybe the only way I can bleed
is through words and maybe
I do not bleed red anymore
it is just ink
writings.explanation: The writer says the only way he can let his pain out is by writing. His hurt no longer comes out as blood; it comes out as ink on the page.

writings.title: There are three stages of existence—
writings.content:
There are three stages of existence—
to be born,
to truly live,
and to die.
But people rarely reach the second
and are left as hollow shells,
"so empty" that even death feels like nothing.
And if you ask me whether I am alive or dead,
know that I have survived just enough
to mourn the grief of your loss every day
writings.explanation: The writer says life has three steps: being born, really living, and dying. Most people never really live, so they feel so empty that even death means nothing. He himself is only alive enough to grieve, every day, the person he lost.

writings.title: If you take away all the night from within me,
writings.content:
If you take away all the night
from within me, will I still,
ever be able to outshine the light of her eyes,
I saw when she looked at me?
writings.explanation: The writer asks whether, if all the darkness inside him were taken away, he could ever shine brighter than the light he saw in her eyes when she looked at him. He seems to feel nothing in him could ever match that look.

writings.title: You looked at me with blurry eyes,
writings.content:
You looked at me with blurry eyes,
holding out a bouquet of flowers,
asking if we could start it
all over again in the name of love.
But I stayed silent because
silence is the only weapon I have left,
now that I no longer have the
voice to speak from six feet under.
writings.explanation: Someone he loved comes to him with teary eyes and flowers, asking to start over. But the writer is already dead and buried, so he cannot speak. Silence is all he has left, and it is his only answer.

writings.title: These days the world appears uncannily altered,
writings.content:
These days the world appears uncannily altered,
as though someone has
surreptitiously stole the colour
from everything I once found radiant.
And they say beauty lies
in the eyes of the beholder,
but maybe I've become too
colourblind to understand its meaning...
writings.explanation: The writer says the world now looks strangely different, as if someone secretly took the color out of everything he used to find bright and lovely. People say beauty depends on who is looking, but he fears he can no longer see beauty at all.

writings.title: I smoked love as though it were a cigarette,
writings.content:
I smoked love as though it were a cigarette,
and believe me,
it devastates the lungs far more
mercilessly than any tobacco ever could.
It constricts your breath,
wringing your chest until
air itself becomes a luxury.
Even cancer feels almost courteous in comparison.
And still,
addicted to its ruin,
I lit it up anyway.
writings.explanation: The writer compares love to smoking. He says love hurt him worse than cigarettes ever could, squeezing his chest until he could barely breathe. Even cancer seems gentle next to it. Still, he was hooked and kept going back to it, knowing it would ruin him.

writings.title: It's May again, and I wonder may I ever see you again?
writings.content:
It’s May again, and I wonder
may I ever see you again?
and if I may,
will you be the same again
may I fall in love with you again
may it still be you
or may it just be a memory
wearing your face once more, again...
writings.explanation: It is May again, and the writer wonders if he will ever see the person he loved again. If he does, will they be the same? Will he fall for them again, or will it only be a memory that looks like them?

writings.title: I have lost my perception of time while waiting for you.
writings.content:
I have lost my perception of time
while waiting for you.
They said time would heal everything,
but I lost time,
lost to time,
lost in time itself...
You buried me in it... tell me,
what year is it? when did I die?
writings.explanation: While waiting for the person he loved, the writer lost all sense of time. People said time would heal him, but he only got lost in it. He feels as if they buried him in that waiting, and he asks what year it is and when he died.

writings.title: What is this curse I carry?
writings.content:
What is this curse I carry?
To be abandoned by everything I love,
or to love so deeply that I forget how to stay?
Why does every propinquity turn into distance,
every promise into silence,
and every “forever” into something that leaves?
Is it fate, or is it something in me
that holds too tightly.
until everything slips away?
Like hands that grip,
but instead of hands, it’s the neck...
writings.explanation: The writer asks why everything he loves leaves him: closeness turns to distance, promises to silence, and forever never lasts. He wonders if it is fate, or if he holds on so tightly that his love chokes things, like hands around a neck, until they slip away.

writings.title: Time doesn't heal anything,
writings.content:
Time doesn’t heal anything,
it makes you rot,
decays every memory,
it only moves on while dragging you with it.
and still,
we live on with the decay
of our rotting bodies,
surviving but at what cost?
writings.explanation: The writer says time does not heal pain. It makes everything rot, wears away memories, and drags people along with it. We keep living with this slow decay, and he asks whether just surviving is worth what it costs.

writings.title: Strange how love learns to arrive only after absence becomes permanen…
writings.content:
Strange how love learns to arrive
only after absence becomes permanent,
like the flowers on my grave
when I didn’t even receive
one when I was alive,
as if a heartbeat matters only once it stops,
as if I only mattered when I was dead.
writings.explanation: The writer says love often shows up only after someone is gone for good. People bring flowers to his grave, though he never got a single flower while alive. It feels as if a person only matters once their heart stops.

writings.title: love and separation exist as two sides of the same coin,
writings.content:
love and separation
exist as two sides of the same coin,
one always carrying the shadow of the other.
as if every promise already knows its ending.
as if every closeness rehearses its goodbye
and we still call it love,
knowing what it costs...
writings.explanation: The writer says love and parting always come together, like two sides of one coin. Every promise seems to already know how it will end, and every closeness is already practicing its goodbye. Still, people call it love, knowing how much it will cost them.

writings.title: I am a miserable being who sabotages his own happiness
writings.content:
I am a miserable being
who sabotages his own happiness
for others and calls it love,
and somehow I convinced myself
that this slow undoing was devotion,
that losing myself piece by piece
was the purest form of staying.
writings.explanation: The writer calls himself miserable because he gives up his own happiness for others and calls it love. He fooled himself into thinking that slowly falling apart, losing himself bit by bit, was the truest way to stay loyal.

writings.title: words meant to be weightless sink like anchors in the heart
writings.content:
words meant to be weightless
sink like anchors in the heart while feelings
so heavy often float away unheard.
we guard ourselves from emotions
yet let sentences walk in barefoot,
leaving fingerprints on parts of us
that were never meant to be touched.
writings.explanation: The writer says careless words can sink deep in the heart like heavy anchors, while big, heavy feelings often drift away unheard. We protect ourselves from feelings, but let words walk right in, and they leave marks on soft, private parts of us that no one should touch.

writings.title: I stand just to stand till I start to crawl,
writings.content:
I stand just to stand
till I start to crawl,
I feel like falling
but you won’t let me fall,
I call it love or just the need to fall,
I fall, I’m bound to fall... to lose it all,
I just had to say it all.
writings.explanation: The writer is barely holding himself up and feels close to collapse. He wants to fall, but the person he loves will not let him. He cannot tell if this is love or just a need to give in, and he feels sure he will fall and lose everything. He just needed to say it.

writings.title: Perhaps heaven was never above us.
writings.content:
Perhaps heaven was never above us.
Perhaps the body is merely a
failed attempt at containing pain.
Spines bend beneath the unbearable
architecture of suffering
while feathers erupt where
language no longer survives.
What we call pain may not be pain simply...
every angel probably looked
monstrous before the worship began.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if heaven was never in the sky, and if the body simply cannot hold all its pain. Suffering bends people, and wings grow where words run out. He seems to say pain can turn someone into something holy: even angels may have looked like monsters before anyone worshipped them.

writings.title: Some wounds do not bleed,
writings.content:
Some wounds do not bleed,
they bloom beneath the skin.
and perhaps that is why
some people smile so beautifully,
because the flower of grief
learned how to wear their face.
writings.explanation: The writer says some hurts do not show on the outside; they grow quietly inside a person, like a flower under the skin. That may be why some people have such lovely smiles: their grief has learned to hide behind a happy face.

writings.title: I tried to find the missing piece of myself in others,
writings.content:
I tried to find the missing
piece of myself in others,
but the whole of me got lost instead.
Every search for myself led
back to the ruin I became.
I even searched within those ruins for
a soul that disappeared while searching for itself.
writings.explanation: The writer tried to find the part of himself he was missing in other people, but he lost all of himself instead. Every time he looked for himself, he only found the broken person he had become, and even there his soul was gone, lost while searching for itself.

writings.title: I carry grief like a second skin,
writings.content:
I carry grief like a second skin,
stitched into everything I do.
There are days I laugh so naturally
that it feels like I am betraying
this skin of grief I have too.
Memories return like wounds
reopening in the skin,
the skin of grief beneath,
beneath the laugh too.
Maybe grief isn't any of this.
Maybe it's the silence after happiness,
realizing you have no one left to share it with too.
writings.explanation: The writer says grief is like a second skin, part of everything he does. Laughing freely feels like betraying it, and memories keep opening old wounds. In the end he thinks grief may be the quiet after a happy moment, when you realize no one is left to share it with.

writings.title: Do we seek God—
writings.content:
Do we seek God—
because the war inside us needs a religion
or do we seek Him,
repenting for the tragedy
of what the war turned us into?
writings.explanation: The writer asks why we turn to God. Is it because the fight inside us needs something to believe in, or because we are sorry for what that inner fight has turned us into?

writings.title: Mother, I wish I could take away the sadness
writings.content:
Mother,
I wish I could take away
the sadness from which
you showed me love.
in the way you kept giving warmth
while forgetting you were cold too.
writings.explanation: The writer speaks to his mother. He wishes he could take away the sadness she carried while loving him, because she kept giving him warmth while forgetting that she was cold and hurting too.

writings.title: Perhaps the only difference between, love and insanity
writings.content:
Perhaps the only difference between,
love and insanity
is how you distinguish between them,
either ways it consumes you whole long before
you realise it does...
writings.explanation: The writer says love and madness may be almost the same; the only difference is how you choose to tell them apart. Either way, both swallow you whole before you even notice.

writings.title: God must find us embarrassing
writings.content:
God must find us embarrassing
the way we turn people into religions
just because they once knew
how to calm the war inside us
and here I thought healing would feel noble
instead,
it feels like forgetting the sound of your voice...
There was a time
when losing you felt impossible to survive,
now it survives without asking me first..
writings.explanation: The writer thinks God must be embarrassed by how we treat people like gods just because they once calmed the fight inside us. He expected healing to feel proud, but it feels like forgetting the lost person's voice. Once the loss seemed impossible to survive; now he is surviving it without having chosen to.

writings.title: What's beautiful is that after all that you did to me,
writings.content:
What’s beautiful is that
after all that you did to me,
I still love you with everything I have.
What’s beautiful is that
even with the dagger inside my heart,
I would still offer it to you without hesitation.
What’s beautiful is that
I keep returning to the fire,
hoping it won’t burn me this time.
writings.explanation: The writer says that after all the hurt this person caused him, he still loves them completely. Even with the wound they gave him in his heart, he would hand that heart to them. He keeps going back to the one who burns him, hoping this time will be different, and calls this beautiful.

writings.title: Do I not deserve to be loved?
writings.content:
Do I not deserve to be loved?
Or am I so unlovable
that love itself detests me for loving it?
Do I not deserve to be kept?
Or has grief taken a special liking to me
that I keep pushing away
everything that tries to keep me, love me?
writings.explanation: The writer asks if he does not deserve love, or if he is so hard to love that love itself hates him for trying. He asks if he does not deserve to be kept, or if grief likes him so much that he keeps pushing away everyone who tries to love him.

writings.title: What is so wrong with this life of mine
writings.content:
What is so wrong with this life of mine
that everything I drag closer by the day
only goes farther away at night?
I try to be held by those hands of yours
yet I keep slipping away
through the narrow spaces between them.
Why is it that everything I love leaves me
and everything I try to save
kills me instead?
writings.explanation: The writer asks what is wrong with his life, that everything he pulls close during the day slips away by night. He tries to hold on to the person he loves but keeps slipping through their fingers. Everything he loves leaves him, and everything he tries to save ends up destroying him.

writings.title: Sometimes I wonder, if sorrow learned my name so well
writings.content:
Sometimes I wonder,
if sorrow learned my name so well
that even joy arrives feeling unwelcome,
like light entering a house that has
forgotten how to open its windows.
Like the prayer in an abandoned church
that never reaches its God.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if sadness knows him so well that even happiness feels like an unwanted guest when it comes. He feels like a house that has forgotten how to open its windows to let light in, or a prayer in an empty church that never reaches God.

writings.title: Has happiness never found its way to me,
writings.content:
Has happiness never
found its way to me,
or did grief make
its hive inside my chest,
building a home from everything
that I have ever tried to heal from?
writings.explanation: The writer asks if happiness never found him at all, or if grief moved into his chest like bees building a hive, making its home out of every pain he has tried to heal from.

writings.title: And when my soul leaves my body,
writings.content:
And when my soul leaves my body,
it will search for yours through eternity
so that we meet,
we fall in love and
you leave again...
turning me into a poet all over again.
I write for you again... or maybe I already am.
writings.explanation: The writer says that when he dies, his soul will look for this person forever. They will meet, fall in love, and the person will leave again, and the pain will make him a poet once more. He ends by wondering if this is already happening now.

writings.title: There is a stain of memories on my soul that I try to erase,
writings.content:
“There is a stain of memories
on my soul that I try to erase,
but if it is destined to fade,
was it ever truly a stain to begin with?”
God, that name is stitched into my soul.
writings.explanation: The writer has memories stuck to his soul like a stain he tries to wash off. He wonders: if it is bound to fade, was it ever really a stain? But one person's name is sewn into his soul, and that will not come out.

writings.title: I try to hold everything while losing everything of myself.
writings.content:
I try to hold everything
while losing everything of myself.
even so, I keep holding on.
even so, I feel numb,
until my hands no longer know
whether they are carrying love, you,
or just the weight of losing it all.
writings.explanation: The writer tries to hold on to everything while losing himself in the process. He keeps holding on anyway, though he feels numb, until his hands can no longer tell if they are carrying love, the person he loves, or just the heavy weight of losing it all.

writings.title: What do curtains do to a burning room?
writings.content:
What do curtains do to a burning room?
They hide the flames, not the smoke.
love is no different,
it covers the grief and holds your heart gently,
while everything inside your
heart continues to collapse.
writings.explanation: The writer says a curtain in a burning room can hide the flames but not the smoke. Love works the same way: it covers up grief and holds the heart gently, but inside, the heart keeps falling apart.

writings.title: What is the meaning of love?
writings.content:
What is the meaning of love?
Maybe it is a mother cooling hot food
with her breath before feeding her child,
or a trembling hand refusing to let go
of another when the days are numbered,
perhaps it is a prayer whispered for someone
who is ill when life is more uncertain than death,
or maybe the sacrifices we continue to make
even when they offer us nothing in return?
writings.explanation: The writer wonders what love really is. Maybe it is a mother blowing on hot food before feeding her child, a shaking hand that will not let go of someone who is dying, a quiet prayer for someone sick, or the sacrifices we keep making even when we get nothing back.

writings.title: Your presence was a devotion to me.
writings.content:
Your presence was a
devotion to me.

Your absence turned
it into a religion,
and somehow,

I still worship,

as if my God
would finally hear me.
writings.explanation: When this person was near, the writer was deeply devoted to them. After they left, that love grew into something like a religion, and he still worships them, hoping, as with a god, that they will finally hear him.

writings.title: The distance between you and me now is that of heaven and hell
writings.content:
The distance between you and me now
is that of heaven and hell,
heaven, you, and hell, me.
I ache to be with you,
but all these sins
inside me have held me back ,
held me down.
I cannot reach you from here.
writings.explanation: The writer feels the gap between him and the person he loves is as wide as the gap between heaven and hell: they are heaven, and he is hell. He longs to be with them, but his own wrongs hold him back, so he cannot reach them.

writings.title: And maybe death is not a man in black carrying a scythe.
writings.content:
And maybe death is not
a man in black carrying a scythe.
Maybe it is your mother's arms
waiting to hold you warmly.
Maybe it is your father's voice,
filled with pride for the final time
and maybe, it is your lover looking at you again,
with the same love still alive in her eyes.
writings.explanation: The writer says death may not be the scary figure in black that people imagine. Maybe it is your mother's arms waiting to hug you, your father's proud voice one last time, or the one you love looking at you again, still with love in her eyes.

writings.title: dead bodies have no soul, dead souls have bodies
writings.content:
dead bodies have no soul,
dead souls have bodies

that are devoided
of emotions

and somewhere
between the two, i exist..

neither fully dead,
nor fully alive
writings.explanation: The writer says dead bodies have no soul, and some living people have bodies with no feelings, as if their souls have died. He feels he lives somewhere between the two, not fully dead and not fully alive.

writings.title: While trying to hold everything,
writings.content:
While trying to hold everything,
I lost everything of myself
while holding onto it,
until my hands
no longer knew
whether they
were carrying love

or just the weight of losing it.
writings.explanation: While trying to hold on to everything, the writer lost himself. In the end his hands could no longer tell whether they were holding love or only the heavy weight of losing it.

writings.title: I try to be held by those hands of yours
writings.content:
I try to be held by those
hands of yours
yet I keep slipping away
through the narrow spaces
between them.
What is so wrong
with this life of mine
that everything I drag closer by the day
goes farther away at night?
writings.explanation: The writer tries to hold on to the person he loves, but keeps slipping through their fingers. He asks what is wrong with his life, that everything he pulls close during the day drifts far away by night.

writings.title: When love seeps into my veins and reaches through the bone,
writings.content:
"When love seeps into my veins
and reaches through the bone,
it will merge itself
with my soul,
and through the veins,
it will be carried to my heart,
and all they will hear through
my heartbeat will be your name."
writings.explanation: The writer says love will soak into him so deeply, through his blood, his bones and his soul, that it will reach his heart. Then every heartbeat will sound like the name of the person he loves.

writings.title: By the time your silence reaches the deepest parts of me,
writings.content:
By the time your silence reaches
the deepest parts of me,
I fear there
will be nothing
left untouched
by you, love.
Not even this silence will be
able to stop the flowing pulse,
the beating heart,
and the chants they make of your name.
writings.explanation: The writer fears that by the time this person's silence sinks all the way into him, every part of him will already belong to them. Even that silence will not stop his heart from beating, and every beat will still call out their name.

writings.title: My heart beats with devotion" but my God
writings.content:
"My heart beats with devotion"

but my God
is too heartless
to notice how
loudly it begs

untouched by every
"prayer"
inside it,
till it goes silent..
writings.explanation: The writer's heart is full of devotion, but his God, perhaps the person he loves, is too cold to notice how loudly it begs. None of the prayers inside his heart reach them, and it keeps begging until it finally goes silent.

writings.title: I am astonished by how easily I am betrayed rather than stood by.
writings.content:
I am
astonished
by how easily

I am betrayed
rather than
stood by.
writings.explanation: The writer is shocked at how easily people betray him instead of standing by him.

writings.title: Somewhere between your heart and mine,
writings.content:
Somewhere
between your heart
and mine,

there is an unbridgeable
distance which separates
us from all the
love we had.
writings.explanation: The writer feels there is now a gap between his heart and the other person's that can never be crossed. It keeps them apart from all the love they once had.

writings.title: There's a dagger in my heart I've left untouched,
writings.content:
There's a dagger
in my heart
I've left untouched,
because removing it
somehow,
feels more painful
than letting it stay there.
writings.explanation: The writer has a deep hurt in his heart, like a knife, that he has not tried to remove. Taking it out feels like it would hurt even more than living with it.

writings.title: What scares me is that I'll have to spend a lifetime with memories
writings.content:
"What scares me is
that I'll have to
spend a lifetime
with memories
which will end with
me one day."
writings.explanation: The writer is scared that he must carry his memories for a whole lifetime, and that they will only end when he does.

writings.title: Maybe at the end of the day I just want to rest my heart in a place
writings.content:
Maybe at the
end of the day

I just want to rest
my heart in a place
which belongs to me,

in a heart which is mine,
in a heart which is devoted to mine.
I too a heart belong somewhere.
writings.explanation: At the end of the day, the writer just wants a place where his heart can rest and belong: a heart that is his, and one that loves his back. He wants his heart to belong somewhere too.

writings.title: every person has their own language of good and evil,
writings.content:
every person has
their own language
of good and evil,

maybe that's why
I became one in yours
and even mine.
writings.explanation: The writer says each person has their own idea of what is good and what is evil. He seems to say that is why he became the bad one in the other person's eyes, and even in his own.

writings.title: There's a lifetime within my mind,
writings.content:
There's a lifetime
within my mind,
yet all
I could ever explain
to you was a moment.
I could have
said more, but those
feelings had grown
too vast for words and
too heavy for a heart
to carry into another's hands.
writings.explanation: The writer has a whole lifetime of thoughts and feelings inside him, but could only share a tiny moment of it with the person he loves. He could have said more, but his feelings had grown too big for words and too heavy to hand to someone else.

writings.title: I try to hide your pain in the words
writings.content:
I try to hide ~~you~~
pain in the words
but they just spill

through the pages ,
and I find my heart
in those ~~blood~~ inks.
writings.explanation: The writer tries to hide his pain in his writing, but it spills out onto the pages anyway, and in the ink he finds his own heart. The crossed-out words hint that the pain is really about a person, and that the ink feels like blood.

writings.title: Mother, The kindest place I have been to is still your womb.
writings.content:
Mother,
The kindest place
I have been to is still
your womb.
because the world has
spent years trying to
make me feel like
I take up too much space.
for the same existence
you once carried without
complaint.
writings.explanation: The writer tells his mother that her womb is still the kindest place he has known. The world has spent years making him feel like he takes up too much room, while she carried that same life inside her without ever complaining.

writings.title: If loving YOU was a way to hell then I would walk into the fire
writings.content:
If loving YOU
was a way to hell then
I would walk
into the fire thinking
your name was another
word for heaven.
and maybe that is
the tragedy of my heart,
that even destruction felt
beautiful as long as it
arrived wearing your face.
writings.explanation: The writer says that if loving this person led to hell, he would walk into the fire believing their name meant heaven. That is the sad part of his heart: even being destroyed felt beautiful, as long as it came looking like the person he loved.

writings.title: Perhaps in my heart I was never searching for love,
writings.content:
Perhaps in my heart
I was never searching for love,
only for a place where my soul
didn't feel temporary,
for eyes that looked at me
and chose to stay.

and perhaps
I always knew that
some people are meant to feel like home,
even if they
were never meant to stay.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks he was never really looking for love, but for a place where his soul did not feel like a short visitor, and for someone who would look at him and choose to stay. Deep down he always knew some people feel like home, even if they are never meant to stay.

writings.title: There's a distance between us that I can't cross,
writings.content:
There's a distance between us
that I can't cross,
you and I were always meant
to be like the sun and the moon,
existing beneath the same sky
yet never enough to stay close.

You the sun and I the moon,
always taking your light just to survive but
I am afraid to even call myself the moon,
because I saw the moon in your eyes,
but never myself within them.
writings.explanation: The writer says he and the person he loves are like the sun and the moon: under the same sky but never close. Like the moon, he lives off their light. Yet he is afraid to call himself their moon, because he saw a moon in their eyes, and it was never him.

writings.title: What would happen if an angel and a demon fell in love?
writings.content:
What would happen
if an angel and a demon
fell in love?
They would be bound
by reality for eternity,
punished with the sin
of never meeting again.

and maybe that is what
happened when I fell for an angel,
because loving you felt like standing
at heaven's gates with
hell inside my chest.
writings.explanation: The writer imagines an angel and a demon falling in love: they would be punished forever by never meeting again. He feels that is what happened when he loved someone so good, because loving them felt like standing at heaven's door with hell inside his chest.

writings.title: I see you in old streets, in unfinished poems,
writings.content:
I see you in old streets,
in unfinished poems,
in every passing face that
carries a fragment of your eyes.

Perhaps that is what love does.
It dissolves into your existence
until every beautiful thing begins
to resemble them, until they
stop being a person and
become the way you see the world.
writings.explanation: The writer sees the person he loves everywhere: in old streets, unfinished poems, and strangers' eyes. He says love does this. It soaks into your life until every beautiful thing looks like them, and they become not just a person but the way you see the world.

writings.title: There's love you left in my heart,
writings.content:
There's love you
left in my heart,
in every grain
of existence I have,

I said there's "love you left"
like a footprint on my heart
that even
my own footprint
has became that of yours.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person he loved left love in every part of him, like a footprint pressed into his heart. Their mark is so deep that even his own footprints now look like theirs, as if he has turned into them.

writings.title: You exist in the smallest parts of my life.
writings.content:
You exist
in the smallest
parts of my life.

so naturally
that sometimes I forget
where the world ends
and where you begin.

what do you call this?
love or a paradox?
writings.explanation: The writer says this person is part of even the smallest things in his life, so naturally that he sometimes cannot tell where the world stops and they start. He wonders whether this is love or something that makes no sense.

writings.title: We say "light" and refer to the fire.
writings.content:
We say "light"
and refer to the fire.

My body was
engulfed with light,
but was I burning
or was it just love?
writings.explanation: The writer notes that we call fire light. He felt full of light, and he wonders whether he was being burned or simply in love, as if the two might feel the same.

writings.title: How much grief can a little child's hand hold?
writings.content:
How much grief can
a little child's hand hold?

any amount that is
placed into it by their parents,
and somehow they keep
carrying it throughout their life.
writings.explanation: The writer asks how much sadness a small child's hand can hold. His answer is: as much as the parents put into it. And the child somehow keeps carrying it for the rest of their life.

writings.title: Do not pretend to be a saint when your hands are stained with my bloo…
writings.content:
Do not pretend to be a saint
when your hands are stained
with my blood,
You speak of devotion
as if I wasn't the sacrifice
laid beneath your feet,
as if my pain wasn't
the price of your peace.

All this was still fine
until I saw you washing
your hands and pretending
the blood wasn't even mine.
writings.explanation: The writer tells someone not to act like a good person after hurting him so badly. They talk about love while he was sacrificed for their peace. He could bear even that, until he saw them wash their hands of it and act as if his pain had nothing to do with them.

writings.title: The distance between heaven and earth
writings.content:
The distance
between heaven and earth
is that of the space
between our hands
when they hold each other,

small enough to disappear
in a moment and
vast enough to carry
everything we never say.
writings.explanation: The writer says the gap between heaven and earth is like the small space between two people's hands when they hold each other. It is small enough to vanish in a moment, yet big enough to hold everything they never say.

writings.title: There are nights when I sit beside my window watching the moon
writings.content:
There are nights when
I sit beside my window watching
the moon and mistaking
every passing breeze for your arrival
and every ray of moonlight
for your eyes,

as if my lungs still
remember your smell,
as if my eyes still seeks your light
in every shard of the moon,
as if my heart has forgotten
the difference between hope and memory.
writings.explanation: On some nights the writer sits by his window looking at the moon. Every breeze feels like the person he loves arriving, and every moonbeam reminds him of their eyes. He still seems to remember their smell and look for their light, and his heart can no longer tell hope from memory.

writings.title: I sometimes wonder how a heart continues beating
writings.content:
I sometimes wonder how
a heart continues beating
after carrying so many funerals
inside itself,

how it continues to love even
after burying people who are
still alive somewhere
beneath the same sky.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders how a heart keeps beating after so many losses, as if it holds many funerals inside. He asks how it keeps loving after letting go of people who are not dead, but still alive somewhere under the same sky.

writings.title: if there is a God listening beyond all this silence,
writings.content:
if there is a God
listening beyond all this silence,
then let Him forgive me
for having loved this life
so painfully,

even when it gave me
every reason not to.
I am the sin
I am the sinner
writings.explanation: The writer says that if God is out there listening past all the silence, he hopes God will forgive him for loving this life so painfully, even though life gave him every reason not to. He feels he is both the wrong and the one who did it.

writings.title: May someone one day love you without fear,
writings.content:
May someone one day
love you without fear,
without leaving wounds
between their affection,
without turning tenderness
into tragedy and when they
hold your hands,
I hope they do not tremble
the way mine always did,
as if they already knew
they were destined to lose you.
writings.explanation: The writer hopes that one day someone will love this person without fear, without hurting them, and without turning gentle love into pain. He hopes their hands will not shake when they hold this person, the way his always did, as if they knew from the start he would lose them.

writings.title: If you remember me, remember not my suffering,
writings.content:
If you remember me,
remember not my suffering,
but the way I continued
to survive it.
Remember that even in
the darkest corners of human despair,
I still searched desperately
for your light,
for something that kept me
alive in this rotten world.
At last, remember me as a human,
not as something that
slowly rotted away by suffering.
writings.explanation: The writer asks to be remembered not for his pain but for how he kept going through it. Even at his darkest, he kept searching for the other person's light to stay alive in a cruel world. Most of all, he wants to be remembered as a human, not as something pain slowly destroyed.

writings.title: The lover, the sinner, the saint.
writings.content:
The lover, the sinner, the saint.

i stayed, i waited beside heavens
for your voice with empty hands.

but it is your silence which became a prayer,
that stayed inside me, that no god answered.

i stayed long after
the light left, you ruined my temple.

loving you that it felt like devotion,
felt like worship and too much like grief

and still, i knelt before
my ruin your altar.

thoughts of
a man mourning
a lover.
(the abandoned)

thoughts of
a dying believer.
(the martyr)

thoughts of a sinner kneeling
before something holy.
(the sinner)
writings.explanation: The writer waited, empty-handed, for the voice of the one he loved, but got only silence, a prayer no god answered. Loving them felt like worship and grief at once, and even after they ruined him, he still knelt before them. He sees himself as an abandoned lover, a dying believer and a sinner.

writings.title: But still, despite everything, I wish you a beautiful life.
writings.content:
But still,
despite everything,
I wish you a beautiful life.

Even if it is one that
no longer has me in it.
I hope you don't come
searching for me within
those memories of ruin..
writings.explanation: Even after everything, the writer wishes the other person a beautiful life, even one without him in it. He hopes they never come looking for him in those broken, painful memories.

writings.title: I have forgotten many things about you.
writings.content:
I have forgotten
many things about you.
the exact shape
of your smile,

the sound of your step.
but somehow my grief
remembers everything,
and refuses to tell me
what it knows.
writings.explanation: The writer has forgotten many small things about the person he lost, like the exact shape of their smile and the sound of their footsteps. But his grief seems to remember everything, and it will not give those memories back to him.

writings.title: I know I will be abandoned.
writings.content:
I know
I will be abandoned.

Yet still,
I pour the glass
full of love.

There is a strange
beauty in offering
abundance to a world .

that has taught
you scarcity.
To love is to never
cease to exist
writings.explanation: The writer knows he will be left in the end, yet he still loves fully, like filling a glass to the top. He finds something beautiful in giving so much to a world that taught him to expect little. To him, loving is how a person never stops existing.

writings.title: I know one day these hands will close with emptiness
writings.content:
I know one day these
hands will close with emptiness
and I will still
be brim with love,
as my heart has never learned
the difference between love and loss,
so I'll call it a doomed act of faith,
repeated until my hands forget
how to hold anything else
except for joining them
and I'll let you decide
whether it's begging or praying.
writings.explanation: The writer knows his hands will one day be empty, yet his heart will still be full of love, because it cannot tell love and loss apart. He calls it a hopeless act of faith, kept up until his hands can only fold together, and lets the listener decide if that is begging or praying.

writings.title: It's June again and there is something cruel about it
writings.content:
It's June again
and there is something cruel about it.
It teaches flowers how to bloom while
teaching my hearts how to ache again.
Is it the smell of wet soil
or my rotting skin that is
in the air beside these
old memories like withered flowers?
I cannot tell anymore.
What is it that kept me alive,
It's June again and somehow both
my love and my grief still resemble you.
writings.explanation: It is June again, and the writer finds it cruel: it makes flowers bloom but makes his heart ache again. He cannot tell if the air smells of wet soil or of himself rotting among old, dead memories. Somehow both his love and his grief still look like the person he lost.

writings.title: I have worn the appearance of being well for so long
writings.content:
I have worn the appearance
of being well for so long
that I can no longer distinguish
myself from the disguise.

I wonder now whether
pretense was only a way to survive,
or whether it slowly became
the god I learned to worship.
writings.explanation: The writer has pretended to be fine for so long that he can no longer tell his real self from the act. He wonders if pretending was just a way to get by, or if it slowly became the thing he bows to, like a god.

writings.title: a cracked cup remains on the shelf longer than a broken one.
writings.content:
a cracked cup remains
on the shelf longer
than a broken one.

No one throws it away,
yet no one trusts it either.
there are people
who live exactly this way
too damaged to be held,
too intact to be mourned.
writings.explanation: The writer says a cracked cup stays on the shelf longer than a broken one: no one throws it out, but no one trusts it either. Some people live just like that, too hurt for anyone to hold them, yet not broken enough for anyone to grieve for them.

writings.title: I hope the next time we meet, my hands won't tremble at the sight of…
writings.content:
I hope the next time
we meet,
my hands won't tremble
at the sight of you.
I hope your name
will no longer
echo like a prayer
inside my empty chest.
I hope, for once,
I will be able to look
at you without my heart
remembering everything.
writings.explanation: The writer hopes that the next time he meets this person, his hands will not shake when he sees them. He hopes their name will stop sounding like a prayer in his empty chest, and that he can finally look at them without his heart remembering everything.

writings.title: When they check the pulse of the dying man, what will they hear?
writings.content:
When they check
the pulse of the dying man,
what will they hear?

1) ~~you~~ blood flowing

2) ~~you leaving~~ blood stopping

3) ~~you~~ pulse of a dying man

~~4) or the you sitting beside me,~~
~~caressing my hair?~~
writings.explanation: The writer asks what people will hear when they check a dying man's pulse, meaning his own. He lists plain answers, like blood flowing or stopping, but the crossed-out words show his pulse is really full of the person he loves and their leaving, and he wishes they were beside him, stroking his hair.

writings.title: What is love? to make an ocean fit inside a bowl for a fish,
writings.content:
What is love?
to make an ocean
fit inside a bowl
for a fish,
or to admire its waves
without ever
claiming the sea?
Possession or devotion?
writings.explanation: The writer asks what love really is. Is it squeezing an ocean into a small bowl to keep a fish, or enjoying the waves without ever trying to own the sea? He wonders if love means owning someone or loving them freely.

writings.title: I hope I dream so well that..
writings.content:
"I hope I dream
so well that..

I don't have
to wake up
the next day."
writings.explanation: The writer hopes he will have such a good dream that he will not have to wake up the next day. It reads as a quiet wish not to wake up at all.

writings.title: Grief love is absurd
writings.content:
Grief ~~love~~ is absurd.
I can bury
an entire lifetime,
watch the earth
close over it,
and still turn my head
at certain footsteps,
like a fool who believes that
the dead can resurrect.
writings.explanation: The writer says grief makes no sense. He can bury a whole lifetime and watch the ground close over it, yet still turn his head at certain footsteps, like a fool who believes the dead can come back. A crossed-out word hints that love is just as strange.

writings.title: You and I are meant to be like parallel lines
writings.content:
You and I are meant to be like parallel lines,
cursed forever within sight of one
another, forever forbidden
from touching.
We travel in the same direction,
witness the same horizons and yet
the universe keeps us apart all the
way to infinity.
writings.explanation: The writer says he and the person he loves are like two lines that run side by side forever. They go the same way and see the same things, but they can never meet or touch.

writings.title: If I could hear your name within this hell, it wouldn't be hell…
writings.content:
If I could hear
your name within this hell,
it wouldn't be hell
anymore

and if you were
to call this broken soul
by its name,
even this wreckage
would mistake itself
for paradise.
writings.explanation: The writer is in deep pain, but just hearing the name of the one he loves would end that pain. If she called him by his name, even his broken life would feel like heaven.

writings.title: You have seeped into my bones so well that I can't distinguish
writings.content:
You have seeped
into my bones
so well that I can't
distinguish between
you and the marrow

and perhaps that
is why broken ones
hurts the most.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person he loves has gone so deep inside him that he can't tell her apart from his own bones. Maybe that is why, when it breaks, it hurts the most.

writings.title: Perhaps what love is can be heard between the pulses of my flowing…
writings.content:
Perhaps what love is can
be heard between the pulses
of my flowing blood,
for what they chant
is your name and it is
the same blood that flows
through my whole body...

my heart, my eyes, my brain, my lungs.
I love you, I see you,
I think you, I breathe you.

Tell me, how am I to love anything but you?
Tell me, how am I to forget you?
writings.explanation: The writer feels his love in his blood, which seems to repeat her name as it reaches every part of him. His heart, eyes, mind and lungs all love her, so he asks how he could ever love anything else or forget her.

writings.title: If eyes could speak, they would tell you of the wars I survived
writings.content:
If eyes could speak,
they would tell you of the wars
I survived and the one I never did.

They would tell you that grief
is sometimes just love
with nowhere left to go.

They would tell you how
a single absence can
outlive a thousand presences,
how some names become prayers
without ever being spoken.
writings.explanation: If his eyes could talk, they would tell of the hard times he survived and the one he did not. They would say grief is love left with no one to give it to, that missing one person lasts longer than many others being near, and that some names become silent prayers.

writings.title: If eyes could speak, they would ask why the universe made…
writings.content:
If eyes could speak,
they would ask why the universe
made recognition so easy
and belonging so difficult.
Why I could find you in a crowd of thousands,
yet could not find a place beside you.
and if eyes could speak, they would not weep.
They would stand as witnesses
to every word I swallowed,
every hope I buried,
and every part of me
that still turns toward you
as flowers turn toward light.
writings.explanation: His eyes would ask why it is so easy to spot her in a huge crowd, yet so hard to have a place beside her. They would not cry; they would quietly show every word he held back, every hope he gave up, and how part of him still turns toward her.

writings.title: I believed all I had was suffering, but I was wrong
writings.content:
I believed all
I had was suffering,
but I was wrong.
all feelings in
me were suffering,
as if they were
in a prison,
as if suffering itself
was a prison,
and all I could do
was watch.
writings.explanation: The writer first thought pain was just one thing he had. Then he saw that all his feelings had turned into pain, locked up as if in a jail, and he could do nothing but watch.

writings.title: The cruelest part of my existence is not that I can't love anymore
writings.content:
The cruelest part of my existence
is not that I can't love anymore.
I can. But everywhere my sight goes,
it is still you.
and that is the tragedy of this
miserable being.
writings.explanation: The writer says he can still love, so that is not the worst part. The worst part is that wherever he looks, he still sees only her, and that makes his whole life sad.

writings.title: One day, when everything grows apart, I won't know your story anymore
writings.content:
One day, when everything
grows apart, I won’t know
your story anymore.
I won’t know what
makes you smile,
what keeps you awake, or
who you became without me.
I’ll only remember that once,
I was a chapter in it,
before the pages turned
without me.
writings.explanation: The writer knows that one day they will drift apart and he won't know her life anymore, like what makes her smile or who she has become. He will only remember that he was once part of her story, before it went on without him.

writings.title: There's a fire burning me from within, which only you can extinguish
writings.content:
There’s a fire burning me from within,
which only you can extinguish,
for I have carried these flames
for longer than I can remember,
amid the burning of countless me, myself
and when they finally burn me,
you won’t smell anything,
for empty things leave no scent behind.
So come before I am only ashes.
Make your home within this burning heart.
Find me before they scatter these ashes
and leave me whole before
I disappear into emptiness.

Now Read the underlined part
writings.explanation: The writer has carried a pain like a fire inside him for a very long time, and only the one he loves can put it out. He begs her to come and live in his heart before it burns him down to nothing. The last line points to a hidden message in underlined words.

writings.title: And when death fills my chest and I am not able to breathe anymore
writings.content:
And when death
fills my chest
and I am not able
to breathe anymore,

it’ll still be less
suffocating than
the night you left.
writings.explanation: The writer says that even dying, when he can no longer breathe, will feel easier than the night the person he loved left him.

writings.title: A writer is often a liar
writings.content:
A writer is often a liar.
He lies to himself
with things he never got
and the presence
of the things he lost.

He writes people
back into his life,
knowing they are already gone,
because what he calls
“imagination” is just a
recycled piece of reality.
writings.explanation: The writer says a writer often fools himself. He writes about things he never had and people he has lost as if they were still there, and what looks made-up is really just pieces of his real life used again.

writings.title: Maybe that's what belief has always been closing your eyes
writings.content:
Maybe that’s what belief
has always been
closing your eyes
and hoping that when
you open them again,

the person you trusted
hasn’t disappeared or worse,
hasn’t become someone
you never knew.
writings.explanation: He says trusting someone may be like shutting your eyes and hoping that when you open them, that person is still there, and has not turned into someone you don't know at all.

writings.title: I do not hope you'll remember my face forever
writings.content:
I do not hope you’ll
remember my face forever.
I only hope that when my
name wanders through your
mind years from now,
it will not feel like
the name of a stranger
who happened to pass by,
but like a room you once lived in,
because for a brief
and terrible moment,
we mistook each other for home.
writings.explanation: The writer does not need her to remember his face forever. He only hopes that years later his name feels to her not like a passing stranger but like a home she once lived in, because for a short, painful time they each felt like home to the other.

writings.title: God, If You ever wonder why I no longer pray with folded hands
writings.content:
God,
If You ever wonder why
I no longer pray
with folded hands,

know that I spent them
holding together a
heart You kept breaking.
writings.explanation: The writer tells God he no longer prays with folded hands. His hands have been busy holding his heart together, because God kept letting it break.

writings.title: I wait for you
writings.content:
I wait for you.
I wait for you like
a blind man walking
across the street.

I wait for you the way
he lives, desperately.

I wait for you
like a blind man
waits for light
in his darkest dark.
writings.explanation: The writer waits for the person he loves with great need and little hope, like a blind man crossing a street, or a blind man longing for light when all he knows is darkness.

writings.title: I think hell may be far simpler than what you and I imagined
writings.content:
I think hell may be
far simpler than
what you and I imagined.

to meet, by chance,
the person you could have been,
and discover that he
suffered no less than you did.

or the eyes you
thought would look at you
looking at other.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks hell might be simple. It could be meeting the person you might have become and finding he hurt just as much, or seeing the eyes you hoped would look at you looking at someone else.

writings.title: God, if loss is a part of Your design,
writings.content:
God,
if loss is a part
of Your design,

then tell me why
did You make the heart
so stubborn that it
continues loving
what You have already
taken away?
writings.explanation: The writer asks God: if losing people is part of His plan, why did He make the heart so stubborn that it keeps loving the ones He has already taken away?

writings.title: When they burn me, they won't just burn my body
writings.content:
When they burn me, they won’t just
burn my body. They will burn the skin you
once loved dearly they will burn the bones
that held together a man who died long ago.

And when the fire reaches
the deepest parts of
my mind and soul,
my heart and brain,
it will burn all the memories
I once held close.

But when it reaches my chest, I hope it does
not extinguish beneath the weight of losing you.
writings.explanation: The writer pictures his body being burned after death: the skin she once loved, the bones of a man who died inside long ago, and all his memories. He seems to say the pain of losing her sits so heavy in his chest it could put out even that fire, and hopes it does not.

writings.title: What a ridiculous creature man is.
writings.content:
What a ridiculous
creature man is.
spending half his life
longing for what he
does not possess

and the other half
grieving what
he has already lost.
writings.explanation: The writer says people are silly: they spend half their life wanting what they don't have, and the other half being sad about what they have lost.

writings.title: There are parasites within my heart
writings.content:
There are parasites within my heart.
They do not feed on flesh,
they feed on proportion.
Grain by grain,
they alter the measurements
of my inner world until an
entire mountain can pass
through the eye of a needle,
and a single missing stone outweighs the earth
itself and I, the victim, notice nothing.
I merely wake up one day to find that
gravity has developed a preference.
writings.explanation: The writer says something in his heart slowly changes how big or small things feel. Bit by bit, huge things feel tiny and one small loss feels heavier than the whole world, and he does not notice until one day everything in him pulls toward that one loss.

writings.title: Years later, when I remember us, what will remain is neither love nor
writings.content:
Years later,
when I remember us,
what will remain is
neither love nor

the one who was loved
but a careful arrangement
of absences pretending
to be memory.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks that years from now, when he looks back on them, he won't really remember the love or the person. He will only have the empty spaces they left, set up to look like memories.

writings.title: 7 stages of love
writings.content:
7 stages of love

Attraction
attachment
Trust
Worship
Passion
death
Love

There is a space between "you" and "I".
From "I" to "you", and I call it love.

Attraction

At first you think you have found
another person. In truth, you have
only misplaced the boundary of your
own existence. Everything appears
larger because you have become
smaller. You call this happiness. No
one corrects you. Like dawn entering
a valley that has never known light.
Like a drop of rain believing it has
discovered the sea.

Attachment

It is like a blind man waiting for light
in his darkest dark, learning the shape
of a face with his bare hands. He does
not know its colour nor the light that
falls upon it. He only knows that the
world ends where that face is absent.
So his hands continue searching with
the same certainty. No one has the
heart to tell him that hope can survive
even where light cannot. Perhaps
attachment is not refusing to let go but
forgetting that there was ever anything
else to hold.

Trust

Maybe that's what trust has
always been closing your eyes
and hoping that, when you
open them again, the person
you trusted hasn't disappeared
or, worse, hasn't become
someone you never knew. You
never ask to see the path you
just walk walk into it.

Love

Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into
"us" is love. Maybe giving yourself
wholly is love. Maybe existing for
one particularity entirely is love.
maybe to love is to love beyond
yourself, Maybe it is remembering
another heartbeat before your own
and maybe I am still figuring out
what love is and that for me that is
very much love.

Devotion

Then love becomes a cathedral
with no god inside it. You kneel
anyway because the echo sounds
more merciful than the beloved's
screams. Every prayer returns
wearing the beloved's voice. Faith
grows larger than truth. Soon you
cannot tell whether you worship a
person or the space they carved in
your heart to be worshipped.

Passion

Perhaps passion is the moth, circling
a flame it knows will ruin it, yet
mistaking its warmth for mercy. Or
perhaps I was the flame, burning
through every hope and calling the
ashes "moths." And if you ask
whether I loved, I did... enough to
offer myself to the fire(love),
mistaking its hunger for warmth.

Death

And if they ask me how much
I loved, I would say, enough to
be Icarus. Because the sea
remembers only the fall, but I
remember the sun. Because the
fall meant I flew, and the death
meant I loved.
Such is the fate of the "fool" in
love.
writings.explanation: The writer walks through the stages of love: feeling the world grow bigger, needing the person, trusting them, giving all of yourself, almost worshipping them, and burning for them. In the end loving that much ruins him, like a boy in an old story who flew too near the sun, yet he would choose it.

writings.title: But just when you believe life has exhausted all its cruelties,
writings.content:
But just when you believe
life has exhausted
all its cruelties,
it comes with another to
ruin you in a different way.

What is peace,
if not merely an
interval between one
catastrophe and another?
writings.explanation: The writer says that just when you think life has no more ways to hurt you, it finds a new one. He wonders if peace is only a short break between one disaster and the next.

writings.title: The strangeness of the human heart is that it desires the very things
writings.content:
The strangeness of the
human heart is that
it desires the very things
which will ruin it,
which has ruined it.

He who sees it ,
he who feels it calls it love.
What a fool
writings.explanation: The writer says the human heart is strange because it wants the very things that hurt it, again and again. People who see and feel this call it love, and he calls that foolish.

writings.title: The tragedy of longing is not that it reaches for what it cannot…
writings.content:
The tragedy of longing
is not that it reaches for
what it cannot possess.
It is that, given the
entire world, it would
still choose the locked door.
because some desires
do not seek fulfillment.
They seek permanence.

What is love if not permanence
in the architecture of heart.
writings.explanation: The writer says the sad thing about longing is that, even with the whole world open to it, it would still choose the one thing it can't have. Some wishes don't want to come true; they want to last forever, and he says love is that lasting thing built inside the heart.

writings.title: we can survive almost any truth.
writings.content:
we can survive almost
any truth. What ruins us
are the possibilities.

The lives we might
have lived, the words we
might have said, the people
we might have kept.

In the end,
ghosts require no death
to exist they die inside us,
they live inside us.
writings.explanation: The writer says we can handle almost any hard truth, but what breaks us is thinking about what might have been: other lives, unsaid words, people we could have kept. These what-ifs are like ghosts that live inside us, and no one has to die for them to exist.

writings.title: I think love and loss go hand in hand.
writings.content:
I think love and loss
go hand in hand.

Because I have lost
everyone I have loved.

I tell you, the heaviest tears are those
which are shed at loss, because you lose
yourself too. Parts of you leave because
you aren’t you anymore, and what you
once were never finds its way back to you
ever again.
writings.explanation: The writer feels love and loss always come together, since he has lost everyone he loved. He says the tears over a loss are the heaviest because you lose part of yourself too, and the person you were never comes back.

writings.title: Attraction: At first you think you have found another person
writings.content:
Attraction

At first you think you have found
another person. In truth, you have
only misplaced the boundary of your
own existence. Everything appears
larger because you have become
smaller. You call this happiness. No
one corrects you. Like dawn entering
a valley that has never known light.
Like a drop of rain believing it has
discovered the sea.
writings.explanation: At the start of love, you think you have found someone new, but really you have lost track of where you end and they begin. The world feels bigger because you feel smaller, and you call it happiness, like a raindrop thinking it has found the sea.

writings.title: Attachment: It is like a blind man waiting for light in his darkest…
writings.content:
Attachment

It is like a blind man waiting for light
in his darkest dark, learning the shape
of a face with his bare hands. He does
not know its colour nor the light that
falls upon it. He only knows that the
world ends where that face is absent.
So his hands continue searching with
the same certainty. No one has the
heart to tell him that hope can survive
even where light cannot. Perhaps
attachment is not refusing to let go but
forgetting that there was ever anything
else to hold.
writings.explanation: Being attached is like a blind man learning a face with his hands. He doesn't know how it looks, only that his world ends where that face is gone, so he keeps searching. The writer says attachment is not refusing to let go, but forgetting you ever had anything else to hold.

writings.title: Trust: Maybe that's what trust has always been closing your eyes
writings.content:
Trust

Maybe that's what trust has
always been closing your eyes
and hoping that, when you
open them again, the person
you trusted hasn't disappeared
or, worse, hasn't become
someone you never knew. You
never ask to see the path you
just walk walk into it.
writings.explanation: Trusting someone is like shutting your eyes and hoping that when you open them, that person is still there and has not become a stranger. You don't ask to see the road first; you just walk into it.

writings.title: Love: Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into "us" is love
writings.content:
Love

Maybe the slow erosion of "I" into
"us" is love. Maybe giving yourself
wholly is love. Maybe existing for
one particularity entirely is love.
maybe to love is to love beyond
yourself, Maybe it is remembering
another heartbeat before your own
and maybe I am still figuring out
what love is and that for me that is
very much love.
writings.explanation: The writer tries to say what love is: slowly turning from me into us, giving all of yourself, living fully for one person, caring about their heartbeat before your own. He admits he is still working it out, and that this searching is love to him too.

writings.title: Devotion: Then love becomes a cathedral with no god inside it
writings.content:
Devotion

Then love becomes a cathedral
with no god inside it. You kneel
anyway because the echo sounds
more merciful than the beloved's
screams. Every prayer returns
wearing the beloved's voice. Faith
grows larger than truth. Soon you
cannot tell whether you worship a
person or the space they carved in
your heart to be worshipped.
writings.explanation: Here love turns into worship, like praying in a church with no god inside. You keep praying anyway, and every prayer comes back sounding like the one you love. In time you can't tell if you love the person or just the place they made for themselves in your heart.

writings.title: Passion: Perhaps passion is the moth, circling a flame it knows will…
writings.content:
Passion

Perhaps passion is the moth, circling
a flame it knows will ruin it, yet
mistaking its warmth for mercy. Or
perhaps I was the flame, burning
through every hope and calling the
ashes "moths." And if you ask
whether I loved, I did... enough to
offer myself to the fire(love),
mistaking its hunger for warmth.
writings.explanation: Passion is like a moth flying around a flame that will kill it, thinking the heat is kindness. Or maybe the writer was the flame, burning up every hope. He says he did love, enough to throw himself into it, thinking its hunger was warmth.

writings.title: And if they ask me how much I loved, I would say, enough to be Icarus
writings.content:
Death

And if they ask me how much
I loved, I would say, enough to
be Icarus. Because the sea
remembers only the fall, but I
remember the sun. Because the
fall meant I flew, and the death
meant I loved.
Such is the fate of the "fool" in
love.
writings.explanation: The writer says he loved like a boy in an old story who flew too close to the sun and fell into the sea. Others remember only the fall, but he remembers the sun: falling meant he flew, and dying meant he loved. He calls this the fate of a fool in love.

writings.title: Father, I have always carried you within my anger
writings.content:
Father,
I have always carried you
within my anger.
I sometimes become you.
Tell me, how did you manage to
control it after the world gave you
every reason not to?
I inherited your anger,
but I fear I did not inherit your strength.
What is this incurable wound
that you have carried without
ever showing it?
