writings.explanation: The writer tells his father he has the same anger and sometimes acts just like him. He asks how his father kept it under control when life gave him every reason not to, fears he got the anger but not the strength, and wonders what hidden pain his father carried.

writings.title: There's something tragic about me, because when love happened
writings.content:
There’s something tragic
about me, because
when love happened
i had let it consume me.
When absence happened
i let it consume me too.

If I love i love everything
about it. Even the presence,
even the absence.
What is love if not this?
writings.explanation: The writer gives himself fully to whatever he feels. When love came, he let it fill him, and when it was gone, he let the missing fill him too. To him, real love means loving all of it, both the being together and the being apart.

writings.title: Then you arrived and what neither time nor loneliness could break
writings.content:
Then you arrived
and what neither time
nor loneliness could break,

you did with nothing more
than your presence.
Perhaps that is the tragedy
of warmth once
you have known it,
the cold becomes unbearable.
writings.explanation: The writer had a hardness that time and being alone could not break, but the person he loves broke it just by being near. The sad part is that once you have felt that warmth, being cold and alone again becomes too hard to bear.

writings.title: I loved you even when I was told not to
writings.content:
I loved you even
when I was told not to.
Long after reason had
withdrawn its support,
long after hope had strangled me,
I kept hanging from hope itself.
Hope acted like an anesthesia
upon my soul. It numbed me
so completely that I failed
to realize how long
I had been hanged.
writings.explanation: The writer kept loving her even when he was told to stop and when it made no sense. Hope kept him holding on, but it also numbed him like a painkiller, so he did not notice how long it had been choking him.

writings.title: There is a peculiar dignity in destruction when it was earned by…
writings.content:
There is a peculiar dignity in destruction
when it was earned by caring too deeply.
For what is more tragic to leave blood upon
the earth because you held on too long,
or to leave none at all because you never
dared to hold anything close?
writings.explanation: The writer says there is something to respect in being hurt because you cared too much. He asks which is sadder: being torn up because you held on too long, or never being hurt because you never dared to get close to anything.

writings.title: This wreckage takes pride in its own ruin
writings.content:
This wreckage takes pride in its own ruin
because innocent leave no scars upon the world.
It is those who have loved recklessly,
disastrously, beyond reason, he who walks away
stained by their own devotion has every wound
bearing the shape of a dagger they never refused
to stop loving.
writings.explanation: The writer is proud of how broken he is, because people who never risked anything leave no marks on the world. Those who loved wildly, beyond sense, come away hurt, and each wound comes from something they kept loving even though it cut them.

writings.title: I am proud of this tragedity of my ruin
writings.content:
I am proud of this tragedity of my ruin
because it proves there was once something
magnificent enough to collapse. The blood
upon my hands condemns me. The love inside
my heart absolves me and somewhere between
those two verdicts, I continue to live.
writings.explanation: The writer is proud of how badly he was broken, because it shows there was once something great enough to fall apart. The wrong he has done makes him guilty, but his love makes him feel forgiven, and he goes on living stuck between those two.

writings.title: All hatred returns to the self.
writings.content:
All hatred returns
to the self.
writings.explanation: The writer says any hate you feel ends up coming back to hurt you.

writings.title: we do not suffer from the lives of others
writings.content:
we do not suffer from
the lives of others.
We suffer from our inability
to stop devouring our own.
The stars do not steal
light from the moon.

The serpent never catches
what it seeks because
what it seeks is itself.
So do we.
writings.explanation: The writer says we are not hurt by other people's lives but by how we keep eating away at our own. Stars don't take light from the moon, so others are not the problem. Like a snake chasing itself, we never catch what we chase, because what we chase is ourselves.

writings.title: The child longs to become an adult.
writings.content:
The child longs
to become an adult.
The adult longs
for his childhood again.
The lonely pray for love.
The loved mourn
who they were before it.
No one is truly happy
because we spend our lives
chasing what is absent,
only to realise we
abandoned what was
already ours.
writings.explanation: The writer says people always want what they don't have: children want to grow up, adults miss being children, lonely people want love, and people in love miss who they were before. No one is fully happy, because we chase what is missing and leave behind what we already had.

writings.title: There was a time I believed every wound deserved a wound in return
writings.content:
There was a time
I believed every
wound deserved a
wound in return.

That if the world
handed me fire,
I was entitled to
become the one to burn.
What a magnificent lie.
writings.explanation: The writer once believed that if someone hurt him, he had the right to hurt back, and if life gave him pain, he could pass it on. Now he sees that this was a big, grand lie.

writings.title: There's a fire within me that burns through every emotion I have
writings.content:
There’s a fire within
me that burns through
every emotion I have.
I think the cruelest thing
about these flames is that
they do not distinguish
between enemy and a shelter,
they burn all indiscriminately.
I wonder how much
they have taken away from me,
and how much
I have willingly sacrificed.
writings.explanation: The writer feels a fire inside him that burns through all his feelings. The worst part is that it burns everything, both what hurts him and what keeps him safe, and he wonders how much it took from him and how much he gave up himself.

writings.title: My father's eyes carried enough fire to burn through every happiness
writings.content:
My father’s eyes carried
enough fire to burn through every
happiness my family ever knew.

Still, I could not
help becoming him.

cruelest inheritance of all
is not the wounds he left behind,
but the realization that
I spent years running from his
shadow only to become
him when the light left.
writings.explanation: The writer's father had an anger that burned away his family's happiness. The writer spent years trying not to be like him, but when the good times ended he became just like him, and that hurts more than any wound his father left.

writings.title: the greatest love is the one that does not bounds itself for…
writings.content:
the greatest love is the
one that does not bounds
itself for possession.

For there is a peculiar
tragedy in belonging
the hunger that once made
us reach so desperately
often dies the moment our
hands finally close around
what they desired.
writings.explanation: The writer says the greatest love does not try to own the other person. The sad thing about having someone is that the strong wish that pulled you to them often fades the moment you finally have them.

writings.title: perhaps the rarest freedom is not having everything
writings.content:
perhaps the rarest freedom is not
having everything. Perhaps it is looking
at what remains, at who remains,
and finding no desire to ask for more.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks real freedom may not be having everything. It may be looking at what and who you still have, and feeling no need to ask for anything more.

writings.title: What I possessed ceased to move me, and what I lacked became sacred
writings.content:
What I possessed
ceased to move me,
and what I lacked
became sacred.

but to spend a lifetime
possessing more is the
greatest slavery of all,
but at some point,
I just want to belong
and never ask for more.
writings.explanation: What the writer had stopped meaning much to him, and what he didn't have started to feel holy. He sees that always wanting more is like being a slave, and now he just wants to belong somewhere and stop asking for more.

writings.title: What a strange thing it is to admire a flower, then wish to pluck it
writings.content:
What a strange thing
it is to admire a flower,
then wish to pluck it.

Perhaps some desires are
not born from love at all.
Perhaps they are born
from our inability to let
beautiful things remain free.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it strange that we see a beautiful flower and then want to pick it. He thinks some wants don't come from love at all, but from not being able to let beautiful things stay free.

writings.title: a bird sings because it belongs to the sky
writings.content:
a bird sings because
it belongs to the sky.
The moment we place
it in a cage, we keep the
bird and lose the song.

We become so afraid
of losing beautiful things
that we clutch them tightly
enough to crush them.
writings.explanation: A bird sings because it is free in the sky; put it in a cage and you keep the bird but lose its song. The writer says we are so scared of losing beautiful things that we hold them too tight and crush them.

writings.title: There are ways of looking at a person that resemble blindness
writings.content:
There are ways of
looking at a person that
resemble blindness.
I knew the color of
her eyes long before I knew
what made them weep
by the time I distinguished
between her eyes and her tears
she had already become
a stranger I thought I loved.
It isn’t about the shell
it is about the soul.
writings.explanation: The writer says you can look at someone and still not really see them. He knew how she looked long before he knew what made her sad, and by the time he understood her pain, she had become a stranger. What matters is the person inside, not the outside.

writings.title: I wonder how much grief I had to devour every bit of my happiness
writings.content:
I wonder how much grief
I had to devour every bit
of my happiness.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders how much sadness it took to eat up every bit of his happiness.

writings.title: I desired love, yet each time it was offered, it felt lesser than…
writings.content:
I desired love,
yet each time it was offered,
it felt lesser than before.
I kept asking for more
and more, until one day
I could feel none of it at all.
Perhaps that is the tragedy
of an endless hunger it does not
starve because it is empty.
It starves because nothing
is ever enough and while
understanding it all I was left
with nothing at all.
writings.explanation: The writer wanted love, but each time he got it, it felt like less than before. He kept wanting more until he couldn't feel it at all. He says that kind of hunger starves not because it has nothing, but because nothing is ever enough, and in the end he was left with nothing.

writings.title: to fill the void inside me, I have devoured many things
writings.content:
to fill the void inside me,
I have devoured many things.
even you even your memories.
writings.explanation: To fill the emptiness inside him, the writer has used up many things, even the person he loved and his memories of her.

writings.title: you could, but did you?
writings.content: you could, but did you?
writings.explanation: The writer asks someone a short, sharp question. He seems to say that being able to do something is not the same as actually doing it.

writings.title: I deserve neither hell nor heaven;
writings.explanation: The writer feels he deserves neither heaven nor hell. The only place he feels he belongs is in the eyes of the woman he loves.

writings.title: There is a prison that has no walls
writings.content:
There is a prison
that has no walls.
It is built from all the
lives we meant to live
and never began

and it is funny how
I did not lose myself
chasing the wrong path.
I lost it while standing still,
waiting for the right one.
writings.explanation: The writer says there is a jail with no walls, made of all the lives we planned but never started. He finds it strange that he didn't lose himself by going the wrong way, but by standing still and waiting for the right one.

writings.title: What is peace, if not merely an interval between one catastrophe and…
writings.content:
What is peace, if not merely
an interval between one catastrophe
and another?
writings.explanation: The writer wonders if peace is only a short break between one disaster and the next.

writings.title: What a peculiar curse it is. To stand at heaven's gate
writings.content:
What a peculiar
curse it is.
To stand at heaven's gate
and still searching for the
hell inside it.

To hate
the very love which once
kept you alive.
i fear this tragic end..
writings.explanation: The writer says it is a strange curse to be somewhere wonderful and still look for the bad in it, or to hate the love that once kept you alive. He is afraid this sad ending will be his own.

writings.title: While writing live, my autocorrect changed it to love.
writings.content:
While writing live,
my autocorrect changed it to love.
Then I realized—
to love is to live.
But to love is to die too.
and if love contains both life and death,
perhaps living is merely
learning how to die for
the things we cannot bear to lose.

So, to live is to love = To love is to die
= and to die, perhaps, is simply
another way of having lived.
writings.explanation: When his phone changed live to love, the writer started thinking. Loving is living, but loving also means losing, a kind of dying. So he thinks living may be learning to give yourself up for what you can't bear to lose, and dying may just be another way of having lived.

writings.title: Smoking is injurious to health
writings.content:
Smoking is injurious
to health

So is love Maybe
I don't deserve it
all, maybe it's me ,
maybe it's my fate.
because everything
i love leaves me
i have no faith left
in permanence.
writings.explanation: The writer says love, like smoking, is bad for you. Everything he loves leaves him, so he wonders if it is his fault or just his fate, and he no longer believes anything can last.

writings.title: My rib is a cage that keeps my heart from coming to you.
writings.content:
My rib is a cage
that keeps my heart
from coming to you.

What a cruel design
to carry the prisoner
that longs for you
and the prison that
keeps it away within
the same body.
writings.explanation: The writer says his ribs are like a cage that keeps his heart from going to the person he loves. He finds it cruel that his one body holds both the heart that wants her and the cage that keeps it away.

writings.title: I do not ask you to remember me forever.
writings.content:
I do not ask you to
remember me forever.
I only ask that,
if you ever go looking
for someone again,
remember me for once.
I only ask that you
remember me the way
I loved you, not the
way you thought I did.
I ask you Let yourself
be loved let yourself stay.
writings.explanation: The writer does not ask to be remembered forever. He only asks that if she ever looks for love again, she remembers him once, and remembers how he truly loved her, not how she thought he did. He asks her to let herself be loved and to stay.

writings.title: But to survive what you once loved is the greatest tragedy of all
writings.content:
But to survive what you once loved is the
greatest tragedy of all. How do I make
peace with the fact that the person I
once believed was my everything is now only
a scar across my chest?
writings.explanation: The writer says the worst thing is to keep living after losing someone you loved. He asks how to accept that the person who was once his whole world is now just a painful mark on his heart.

writings.title: July came by again, but still you haven't
writings.content:
July came by again,
but still you haven't.
How much more
do I have to wait?
How much more
do I have to pray?

Soon it'll be October.
Soon, the prayer will
turn into a dirge for us.
writings.explanation: July has come again, but the person he waits for has not. He asks how much longer he must wait and pray, and fears that soon, by October, his prayers for them will turn into a funeral song.

writings.title: If you keep a rose beside my flowing blood
writings.content:
If you keep a rose
beside my flowing blood,
I don't know how
much difference in color
you'll see.

But whatever difference
remains that difference
will be my love for you.
writings.explanation: The writer says if you put a red rose next to his blood, you might barely see a difference in color. Whatever small difference there is, that is his love for her.

writings.title: It's not about who stays or who leaves
writings.content:
It's not about who
stays or who leaves.
It's about for whom
you stop in the middle
of a prayer just to pray
for them as well.

Because there are
people you stop asking
God to bring back,
yet you never stop asking
God to keep them safe.
writings.explanation: The writer says what matters is not who stays or leaves, but who you stop to pray for in the middle of your own prayer. Some people you stop asking God to bring back, but you never stop asking God to keep them safe.

writings.title: Maybe that's my problem. I would give everything and ask for nothing…
writings.content:
Maybe that's my problem.
I would give everything and
ask for nothing in return.
But there is a peculiar
tragedy in giving
you never know when
the cup has become full,
when it has begun to overflow.
You never know where generosity ends
and self-abandonment begins.
You never know where to stop.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks his problem is that he gives everything and asks for nothing back. The sad part of giving is that you can't tell when it is too much, or where being kind ends and losing yourself begins, so you never know when to stop.

writings.title: I search for you the way my fingers trace old memories
writings.content:
I search for you
the way my fingers
trace old memories, only to
find the friction of love,
like the way you
used to caress my hair.
My fingers always return
to the same place,
and still I wonder, why do
I keep living through a heart
that no longer knows whether it
beats out of love or out of habit?
writings.explanation: The writer looks for the person he lost in old memories, like the feel of her hand in his hair. He keeps going back to the same memories and wonders if his heart still beats out of love for her or just out of habit.

writings.title: There are ways people survive after love
writings.content:
There are ways people
survive after love.
I think it's only two
strangers learning how
to share the same body
without actually sharing one.

One still waits at a
door that will never open.
The other has already
started walking home.
writings.explanation: He seems to say that after love ends, it is like two strangers living in one body. One part still waits at a door that will never open, while the other part has already started moving on.

writings.title: There's a cruelty in writing your name and forgetting what to write a…
writings.content:
There's a cruelty in
writing your name
and forgetting what
to write after it.

"Perhaps love was
never the words
I wrote."
Perhaps it was always
your name.
writings.explanation: The writer finds it painful to write her name and then not know what to write next. He thinks maybe love was never in the words he wrote, but only in her name itself.

writings.title: The more I talk to people, the more I realize how unbearable your abs…
writings.content:
The more I talk to
people, the more
I realize how
unbearable your
absence has become.

There is a repetitive disaster
in taking out your pictures
from my wallet and keeping
them inside it again.
I am stuck.
writings.explanation: The more the writer talks to other people, the more he feels how much he misses the person who is gone. He keeps taking her photos out of his wallet and putting them back again, and he feels stuck.

writings.title: Perhaps love was never the opposite of sorrow
writings.content:
Perhaps love was
never the opposite
of sorrow.

Perhaps it was simply
the name we gave to
what we knew we
would lose and chose
to love anyway.
writings.explanation: The writer thinks love may not be the opposite of sadness. Maybe love is just the name for caring about something we know we will lose, and choosing to care anyway.

writings.title: Roses are red. So is my blood.
writings.content:
Roses are red. So
is my blood. Is that
why you mistook
them for it? Tell me,
which one do you
love? I'll bring that
for you next time.

If you don't
know what is
grief, then
what is grief?

There's you and
then there are
things that makes
me remember
you, oh god how
beautiful they are.

कह देना कि प्यार है,
भी प्यार है♡

If you don't
know what's
wrong, then
what's
wrong?

If you don't
know what's
wrong, then
what's
wrong?
writings.explanation: These are short thoughts. The writer asks if she mistook his blood for roses, since both are red, and which she loves. He wonders what grief or wrong even is if you can't name it, finds things that remind him of her beautiful, and says in Hindi that saying it is love is love too.

writings.title: To be forgiven is to admit that one has been seen completely
writings.content:
To be forgiven is to
admit that one has
been seen completely
and loved nonetheless,

and there are souls
for whom such a thing
is more unbearable
than punishment.
writings.explanation: The writer says being forgiven means someone has seen all of you, even the bad parts, and still loves you. For some people, that is harder to bear than being punished.

writings.title: Behind my every breath, there is an air of you
writings.content:
Behind my every breath,
there is an air of you.
and I keep
forgetting that what
I once inhaled,
I must now exhale.
Perhaps that is why
I fear breathing now,
unable to bear this loss,
I may simply forget
how to breathe.
writings.explanation: The writer feels the person he lost is in every breath he takes. He keeps forgetting that he must let her go, like breathing out, and because the loss is too much, he fears he might just forget how to breathe.

writings.title: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us
writings.content:
Perhaps we do not
cling to our suffering
because it is dear
to us.

Perhaps we cling
to it because it is
the last hope that
cannot be taken away
without taking us with it.

(now read the
underlined part)
writings.explanation: The writer thinks we don't hold on to our pain because we love it. We hold on because it is our last hope, and it cannot be taken without taking us too. The last line points to a hidden message in underlined words.

writings.title: I have begun to suspect that the most terrible thing about guilt
writings.content:
I have begun to
suspect that the
most terrible thing
about guilt is not that
it condemns a man,

but that it leaves
him with nothing
left to accuse except
himself.
writings.explanation: The writer has started to think the worst thing about guilt is not that it judges a man. It is that it leaves him with no one to blame but himself.

writings.title: There are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved
writings.content:
There are ways to let go,
there are ways to show
how much you loved,

and then there is
cutting your hair off.
Yes, it held a
lot of memories.
writings.explanation: The writer says there are many ways to let go of someone and to show how much you loved them. He cut his hair off, because that hair carried a lot of memories.

writings.title: I realised i didn't have insomnia at all it was just lack of love
writings.content:
I realised i didn't
have insomnia at all
it was just
lack of love
when I closed my eyes,

uncertainty that,
when I close my eyes
there will be no you in it,
there will be no you in it..
writings.explanation: The writer thought he had trouble sleeping, but it was not an illness. He could not sleep because he felt a lack of love, and he was afraid that when he closed his eyes, the person he loves would not be there anymore.

writings.title: Between your heart and mine lies an unbridgeable distance
writings.content:
Between your heart and mine
lies an unbridgeable distance,
somewhere along it,
I am lost.
But how can I stop
admiring you when you
are all that my heart desires?
writings.explanation: The writer feels a huge distance between his heart and the heart of the person he loves, too big to ever cross, and he feels lost in it. Still, he cannot stop admiring that person, because they are all his heart wants.

writings.title: Grief, chaos, and an endless noise of things that rots within me
writings.content:
Grief, chaos, and an endless noise
of things that rots within me,

I die everyday a little more than yesterday,

Perhaps I am more dead than alive
each passing day..
writings.explanation: The writer is full of grief, mess and noise, like something rotting inside him. He feels a little more of him dies each day, until he seems more dead than alive.

writings.title: there are ways to let go, there are ways to show how much you loved
writings.content:
there are ways to let go,
there are ways
to show how much
you loved,

and then there is
cutting your hair off
to show how much
you did. yes, it held
alot of memories.
writings.explanation: The writer says there are many ways to let go and to show how much you loved someone. He cut his hair off to show how much he loved, because that hair held many memories.

writings.title: Any place where you stay for long becomes your home
writings.content:
Any place where you stay for long
becames your home,

Some places Dont ask you to stay,
Only to rest for a while,

Enough to let the storm calm down..

It can be anywhere, even a person, even a heart,
even a presence, even a feeling.

Do not mistake it for permanence...
writings.explanation: The writer says any place you stay in long becomes home. But some places, even a person or a feeling, only let you rest for a while until your troubles calm down. He says not to think they will last forever.

writings.title: Unfortunately after you everything was going well when I thought it w…
writings.content:
Unfortunately after you
everything was going
well when I thought
it wouldn't.

But some how my heart
still remembers what
you gave to it I still ache
for you that's
the biggest tragedy.
writings.explanation: After the person left, the writer's life went well, even though he expected it would not. Still, his heart remembers what that person gave it, and he still longs for them. To him, that longing is the saddest part.

writings.title: Tragedy is, Like oranges i would peel my heart out to you too
writings.content:
Tragedy is, Like oranges
i would peel
my heart out to you too.

But like my heart
you would never
keep ~~eat~~ them too.

But yet foolishness of love
never made me realise that
the peels you loved so much
were always to spray
the citrus into my eyes.

I am blind ~~in love~~ now.
writings.explanation: The writer opened his heart to the person he loved, the way you peel an orange for someone. But that person never kept it, and the parts they liked were only used to hurt him. Love kept him from seeing it, and now he is blinded, by pain and by love.

writings.title: Somewhere along the way, I stopped becoming myself
writings.content:
Somewhere
along the way,
I stopped becoming myself.

I am what
I was never
meant to be.
I am what
I was left with.
writings.explanation: The writer says that at some point he stopped being his true self. Now he is someone he was never supposed to be, just what was left of him after everything that happened.

writings.title: Mother, I have been hiding myself
writings.content:
Mother,
I have been hiding
myself. But you looked
at my face

and knew something
was wrong with me.
No one else noticed.
Only you.
writings.explanation: The writer had been hiding his pain from everyone. His mother looked at his face and knew something was wrong, and she was the only one who noticed.

writings.title: There are certain people whom you can know by my smiles
writings.content:
There are certain
people whom you
can know
by my smiles

because behind
every smile I still
carry a fragment
of their existence
writings.explanation: The writer says some people still live on in his smiles. Every time he smiles, he carries a small piece of them, so you could know those people just by watching him smile.

writings.title: Flowers aren't meant to be plucked
writings.content:
Flowers aren't
meant to be plucked.

But who am
I to say that,
when I was the one
who plucked my
own happiness every
time it came alive?
writings.explanation: The writer says flowers should not be picked. But he feels he has no right to say that, because every time happiness started to grow in his life, he was the one who killed it.

writings.title: If loving me comes with a cost then I hope it's not love
writings.content:
If loving me
comes with a cost
then I hope
it's not love

Because my love
was never meant
to be felt like
something you had
to pay for.
writings.explanation: The writer says that if loving him feels like it costs something, he hopes that is not really his love. His love was never meant to feel like a price someone has to pay.

writings.title: Living ofcourse is merely an act letting go
writings.content:
Living ofcourse
is merely an act
letting go.
Even your breath,
even your love.
writings.explanation: The writer says living is really just letting go, again and again. We let go of every breath, and we let go of love too.

writings.title: There were endless possibilities but life chose to do us apart
writings.content:
There were endless
possibilities
but life chose
to do us apart ,

i wonder how,
i wonder why.
writings.explanation: The writer says he and someone else could have had many different futures together, but life pulled them apart. He keeps wondering how and why it happened.

writings.title: Every time I cry, my tears begin to shape you
writings.content:
Every time I cry,
my tears begin to shape you

from the traces you left behind,
so that the next time I miss you,

I can look upon them
and find another reason to weep.
writings.explanation: Each time the writer cries, his tears seem to build a picture of the person he lost from what they left behind. So the next time he misses them, he has one more reason to cry.

writings.title: I carry grief like a second skin, stitched into everything I do
writings.content:
I carry grief like
a second skin,
stitched into
everything I do.

There are days
I laugh so naturally
that it feels like
I am betraying this
skin of grief I have too.
writings.explanation: The writer says grief is part of him, like a second skin that touches everything he does. On days he laughs easily, he feels guilty, as if being happy is turning his back on his grief.

writings.title: The most dangerous thieves don't wear masks, they wear authority
writings.content:
The most
dangerous thieves
don't wear
masks, they wear
authority.
writings.explanation: The writer says the most dangerous people who steal do not hide behind masks. They are the ones in power, who take from others openly.

writings.title: My mother says there are some people you should never wait for
writings.content:
My mother says
there are some people
you should never
wait for.

I smile, because
she doesn't know
that my entire way of
living is waiting.
writings.explanation: The writer's mother tells him some people are not worth waiting for. He smiles, because she does not know that his whole life has become waiting.

writings.title: The spine is a strange thing like a ladder built inside us
writings.content:
The spine is
a strange thing
like a ladder
built inside us

so that someday
memory may climb
to our throat
and die there,
unable to become
a language.
writings.explanation: The writer pictures the backbone as a ladder inside the body. Memories climb it up to the throat, but get stuck there and die, because they can never be turned into words.

writings.title: The rain always knows when to stop. My grief never does
writings.content:
The rain always knows when to stop.
My grief never does.

I gaze at the puddle to see my reflection,
but even the reflection shows your face.

I wonder why it shows you when you were
the very one who left me standing in the rain.
writings.explanation: The writer says rain knows when to stop, but his grief does not. When he looks at his reflection in a puddle, he sees the face of the person he lost, and wonders why, since that person left him alone in his hard times.

writings.title: I wonder why leaving and living sound so similar.
writings.content:
I wonder why leaving and living
sound so similar.
Is it because living is merely
the slow act of leaving
behind everything we have loved
our whole lives,
or because to leave is,
in its own cruel way, to love?
Or is it because they knew we would
lose everything we ever loved?
Because I am still trying
to understand why you left.
writings.explanation: The writer notices that leaving and living sound almost the same. He wonders if living is just slowly leaving behind everyone we love, or if leaving is a hard kind of love. Under it all, he is still trying to understand why the person he loved left.

writings.title: If there is a God inside the human body, He abandoned mine long ago
writings.content:
If there is a God
inside the human body,
He abandoned
mine long ago.
All that remains
is a cathedral like
empty chest,
full of abandonment,

where my thoughts kneel every night,
praying to a saint who has forgotten
the language of mercy. oh, and love too.
writings.explanation: The writer feels that if God lives inside people, God left him long ago. His chest feels like an empty church, and every night his thoughts pray to someone who no longer shows kindness, or love.

writings.title: I have forgotten the language my heart spoke before it became fluent…
writings.content:
I have forgotten
the language my heart
spoke before it became
fluent in loss,
yet I remember the exact
silence that settled
between my heart and you
before you left.
I remember the weight of the air,
the way the world was silent,
as if my heart wasn't screaming enough.
writings.explanation: The writer has forgotten how his heart felt before it was full of loss. But he clearly remembers the silence between him and the person just before they left, how heavy the air felt, and how quiet the world was while his heart was screaming inside.

writings.title: But every now and then, your memories rush into me
writings.content:
But every now and then,
your memories rush into me.
Then I hear things
collapsing inside me,
i wonder what tragedy
you left me into,
That I never collapsed at once
just peice by peice, Weathering.
perhaps I have spent my whole
life arriving too late to rescue myself,
if only i had come a little sooner,
i could have saved it all.
writings.explanation: Sometimes memories of the person flood back, and the writer feels himself breaking inside. He did not fall apart all at once, but slowly, bit by bit, over time. He feels he has always come too late to save himself, and wishes he had come sooner.

writings.title: I used to think poison kills
writings.content:
I used to think poison kills.
Then I met your memories
that arrive as comfort,
speaks like home, and leaves,
that you mistake the
abandonment, slowly,
for your own heartbeat.

You know, the cruelest poisons are
not the ones that stop your heart.
They are the ones that teach it
to survive on what is killing it.
writings.explanation: The writer once thought only poison could kill. But memories of the lost person feel like comfort and home, until being left alone feels as normal as his own heartbeat. He says the worst poison does not stop your heart; it teaches it to keep living on what is hurting it.

writings.title: I wonder why nails grow beneath the grave too
writings.content:
I wonder why
nails grow beneath
the grave too.
Is it because even
after everything ends,
things still find
a way to grow?
I think it is a universal law
that nothing ends when it truly does.
Thus, my love for you.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders why nails keep growing even in the grave. He takes it to mean that even after things end, something still grows. His love for the person is like that: it keeps going even though it is over.

writings.title: It's August now, and I wonder how you've been
writings.content:
It's August now,
and I wonder how you've been.
I wonder whether you've
eaten today or not.
I am no longer close enough to ask,
but then I wonder—
How far apart can two people truly be
after having shared so much of themselves?
writings.explanation: It is August, and the writer wonders how a person he was once close to is doing, even whether they have eaten today. He is no longer close enough to ask, but he wonders how two people who shared so much can ever be truly far apart.

writings.title: tears will tear you.
writings.content: tears will tear you.
writings.explanation: The writer says that crying from sadness, if it goes on, will rip you apart inside.

writings.title: My existence in the lives of others has always been measured by the…
writings.content:
My existence in the lives of others
has always been measured by the

weight of what I could offer.

Once their need for me faded,
so did my place in their world.
writings.explanation: The writer feels people only valued him for what he could give them. When they no longer needed him, they no longer kept a place for him in their lives.

writings.title: You happened to me, poetry came much later.
writings.content:
You happened to me,
poetry came much later.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person came into his life first, and his poems came only later, because of them.

writings.title: I know I will be abandoned. Yet still, I pour the glass full of love
writings.content:
I know I will be abandoned.
Yet still,
I pour the glass full of love.

There is a strange beauty in offering abundance
to a world that has taught you scarcity.
To love is to
never cease to exist,
to love is to live and give.
writings.explanation: The writer knows he will be left alone in the end, but he still gives his love fully. He finds something beautiful in giving a lot to a world that has given him little, and believes loving means truly living and giving.

writings.title: There's a tight rope of hope that binds me with you!
writings.content:
There's a tight rope of hope
that binds me with you!

But that rope too is about to tear away
just like my heart, just like us.
I wonder is it the hope that binds me
or just a glimpse of you,
again or is it love I wonder....
writings.explanation: The writer feels tied to the person by a thin rope of hope, but that rope is about to break, just like his heart and their bond. He wonders what really holds him there: hope, the wish to see them again, or love.

writings.title: soul is deeper than an abyss.
writings.content: soul is deeper than an abyss.
writings.explanation: The writer says what is inside a person goes deeper than any bottomless pit.

writings.title: The grave was never a piece of land, it was always my heart
writings.content:
The grave was never a piece of land, it was
always my heart with all the buried memories.

Every time my heart aches,
I know there are more memorial corpses
being buried alive.
What a tragedy it is to hear
a requiem with every heartbeat,
knowing each pulse is another eulogy
for a part of me that has just died.
writings.explanation: The writer says his heart is the real grave, where his memories are buried. Each time it aches, more memories are buried while still alive, and every heartbeat feels like a funeral song for another part of him that has died.

writings.title: my soul desires to be understood more than it does to be loved.
writings.content:
my soul desires to be understood
more than it does to be loved.
writings.explanation: The writer wants to be understood even more than he wants to be loved.

writings.title: There are only two fates for a single story it happens, or it never d…
writings.content:
There are only two
fates for a single story
it happens,
or it never does.
Everything else is merely the
space between those two truths
the almost and the what happens,
the hands that nearly touch and the hands
that are held. But the story never truly ends.
Some are lived, some are lost, and some
remain suspended on the verge of what could
have been of what could have been of us.
writings.explanation: The writer says a story either happens or it never does, and everything else is the space in between, like two people almost holding hands. Some stories are lived, some are lost, and some, like his story with this person, stay stuck forever at what could have been.

writings.title: you can feel the loss of something before you've even lost it.
writings.content:
you can feel the loss of something
before you've even lost it.
writings.explanation: The writer says you can start to feel the pain of losing something even before it is actually gone.

writings.title: My forbidden fruit was never an apple it was you
writings.content:
My forbidden fruit
was never an apple
it was you. I knew that
loving you would cost me
hell, yet still, I loved you
passionately, as if I were
meant to reach for you
knowing hell means heaven
with you. Perhaps that is
why temptation tastes so
much like grief because
I mistook your sweetness
for my salvation.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person he loved was like forbidden fruit: something he knew he should not reach for. He loved them anyway, even knowing it would cost him dearly. Now that wanting feels like grief, because he thought their sweetness would save him.

writings.title: all these acts, all these pretending only to hide how deeply I feel.
writings.content:
all these acts, all these pretending
only to hide how deeply I feel.
writings.explanation: The writer says all his acting and pretending is only a way to hide how strongly he feels.

writings.title: Being desired isn't the same as being loved.
writings.content:
Being desired isn't the
same as being loved.
writings.explanation: The writer says that someone wanting you is not the same as someone truly loving you.

writings.title: I return to the fire hoping it won't burn me this time.
writings.content:
I return to the fire hoping
it won't burn me this time.
writings.explanation: The writer keeps going back to the thing that hurt him before, hoping that this time it will not hurt him again.

writings.title: love, greif, hope, death all while being alive.
writings.content:
love, greif, hope, death
all while being alive.
writings.explanation: He seems to say that a person goes through love, grief, hope and even something like death, all while still being alive.

writings.title: SMOKING KILLS so does love! i know it will kill me so does memories b…
writings.content:
so does love!
i know it will kill me
so does memories
but can you be saved anyway?
writings.explanation: The writer says love will destroy him, and so will memories. Even knowing this, he asks whether someone can still be saved.

writings.title: Everything you lost will scream through the emptiness it left behind.
writings.content:
Everything you lost will scream
through the emptiness it left behind.
writings.explanation: The writer says everything you lose leaves an empty space behind, and that emptiness keeps loudly reminding you of what is gone.

writings.title: Even heaven would feel hell without you, it's still earth.
writings.content:
Even heaven would feel hell
without you, it's still earth.
writings.explanation: The writer says that without the person he loves, even heaven would feel like hell. He seems to say no place could feel special to him without them.

writings.title: memories don't fade, they feed on you.
writings.content: memories don't fade, they feed on you.
writings.explanation: The writer says memories do not slowly go away. Instead, they keep eating away at you.

writings.title: nostalgia is grief with a memory
writings.content: nostalgia is grief with a memory
writings.explanation: The writer says missing the past is really a kind of grief, sadness tied to a memory.

writings.title: If loving you was a beautiful mistake
writings.content:
If loving you
was a beautiful mistake,
then I would make it again,
knowing exactly where
it would lead me.
Perhaps that is
the tragedy of my heart
I never feared being broken
as long as the pieces
still remembered
the shape of you.
writings.explanation: The writer says loving the person was a beautiful mistake, and he would make it again even knowing how it ends. The sad part is that he never feared being broken, as long as the broken pieces still remembered that person.

writings.title: We miss what made us miserable.
writings.content: We miss what made us miserable.
writings.explanation: The writer says we often miss the very things that made us unhappy.

writings.title: your absence penetrates the deepest parts of me.
writings.content:
your absence penetrates
the deepest parts of me.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person being gone hurts him deep down, in the most hidden parts of him.

writings.title: once your heart turns cold, warmth becomes unbearable.
writings.content:
once your heart turns cold,
warmth becomes unbearable.
writings.explanation: The writer says that once your heart has gone cold from hurt, kindness and love become hard to bear.

writings.title: I saw the moon in your eyes, but never a place for myself in it.
writings.content:
I saw the moon in your eyes,
but never a place for myself in it.
writings.explanation: The writer saw beauty and light in the person's eyes, but never saw any room for himself there.

writings.title: I die when I have to pretend
writings.content:
I die when
I have to pretend
that your absence
does not hurt.
I die when
I see you happy
and realise I am no
longer part of it.

I die when I almost tell you
how much I miss you then
remember you stopped asking.
writings.explanation: The writer feels like he dies inside when he has to pretend the person being gone does not hurt, and when he sees them happy without him. It hurts most when he almost tells them he misses them, then remembers they stopped asking about him.

writings.title: love is a prelude to loss
writings.content: love is a prelude to loss
writings.explanation: The writer says love always comes before loss, as if loving something is the first step to losing it.

writings.title: After love, you start killing it.
writings.content:
After love,
you start killing it.
writings.explanation: The writer seems to say that once love has come, people slowly start to destroy it themselves.

writings.title: All the love lying inside me, Only to become heartless.
writings.content:
All the love lying inside me,
Only to become heartless.
writings.explanation: The writer has so much love inside him, but in the end it has only left him cold and without feeling.

writings.title: people who suffer from cold, would starve themselves for warmth.
writings.content:
people who suffer from cold,
would starve themselves for warmth.
writings.explanation: The writer says people who have felt cold for a long time would give up even food just to feel warm. He seems to mean that people without love will give up a lot to get some.

writings.title: I ache to be held, and yet I stiffen at the touch.
writings.content:
I ache to be held, and
yet I stiffen at the touch.
writings.explanation: The writer badly wants someone to hold him, but when someone does touch him, his body tenses up.

writings.title: If love was a sin, I would be the deepest kind of sinner,
writings.content:
If love was a sin,
I would be the deepest
kind of sinner,
because my love for you
is selfish yet selfless.

I would give you everything
and yet ask for nothing in return,
because if falling out of love after it
ends diminishes what it once was,
then heaven without it would
feel utterly worthless.
writings.explanation: The writer says that if love were a sin, he would be the worst sinner, because his love is both selfish and giving. He would give the person everything and want nothing back. To him, even heaven without this love would be worthless.

writings.title: People choose themselves in the very moment we hoped they would choos…
writings.content:
People choose themselves in the very
moment we hoped they would choose us.
writings.explanation: The writer says people often put themselves first at the exact moment we were hoping they would choose us.

writings.title: Maybe the cruelest thing about time is that it doesn't just pass
writings.content:
Maybe the cruelest
thing about time is
that it doesn't just pass,
it makes us pass with it.
We lose Days,
Days turn into people,
people turn into pieces of ourselves.

until one day we realise the person
who once lived through it all is someone
we can no longer return to.
Neither the people nor ourselves.
writings.explanation: The writer says time does not just go by; it changes us as it goes. We lose days, those days become people we lost, and those people become parts of us. In the end, we cannot go back to who we were, or to those people.

writings.title: It's September again, and I still can't let go
writings.content:
It's September again,
and I still can't let go,
your memories with the scent of rain
and the faint aftertaste of promises.
The year is close enough to its ending,
but what about us? Tell me,
how do I tell this heart full of hope
that it was abandoned by the very thing
it ached to belong to?
writings.explanation: It is September, and the writer still cannot let go. Memories of the person come back with the smell of rain and old promises. The year is nearly over, and he wonders how to tell his hopeful heart that the one it longed to belong to has left it.

writings.title: i keep pushing away everything that tries to keep me.
writings.content:
i keep pushing away
everything that tries to keep me.
writings.explanation: The writer keeps pushing away every person and thing that tries to hold on to him.

writings.title: The tragedy of belonging is never finding where you belong.
writings.content:
The tragedy of belonging is
never finding where you belong.
writings.explanation: The writer says the sad part about wanting to belong is that you may never find the place where you truly fit.

writings.title: If loving you was a prayer, then I would pray until your eyes finally…
writings.content:
If loving you
was a prayer,
then I would pray until
your eyes finally gazed
upon this filthy soul.
There is a strange beauty in praying even
after the answer has refused you. You do
not stop because you did not receive what
you asked for, you pray harder. Perhaps
that's exactly how love is you cling to it
despite knowing you can never make it yours.
It's all hope until it's your love.
writings.explanation: The writer says that if loving the person were a prayer, he would keep praying until they finally looked at him, even though he feels unworthy. Like someone who prays harder after the answer is no, he holds on to his love even knowing that person can never be his.

writings.title: Even the lines on my hand says your name how could I not mistake you…
writings.content:
Even the lines on my hand
says your name
how could I not mistake you
for destiny?
writings.explanation: The writer feels the person is so much a part of him that even the lines on his palm seem to spell their name. So it was easy for him to believe, maybe wrongly, that they were meant to be.

writings.title: flowers of grief grows beneath my skin.
writings.content: flowers of grief grows beneath my skin.
writings.explanation: The writer says grief is growing inside him, under his skin, the way flowers grow from the ground.

writings.title: They say panic attacks come from nowhere
writings.content:
They say panic attacks come from nowhere
but the body usually knows
before the mind admits it
funny how it senses old memories rushing back
breath turns shallow like it's bracing for impact
the room stays the same
and you wait to settle again
writings.explanation: The writer says panic attacks seem to come from nowhere, but the body often knows first, sensing old memories coming back. Breathing gets short as if getting ready for a hit, and though nothing in the room changes, you just wait to calm down again.

writings.title: Heaven above my thoughts, A hell beneath my skin.
writings.content:
Heaven above my thoughts,
A hell beneath my skin.
writings.explanation: The writer says his mind reaches for something peaceful and good, while under his skin he is suffering badly.

writings.title: Scars on my hand, Bleeds nothing but you.
writings.content:
Scars on my hand,
Bleeds nothing but you.
writings.explanation: The writer says the scars on his hand hold nothing but the person he lost; all his pain comes from them.

writings.title: I stink of the memories that rot within me
writings.content:
I stink of the
memories that
rot within me,

their decay fermenting beneath
the skin of my consciousness,

until even maggots refuse
to eat what I have become,
until forgetting itself
becomes impossible,
and nothing remains but the rot.
writings.explanation: The writer feels his memories are rotting inside him, so badly that he feels spoiled by them. The rot goes so deep that even maggots would not want him, he can no longer forget, and nothing is left of him but the rot.

writings.title: I dream of heaven with, a hell inside my chest.
writings.content:
I dream of heaven with,
A hell inside my chest.
writings.explanation: The writer dreams of a happy, peaceful place, even while his chest feels full of pain.

writings.title: I hope when your lips meet mine
writings.content:
I hope when your
lips meet mine,
they'll tell all the stories
that we have been hiding
from each other.
I hope they'll tell how
much you have loved
me along the way and
through all the memories.
I hope they'll say that the
distance has been unbearable,
just like mine would say to yours.
writings.explanation: The writer hopes that when he and the person kiss, it will say all the things they have kept hidden from each other. He hopes it will show how much the person has loved him, and that being apart has been as painful for them as it was for him.

writings.title: Memories in my heart burn, like my soul is in purgatory.
writings.content:
Memories in my heart burn,
like my soul is in purgatory.
writings.explanation: The writer says the memories in his heart burn him, as if his soul is stuck in a place of punishment, waiting between heaven and hell.

writings.title: I still think you love me, just like I still think the moon follows us
writings.content:
I still think you
love me,
just like I still think
the moon follows us.

Isn't it funny how
we create our own
delusions to survive the grief,
because what used to make
us happy isn't there to
make us smile anymore?
writings.explanation: The writer still believes the person loves him, the same way people believe the moon follows them. He says we tell ourselves untrue things to get through grief, because what once made us happy is gone.

writings.title: to mother, I say, "I am tired.
writings.content:
to mother, I say,
"I am tired."

And she looks at me
as if she has known
all the ways
I have been breaking
before I ever learned
how to call it grief.
writings.explanation: The writer tells his mother he is tired. She looks at him as if she has always known how he has been breaking inside, even before he knew to call it grief.

writings.title: Loneliness is a religion of the forsaken, and grief is its only scrip…
writings.content:
Loneliness is a religion of the forsaken,
and grief is its only scripture.
writings.explanation: The writer says loneliness is like a religion for people who have been left behind, and grief is the only holy book it has.

writings.title: Perhaps we do not cling to our suffering because it is dear to us
writings.content:
Perhaps we do not
cling to our suffering
because it is dear
to us.

Perhaps we cling
to it because it is
the last hope that
cannot be taken away
without taking us with it.
writings.explanation: The writer says maybe we do not hold on to our pain because we love it. Maybe we hold on because it is the last hope we have, and it cannot be taken from us without taking us too.

writings.title: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence.
writings.content:
I would trade my soul with the devil
for a moment of your presence.
writings.explanation: The writer would give up his soul to the devil just to be near the person for one moment.

writings.title: Absence of hope leads to despair.
writings.content: Absence of hope leads to despair.
writings.explanation: The writer says that when there is no hope left, a person falls into deep sadness and gives up.

writings.title: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what destroyed it.
writings.content:
Nostalgia seduces the soul
into worshipping what destroyed it.
writings.explanation: The writer says missing the past can trick a person into loving and longing for the very thing that ruined them.

writings.title: The human heart invents gods to absolve the sins it cannot forget.
writings.content:
The human heart invents gods
to absolve the sins it cannot forget.
writings.explanation: The writer says people make up gods so they can feel forgiven for the wrongs they cannot stop remembering.

writings.title: I would trade my soul with the devil for a moment of your presence
writings.content:
I would trade my soul
with the devil

for a moment
of your presence,
for what is eternity
worth to a heart
that has forgotten
how to feel alive?

Because even heaven
would become unbearably
lonely without you.
writings.explanation: The writer would give his soul to the devil just to be with the person for one moment. Living forever means nothing to a heart that no longer feels alive, and even heaven would feel too lonely without them.

writings.title: Abandonment smells like a perfume we breathe in again and again.
writings.content:
Abandonment smells like a perfume
we breathe in again and again.
writings.explanation: Being left by someone is a hurt that keeps coming back. Like a smell you keep breathing in, it stays close, and we feel it again and again.

writings.title: Nostalgia seduces the soul into worshipping what once destroyed it
writings.content:
Nostalgia seduces
the soul into worshipping
what once destroyed it.
It perfumes the ashes
so that we mistake the smoke for
the scent of home. How nostalgic.

The longer you dwell in memories,
the deeper the ache becomes.
I wonder if ruins grow roses only
because we keep bleeding into their soil.
No wonder memories bloom beautifully,
even when all they ever did was destroy us.
writings.explanation: The writer says missing the past makes us love the very things that hurt us. Memory makes old pain seem sweet, like home. The longer we stay in memories, the more it hurts, and memories look beautiful only because we keep feeding them with our pain.

writings.title: Liar, just like your presence was all that love a lie too?
writings.content:
Lair, just like your presence
was all that love a lie too?
writings.explanation: The writer calls someone a liar. He asks if their love was fake too, just as their being with him turned out to be false.

writings.title: Hunger for warmth will leave you into the cold.
writings.content:
Hunger for warmth will
leave you into the cold.
writings.explanation: Wanting warmth and closeness too badly can end with you being left alone and cold.

writings.title: My Love, is not the desire to have you
writings.content:
My Love,
is not the desire
to have you,

but a defect in the soul
that mistakes the silence
left behind your absence
for a language that would
tell what I did for you to leave,

so I rot and rot and rot
while understanding the meaning
of the closed door that might
open anytime, or maybe not.
writings.explanation: The writer says his love is not about wanting to have the person. It is a broken part of him that keeps listening to their silence, hoping it will tell him what he did to make them leave. So he slowly falls apart, waiting by a door that may or may not open.

writings.title: You don't need a presence to love someone.
writings.content:
You don't need a
presence to love someone.
Love exists with
or without them,
just as faith does not
require God to stand before
you to make you believe.
the existence of love is not dependent on the
existence of the person to whom it belonged.
They may leave you by a random Tuesday
night, disappear , or become a stranger,
but the fire they started in your heart would
still burn without their oxygen like presence.
writings.explanation: The writer says you can love someone even when they are not there. Just as faith in God does not need to see God, love does not need the person. They may leave or become a stranger, but the love they started keeps burning inside you anyway.

writings.title: Love is a habitual process that Stops only when your heart does.
writings.content:
Love is a habitual process that Stops
only when your heart does.
writings.explanation: Love is like a habit that never stops. It only ends when your heart stops beating, which means when you die.

writings.title: I can almost smell the coming of October
writings.content:
I can almost smell
the coming of October,
as someone who
earlier lost his
everything in it.

Autumn of abandonment,
smells like a perfume
we breathe again and again,

like the nostalgia of memories
we know we are bound to lose.
writings.explanation: The writer can feel October coming, the month he once lost everything in. The pain of being left comes back every autumn like a familiar smell, along with memories he knows he will lose one day.

writings.title: The inertia of memories binds you to the grief.
writings.content:
The inertia of memories
binds you to the grief.
writings.explanation: Memories keep you stuck in place, so you cannot move on from your grief.

writings.title: I may tell you I love you
writings.content:
I may tell you
I love you,
But deep down
i know what parts of me
I have abandoned to
keep this love alive.

What parts of me I have thrown
into the fire to keep it burning.

I am the martyr
I am the martyrdom,
and love? it's my religion.
writings.explanation: The writer says he loves someone, but he knows he gave up parts of himself to keep that love going, burning pieces of himself like fuel. He sees himself as the one who suffers for love, and love is what he worships.

writings.title: all I am is an actor, destined to perform for rest of my life.
writings.content:
all I am is an actor, destined
to perform for rest of my life.
writings.explanation: The writer feels his life is just acting, putting on a show, and that he will have to keep doing it for the rest of his life.

writings.title: My rib is a cage that mourns the absence of the bird it lost.
writings.content:
My rib is a cage that mourns
the absence of the bird it lost.
writings.explanation: The writer's chest feels like an empty cage. It is sad because the person he loved, like a bird, has gone.

writings.title: If loving you was a sin I would do it again and again
writings.content:
If loving you
was a sin
I would do it
again and again

Till both god and devil
come to me and ask about
what devotion of faith
I have in you.

I'll tell them about your eyes and
they'll never be able to return again.

Heaven or hell I deserve
neither except for your eyes.
writings.explanation: The writer says if loving the person is wrong, he would still do it again and again. If God and the devil asked about his faith, he would just describe the person's eyes, and they would be lost in them too. He wants neither heaven nor hell, only those eyes.

writings.title: Grief comes from the acceptance of the loss
writings.content:
Grief comes from
the acceptance of the loss,
of things you never
thought you would lose.

To make a home around
a grave called the heart
is what we call existing,
and all we do in that home is mourn.

Nobody prepares you for losing the
permanence you once believed life possessed,
and perhaps that is the cruelest tragedy.
writings.explanation: Grief begins when you accept losing something you never thought you would lose. Living feels like making a home around a heart that is like a grave, and just mourning there. The cruelest part is that nobody warns you that nothing in life lasts forever.

writings.title: Heart is no different than a grave,
writings.content:
Heart is no different than a grave,
both holds people and their memories.
writings.explanation: The writer says a heart is like a grave. Both keep people inside, along with the memories of them.

writings.title: I am Half hope, Half death;
writings.content: I am Half hope, Half death;
writings.explanation: The writer feels split in two: one half still hopes, and the other half feels dead inside.

writings.title: They say energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
writings.content:
They say energy can neither
be created nor destroyed.
Funny because
the energy I poured into
my bonds disappeared
like smoke in an open sky,
nothing to hold, nothing to return.
I was broken by the very hands I warmed.
So tell me, if feelings follow the same laws,
where do they go when they're the ones left
in ruins? Do they stay like ash in the lungs
unseen yet heavy? Or do they learn to survive
by changing form, becoming the silence we
carry forward?
writings.explanation: Science says energy never disappears, but the care the writer gave to people vanished with nothing coming back. The people he loved hurt him. He asks where feelings go after that: do they stay inside as a hidden, heavy weight, or turn into the silence we carry with us?

writings.title: I wish I could tell you that all the abandoned emotions
writings.content:
I wish
I could tell you that
all the abandoned
emotions now lying in the
coldest part of my heart once
belonged to you.

How the colourful flowers that once
bloomed for you have now grown into
thorny vines that pierce me instead.

I hope that someday, when you come back,
I'll have enough flowers left to offer you
not just trembling hands numbed by cold.
writings.explanation: The writer wishes he could tell the person that the feelings now lying cold in his heart were once all for them. The love that grew for them has turned into something that hurts him. He hopes that if they return, he will still have love to give, not just cold, shaking hands.

writings.title: Flower shall grow from within my grave,
writings.content:
Flower shall grow
from within my grave,
and it shall be in
the colour of your eyes.
I won't need any other
visitors to visit my grave
except you.
just visit once in a while ,
you needn't bring flowers because
those flowers will
turn in the direction of your eyes
like sunflower finding its sun.
writings.explanation: The writer imagines a flower growing from his grave in the color of the person's eyes. He wants no visitor but them, now and then. They need not bring flowers, because that flower will turn toward their eyes, the way a sunflower turns to the sun.

writings.title: you were the fire, I was the burning moth.
writings.content:
you were the fire,
I was the burning moth.
writings.explanation: The person was like a flame, and the writer was like a moth flying into it. He was pulled toward them even though it burned him up.

writings.title: Hellfire is still colder than the way love burns me.
writings.content:
Hellfire is still colder than
the way love burns me.
writings.explanation: The writer says love hurts him so much that even the fire of hell would feel cooler than it.

writings.title: My eyes have began to search you desparately in everything,
writings.content:
My eyes have
began to search you
desparately in everything,
what did you do to me.

I go to god to ask
myself from but
I end up asking you again,
what did you do to me.

I search for heaven with
hell within my chest,
What did you do to me.
writings.explanation: The writer keeps looking for the person in everything. He goes to God to ask for himself back, but ends up asking for them instead. He looks for peace while carrying pain in his chest, and keeps wondering how they changed him so much.

writings.title: The desire itself contains its future absence.
writings.content:
The desire itself
contains its future absence.
writings.explanation: The writer says that when you want something, losing it later is already part of that wanting. Everything we long for will one day be gone.

writings.title: It's October now, and I wonder what I shall lose this year
writings.content:
It's October now,
and I wonder what
I shall lose this year.
October has become
a monolithic cycle of losing
things that were once dearer
to me than I was to myself.

Memories come like autumn,
and I fall every time.

I lost you,
and I wonder if I shall lose
these memories too.
writings.explanation: Every October the writer has lost something he loved more than himself, so now he waits to see what he will lose this year. Memories come like falling leaves, and each time he falls apart. He has lost the person and wonders if he will lose the memories too.

writings.title: It's October again, no wonder that it's the season for fall.
writings.content:
It's October again,
no wonder that it's the season for fall.
The leaves begin to wither,
and so do the things I once held dear.
It's October again,
and I find myself wondering
what will fall this time-
the leaves, the memories, or me.
writings.explanation: October is autumn, when leaves fall. The writer says the things he loved fall away too, just like the leaves. He wonders what will go this time: the leaves, his memories, or he himself.

writings.title: Hope lures you into believing there is love waiting beyond the pain.
writings.content:
Hope lures you into believing there
is love waiting beyond the pain.
writings.explanation: Hope tricks you into thinking that love is waiting for you after all the pain.

writings.title: To love is to die; to die is to be loved.
writings.content: To love is to die; to die is to be loved.
writings.explanation: He seems to say love and death are tied together: loving someone means losing yourself, like dying, and in death you are finally loved.

writings.title: Hope is a drug we willingly consume.
writings.content: Hope is a drug we willingly consume.
writings.explanation: The writer says hope is like a drug: we know what it does to us, but we still choose to keep taking it.

writings.title: The rhythm of love is hope
writings.content:
The rhythm of love is hope,
and hope lures you into believing there
is love beyond all the pain & suffering.
How far will you go for love?
Depends on you,
and addicted to hope,
you may stay loyal to pain,
until one day you realise you survive
on hope rather than love itself.
writings.explanation: The writer says hope keeps love going, making you believe love waits after the pain. Hooked on that hope, you may keep staying with the pain, until one day you see you are living on hope, not on real love.

writings.title: The price of loving is never loving again
writings.content:
The price of loving
is never loving again,
because you spend
the rest of your life
comparing every heart
to the one that taught
yours how to beat,
every face to the one that
once made you smile,
because some people become a habit
through which you see the world.
writings.explanation: The writer says once you truly love someone, you may never love again. For the rest of your life you compare every person to the one who first taught your heart to love. Some people become the way you see everything.

writings.title: Love is a myth we die believing.
writings.content: Love is a myth we die believing.
writings.explanation: Love is like a made-up story that we keep believing in until the day we die.

writings.title: Days have started to get shorter, it'll be night soon
writings.content:
Days have started to get shorter,
it'll be night soon,

But in the darkness of the
night grief knocks my door,

night brings me closer
to the things I spend
my days trying to forget.

The longer the night the
Deeper the grief, deeper the grief
colder the heart becomes.
writings.explanation: The days are getting shorter as winter comes. At night, grief comes to the writer and brings back the things he tries to forget all day. The longer the night, the deeper his sadness, and the colder his heart grows.

writings.title: Colder the heart the quieter the soul
writings.content:
Colder the heart
the quieter the soul,
the quieter the soul,
the louder
the memories become.

And the louder
the memories become,
the harder it becomes to sleep.
But you know,
what makes the heart cold is
very much the warmth it sought.
writings.explanation: The writer says when the heart turns cold, the soul goes quiet, and in that quiet the memories get louder and keep him awake. What made his heart cold was the very warmth and love it went looking for.

writings.title: Before feeling nothing at all, you feel alot.
writings.content: Before feeling nothing at all, you feel alot.
writings.explanation: Before you go numb and feel nothing, you first feel far too much. The numbness comes after a lot of pain.

writings.title: why do you keep holding on to every pain inside your heart
writings.content:
why do you
keep holding on
to every pain
inside your heart

when even the heaven's
cry by raining?
writings.explanation: The writer asks why you keep all your pain locked inside, when even the sky lets itself cry by raining. He seems to say it is okay to let the pain out.

writings.title: Till when will you mistake pain for love?
writings.content: Till when will you mistake pain for love?
writings.explanation: The writer asks how long you will keep thinking that being hurt is the same as being loved.

writings.title: If loving you leads me to the loss of myself, then why am I loving…
writings.content:
If loving you
leads me to the loss
of myself, then why
am I loving you?

If loving you feels like
a heaven within my mind
and a hell beneath my ribs,
then why am I loving you?

Why must I become less of me
every time I become more of you?
writings.explanation: The writer asks himself why he keeps loving someone when it makes him lose himself. The love feels like heaven in his mind but like hell in his chest. He asks why he must become less of himself the more he gives himself to them.

writings.title: We came from nothing, and will return to nothing
writings.content:
We came from nothing,
and will return to nothing—
leaving nothing behind but the
ache of having been nothing
to someone
for whom we felt everything.
writings.explanation: We come from nothing and go back to nothing. All that is left behind is the pain of having meant nothing to someone who meant everything to us.

writings.title: when god asks me what my last wish before returning to nothingness is
writings.content:
when god asks me
what my last wish
before returning
to nothingness is.
I'll ask him to let me relive
my moments with you again.
to be 18 again,
naive and full of love,
when I found
my religion in those eyes.
but that will be to much
to ask for so I just die.
writings.explanation: When he dies, the writer would ask God for one last wish: to live his time with the person again, to be 18, young, trusting and full of love, when their eyes were everything to him. But it feels like too much to ask, so he just dies.

writings.title: I am the Sin, I am the Sinner.
writings.content: I am the Sin , I am the Sinner.
writings.explanation: The writer feels he is both the wrong that was done and the one who did it, as if all the blame is his.

writings.title: You are the hope, I am the hopeless.
writings.content: You are the hope, I am the hopeless.
writings.explanation: The writer says the other person is his hope, while he himself has no hope left.

writings.title: Grief is the residue left behind by love.
writings.content: Grief is the residue left behind by love.
writings.explanation: Grief is what is left behind after love. When love ends or is lost, the sadness that stays is grief.

writings.title: Vulnerable heart is a prey to love.
writings.content: Vulnerable heart is a prey to love.
writings.explanation: A soft, open heart is easy for love to catch and hurt, like an animal that gets hunted.

writings.title: we became heartless because, we once gave our heart.
writings.content:
we became heartless because,
we once gave our heart.
writings.explanation: The writer says we turned cold and stopped caring because we once gave our heart to someone, and now it is gone.

writings.title: Half death, Half devotion
writings.content: Half death, Half devotion
writings.explanation: The writer feels he is half dead inside and half still fully given over to the one he loves.

writings.title: The more I love the more they leave.
writings.content: The more I love the more they leave.
writings.explanation: The writer says the more he loves people, the more they leave him.

writings.title: My eyes still look for a glimpse of you
writings.content:
My eyes still look
for a glimpse of you
just like the way

I find the moon
in between the narrow
space of the branches.

I still find you in
the moment of happiness.

I still search for you in every way
possible. everything Reminds me of you.
writings.explanation: The writer still looks for the person everywhere, the way you catch the moon through small gaps between tree branches. He feels them in happy moments too. Everything reminds him of them.

writings.title: you survive on hope, rather than love itself.
writings.content: you survive on hope, rather than love itself.
writings.explanation: You keep going because you hope things will get better, not because the love itself is still there.

writings.title: What is love?
writings.content:
What is love?
Maybe something
which belongs to me,
is me , around me
and I can tell you
so many things about
love and it'll still be less,

there's love in my pulse
and even in my breath.
Love revolves around my heart
just like my existence does around yours.
writings.explanation: The writer says love is part of him, inside him and all around him, and no words could ever fully explain it. Love is in his heartbeat and his breath. It circles his heart, just as his whole life circles around the person.

writings.title: October is about to end, and November will soon arrive.
writings.content:
October is about to end,
and November will soon arrive.
The streets will once again fall silent,
leaving only memories to run aloud.
Soon, the year will come to an end,
but the memories won't.
It's been the same ever since you left.
Come back now.
writings.explanation: As October ends and November comes, the streets will go quiet and only memories will feel loud. The year will end, but the memories will not. It has been like this since the person left, and the writer asks them to come back.

writings.title: Death is an ecstasy, so lovers die every day.
writings.content:
Death is an ecstasy,
so lovers die every day
writings.explanation: He seems to say that losing yourself in love is like a sweet kind of dying, so people in love go through it every day.

writings.title: Of all the ways to become strangers, love is the cruelest.
writings.content:
Of all the ways to become strangers,
love is the cruelest.
writings.explanation: People can drift apart in many ways, but the most painful is when two people who loved each other end up as strangers.
