writings.title: you've grown so accustomed to your suffering…
writings.content:
you've grown
so accustomed to
your suffering that you've
forgotten what it feels
like to exist without it.

And perhaps,
somewhere beneath all that,
there is a part of you
still waiting for them
to notice that you haven't
been okay for a very long time.
writings.explanation: The writer says you have lived with pain so long that you forget what life feels like without it. And deep down, part of you is still waiting for someone to notice that you have not been okay for a long time.

writings.title: It's all love until it's your hope.
writings.content: It's all love until it's your hope.
writings.explanation: He seems to say love feels simple and sweet until you start living on hope for it; then it turns into waiting and hurt.

writings.title: What kind of love we live in?
writings.content:
What kind of
love we live in?
Where loving is mistaken
for an act of weakness
Where waiting is
mistaken for an act
of letting go?
If this is what loving feels
like then I am happy being
away from it because love was
never meant to be our weakness
it was always meant to be our strength.
writings.explanation: The writer asks what kind of love this is, where loving someone is seen as weak and waiting for someone is seen as giving up. If that is love, he would rather stay away from it, because love should make us strong, not weak.

writings.title: Permanence is a myth.
writings.content: Permanence is a myth.
writings.explanation: Nothing lasts forever. The idea that things will always stay the same is not real.

writings.title: There's a familiar chill in the air
writings.content:
There's a familiar chill in the air.
I wonder, is it the
winter or abandonment?
You sit with a profound sense of vulnerability
as the chill seeps into your bones.
and ask what are the boundaries
between the weather and what someone's
absence has left behind? Yeah, coldness.
writings.explanation: The writer feels a familiar cold in the air and wonders if it is winter or the feeling of being left. As the cold sinks in, you feel weak and unsafe, and you cannot tell the weather apart from the emptiness someone's leaving left behind. Both are just cold.

writings.title: I love, love from afar
writings.content: I love, love from afar
writings.explanation: The writer loves someone, but only from a distance.

writings.title: I was born with a fate of moth.
writings.content: “I was born with a fate of moth.”
writings.explanation: The writer feels he was born to be like a moth, always pulled toward the thing that will burn and hurt him, the way a moth flies into a flame.

writings.title: we survive on hope rather than love itself.
writings.content: we survive on hope rather than love itself.
writings.explanation: We keep going because of the hope that things will get better, not because the love is really still there.

writings.title: Life has an unsettling way of putting a catastrophe in front of you
writings.content:
Life has an unsettling
way of putting
a catastrophe in front of you.
On a random Tuesday
you'll be confronted with
the death of things you
thought were eternal.

Do not mistake the sunlight falling
on the floor for a miracle.
It's just sunlight, it's just life.
writings.explanation: Life can suddenly put something terrible in front of you. On an ordinary day, things you thought would last forever can end. The writer says a bit of sunlight on the floor is not a miracle; it is just sunlight, just ordinary life going on.

writings.title: Perhaps the hardest truths are not those that destroy what we possess
writings.content:
Perhaps the hardest truths
are not those that destroy
what we possess,
but those that reveal how
much of our lives we had already
built around love that never existed.
We continue performing the ordinary
rituals of existence, because performing
has became a new way of existing.
We almost get offended by how little
the universe gives us, all lies I must say
whatever, it never promised us anything.
writings.explanation: The writer says the hardest truths are not the ones that take things away, but the ones that show we built our lives around a love that was never real. We keep doing everyday things just to get by. We feel hurt by how little life gives us, but life never promised anything.

writings.title: how many lives have you abandoned?
writings.content:
how many lives have you abandoned?
let me ask you, again.
from how many lives
have you been abandoned by?
or have you truly loved any of them?
sit down stare at the sun, cry.
ask yourself what does living means to you.
I hope it doesn't merely means leaving.
writings.explanation: The writer asks how many people you have left, how many have left you, and whether you truly loved any of them. He tells you to sit, look at the sun, cry, and ask what living means to you, hoping it means more than just leaving.

writings.title: I wonder how much pain do you carry behind that smile.
writings.content:
I wonder how much pain
do you carry behind that smile.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders how much pain someone is hiding behind their smile.

writings.title: Pain is an absurdity of human existence
writings.content:
Pain is an absurdity
of human existence,
There is more perversed
in advance, about how
suffering can render the
inconsequential monumental,

how an unremarkable silence acquires
the jurisdiction of a catastrophe.
Maybe pain teaches you
how to become fluent in loss
and how to die while living it.
writings.explanation: The writer says pain makes no sense. Suffering can make small things feel huge, and a simple silence can feel like a disaster. Maybe pain teaches you to get used to losing things, and to feel dead while you are still alive.

writings.title: fear of loss is bigger than the loss itself
writings.content: fear of loss is bigger than the loss itself
writings.explanation: Being afraid of losing something hurts more than actually losing it.

writings.title: November has come, now everything I lost will echo in the cold air
writings.content:
November has come,
now everything
I lost will echo
in the cold air.

I wonder how many
winters a heart must
endure before it ceases to
distinguish between the
season and its own desolation.

It's Never the cold that kills us
It's always the memories.
writings.explanation: November has come, and in the cold air everything the writer lost comes back to him. He wonders how many winters a heart must go through before it cannot tell the cold season from its own emptiness. In the end, it is memories, not cold, that kill us.

writings.title: your eyes are the sin; I am the fallen.
writings.content: your eyes are the sin; I am the fallen.
writings.explanation: The writer says the person's eyes are what pulled him into wrong, and he is the one who fell because of them.

writings.title: Be good to my soul, November.
writings.content:
Be good to my soul,
November.
October already took a lot.
Now it's just me
and my grief left
to mourn the absence
of everything I have lost.

The trees are shedding what
the seasons could not spare,
much like I have been stripped
of things I once mistook for permanence.
writings.explanation: The writer asks November to be kind to him, because October already took so much. Now it is only him and his grief for all he has lost. Like trees losing their leaves, he has lost things he once thought would last forever.

writings.title: Curse of human soul is that it's never satisfied.
writings.content:
Curse of human soul is
that it's never satisfied.
writings.explanation: The sad thing about people is that they are never happy with what they have; they always want more.

writings.title: you never reach the end of love.
writings.content: you never reach the end of love.
writings.explanation: Love has no ending. However far you go in it, there is always more.

writings.title: I write your name and forget what to write after it.
writings.content:
I write your name and
forget what to write after it.
writings.explanation: The writer writes the person's name, and then his mind goes blank. Thinking of them leaves him with no other words.

writings.title: Flower shall grow from within my grave,
writings.content:
Flower shall grow
from within my grave,
and it shall be in
the colour of your eyes.
I won't need any other
visitors to visit my grave
except you.
just visit once in a while ,
you needn't bring flowers because
those flowers will
turn in the direction of your eyes
like sunflower, like sun.
writings.explanation: The writer pictures a flower growing from his grave in the color of the person's eyes. He wants only them to visit, once in a while, with no need to bring flowers, because that flower will turn toward their eyes like a sunflower turns to the sun.

writings.title: How often have you mistaken kindness for love?
writings.content:
How often have you
mistaken kindness for love?
writings.explanation: The writer asks how many times you have thought someone loved you when they were only being kind.

writings.title: How can two people go so far afar after knowing each other so closely.
writings.content:
How can two people go so afar
after knowing each other so closely.
writings.explanation: The writer wonders how two people who were once so close can end up so far apart.

writings.title: What can a lover do except for waiting?
writings.content:
What can a lover
do except for waiting?
What can a lover
do except for hoping?

they do both to bring back
the ruin of their existence alive,
they do both to delve into those
eyes to ruin themselves again.
and somehow they
still aches for more.
writings.explanation: The writer says a lover can only wait and hope. They do both hoping to bring back the very person who broke them, and to get lost in those eyes and be broken again. Still, they keep wanting more.

writings.title: I'll raise my hands and I'll let you decide whether I am begging or…
writings.content:
I'll raise my hands and I'll let you
decide whether I am begging or praying.
writings.explanation: The writer will raise his hands and let the person decide if he is begging them or praying to them. He seems to say his love is so deep that the two feel the same.

writings.title: But how can I stop loving you when you are all that my heart desires?
writings.content:
But how can I stop loving you when
you are all that my heart desires?
writings.explanation: The writer asks how he could ever stop loving the person when they are everything his heart wants.

writings.title: you are the sun, I am the sunflower.
writings.content: you are the sun, I am the sunflower.
writings.explanation: The person is like the sun to the writer, and he is like a sunflower that always turns toward them and needs them to live.

writings.title: We are the fragments of what we loved.
writings.content: We are the fragments of what we loved.
writings.explanation: We are made of broken pieces of the people and things we loved. What we loved stays in us, in pieces.
